investigation_summary: Cost-price discrepancies were investigated in BUS UAT for test products MC395379T1 and ML351505. MC395379T1 had a manually updated cost price in Bus Price Master Staging that differed from Realtime Staging Master. ML351505 had a NULL Price Group, causing its Realtime Staging Master Cost Price to remain aligned with Bus Price Master Staging; the Price Group was updated and the record reprocessed.
important_findings: For product MC395379T1, the cost price in Bus Price Master Staging was manually updated for testing and differed from Realtime Staging Master.
For product ML351505 in BUS UAT, the Price Group was NULL.
The NULL Price Group caused the Cost Price in Realtime Staging Master for ML351505 to remain the same as the value in Bus Price Master Staging.
The Bus Price Master Staging cost price for MC395379T1 was corrected and the record was reprocessed.
The Price Group for ML351505 was updated and the Bus Price Master Staging record was reprocessed.
root_cause: Manual cost-price modification in Bus Price Master Staging for MC395379T1 and a NULL Price Group for ML351505 in BUS UAT.
resolution: Corrected the cost price for MC395379T1 in Bus Price Master Staging and reprocessed the record; updated the Price Group for ML351505 and reprocessed its Bus Price Master Staging record.

investigation_summary: The Job Card and Activity for Sales Order A042368030 were migrated. Migration of I042297598 was subsequently confirmed, and the ticket was ready to be progressed to "Complete".
important_findings: The Job Card and Activity for Sales Order A042368030 were migrated.
Migration of I042297598 was confirmed.
The incident was considered resolved and ready for closure.
resolution: Migrated the Job Card and Activity for Sales Order A042368030; migration of I042297598 was confirmed.

investigation_summary: The issue was resolved: the Service Purchase Order became visible and the report generated successfully. The comments do not specify the underlying cause or corrective action.
important_findings: Service Purchase Order is visible after the fix.
The report is generating successfully after the fix.
resolution: The issue was fixed; Service Purchase Order visibility and report generation were restored.

investigation_summary: Users could not select model codes while creating quotes, stopping quotation operations. Investigation confirmed that the Catalog File was not imported and that the Model Code and Catalog files were not executed in the correct order. This left model codes unassociated with the Body Type selected in the quote, preventing their display; recovery was completed and models became selectable.
important_findings: Model codes on the quotation screen are displayed based on the Body Type selected in the quote.
The Catalog File was not imported into the system.
The Model Code and Catalog files were not executed in the correct order.
Because of the incorrect execution order, model codes were not configured with the Body Type selected in the quote.
The issue was caused by a work error during the file-loading process.
Recovery was completed and models became available for selection.
root_cause: The Catalog File was not imported and the Model Code and Catalog files were executed in the wrong order, leaving model codes unassociated with the selected Body Type.
resolution: Completed recovery by correcting the file-loading/execution process so that models became available for selection; planned automation and streamlining of catalog-file imports as a preventive measure.

investigation_summary: The AR Service Request approval flow was not progressing according to the configured hierarchy after the CMVM approval flow was migrated from the Chugoku setup. Investigation found that the headquarters position was incorrectly mapped in the migrated approval hierarchy. The mapping was corrected, and approval requests now progress correctly with users assigned based on the positions defined in the approval flow.
important_findings: The CMVM approval flow was initially not configured because required business data was not provided.
The approval flow was migrated from the Chugoku setup.
The headquarters position was not mapped correctly in the migrated approval hierarchy.
No user was assigned to the final approval level because no user existed for the HQ-Finance-GMgr position type.
After correction, approval requests progressed according to the configured hierarchy and users were assigned based on approval-flow positions.
root_cause: The headquarters position was incorrectly mapped in the approval hierarchy during migration of the CMVM approval flow from the Chugoku setup.
resolution: Corrected the headquarters-position mapping in the migrated approval hierarchy, restoring correct approval progression and position-based user assignment.

investigation_summary: Records for Temporary Resale price and Reevaluation request required record patching. After patching, the records were visible in the referenced environments. H000000176 and H000000182 remained unavailable in BUS because they are HDT records.
important_findings: Temporary Resale price and Reevaluation request records required patching.
Records were confirmed visible after the patching activity.
H000000176 and H000000182 are not visible in BUS because they are HDT records.
resolution: Patched the affected records, after which the Temporary Resale price and Reevaluation request records became visible.

investigation_summary: The initial approval error pop-up message was fixed for all UV entities. Approval history was still not created for UV Purchase Quote and UV Sales Order because approval-flow creation evaluates the Sales Rep Position, and the affected records were mapped to dummy BUS positions that are not processed by Approval Flow Logic. Proposed corrective options were to update the BUS Positions or add the dummy positions to the relevant approval flows.
important_findings: The initial approval error pop-up message was fixed for all UV entities.
Approval history was not created for UV Purchase Quote and UV Sales Order.
Approval-flow creation checks the Sales Rep Position of the transactional entities.
The affected SC Positions were mapped to Dummy Branch User Position values in BUS FORCE, which are not processed by Approval Flow Logic.
UV Purchase Quote 1-AAE27ZI was mapped from SC Position Branch Sales Staff HAOYANA to BUS Position Dummy_AY.
UV Sales Order E045288740 was mapped from SC Position Branch Sales Staff_WB_0013 to BUS Position Dummy_WY.
root_cause: The Sales Rep Position mappings in BUS FORCE assigned affected UV Purchase Quote and UV Sales Order records to dummy BUS positions, and those dummy positions were not processed by Approval Flow Logic.

investigation_summary: Cost-price discrepancies were investigated for products MC395379T1 and ML351505. The affected staging records were corrected and reprocessed, but the reason the Price master was missing during the initial setup despite the LPP material master existing was not established in the comments.
important_findings: For product MC395379T1, the Cost Price was manually updated in Bus Price Master Staging, causing it to differ from Realtime Staging Master.
For product ML351505 in BUS UAT, Price Group was NULL, so the Cost Price in Realtime Staging Master remained the same as Bus Price Master Staging.
The Cost Price and Price Group data were corrected in Bus Price Master Staging and the records were reprocessed.
The missing Price master during initial setup requires verification of export criteria, sample-data selection, and production environment setup procedures.
Material and price must always be paired.

investigation_summary: Drill-down for Job Cards with codes other than *AY* or *GY* was not functioning. The issue was resolved, and the customer confirmed that the drill-down now works normally.
important_findings: The incident affected drill-down of Job Cards with codes other than *AY* or *GY*.
After the corrective action, Job Cards with codes other than *AY* or *GY* could be drilled down successfully.
The customer verified normal operation and requested closure of the ticket.
resolution: Resolved the drill-down issue so that Job Cards with codes other than *AY* or *GY* can be drilled down successfully.

investigation_summary: Job Cards were initially stuck in Pending Approval because no approval flow was configured in the Service module. After the required approval flow was created, closure processing was validated and Job Cards closed successfully through automatic approval. In the FDP version, the Closure Approval Request process is designed to skip manual approval.
important_findings: No approval flow had been configured for Job Cards in the Service module, causing the Job Card to remain in Pending Approval.
After the approval flow was created, a valid approver was assigned to the Job Card.
Manual approval from the approver's inbox produced an unspecified error for JC I050000544.
In the FDP version, Closure Approval Request is designed to skip the manual approval step through automatic approval.
JC I050000559 and the subsequently tested Job Card were closed successfully through automatic approval.
root_cause: No approval flow was configured for Job Cards in the Service module, causing Job Cards to be stuck in Pending Approval.
resolution: Created the required Job Card approval flow and validated that Closure Approval Request in the FDP version closes Job Cards through automatic approval without manual approval.

investigation_summary: Accounts Receivable data migrated to the Chugoku Environment triggered a validation message when the character "㈱" was used in customer-related name fields. Investigation confirmed that "㈱" was missing from the allowed-character set for Company Name, Customer Name Print Line 1, and Customer Name Print Line 2. Code was updated in UAT to permit the character, and the affected Accounts Receivable data was recovered.
important_findings: The affected Accounts Receivable record had been migrated to the Chugoku Environment.
The character "㈱" was not included in the allowed-character set for Company Name, Customer Name Print Line 1, and Customer Name Print Line 2.
The missing allowed-character configuration caused the validation message.
Validation was explicitly implemented for the three affected fields.
The updated behavior was deployed and available for verification in UAT.
root_cause: The character "㈱" was not registered as an allowed character in validation for Company Name, Customer Name Print Line 1, and Customer Name Print Line 2.
resolution: Modified the code to add "㈱" to the allowed characters for the three affected fields in UAT and recovered the impacted Accounts Receivable data.

investigation_summary: The reported discrepancy in UV Assessment record counts was investigated between SC PROD and BUS UAT. The apparent lower record count was caused by a predefined query applied on the screen, not by incomplete migration. UV Assessment data from SC PROD was migrated to BUS UAT, with additional records created for testing/SIT.
important_findings: A predefined query on the screen limited the displayed UV Assessment records.
SC PROD contained 2,668 Vehicle type HDB, MDB, and LDB records.
BUS UAT contained the 2,668 UV Assessment records migrated from SC PROD.
BUS UAT also contained additional UV Assessment records created for testing/SIT.
root_cause: A predefined screen query caused fewer UV Assessment records to be displayed.
resolution: Confirmed that the SC PROD UV Assessment data had been migrated to BUS UAT and clarified that the record-count discrepancy was due to the predefined query.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned availability of orders after migration to target Bus NV Sales Orders. Engineering confirmed that only Insurance Orders were migrated, as previously agreed during target data migration discussions with the business.
important_findings: Insurance orders corresponding to target Bus NV Sales Orders were migrated.
Only Insurance Orders are available in the target.
The migration scope had already been communicated during target data migration discussions with the business.
root_cause: The target data migration scope included only Insurance Orders.
resolution: Insurance orders corresponding to target Bus NV Sales Orders were migrated; no additional corrective action was documented.

investigation_summary: The Delivery & Invoice BIP Reports populated the branch name from inventory information on the Service Purchase Order. For order J044501916, no inventory existed for the WY Branch, so the BUS head office inventory BUS FORCE was used. The organization configured on BUS FORCE was incorrect; it was corrected to Headquarter (B), after which the correct headquarters name populated in BIP.
important_findings: Branch Name in Delivery & Invoice BIP Reports is referenced from the inventory on the Service Purchase Order.
SC Force inventories are mapped to BUS inventories under the transactional data migration logic.
No corresponding inventory data existed for the WY Branch for order J044501916.
BUS FORCE was used as the fallback inventory for cases without WY Branch inventory.
The organization configured on BUS FORCE was incorrect, causing the incorrect branch/headquarters name in BIP.
Other BIP reports were requested for verification after the mapping correction.
root_cause: The organization mapped to the fallback BUS FORCE inventory was incorrect.
resolution: Updated the BUS FORCE inventory organization mapping to Headquarter (B) and confirmed that BIP populated the correct headquarters name.

investigation_summary: The latest Sales Quote revision was not reflected in the Sales Order because quote synchronization stopped during processing. The Sales Order had synchronized successfully through Sales Quote Revision 4, but a concurrent manual update to Line Number 30 (Additional Body) caused a Siebel record-concurrency error. The affected data was recovered, and normal operation was confirmed in UAT; no system modification was required.
important_findings: Sales Order synchronization completed successfully through Sales Quote Revision 4.
The Sync Sales Order step failed in EAI Siebel Adapter > Synchronize while writing MF RF Order Entry - Line Items / MF Order Item record 30.
The backend logged SBL-DAT-00523, indicating the selected record was modified by another user after retrieval, along with SBL-BPR-00162 and SBL-EAI-04451.
All line items except Line Number 30 (Additional Body) were updated at the same time by Siebel Script, confirming normal synchronization for those items.
Line Number 30 (Additional Body) had a different Last Updated Source and Last Updated timestamp, showing an application-user update; it was also recorded in CX_EAI_LOGS.
Recovery of the affected record was completed, and the process operated normally in UAT.
root_cause: A user manually updated Sales Order Line Number 30 (Additional Body) while the latest Sales Quote synchronization was in progress. Siebel detected the concurrent record change and stopped synchronization with SBL-DAT-00523.
resolution: Recovered the affected record. No system fix was implemented because the issue was identified as a rare concurrent-user-operation scenario and normal operation was confirmed in UAT.
technical_entities: MF RF Order Entry - Line Items

investigation_summary: MF NV Sales Order TOB Sales Posting and MF Recycle Reconcile KB WF were successfully processed after restarting the Batch Components. MF NV Reservation Request Batch Process could not be meaningfully tested because the expiration date is read-only.
important_findings: Restarting the Batch Components allowed MF NV Sales Order TOB Sales Posting to process successfully.
Restarting the Batch Components allowed MF Recycle Reconcile KB WF to process successfully.
MF NV Reservation Request Batch Process test preparation was not feasible because the expiration date is always read-only.
resolution: Restarted the Batch Components.
technical_entities: MF NV Sales Order TOB Sales Posting
MF NV Reservation Request Batch Process

investigation_summary: The Discount value for JC# I050852399 was transmitted as 0 from Siebel. Investigation confirmed that the Discount field is mapped to "Quote Line Item -> Manual Discount Amount", which was 0 for the affected Quote Line Item. Recovery was completed by setting the Manual Discount Amount to the Total Discount Amount Available so correct invoices could be issued.
important_findings: The Discount field is mapped to "Quote Line Item -> Manual Discount Amount".
For JC# I050852399, the Quote Line Item Manual Discount Amount was 0.
Siebel therefore transmitted the Discount amount as 0.
The mapping change was implemented through CR MFTBCFFR:3251.
Recovery updated the Manual Discount Amount according to the Total Discount Amount Available.
root_cause: The Discount mapping uses "Quote Line Item -> Manual Discount Amount", and the Manual Discount Amount for JC# I050852399 was set to 0.
resolution: Set the Manual Discount Amount for JC# I050852399 to the Total Discount Amount Available, enabling correct invoices to be issued.

investigation_summary: Dealer code was updated to 'B' and Dealer Name to 'FUSO BUS' for Minor parts/replacement parts storage. The comments do not confirm validation results, root cause, or incident closure.
important_findings: Dealer code was updated to 'B'.
Dealer Name was updated to 'FUSO BUS'.
The update applies to Minor parts/replacement parts storage.
Validation was requested but no outcome was provided.

investigation_summary: The incident involved an inactive Re-edit button on the Japanese screen and failure to create a JV when a Job Card was closed. The initial Re-edit fix was not effective for the Japanese version. The Re-edit button was subsequently enabled on the Japanese screen, and JV creation on Job Card closure was restored.
important_findings: The Re-edit button was initially reported as fixed but remained inactive on the Japanese screen.
The Japanese-screen Re-edit button was later enabled.
JV was not being created when the Job Card was closed.
JV creation was later confirmed to work successfully when the Job Card was closed.
resolution: Enabled the Re-edit button on the Japanese screen and fixed JV creation when the Job Card is closed.

investigation_summary: Company details were not visible in the top-left section of the used vehicle sales order form. The issue was fixed, and retesting passed.
important_findings: Company details are displayed in the top-left section of the used vehicle sales order form after the fix.
Re-test passed.
resolution: Fixed the issue so that Company details are visible in the top-left section of the used vehicle sales order form.

investigation_summary: The issue was caused by an incorrect language code configured in the LOVs for Plan Date Addition Master. The language code was corrected.
important_findings: A wrong language code was present in the LOV configuration.
The affected area was Plan Date Addition Master.
Correcting the language code for the LOVs resolved the issue.
root_cause: Incorrect language code configured in the LOVs for Plan Date Addition Master.
resolution: Fixed the language code for the LOVs in Plan Date Addition Master.

investigation_summary: Job Cards were assigning incorrect labor price lists for their creation branch. In BUS UAT, Branch Price List selection depends on the Billing Type and a non-blank Discount Classification from the Vehicle/Chassis; otherwise the system defaults to an SC Price List such as FDP B Price List. The price list setup was corrected, and newly created Job Cards correctly selected the applicable Branch Price List; existing Job Cards retained the previously stamped Branch Labor Price List Id.
important_findings: Branch Price List is selected only when Billing Type is an eligible inspection-related value and Discount Classification is populated.
Discount Classification is sourced from the Vehicle/Chassis record.
When the selection conditions are not met, the system defaults to the SC Price List, including FDP Price List/FDP B Price List.
Job Card I050000511 used a Vehicle/Chassis with blank Discount Classification, causing FDP B Price List to be selected.
Existing Job Cards created before the price list setup correction retain the old Branch Labor Price List Id, including for newly added labor line items.
A newly created Job Card correctly selected Branch GY Price List after the setup update.
root_cause: The price list setup contained an incorrect Branch Labor Price List configuration; Job Cards created before the correction had the old/wrong Branch Labor Price List Id stamped on them. Additionally, blank Discount Classification causes the expected fallback to the SC/FDP Price List rather than a Branch Price List.
resolution: Updated the price list setup and validated that newly created Job Cards select the correct branch-specific price list, including Branch GY Price List. Existing Job Cards must be replaced with newly created Job Cards to use the corrected stamped price list.

investigation_summary: The MF EIM Product Release process was retested using products created through EIM rather than manually created products. Products created from EIM were released successfully. The issue was resolved by using EIM-created products for the product release process.
important_findings: The product release process was retested after creating products with EIM instead of manually.
Products created through EIM were released successfully.
Product release occurs when the product is created from EIM.
MF Account Revenue Process job was stated as not required in FDP or Bus.
root_cause: Products were initially created manually rather than through EIM, while the product release process requires products to be created from EIM.
resolution: Create products through EIM before running the MF EIM Product Release process.

investigation_summary: Insurance Company Code (10 Digit) options were initially configured only for Insurance Company Name codes 17, 09, EJ, and WD because the original business file contained only those codes. The business requested coverage for all insurance companies and supplied a new initial settings file. The initial records were replaced by importing the updated file into the bus UAT application.
important_findings: The original Insurance Company Code (10 Digit) file contained only codes 17, 09, EJ, and WD.
Insurance Company Code (10 Digit) options were visible only when an Insurance Company Name associated with one of those codes was selected.
A new initial settings file was provided with instructions to delete the initially imported records and import the replacement file.
The updated business file was imported into the bus UAT application.
A question was raised that the Company appeared as "SC" although the provided file was labeled "FDP"; no explicit explanation was recorded.
root_cause: The initial configuration was based on a business file containing only Insurance Company Name codes 17, 09, EJ, and WD.
resolution: Deleted/replaced the initially imported configuration and imported the new initial settings file for Insurance Company Code (10 Digit) into the bus UAT application.

investigation_summary: The New car / NV incident covered multiple configuration, data, workflow, and BIP report-output defects. Direct option entry, part-number filtering, recycling-fee detail generation, registration-fee amounts, and several quotation/order-form report issues were corrected or validated. However, the final status still listed unresolved defects, including Purchase Plan configuration, recycling-fee labeling, quotation report formatting, approval navigation, mapping, and downstream workflow issues.
important_findings: Direct option entry failed because the option price was not fetched from VC; after the fix, the option price was fetched correctly and no error was displayed.
Additional part-number options appeared because the filter had been removed for a CR requirement; correcting the filter logic restricted the selection.

Recycling Fee and taxable/non-taxable registration-fee details were created after Vehicle Classification was aligned with the Recycle Fee Master and Add Taxes & Expenses was used; the registration-fee amount display was subsequently fixed.

Purchase Plan Master records were missing for HB, LB, and MB compared with SC PROD. Temporary records allowed Purchase Plan PDF generation, but were reverted pending confirmation of the required product-class scope.
Purchase Plan PDF generation requires Purchase Plan Generation = Y on the NV Quote screen; the flag becomes Y when MF Sales Profit >= MF First Profit Amount.

Order-form address data was missing because relevant transaction data was NULL on the SC side; a data patch for NV Transactional Migration records in BUS restored address retrieval in Order Sheet BIP's.

investigation_summary: Migrated accounts in the Chugoku environment displayed mismatched address details, including street number, building name, and room number. Investigation confirmed that address information IDs were migrated incorrectly during a re-patch performed approximately 20 days after the initial SC-to-Chugoku migration. Recovery was completed for all shared affected records; no similar issue was found in other production environments, and no code or system modification was required.
important_findings: Affected accounts were migrated from the SC environment to the Chugoku environment.
Most records were imported successfully during the initial migration, but some records required a re-patch approximately 20 days later.
The re-patch incorrectly migrated address information IDs, causing address-detail mismatches.
Recovery was completed for all previously shared affected records, including account 0000L43620.
Checks of other production environments found no similar incidents.
The issue was data-migration-related, not code-related; future migration verification will be strengthened.
root_cause: During the re-patch of records following the initial migration from the SC environment to the Chugoku environment, address information IDs were migrated incorrectly, resulting in mismatched address details.
resolution: Recovered all shared affected records and committed to strengthened verification during future data migration activities. No system modification was required.

investigation_summary: The blank expense calculation sheet behavior was investigated and determined to be expected system configuration, not a defect. The implemented logic generates expense calculation sheet data from an Invoice only when the associated Order Amount is greater than 0. The behavior was replicated in FDP UAT using UV Sales Orders with zero and positive amounts.
important_findings: Expense calculation sheet generation from Invoice requires Order Amount to be greater than 0 for report data to be populated.
An Order Amount of 0 generates a blank expense calculation sheet.
The behavior was replicated in FDP UAT.
UV Sales Order E001305081 had Amount = 0.
UV Sales Order E001302483 had Amount > 0.
root_cause: Configured logic only populates the expense calculation sheet when the Invoice's associated Order Amount is greater than 0; zero-value orders produce a blank report.
resolution: No code fix was required; the incident was classified as system configuration/expected behavior and proposed for rejection.

investigation_summary: An issue prevented Expense Invoice generation. The issue was fixed, and Expense Invoice generation completed successfully without errors. Retesting passed.
important_findings: Expense Invoice generation was failing before the fix.
After the fix, the Expense Invoice was generated successfully without error.
Re-testing passed.
resolution: The issue was fixed; the specific corrective action was not documented.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned the warning symbol in the UV Vehicle Delivery Slip Report generated as a PDF in BUS. Initial checks of multiple Delivery Slip Report records did not reproduce an issue. The PDF was modified for the normal case, and retesting passed.
important_findings: The issue involved the warning symbol in the Delivery Slip Report.
The report is issued to users in PDF format in the normal case.
The affected report was the UV Vehicle Delivery Slip Report generated in BUS.
The PDF was fixed and the customer confirmed that retesting passed.
resolution: Modified the PDF for the UV Vehicle Delivery Slip Report generated in BUS; re-test passed.

investigation_summary: The BUS logo on the UV Sales Order Sheet 2 was initially positioned according to the referenced FDP Force template, but both BUS UAT and FDP Chugoku logo alignment were found to be incorrect relative to the center line. After adjusting placement, the logo was also found to be horizontally stretched compared with the Brand Policy. The BUS logo was corrected to its original size and approved; re-test passed.
important_findings: Bus Force BIP templates reference FDP Force templates.
The initial BUS logo placement matched the FDP template, but the logo appeared shifted because of differing logo widths and was not correctly centered.
FDP Chugoku and BUS logo placement were both identified as being to the right of the center line.
The updated UV Sales Order Sheet 2 logo was horizontally stretched compared with the Brand Policy.
The BUS logo was corrected to its original size and the resulting balance was approved.
root_cause: The BUS logo configuration inherited from the FDP Force template used incorrect positioning for the logo dimensions and resulted in a horizontally stretched logo on UV Sales Order Sheet 2.
resolution: Adjusted the BUS logo placement and restored the logo to its original size in Bus Force; the corrected layout was approved and re-test passed.

investigation_summary: Engineering tested generation of the Used Vehicle Purchase Quote PDF across multiple quote statuses and successfully generated the PDFs. No PDF-generation issue was reproduced, and the incident was confirmed as re-test passed.
important_findings: Used Vehicle Purchase Quote PDF generation succeeded for quote 2-LOTV7 with status Approved.
Used Vehicle Purchase Quote PDF generation succeeded for quote 2-LKD7G with status Pending Approval and quote 1-CVWGUF6 with status In Progress.
No specific affected record was provided for further investigation.
Re-test Passed.

investigation_summary: The issue was replicated while saving a record and occurred once per session. Investigation identified a database parameter configuration issue. The database configuration was corrected, and subsequent application validation showed no further errors; retesting passed.
important_findings: The issue occurred while saving a record.
The error occurred one time in a session.
The cause was identified as a parameter issue in the database configuration.
After the configuration fix, no further application error was observed.
Retesting passed.
root_cause: Incorrect database parameter configuration.
resolution: Fixed the database parameter configuration and validated that saving records no longer produced the error.

investigation_summary: The incident involved duplicate values in the Vehicle Type list. An initial fix was incomplete because MDT, Trailer, and LB still each had two values. The duplicate values were subsequently fixed for all Vehicle Type entries and the result was accepted.
important_findings: Duplicate values existed for Vehicle Type.
The initial correction did not remove duplicate entries for MDT, Trailer, and LB.
A subsequent fix addressed duplicate values for all Vehicle Type entries.
The final result was confirmed as passed.
resolution: Corrected duplicate values for all Vehicle Type entries, including MDT, Trailer, and LB.

investigation_summary: The vehicle inspection certificate import error was resolved by correcting a parameter configuration in OCI setup. The reported customer code in the User-Customer Code Pick Applet was identified as an Account Receivable (AR) code rather than a missing customer-master account. The pick applet is designed to display both Account and corresponding AR codes, consistent across Bus Force, SC Force, and SC Production; Japanese character display was also corrected.
important_findings: The vehicle inspection certificate import error was caused by an OCI setup parameter configuration issue.
Customer code "0009381071" was identified as an AR code of an account.
User-Customer Code Pick Applet displays both Account codes and Account Receivable(Customer) codes.
When an AR code differs from its Parent Account code, it cannot be directly searched in Accounts master; the Parent Account can be identified by customer name.
The behavior in Bus Force was confirmed to match SC Force and SC Production.
Japanese characters were subsequently displayed correctly.
root_cause: The vehicle inspection certificate import issue was caused by an incorrect parameter configuration in OCI setup. The apparently unmigrated customer shown in the pick applet was an expected Account Receivable (AR) code displayed alongside its Parent Account, not a missing customer-master record.
resolution: Corrected the OCI setup parameter configuration, restoring vehicle inspection certificate import processing. Confirmed that the User-Customer Code Pick Applet intentionally shows both Account and corresponding AR codes, and corrected Japanese character display.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned missing approval configuration for Parts Quotes. Approval Eligibility Master was created to match the FDP Chugoku Production environment, and approval flows for Parts Quotes were configured. Parts Quotes subsequently moved to Pending Approval status.
important_findings: Approval Eligibility Master was configured to match the FDP Chugoku Production environment.
Approval flows were created for Parts Quotes.
After configuration, the Parts Quote transitioned to Pending Approval status.
root_cause: Approval Eligibility Master and approval flows for Parts Quotes were not configured.
resolution: Created the Approval Eligibility Master and configured approval flows for Parts Quotes to match the FDP Chugoku Production environment.

investigation_summary: The approval flow for Parts Sales Return was created to match the FDP Chugoku Production Environment. The reported Parts Sales Return order M050000356 was below 100000 Yen, while Chugoku production auto approval is configured for return orders above 100000 Yen.
important_findings: The Parts Sales Return approval flow was created to match the FDP Chugoku Production Environment.
Parts Sales Return order M050000356 had an amount below 100000 Yen.
In Chugoku production, auto approval is configured for return orders with amounts greater than 100000 Yen.
root_cause: Parts Sales Return order M050000356 did not meet the Chugoku production auto-approval threshold, which applies only to return orders above 100000 Yen.
resolution: Created the Parts Sales Return approval flow to match the FDP Chugoku Production Environment configuration.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned an incorrect logo. The logo was corrected and shared for customer review.
important_findings: The reported issue involved a logo.
The logo was fixed as shown in an attached file.
resolution: Fixed the logo.

investigation_summary: SC Price Lists header records were created in Bus Force solely to support transactional data migration; price list items were not migrated. The headers must remain after migration because transactional data, including service line items, references them. Deleting the price lists would remove those references.
important_findings: Only SC Price Lists header records were migrated for transactional data migration.
Price list items were not migrated.
During transactional-data processing in Bus, the price list is re-selected according to Bus price list data.
Migrated price list headers are referenced by transactional data and service line items.
Deleting the price lists would delete their references from service line items.
root_cause: Price list header records cannot be deleted after migration because they are referenced by migrated transactional data, including service line items.
resolution: Retain the migrated SC Price Lists header records after transactional data migration.

investigation_summary: The BIP logo issue was corrected. The comment indicates the fix was completed and provided for review.
important_findings: The BIP logo was fixed.
Attached files were provided for review.
resolution: Fixed the BIP logo.

investigation_summary: Vehicle data in the BUS environment had incorrect Dealer Code values and missing migration coverage for related fields from the Chugoku migration. Dealer Code was corrected to 1001 for all vehicles, Latest Supplier Code was updated, and a data patch was completed for Latest Transfer Date and Latest Transferee Code. Data validation was completed by Mr. Sasaki.
important_findings: Incorrect Dealer Code values were stamped for all vehicles in the BUS environment.
Dealer Code was corrected to 1001 for all vehicles.
Latest Supplier Code was updated for all vehicles.
Some fields in the same tab were not included in the Chugoku migration; the reason for the exclusion was not identified.
A data patch was completed for Latest Transfer Date and Latest Transferee Code.

investigation_summary: The latest Sales Quote revisions were not reflected in the Sales Order after the original quote line was deleted and replaced with a new line using a different Model Code. Deleting the original line removed the line-number reference required by the quote-to-Sales Order synchronization. The new quote line's line number was updated to match the original line, and the Sales Order then synchronized successfully with the latest quote revision.
important_findings: The initial quote used Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4', and the Sales Order was created from that quote.
In quote revision 2, the original line item was deleted and replaced with a new line using Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4-G830'.
Deleting the original quote line caused the original line-number reference to be lost, preventing Sales Quote synchronization with the Sales Order.
The Sales Order remained synchronized only through revision 1 despite subsequent quote revisions up to revision 5.
Updating the replacement quote line's line number to match the original line restored synchronization with the latest quote revision.
Users should update the Model Code on an existing quote line instead of deleting and recreating the line.
root_cause: User deleted the original quote line item and created a replacement line with a different Model Code, which removed the line-number reference required to synchronize the Sales Quote with the Sales Order.
resolution: Updated the line number of the quote line with Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4-G830' to match the previously created quote line; the Sales Order then synchronized with the latest quote revision. No system fix was required.

In Production, only records specified in the initial file will be registered in the SC master.

investigation_summary: Migration validation identified mismatched record counts and non-bus data in Bus Force/BUS UAT across NV Opportunities, NV Quotes, NV Sales orders, Chassis Orders, and Body Orders. The migration logic included NV Opportunities when at least one related entity had a bus product class, which could include associated truck data. A confirmed mapping defect caused SC name and Branch Name values to be reversed or displayed incorrectly; Branch Mapping and SC-level mapping were corrected, while several other migration defects remained under investigation.
important_findings: Bus migration criteria included records where NV Opportunity, NV Quote, Vehicle, or Model Code contained a bus product class: HB, MB, LB, 320, 330, or 340.
The migration criteria could include truck-associated data when a related entity contained bus information, resulting in records considered unnecessary for Bus Force validation.
For Daisuke Higuchi records created before 2026/06/01, Bus UAT and SC showed matching counts of 148 NV Opportunities and 318 NV Quote records when equivalent filters were applied.
For Chassis Orders created before 2026/06/01 with product class HB, MB, or LB, SC Force had 9,107 records and Bus Force had 9,051 records; 56 records were not migrated for documented reasons.
The SC name/Branch Name reversal was caused by missing SC-level mapping, preventing correct mapping.
NV Sales order Branch Name information was updated using the revised Branch Mapping; competitor data for new car deals was migrated to BUS UAT.

The JCO creator was set to "Siebel Administrator" instead of a regular user.
The workshop code was blank, causing Department Code(CSJS200) and Department Code(CSJS300) to be blank.
Blank department codes prevented the JVs for JC I050809872 and I050809889 from being linked to KB.
The issue was classified as a recovery error rather than a logic issue.
root_cause: Manual setting of the quote to "Customer Approved" in MFTBCFFR-5819 caused the JCO creator to be "Siebel Administrator", resulting in a blank workshop code and blank Department Code(CSJS200) and Department Code(CSJS300), which prevented JV linkage to KB.
resolution: Recovery was completed; the JVs for JC I050809872 and I050809889 were to be linked to KB that night. No logic fix was required.

resolution: The original position associated with department code 2011 was mapped back to user HKAKIYA.

investigation_summary: Multiple New/Used Vehicles/NVUV master-data migration and configuration discrepancies were identified during UAT and Production environment validation, including incorrect model-code relationships, mismatched master records, and options not displayed in VC. Investigation showed that several migrated masters and configurations were not aligned with the SC version or contained additional/incorrect values. The affected master data was corrected, required Campaign model codes were added, and VC option display was fixed; final confirmation was received from Mr. Tsunoda.
important_findings: Campaign Master data received from the business initially lacked model information, resulting in incorrect or missing target model codes.
Recommended Model Master/Substitute&Recommend contained additional records with relation type Campaign under model codes that were not applicable.
Registration&Deliveryrequestdeadlinemaster was corrected to retain only records for the 11SC organization, matching the SC version.
RecycleFeeMaster contained an unknown selection value "AB", which was removed.

Option Category Master/Optcategory and Option Information Master/Optinformation could not be validated because options were not displayed in VC; the fix restored option and corresponding price display.
KitMaster had not been migrated during the Chugoku migration and was subsequently migrated from SC, using 5SCB for the 5SC ID in Bus Force.
root_cause: Master-data migration and configuration were not consistently aligned with the SC version, causing incorrect model-code relationships, extra or invalid master values, missing migration data, and VC option-display issues.
resolution: Corrected the affected master data and configurations to align with SC, removed invalid RecycleFeeMaster value "AB", added all required model codes to Campaign, migrated KitMaster from SC, and fixed VC so all options and corresponding prices display correctly. Final validation was confirmed by Mr. Tsunoda.

investigation_summary: Job Card I000471957 was initially closed on 23/06/2026, later re-edited, and closed again on 30/06/2026. Re-Edit Journal vouchers were not created if the re-edit occurred before the issue was fixed on 24/06/2026. Recovery covered impacted Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026, so this later re-closed Job Card was not captured; ongoing functionality was confirmed as working.
important_findings: Job Card I000471957 was closed on 23/06/2026, re-edited, and closed again on 30/06/2026.
The Re-Edit Journal voucher creation issue was resolved on 24/06/2026.
Recovery was performed for impacted Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026.
I000471957 may have been re-edited before 24/06/2026, when Re-Edit JVs were not created, but was re-closed after the recovery cutoff.
The incident was considered an uncatchable historical event; no issue was identified in ongoing functionality.
root_cause: Job Card I000471957 was likely re-edited before the 24/06/2026 fix, when Re-Edit Journal vouchers were not created, but its subsequent closure on 30/06/2026 caused it to fall outside the recovery scope for Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026.
resolution: The Re-Edit Journal voucher creation defect was fixed on 24/06/2026 and recoveries were completed for impacted Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026. No additional action was taken for I000471957 because it was identified as an uncatchable historical case and ongoing functionality was working.

investigation_summary: Goodwill quote approvals created by the Branch Service Manager failed to update the header status when the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow was generated. The issue was replicated on FDP-UAT1 and traced to a missing LOV required by that approval flow. A corresponding LOV was created and verified on FDP-UAT1; deployment to FDP-Shikoku-PROD was approved.
important_findings: The issue was replicated on FDP-UAT1 for JC#: I001305186 and Quote#: 1-8H5UAJ.
The issue occurred when approval was generated for the Branch Head using the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow.
Quotes containing Goodwill line items created by the Branch Service Manager generated the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow.
The required LOV for the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow was missing.
The missing LOV caused an approval-process error and prevented the header status from being updated correctly.
After creating the corresponding LOV on FDP-UAT1, header status updates were verified for JC#: I001305215 and Quote#: 1-8H3NSR.
root_cause: The LOV required by the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow was missing, causing the approval process to error and preventing the quote header status from updating.
resolution: Created the corresponding LOV for the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow on FDP-UAT1, verified correct header-status updates, and received approval to deploy the change to FDP-Shikoku-PROD.

investigation_summary: The Recycle Fee Order was not displayed in the corresponding Chassis Order because the D21F file was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file from TOB. At D21F processing time, the Chassis Order and vehicle record did not exist, so the Recycle Fee Order could not be created. Recovery was completed by re-executing D21F after D21A completed; however, the requested permanent problem resolution was not accepted, and Jira closure was rejected.
important_findings: D21F was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file, as confirmed by the attached file timestamps.
The Chassis Order and vehicle record had not been created when D21F was processed, preventing creation of the Recycle Fee Order.
Processing D21A later created the Chassis Order, but did not automatically recreate the already missed Recycle Fee Order.
Re-executing D21F after successful D21A processing created the Recycle Fee Order and made it visible in the Chassis Order.
The incident was attributed to TOB file processing sequence rather than a Siebel system defect.
Email monitoring was implemented for FDP Production, but it was characterized as supporting recovery rather than resolving the underlying ordering issue.
root_cause: The TOB D21F file was processed before the corresponding D21A file, so the required Chassis Order and vehicle record did not exist when the Recycle Fee Order creation process ran.
resolution: The affected record was recovered by re-executing the D21F process after successful completion of the D21A process.

investigation_summary: Delivery completion approval history was not created when a rejected Delivery Approval Request was regenerated. After rejection, the Sales Order status changed to "Rejected" and the user could trigger "Generate Approval" again; the status then changed to "Delivery Pending Approval" without generating approval history. The affected record was recovered, and corrected approval flows were implemented in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to Production on June 30 after business hours.
important_findings: The issue occurred after a Delivery Approval Request was rejected and "Generate Approval" was triggered again.
After rejection, the Sales Order status changed to "Rejected" and the "Generate Approval" button became active again.
On the second "Generate Approval" action, the Sales Order status changed to "Delivery Pending Approval", but no approval history was generated.
The configured approval flow for this scenario was not functioning as expected.
Recovery for the affected record was completed and its approval history was generated successfully.
Corrected approval flows were implemented in FDP UAT-1, validated with reference record UV SO#: E001305061, and deployed to Production.
root_cause: The approval flow configured for regenerating a Delivery Approval Request after rejection was not functioning as expected, so the approval flow did not execute and approval history was not generated.
resolution: Recovered the affected record and implemented corrected approval flows in FDP UAT-1, then deployed the corrected approval flows to Production on June 30 after business hours.

investigation_summary: The incident was recovered on 2026-06-29. Engineering continued investigating the root cause and attempted to reproduce the scenario in the UAT environment, but no findings or confirmed cause were reported.
important_findings: Recovery for the incident was completed on 2026-06-29.
The root-cause investigation remained ongoing after recovery.
Engineering attempted to reproduce the scenario in the UAT environment.
No replication results, root cause, or permanent corrective action were documented.

investigation_summary: The user could not create a Body Building purchase order in UV SO for body building line item Row ID 1-3Z76YI. Investigation confirmed that PO# F000601618 had already been created for this line item. The subsequent manual update of the Body Building Unit Price from ¥16,000 to ¥17,600 did not allow creation of another PO; existing functionality permits only one PO per line item.
important_findings: PO# F000601618 was already associated with body building line item Row ID 1-3Z76YI.
The Body Building Unit Price in the existing Body Building Purchase Order was manually changed from ¥16,000 to ¥17,600.
Existing functionality prevents creation of a second Purchase Order for the same line item after a PO has been created.
The behavior was reproduced in UAT-1 using UV SO# E001305053 and PO# F001305055 after changing the Body Building Unit Price from ¥22,000 to ¥27,900.
root_cause: A Purchase Order, PO# F000601618, already existed for body building line item Row ID 1-3Z76YI; the system does not allow a second PO for the same line item, regardless of a subsequent Body Building Unit Price update.
resolution: No recovery or fix was required because the observed behavior is existing functionality.

investigation_summary: Users could not create a Body Building Purchase Order from a UV Sales Order because the 'Create Purchase Order' button was inactive when the Delivery Completion Request was Rejected. The existing logic enabled the button only for Sales Order statuses Approved, Registration Completed, and Sales Posting Completed. The logic was changed in FDP UAT-1 and released to production on 09 July.
important_findings: The 'Create Purchase Order' button was inactive because the UV Sales Order status was Rejected.
Existing button-enable logic allowed only Approved, Registration Completed, and Sales Posting Completed Sales Order statuses.
The requested behavior was to keep 'Create Purchase Order' active when the Delivery Completion Request is Rejected.
An Approval Request was accidentally clicked, leaving the Approval workflow in Pending status although approval history was not generated.
The fix was applied and verified using FDP UAT-1 reference UV SO# E001305061 before production release.
root_cause: The existing UV Sales Order logic did not enable the 'Create Purchase Order' button when the Delivery Completion Request was Rejected.
resolution: Updated the logic so users can create a Body Building Purchase Order in UV Sales Order when the Delivery Completion Request is Rejected; deployed to FDP UAT-1 and released to production on 09 July.

investigation_summary: Journal vouchers (JVs) were not created for Parts Sales Return Order M000486052 because its base amount was negative. The JV creation logic was updated to support negative base amounts for all JV types of Parts Sales Return Order, and missing JVs were manually recovered. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and deployed to production in the regular release on 2026-07-09.
important_findings: JV creation for Parts Sales return types previously occurred only when the base amount was greater than 0.
Order M000486052 had a negative amount, preventing JV creation.
Missing JVs for the affected order were manually created and scheduled to link to KB through the regular batch.
The updated logic allows JV creation for all JV types of Parts Sales Return Order when the base amount is negative.
The fix was tested using UAT-1 Test Record M001305079 and approved for production release.
root_cause: The JV creation logic excluded Parts Sales Return Orders with negative base amounts because it only allowed creation when the base amount was greater than 0.
resolution: Manually created the missing JVs for order M000486052 and deployed an updated JV creation logic that supports negative base amounts for all JV types of Parts Sales Return Order to production on 2026-07-09.

investigation_summary: The Branch Manager Name was blank or incorrect in the NV Quotation BIP report for Chugoku Production after logic from MFTBCFFR-5622 was applied. MFTBCFFR-5622 selected a Branch-Head from the Sales Representative's branch organization, which did not meet the required Fuso Chugoku hub-and-spoke behavior. Reverting MFTBCFFR-5622 restored previous behavior but did not satisfy the requested requirement to display the hub branch manager name. The final requested correction and implementation schedule were not provided.
important_findings: MFTBCFFR-5622 logic was applied to all production environments and displayed the Branch-Head based on the branch organization of the Sales Representative at quote creation.
For NV Quote# 2-BUK481, Sales Representative D8HIDMUR had no user with position type "Branch-Head" in the corresponding branch organization, causing the BIP field to be blank.

The required behavior for Fuso Chugoku is to display the hub branch manager name according to the SC hub-and-spoke structure, rather than a fixed personal name or the Sales Representative's branch Branch-Head.
The Branch Manager Name is not obtained from the Employee Master; prior logic displayed a system-configured value based on the branch where the quotation was originally created.
Reverting MFTBCFFR-5622 in FDP UAT-8 and Chugoku Production restored pre-MFTBCFFR-5622 report behavior, but the customer confirmed this was still incorrect.
root_cause: The MFTBCFFR-5622 BIP report logic selected the Branch-Head from the Sales Representative's branch organization, rather than using the required Fuso Chugoku hub-and-spoke mapping to display the hub branch manager name.

investigation_summary: The Trade-in Assessment Purchase Order was not generated because the UV Sales Order status was manually changed to "Approved" during backend recovery activity for MFTBCFFR-5894. This bypassed the standard approval process and its dependent PO-generation trigger. Recovery was completed successfully, and the recovery SOP was updated to require validation of triggers and dependent processes during backend recovery activities.
important_findings: The UV Sales Order status was manually updated to "Approved" from the backend.
The manual status update bypassed the standard approval process.
The bypassed approval process normally generates the Trade-in Assessment Purchase Order.
The status update was performed during a recovery activity for MFTBCFFR-5894.
No application defect or code fix was required.
root_cause: A backend manual update changed the UV Sales Order status to "Approved", bypassing the standard approval workflow that generates the Trade-in Assessment Purchase Order.
resolution: Completed the recovery and updated the recovery SOP to verify all related triggers and dependent processes before and after backend recovery activities.

investigation_summary: A formatting discrepancy introduced during non-repository changes for CR MFTBCFFR-4378 caused failures in Re-Edit JV creation in the Hakodate and Shikoku production environments. The backend configuration was corrected on 24 June 2026, and Re-Edit JV creation was verified as working correctly. Re-Edit JVs were manually created for all affected records.
important_findings: An extra leading space was introduced into configuration logic during non-repository changes for CR MFTBCFFR-4378.
The configuration issue affected the Hakodate and Shikoku production environments.
The component responsible for creating Re-Edit JVs encountered an error, preventing Re-Edit JV creation for affected records.
The non-repository configuration was corrected from the backend on 24 June 2026.
All affected records were recovered through manual creation of Re-Edit JVs.
An additional validation step was added to post-production release verification for non-repository changes.
root_cause: An extra leading space in configuration logic introduced during non-repository changes for CR MFTBCFFR-4378 caused the Re-Edit JV creation component to error in the Hakodate and Shikoku production environments.
resolution: Corrected the backend non-repository configuration, verified Re-Edit JV creation in both production environments, manually created Re-Edit JVs for all affected records, and added post-production validation for non-repository changes.

important_findings: The issue was not caused by Siebel.

HQLBC data was required for LBC "10188771418" in the Chugoku region.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT because its connected database referenced Production environment data.
root_cause: Required HQLBC information was not registered for LBC "10188771418", causing errors when creating a new account.
resolution: Register the HQLBC data corresponding to LBC "10188771418" in the Chugoku region.

investigation_summary: In Okayama Production, users assigned to 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Mgr' and 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff' could not edit the affected applet, while editing was possible in UAT1 and other production environments. Investigation found that these roles had been configured as Read-Only since production go-live. The Read-only configuration was removed, and the user confirmed that input was possible.
important_findings: The issue affected the specified applet in Okayama Production only.
'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Mgr' and 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff' were configured with Read-Only access.
The Read-Only behavior had existed since production go-live; no recent functional changes were identified.
Other production environments allowed these roles to make changes as expected.
After removing the Read-only configuration, the vehicle manager confirmed that input was possible.
root_cause: The affected applet was configured as Read-Only for 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Mgr' and 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff' in Okayama Production.
resolution: Removed the Read-only configuration for the affected applet for 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Mgr' and 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff' in Okayama Production.

investigation_summary: In PROD, a quotation retained the price for model code FDA60B21S00G-5 after the user changed the model code to FDA60B21S00L-7. Investigation found both model-code master records and current database/system data to be correct, with no data correction or system modification performed during the investigation. Clearing the cache immediately restored the correct FDA60B21S00L-7 price, and the issue could not be reproduced afterward in the verification environment.
important_findings: The quotation initially used FDA60B21S00G-5; after it was changed to FDA60B21S00L-7, the quotation continued to display the previous model code's price.

investigation_summary: In FDP, a Quote's Required Quantity could be changed from 3 to 1 after a Sales Order and three child Sales Orders had been created. Although the child Sales Orders were cancelled, the backend retained their linkage to the parent Sales Order, causing Sales Posting to fail. The recommended remediation was to align FDP with SC Production by making Required Quantity read-only after Sales Order creation; PROD deployment was requested, but completion is not documented.
important_findings: A Required Quantity of 3 created three child Sales Orders during Sales Order approval.
After a Quote revision changed Required Quantity from 3 to 1, added options were synchronized to all existing child Sales Orders.
Cancelling all child Sales Orders did not remove their backend association with the parent Sales Order, so Sales Posting failed.
FDP allowed Required Quantity changes after Sales Order creation, enabling the failing scenario.
The proposed FDP behavior is to make Required Quantity read-only after Sales Order creation, matching SC Production.
For post-order quantity increases, the proposed process requires cancelling the current Sales Order and creating a new Quote and Sales Order.
root_cause: FDP allowed Required Quantity to be reduced after Sales Order creation, but the backend logic did not automatically unlink existing child Sales Orders from the parent Sales Order when Required Quantity became 1.

root_cause: Incorrect ownership and access permissions on BI Publisher-related directories prevented log output and caused BI Publisher service startup failures.
resolution: Corrected ownership and access permissions on the affected directories, then performed a planned BI Publisher restart to apply the permission changes, clear application cache, and eliminate residual abnormal processes.

root_cause: An invalid Planned Delivery Date of 2007/03/30 in the NV Sales Quote caused the Tax Rate for NV Sales Order SO# A000497806 to remain blank, resulting in NV Sales Order Sheet BIP Report generation failure.
resolution: A corrected Planned Delivery Date validation fix for NV Sales Quote was tested in FDP UAT-1 and released to all FDP-PRODs on July 10 to prevent invalid date input and resulting blank Tax Rate values.

investigation_summary: Recycle Invoice DT27 processing created incorrect Journal Voucher values, initially affecting Segment2 Code fields and later Posting Date and client-code fields. The investigation identified chassis-number derivation/mapping issues, DT27 file formatting sensitivity, and UAT8 mapping differences from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs. The corrected UAT logic was verified with test data, and the fix was scheduled for the 2026-07-23 FDP release.
important_findings: The calculation and reconciliation process formed the chassis number using "Stamp Code-C#", rather than the chassis-number position highlighted in the DT27 file.
Incorrect Segment2 Code(CSJS210) and Segment2 Code(CSJS310) values were initially associated with data received from TOB, including "********************" values in the DT27 Recycle Invoice file.
An extra space in the DT27 file caused amount value 80 to be treated as 8 during JV creation.
Client Code(CSJS208) and Client Code(CSJS308) mappings in UAT-8 differed from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, resulting in incorrect Recycle Invoice JV data.
UAT8 master data also caused client-code issues and was updated to match Chugoku prod.
After mapping updates, test data verified that JVs were created correctly with the correct Posting Date(CSJS005) and client-code values.
root_cause: UAT-8 mappings for Client Code(CSJS208) and Client Code(CSJS308) differed from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, causing incorrect Recycle Invoice Journal Voucher data. DT27 input formatting, including an extra space that converted 80 to 8, also caused an incorrect JV amount during testing.
resolution: Updated UAT-8 mappings and master data based on Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, corrected DT27 test-file formatting, and verified correct Journal Voucher creation with new test data. The approved fix was scheduled for the 2026-07-23 FDP release.

investigation_summary: Price Master creation failed for newly received materials in Wakayama and Okinawa - PROD because the Price Master job could start before batch product release completed. Materials arrived through the D2S_MATERIAL_MASTER file, and high material volumes extended the product-release processing time. Realtime job schedules were shifted by 30 minutes on all FDP environments, and successful price uploads were verified in all FDP-PROD environments.
important_findings: Materials were received through the D2S_MATERIAL_MASTER file.
A batch job scheduled at 02:50 AM releases products after Material Master updates.
High volumes of received materials can delay completion of the product-release process.
The Price Master creation job was scheduled at 04:30 AM and could overlap with incomplete product release.
The error "Issue While Updating/Inserting Price Master with Product Name: MK718834" occurred when the material had no existing Price Master record.
Realtime jobs were delayed by 30 minutes, and price uploads subsequently succeeded on all FDP-PROD environments.
root_cause: The Price Master creation job started before the batch product-release process completed for high-volume Material Master updates, causing Price Master insert/update errors for materials without existing price records.
resolution: Increased scheduled timings of the Realtime jobs by 30 minutes on all FDP environments, shifting Price Master creation and related batch jobs to prevent overlap; verified successful price uploads on all FDP-PROD environments.

investigation_summary: “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS” and “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS GI” JVs were missing for Body orders because POs for newly added Body line items were created only after Sales Posting had completed. Recovery was completed for the orders listed in the Jira, and additional records with POs created after Sales Posting were identified for review. The current system cannot create the requested Body GI JV after Sales Posting; a permanent enhancement requires new Body Building Order logic and must be handled through PJ-CR.
important_findings: An NV Quotation revision added Body line items and synchronized them to the Sales Order, but POs were not created for all Body-tab line items before Sales Posting.
Sales Posting created JVs only for the Sales Order and POs mapped at the time of Sales Posting; remaining POs were created afterward.
“Sales Posting Body GI” and “Sales Posting Body” JVs are created only during Sales Order Sales Posting and are not generated retrospectively for POs created afterward.
The existing “Revised Sales Posting” Journal Event Type creates delta-value JVs for post-Sales-Posting PO creation, but does not provide the requested Body GI JV behavior.
Supporting post-Sales-Posting creation of Body GI JVs requires changes to multiple objects and testing of Body Building Order processes and related interfaces.
Recovery was completed for the Jira-listed orders, and records with POs created after Sales Posting were shared for review.
root_cause: POs for Body line items added through an NV Quotation revision were not created before Sales Posting. When the remaining POs were created after Sales Posting, the system did not create “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS GI” JVs because those JVs are generated only at Sales Order Sales Posting.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected orders listed in the Jira using recovery JV data linked to KB in the nightly daily batch. A permanent post-Sales-Posting Body GI JV enhancement remains pending and requires PJ-CR.
