root_cause: No Wakayama user was assigned to the SCHQ-Sales-UV-Mgr approver position in the "UV Purchase Order Cancel UV Mgr Approval Request" workflow, causing a blank Approvers field and triggering CR-4196 validation that deleted the Approval History record.
resolution: Updated the logic so that an Approval flag of True in New Vehicle Sales Cancellation does not impact Used Vehicle; the fix was deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.
technical_entities: UV Purchase Order Cancel UV Mgr Approval Request

investigation_summary: Journal Voucher Department Code mapping used different branch sources when the Job Card (JC) creator and Job Card Order (JCO) creator differed. The initial UAT fix changed Credit Department Code (CSJS300) to the JC Creation Branch for three Job Card Sales journal voucher types. Subsequent validation found that Job Card - Labor cost JVs still used the JCO Creation Branch, and confirmation was requested on extending the JC Creation Branch mapping to all Job Card Journal Voucher types.
important_findings: For Job Card Sales Amount Taxable, Job Card Sales Amount CT, and Job Card Sales Amount Non-Taxable, Responsible Service Shop Code was mapped to Debit Department Code (CSJS200) and Branch Code was mapped to Credit Department Code (CSJS300).
The original issue occurred because Debit and Credit Department Codes could use different sources: JC workshop/shop code for debit and JCO creator Branch Code for credit.
UAT changed CSJS300 in JV to use the JC creator's Branch Code; test record I001305002 had JCO Creator 40 and JC Creator 20.
For JC I001305241, Job Card Sales correctly set CSJS200 and CSJS300 to JC Creation Branch 10, while Job Card - Labor set both codes to JCO Creation Branch 40.
The remaining incorrect mapping was suspected to be in the cost JV creation section.
A decision was still pending on whether CSJS200 and CSJS300 should use JC Creation Branch Code for all Job Card Journal Voucher types.
root_cause: Department Code mapping was only corrected for the three Job Card Sales journal voucher types, while Job Card - Labor cost JV creation continued to use the JCO Creation Branch instead of the JC Creation Branch.

investigation_summary: The issue was addressed by adding the SDS Category on Form Applet. The change was approved for production and released through the FDP-PROD release on 26th May.
important_findings: SDS Category was missing from Form Applet.
The fix consisted of adding the SDS Category on Form Applet.
The change was approved for PROD.
The fix was deployed through the FDP-PROD release of 26th May.
root_cause: SDS Category was not configured on Form Applet.
resolution: Added the SDS Category on Form Applet and released the fix to PROD through the FDP-PROD release of 26th May.

investigation_summary: The incident was investigated with the Falcon team and was resolved across all FDP-PROD environments. The timeout value was increased from 180 seconds to 300 seconds, matching the SC PROD environment, and the release was approved for closure.
important_findings: The issue was investigated in coordination with the Falcon team.
The timeout period was changed from 180 seconds to 300 seconds.
The 300-second timeout was aligned with the SC PROD environment.
The fix was deployed to all FDP-PROD environments.
The customer approved the timeout change and release closure.
root_cause: The timeout value of 180 seconds was insufficient; it was increased to 300 seconds.
resolution: Increased the timeout value from 180 seconds to 300 seconds on all FDP-PROD environments, matching SC PROD.

investigation_summary: An order remained in Pending Approval and was manually recovered by updating its status to Approved. Engineering reviewed the complete flow, logs, and database entries and assessed the incident as a rare multi-user case. Reproduction attempts in UAT using multiple user sessions and Approved, Rejected, and Completed actions did not reproduce the issue; no product fix was required.
important_findings: The affected order was recovered and its status was updated to Approved.
Logs, database entries, and the complete processing flow were reviewed.
The incident was assessed as a potential multi-user case.
UAT testing with multiple user sessions and Approved, Rejected, and Completed actions always updated the final status according to the latest action.
The issue could not be reproduced and no similar recurring cases were identified.
No fix was required; the incident was requested for closure.
resolution: The affected order was manually recovered by updating its status to Approved; no product fix was required.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned Chassis GI JV records not being created despite GR JV creation for selected orders. Initial analysis attributed missing GI JVs for several chassis orders to absent Model Code pricing in the Price Master/Price List, but the issue was subsequently addressed in UAT by updating the GI JV filter condition. After the change, Chassis GI JV creation was confirmed for test records A001304859 and B001258096.
important_findings: GI JV was not created for orders B000121443, B000062227, B000062228, B000062229, and B000001569, while other reviewed records were reported as correct.
For B000062227, B000062228, B000062229, and B000001569, the Model Code had no price in the Price Master/Price List when the Chassis Orders were created.
Without Model Code pricing, GR JV included only priced items such as Options and Colors; the Model Code amount was excluded.
A GI JV filter condition was updated in UAT, after which Chassis GI JV was created correctly for test records A001304859 and B001258096.
The reported concern was that GI was not created despite GR being present.
root_cause: The GI JV filter condition required correction; updating this condition in UAT enabled Chassis GI JV creation.
resolution: Updated the filter condition in GI JV in UAT and verified correct Chassis GI JV creation using test records A001304859 and B001258096.

investigation_summary: The incident involved an MF Repair Fee amount that was lower than expected and a quote that could not be approved through the normal process. Investigation found no confirmed issue with Siebel functionality; required recoveries were completed and the quote was updated to Customer Approved through the recovery process.
important_findings: The SV cost of 22,870 JPY was successfully added to the Repair Fee amount in UV Inventory.
JC I050756954 did not meet the selection criteria used to update the Repair Fee amount; its related cost was not added to UV Inventory or included in the MF Repair Fee calculation.
A cost related to JC I050662915 was included in the Repair Fee calculation, resulting in an MF Repair Fee amount lower than expected.
The quote could not be approved through the normal process and was updated to Customer Approved through the recovery process.
No issues were confirmed in Siebel functionality.
resolution: Completed the required recoveries and updated the quote status to Customer Approved through the recovery process; the incident was closed because no Siebel functionality issue was confirmed.

investigation_summary: An affected UV Body Building Order was created by a user whose Position Type was "Branch-Head". "Branch-Head" is not available in the new Position Master and has no approval flow configured on the Aomori Production environment, preventing approval generation. The user was advised to cancel the order and create a new one using the correct Position Type.
important_findings: The affected business object was a UV Body Building Order.
The order creator had Position Type "Branch-Head".
"Branch-Head" is not available in the new Position Master.
No approval flow exists for the "Branch-Head" position type in the Aomori Production environment.
The unavailable position type and missing approval flow prevented generation of approvals.
root_cause: The UV Body Building Order was created using the "Branch-Head" Position Type, which is absent from the new Position Master and has no configured approval flow on Aomori Production.
resolution: Cancel the affected Body Building Order and create a new order using the correct Position Type.

investigation_summary: Following an FDP release, scheduled ODI package executions failed because the ODI Agent was not functioning properly. This prevented Price Master related jobs from creating price records in all FDPs. The ODI Agent service was restored and failed ODI packages were re-executed, after which pending price data was created and validated successfully.
important_findings: The issue occurred in the ODI job execution process after the FDP release activity.
The ODI Agent was not functioning properly during the scheduled processing window.
Price Master related jobs failed, causing corresponding price records not to be created in all FDPs.
Restoring the ODI Agent service and re-executing failed ODI packages created and validated the pending price data.
Post-release monitoring and execution checks were implemented to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: The ODI Agent was not functioning properly after the FDP release, causing scheduled ODI package executions to fail.
resolution: The ODI Agent service was restored and the failed ODI packages were re-executed successfully; pending price data was then created and validated.

investigation_summary: A Parts Return Order processed after JC closure caused Quote and JCO amounts to differ, creating a risk of incorrect invoice amounts. Standard behavior requires creating a new Quote and completing Customer Approved after a return order; otherwise JC closing should show "Please synchronize the quote first." The originally reported bypass of this validation could not be consistently reproduced in UAT, logs, or database checks. Preventive validations and post-closure return-order restrictions were implemented in UAT-1 and scheduled for release to FDP-PROD.
important_findings: A completed Parts Return Order does not automatically synchronize updated return amounts to an existing JCO.
After a return order, a new Quote must be created and Customer Approved to synchronize the latest amounts between Quote and JCO.
If the required Quote recreation and approval are not performed, JC closing is expected to display "Please synchronize the quote first."
The reported case proceeded without the expected synchronization validation, but the behavior could not be consistently reproduced through UAT scenarios, log review, or database verification.
The implemented validation compares Quote and JCO Parts/Oil and Labor totals and blocks processing when values differ.
The Create Parts Return Order button was disabled for closed JCs to prevent return orders after JC closure.
resolution: Implemented in UAT-1: error pop-ups for mismatches between Quote and JCO Parts/Oil List Price Total, Discount Total, Sales Price Total, and Labor List Price Total, Discount Total, Sales Price Total; disabled Create Parts Return Order when the JC is Closed. Deployment to FDP-PROD was requested and scheduled for the 2026-07-23 release.
technical_entities: Quote and JCO Order Parts/Oil totals is not same. Kindly sync quote to continue.
Quote and JCO Order Labor totals are not the same. Kindly sync quote to continue.

investigation_summary: The "Order Date" field on Chassis Orders displayed the Sales Order creation date when a Chassis Order was synchronized or mapped to a Sales Order. The behavior was confirmed as existing system logic, including in the SC environment. Based on the confirmed requirement, the logic was changed so that "Order Date" displays the Chassis Order creation date, and the fix was deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.
important_findings: Existing logic populated the Chassis Order "Order Date" field with the Sales Order creation date during Chassis Order and Sales Order synchronization.
The same behavior was confirmed in the SC environment.
The required value for "Order Date" was confirmed as the Chassis Order creation date.
The field is editable in the UI.
The change was validated in UAT-1 using Chassis Order B001248284 and in UAT-6 using Chassis Order B000007110.
The Production fix was deployed as part of the 11 June FDP release.
root_cause: Existing system logic set the Chassis Order "Order Date" field to the Sales Order creation date when the Chassis Order was synchronized or mapped to a Sales Order, rather than using the Chassis Order creation date.
resolution: Modified the "Order Date" logic to display the Chassis Order creation date; validated in UAT and deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.

investigation_summary: A delivery approval error occurred in UV Sales Order because an Activity was marked Closed while its mapped Job Card had been canceled. During delivery approval, the system validates that an active Job Card is linked to the Activity; no valid active Job Card was found. Recovery was completed by updating the Activity status to Work Completed, and no product fix was required.
important_findings: An Activity in UV Sales Order is considered completed when its status is Work Completed or Closed.
Closing the Job Card normally sets the related Activity status to Work Completed.
The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 by canceling a Job Card and then manually changing the related Activity from Open to Closed.
Delivery approval validates that the Activity has a valid active linked Job Card.
A canceled mapped Job Card caused the validation failure because the Activity was Closed without an active Job Card.
When a Job Card is canceled, the linked Activity must be manually set to Cancel Request.
root_cause: The linked Job Card was canceled, but the related UV Sales Order Activity was manually set to Closed instead of Cancel Request, causing delivery approval validation to fail because no valid active Job Card was linked.
resolution: Recovery was completed by setting the Activity status to Work Completed. No fix was required; for canceled Job Cards, users must manually set the linked Activity status to Cancel Request.

investigation_summary: A fix for AMS CR MFTBCFFR-5210, intended to default the vehicle "Service Person" field to blank instead of "Siebel Administrator", unintentionally affected standard ODI functionality. As a result, the Asset number was not captured in the Serial Number field. The MFTBCFFR-5210 changes were reverted in production and affected records were recovered.
important_findings: The MFTBCFFR-5210 change correctly set the vehicle "Service Person" field to blank by default; previously it was set to "Siebel Administrator".
The MFTBCFFR-5210 implementation unintentionally impacted standard ODI functionality.
The impact was that the Asset number was not updated/captured in the Serial Number field.
In Sales Order, header VIN# is obtained from "Vehicle No C#" on the Vehicle Screen, while Form Applet VIN# is obtained from "Key" on the Vehicle Screen.
Records requiring recovery were identified and recovered.
Incidents 5642, 5674, and 5737 were caused by similar issues and were fixed in the production environment.
root_cause: The fix implemented for AMS CR MFTBCFFR-5210 unintentionally affected standard ODI functionality, preventing the Asset number from being captured in the Serial Number field.
resolution: Reverted the changes made for MFTBCFFR-5210 in the production environment and performed recovery for affected records; an alternative fix approach for MFTBCFFR-5210 was to be considered.

investigation_summary: The JV for spreadsheet 11SC000000000O-09-26-00008-01 had previously been created and was later manually removed through SR 5709. When the spreadsheet was approved again, the duplicate-JV prevention logic correctly prevented creation of another JV. The issue was classified as not being an incident, and a recovery JV was planned.
important_findings: A JV was initially created when the spreadsheet was first approved.
The JV was manually removed through SR 5709.
Re-approving the spreadsheet did not create a new JV because of logic that prevents duplicate JV creation.
A recovery JV was planned for spreadsheet 11SC000000000O-09-26-00008-01.
root_cause: The original JV was manually removed through SR 5709, and duplicate-JV prevention logic prevented a new JV from being created when the spreadsheet was approved again.

investigation_summary: The incident was recovered during initial support handling. It was confirmed to be a bug already addressed under incident number 5472 and deployed to prod in the 2026-05-13 release.
important_findings: Recovery was performed during the incident response.
The issue was identified as a bug.
The fix was tracked under incident number 5472.
The fix was deployed to prod in the 2026-05-13 release.
resolution: The bug fix was deployed to prod in the 2026-05-13 release.

investigation_summary: The Weight Tax JV for the order was missing after a recovery activity related to MFTBCFFR-5709. Recovery removed all JVs associated with spreadsheet Number 11SC000000000O-09-26-00008-01, including the Weight Tax JV. The JV was recreated and the issue was recovered.
important_findings: The JV for the order was originally created on 30th April.
A recovery performed for MFTBCFFR-5709 requested removal of all JVs associated with spreadsheet Number 11SC000000000O-09-26-00008-01.
The Weight Tax JV was deleted together with the other associated JVs during the recovery.
The missing JV was recreated as part of issue recovery.
The issue was identified as a recovery error rather than a logical system defect.
root_cause: A recovery activity for MFTBCFFR-5709 deleted all JVs associated with spreadsheet Number 11SC000000000O-09-26-00008-01, including the Weight Tax JV.
resolution: Recreated the deleted JV. No product fix was required because the incident resulted from a recovery error.

investigation_summary: Change Order# K000442780 was missing from the end-of-April bulk invoice data. The final investigation determined that a KB batch error in shikoku required manual file regeneration, during which records were missed because a flag was updated after bulk data generation. The affected bulk data was regenerated and linked to KB; a separate retriggering and recovery logic clone had already been implemented under MFTBCFFR-5711.
important_findings: Change Order# K000442780 involved a Payer Change from 0000807603 to 0000201611 and a closing change from 15th of the month closing to end of month closing.
End-of-month bulk invoice processing uses the billing account closing date of the Job Card; billing account 0000807603 had a 15th closing date.
A KB batch error in shikoku required manual file regeneration.
Some records were missed during manual data generation because a flag was updated after bulk data generation.
A separate logic clone for retriggering and recovery was created as a countermeasure under MFTBCFFR-5711.
root_cause: Following a KB batch error in shikoku, manual file regeneration missed records because a flag was updated after bulk data generation.
resolution: Regenerated the bulk data for the affected records and linked it to KB. A separate retriggering and recovery logic clone had already been implemented under MFTBCFFR-5711.

investigation_summary: The Material Master Batch process uses a three-step Siebel data-insertion flow: Runs package, Insertion, and Release. Investigation found that some records were not processed during the Insertion step. The affected parts were recovered in all environments, with daily monitoring required until a Kaizen improvement is developed and tracked through ServiceNow ticket RITM1971770.
important_findings: The Siebel data-insertion process consists of Runs package, Insertion, and Release steps.
Some records did not get processed during the Insertion step.
Recovery of the affected parts was completed in all environments.
Daily monitoring of the Material Master Batch process is required until the Kaizen improvement is released.
The Kaizen related to EIM tables data was approved by IT and is being tracked in ServiceNow ticket RITM1971770.
root_cause: Some records were not processed during the Insertion step of the Siebel data-insertion process.
resolution: Recovered the affected parts in all environments; continue daily monitoring and track the Kaizen improvement through ServiceNow ticket RITM1971770.

investigation_summary: In UAT1, spreadsheet 1-502819545 appeared not to send an approval request after recovery in SR# 5709, although a pending request remained in the approver's Inbox. Recovery changed the spreadsheet from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed its approval history without removing the associated Inbox request entity. When the approver approved the remaining request, the spreadsheet changed to Spreadsheet Approved; JVs were created for the affected Job Cards. The system was determined to be behaving as expected, and the recovery procedure will be updated to deactivate pending approval requests during recovery.
important_findings: Recovery in SR# 5709 changed the spreadsheet status from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed approval history.
The request entity remained in the designated approver's Inbox after approval history was removed.
A subsequent approval submission did not create approval history, creating the appearance that no approval request had been sent.
Approving the remaining Inbox request changed spreadsheet 1-502819545 in UAT1 to Spreadsheet Approved.
JVs were created for 37 Job Cards associated with the Insurance Spreadsheet, totaling 148 Journal Voucher Items.
Future recovery procedures must deactivate pending approval requests to prevent hidden approvals.
root_cause: The recovery performed in SR# 5709 removed the spreadsheet approval history but did not remove the pending approval request entity from the approver's Inbox, disrupting the normal approval-history flow.
resolution: Created JVs for the 37 affected Job Cards (148 Journal Voucher Items) and updated the recovery procedure requirement to deactivate pending approval requests to designated approvers during spreadsheet recovery.

investigation_summary: A mismatch in ctrl.txt file counts occurred during last night's batch processing after recovery from MFTBCFFR-5656, when an incorrect bulk invoice file had been generated. The bulk invoice file and Ctrl file were resent, and recovery was completed according to MDIS's recovery plan with the data relinked. No product logic fix was required because the incident was attributed to execution of the KB batch during recovery.
important_findings: The ctrl.txt count mismatch followed recovery performed after an incorrect bulk invoice file was generated under MFTBCFFR-5656.
SMDO0064 had existing issues that set quantity values between 0 and 1 as ".3, .7"; a fix passed UAT but the batch errored in production because of the large data volume.
The bulk invoice file and Ctrl file were resent, and recovery was completed according to MDIS's recovery plan.
The incident was attributed to KB batch execution during recovery rather than a logical bug.
A dummy recovery and testing logic was created, and KB recovery will not be performed without prior approval from MDIS and Miyauchi-San.
root_cause: Execution of the KB batch during recovery caused the ctrl.txt file count mismatch.
resolution: Completed recovery according to MDIS's recovery plan, relinked the data, and resent the bulk invoice file with the Ctrl file. A dummy recovery/testing logic was created to prevent similar issues, with KB recovery requiring prior approval from MDIS and Miyauchi-San.

investigation_summary: The 'Create Activity' button was inactive in UV Sales Order after an Activity had been created. Code-level analysis found that the existing logic created one Activity for all Service Effort line items and then disabled the button. The functionality was changed to allow creation of a second Activity when the previous JCO is in Closed or Cancelled status, tested in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to production.
important_findings: For Order# E000452245 on Shikoku Prod, two Service Effort line items existed when the Activity was created.
The original logic created only one Activity for all Service Effort line items in a Sales Order and then set the 'Create Activity' button to inactive.
The updated functionality allows a second Activity to be created in UV Sales Order if the previous JCO status is Closed or Cancelled.
The change was tested successfully in FDP UAT-1 using UV SO# E001304686.
The fix was applied to the production environment through the regular release on the 23rd.
root_cause: The existing 'Create Activity' button logic disabled the button after creating one Activity for all Service Effort line items, without allowing another Activity based on the status of the previous JCO.
resolution: Updated the UV Sales Order logic to enable creation of a second Activity when the previous JCO is Closed or Cancelled; tested in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to production.

investigation_summary: Investigation of reported Siebel downtime confirmed that FDP-JPN (Shikoku-PROD) shut down through its scheduled daily maintenance process at 9:00 PM JST. Server logs showed a service stop command at 2026-04-28 21:00:37, with no abnormal behavior or delay identified. The ENU environment was manually maintained after 9:00 PM JST with prior IT approval; the incident was approved for rejection.
important_findings: FDP-JPN (Shikoku-PROD) performs an automatic daily scheduled shutdown at 9:00 PM JST.
Server logs recorded "Shutting down due to service stop command" at 2026-04-28 21:00:37.
No abnormal shutdown behavior or timing delay was identified in the Japanese environment.
ENU maintenance was performed manually after 9:00 PM JST with prior IT-team approval.
root_cause: The reported downtime was expected scheduled maintenance activity, not an abnormal Siebel issue.
resolution: Incident rejected after confirming the shutdown occurred within the defined maintenance schedule.

investigation_summary: The affected record was recovered, and re-executing the same D21F file under identical conditions successfully created the Recycle Order. The investigation could not determine a definitive cause because historical import data for the incident was no longer available. A Kaizen improvement was deployed to FDP Production to retain import history and notify the support team of import failures.
important_findings: All required processing conditions were reported as satisfied when the issue occurred.
Re-executing the same D21F file under identical conditions completed successfully and created the Recycle Order without errors.
The affected D21F file was received at approximately the same time as a previous related incident.
Before the Kaizen change, re-executing the same ODI package overwrote or deleted past import history in the database, preventing retrospective investigation.
The implemented Kaizen archives data import history, including order number/asset number, import status, source file name, and package name.
The archive capability supports future investigation and analysis but did not establish the root cause of this incident.
resolution: Recovered all affected records. Deployed the RITM1971770 Kaizen improvement to FDP Production to archive TOB and D2S import history and automatically notify the support team when data imports fail.

investigation_summary: No technical investigation details, findings, root cause, or corrective actions were documented in the comment timeline. The incident was rejected following approval received by email.
important_findings: The incident was acknowledged for investigation.
The incident was rejected based on approval received by email.

investigation_summary: The reported login/access issue was investigated for the affected time span. No discrepancy, server health issue, memory spike, or application login problem was found in SIEBEL. The incident was attributed to possible FDP-level network slowness or interrupted internet connectivity and was closed.
important_findings: No system discrepancy was identified during the reported time span.
Server health and memory usage were optimal, with no spikes observed.
The support team could log in to the application without issue.
SIEBEL was confirmed not to be the cause of the incident.
The likely cause was FDP-level network slowness or interrupted internet connectivity.
root_cause: FDP-level network slowness or interrupted internet connectivity; no SIEBEL system issue was identified.
resolution: No system corrective action was required; the incident was closed after confirming SIEBEL was not the cause.

investigation_summary: The incident involved duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders, causing a shipment to be created while the chassis-order status was not updated. The established analysis attributes the duplication to a Model Code change that caused a mismatch between an existing Vehicle and its Chassis Order when a D21A file was received from TOB. A fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871, but the FDP deployment and shipment-status validation remained pending.
important_findings: Duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders were created for C# 20287.
A Model Code change on an existing Vehicle resulted in different Model Codes between the Vehicle and the existing Chassis Order.
When D21A was received from TOB, the mismatch caused creation of a new Vehicle and a new Chassis Order with the old Model Code.
After D21N was received, the combination associated with PO Number B000362896 was shipped, while the combination associated with PO Number B000350487 remained in C# contact.
The SC fix matches the incoming TOB Model Code against the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record, and simultaneously updates the Vehicle Model Code.
The final feedback states that shipping had not been updated and required reconfirmation.
root_cause: A Model Code change on an existing Vehicle created a Model Code mismatch with the existing Chassis Order; subsequent D21A processing created duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders.

investigation_summary: Bulk updates in SR#5491 updated fields displayed on the Accounts Receivable UI, but the Update AR logic reads values from separate, non-UI columns that were not updated. This caused previously stored values to appear after Update AR; the behavior was determined to follow existing business logic rather than represent a defect. All identified inconsistent records were recovered in Chugoku Prod across NV, UV, PT, and SV.
important_findings: SR#5491 updated UI-visible responsible employee/shop code fields but did not update the separate columns used by Update AR logic.
The data used by Update AR logic is not displayed on the UI, creating the potential for inconsistent values when only visible fields are bulk updated.
The issue was classified as expected behavior under the current business logic; no program change was implemented.
Data recovery was completed for all inconsistent records in NV, UV, PT, and SV on Chugoku Prod.
Future bulk updates must update both UI-display fields and the fields used by the logic to maintain data consistency.
root_cause: Bulk updates modified only UI-visible fields, while Update AR retrieves values from different non-UI columns that were not included in the updates.
resolution: Recovered all inconsistent records in NV, UV, PT, and SV on Chugoku Prod; future updates must update both the UI-mapped fields and the columns used by Update AR logic.
technical_entities: CMVM_FDP Customer Accounts Receivable Collection Person Bulk Change (China)

investigation_summary: A TOB chassis invoice record in DT01 for C#: FP84HG-500043 did not create a Journal Voucher (JV). The record resulted in a NULL line type/product type because the relevant product-type field was NULL and Siebel did not have logic to create a JV for that condition. Subsequent analysis also found that the invoice line had no matching Chassis Order Line Item, causing the default Project Code AA00000000 rather than a chassis order number. Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions.
important_findings: The affected record was FP84HG-500043 in the DT01 Chassis Invoice file for the Okayama FDP environment.
The billing-data type is identified from the 25th character; the affected record was identified as Post-OP.
For the Post-OP record, the 2-character product-type value after the 66th character was NULL, causing the line type/product type to be NULL.
Siebel did not contain logic to create a JV when the line type was NULL, so no JV was created.

The corresponding invoice data did not exist in the Chassis Order Line Items, although it existed in an associated Sales Order line item; therefore reconciliation could not set the Chassis Order Number as Project Code (CSJS211).
When no matching Chassis Order Line Item is found, AA00000000 is assigned as the default project code; manual recovery was confirmed to process all TOB invoices without omission.
root_cause: The DT01 Post-OP invoice record had a NULL product-type field, which produced a NULL line type; Siebel had no JV-creation logic for records with a NULL line type. The related invoice line also had no matching Chassis Order Line Item for reconciliation.
resolution: Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions. Future TOB invoice processing will be monitored, and a JV will be created manually when a DT01 record does not produce a JV.

investigation_summary: The incident involved an error when requesting acceptance inspection approval in FDP. Investigation identified that the Approval Master Data did not contain all required requester positions/UIDs; the master was updated in UAT-1 and deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.
important_findings: FDP approval requests are permitted only for UIDs maintained as valid requestors in the master data.
Users not listed as valid requestors receive the error message "Please select a valid approver" when generating an approval request.
The existing master was compared with positions provided by Shiromoto San, and missing positions were added.
The updated Approval Master Data included existing requestors and newly added requestors.
The fix was validated in UAT-1 before deployment to Production.
root_cause: Required requester positions/UIDs were missing from the Approval Master Data, causing FDP approval requests from those users to be rejected as invalid.
resolution: Updated the Approval Master Data/Multiple_UID_Master with the missing requester positions and valid UIDs, validated the change in UAT-1, and deployed it to Production in the 11 June FDP release.

investigation_summary: The affected record and other affected records were recovered. This incident was identified as having a similar issue to MFTBCFFR-5642 and MFTBCFFR-5737, with analysis shared under MFTBCFFR-5737. Fixes were applied in the production environment, and recurrence was not expected.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the affected record and other affected records.
MFTBCFFR-5674, MFTBCFFR-5642, and MFTBCFFR-5737 were caused by similar issues.
The RCA and analysis results were shared in MFTBCFFR-5737.
All related incidents were fixed in the production environment.
The Jira status had not been updated as of the final comment.
resolution: Recovered the affected records and applied fixes for all related incidents in the production environment.

investigation_summary: The D2S Invoice Mismatch screen had slow loading caused by inefficient processing in the PDQ. Initial indexing and removal of the sort specification did not fully resolve the production issue. The PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)" was subsequently optimized, significantly improving screen loading time while preserving export functionality.
important_findings: The PDQ scanned the full available dataset because unmatched records from all periods must remain available for review and export.
Initial analysis identified sorting on _D2S SO Number_, _D2S Line Number_, and _Part Number_ as a performance factor because the fields were not indexed.
An index based on the sort order was deployed to UAT and then production, but additional performance improvements were still required.
The configured sort order was D2S Order Number, Sales Order Item, and Part Number; the sort specification was removed, but the issue persisted after production release.
Optimizing PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)" significantly improved loading performance, and export functionality was verified successfully.
root_cause: Inefficient PDQ processing over the full dataset, including sorting operations on unindexed fields, caused slow loading of the D2S Invoice Mismatch screen.
resolution: Optimized PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)"; screen loading performance improved and export functionality was verified.

investigation_summary: Bulk Invoice data generation omitted the leading zero for SMDO064 quantity values between 0 and 1. The issue was traced to number-to-character conversion during bulk data generation. The Bulk Invoice and batch-file logic was updated, validated in UAT/UAT1, and deployed to PROD on 20 May 2026.
important_findings: SMDO064 values between 0 and 1 lost the leading zero during number-to-character conversion in bulk data generation.
The logic for the SMDO064 data type was updated to preserve correct quantity values.
Corrected Bulk Invoice output was validated in UAT and approved for PROD deployment.
The UAT1 KB batch generated 150 KB Bulk Invoice records successfully after the logic change.
The final changes were deployed to PROD after business hours on 20 May 2026.
root_cause: Number-to-character conversion during bulk data generation omitted the leading zero for SMDO064 values between 0 and 1.
resolution: Updated the Bulk Invoice and batch-file logic, including SMDO064 data-type handling; validated the output in UAT/UAT1 and deployed the changes to PROD on 20 May 2026.

investigation_summary: Two affected records were identified in the Production environment. The issue was assessed as a rare occurrence potentially caused by a temporary system-related problem during processing, with no additional impacted records found. The incident was closed without a documented corrective action.
important_findings: Only 2 affected records were identified in the Production environment.
The occurrence was considered rare and limited to a small number of records.
The issue may have resulted from a temporary system-related problem during processing.
No further impacted records were identified before closure.

investigation_summary: The Service Cost Price field on the UV Sales Quote form did not include costs for part line items. Service cost was previously calculated only from Total prices of Labor, Lubricant, and Service Line Effort, affecting the base amount stamped for the Revise Sales Posting Service Cost JV when a quote was revised. The fix was tested in UAT, approved, and released to production in the 13 May FDP release.
important_findings: Service Cost Price on UV Sales Quote previously excluded part line-item costs.
The field contained the sum of Total prices for Labor, Lubricant, and Service Line Effort.
On UV Sales Quote revision, the Service Cost difference from the previous quote is stamped as the base amount of the Revise Sales Posting Service Cost JV.
Parts can be added through a Job Card or directly on the quote using the plus button.
The implemented calculation includes only parts added through the Job Card and excludes parts added directly on the quote.
The fix was released to production in the 13 May FDP release.
root_cause: The Service Cost Price calculation on the UV Sales Quote form did not include costs for part line items.
resolution: Updated the service cost calculation to include parts added through the Job Card; the change was validated in UAT and released to production in the 13 May FDP release.
technical_entities: Revise Sales Posting Service Cost JV

investigation_summary: The incident involved a limited set of impacted records across Shikoku, Okayama, and Hakodate. All affected records were more than one year old, and the lack of historical logs prevented identification of an exact root cause. No recovery was required, no similar records were found, and the incident was closed with ongoing monitoring.
important_findings: Impacted records were Shikoku: F000289835 and F000333481; Okayama: F000251965, F000238478, and F000238479; Hakodate: F000184478.
Only a small number of records were impacted.
All impacted records were more than one year old.
Historical logs were unavailable, preventing determination of the exact root cause.
No further recovery was required for the impacted records.
No similar records were identified; the system will be monitored for recurrence.
resolution: No recovery action was required. The incident was closed after confirming no similar records were present, with continued monitoring for similar cases.

investigation_summary: The initial analysis attributed inconsistent price-master processing to D2S records containing end year "9998" instead of "9999", which caused existing records to receive end dates and prevented creation of new records. A change was deployed to new package processing on FDP-PROD to handle the date condition. However, the reported root cause and recovery were challenged because the mismatch differed by FDP and recovery was stated to be incomplete; further analysis was requested.
important_findings: The system treats an end date with year "9999" as open-ended validity and displays it as blank (NULL) on the UI.
Price-master records received with end year "9998" were processed differently, updating the previous record end date and stopping new-record processing.
The processing issue caused inconsistencies in the Siebel system and failure of the batch processing job.
A fix for the date condition was deployed in new package processing on FDP-PROD.
The D2S-file explanation was not confirmed because mismatches varied by FDP, and recovery was reported as incomplete for specified parts in Okayama and Aomori.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed for affected C/# records 450804, 450826, and 450801. MFTBCFFR-5642 was identified as a similar issue to incidents 5674 and 5737; the detailed analysis was shared in 5737. A fix was applied in the production environment, and recurrence is not expected.
important_findings: Affected recovery targets were C/# 450804, 450826, and 450801.
Recovery for the affected records was completed.
Incidents 5642, 5674, and 5737 were caused by similar issues.
The analysis details were documented under incident 5737.
All related incidents were fixed in the production environment.
resolution: Recovered the affected records and applied a fix in the production environment.

investigation_summary: A long-running database query caused system-wide performance degradation affecting the Service Quote screen. AWR and database-level analysis found that database statistics for some tables were missing or outdated, preventing efficient query optimization. DB statistics were gathered and updated after business hours, and subsequent monitoring confirmed normal Service Quote screen performance with no recurrence.
important_findings: AWR reports and database-level analysis identified a long-running query.
The query degraded overall system performance and affected the Service Quote screen.
Database statistics required for query optimization were missing or outdated for some tables.
DB statistics were gathered and updated after business hours.
Post-change monitoring found no further issues and confirmed normal Service Quote screen operation.
root_cause: Missing or outdated database statistics on some tables caused inefficient query optimization, resulting in a long-running query and system performance degradation.
resolution: Gathered and updated DB statistics after business hours; monitoring confirmed the issue did not recur.

investigation_summary: A delivery approval error occurred in a UV Sales Order when completing the delivery process. Investigation reproduced the issue in FDP UAT-1 and determined that the associated Purchase Order had been unmapped after the Body line item was deleted from Sales Quote Revision 2, but its status was not changed to 'Cancelled'. The affected record was recovered; no product fix was required.
important_findings: A Body line item with Net Price '¥135,000' and Cost '¥85,000' was added in Sales Quote Revision 1, and a Purchase Order was created for it.
The Body line item was deleted in Sales Quote Revision 2.
The Purchase Order was unmapped in the UV Sales Order without updating its status to 'Cancelled'.
Delivery completion then displayed the error message 'Please map all purchase orders'.
The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 for UV Sales Order# E001303730 and Assessment# H000053287.
Recovery for the affected record was completed.
root_cause: The user unmapped the Purchase Order for the deleted Body line item without changing the Purchase Order status to 'Cancelled', causing the delivery process to require all Purchase Orders to be mapped.
resolution: Recovered the affected record. No product fix was required because the incident was caused by user misoperation; the Purchase Order status must be updated to 'Cancelled' before/unmapping it.

investigation_summary: Affected records were recovered in FDP Production and other FDP Prod environments. Investigation was limited because historical import records had been overwritten or deleted when the same TOB ODI package was re-executed. A Kaizen under RITM1971770 was deployed to retain import history in an archive table and notify the support team of import failures.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the affected records, including records identified in the attached target-data spreadsheet.
The same issue was identified in other FDP Prod environments.
Before the Kaizen, re-executing the same ODI package overwrote past import history in the database; import history was also described as deleted after package execution.
The absence of historical import data prevented further root-cause investigation for this incident on the Siebel side.
RITM1971770 added an archive table for import history and automatic email notifications to the support team when data import fails.
The deployed Kaizen supports future investigation and analysis but does not itself establish or implement a specific recurrence-prevention fix for the original event.
resolution: Affected records were recovered. RITM1971770 Kaizen was deployed to the FDP Production environment to archive TOB/D2S-to-Siebel import history and send support notifications for import failures.

important_findings: The same scenario affected incidents MFTBCFFR-5625, MFTBCFFR-5630, MFTBCFFR-5632, MFTBCFFR-5635, and MFTBCFFR-5701.
ODI packages and required processing conditions were confirmed as normal, but database updates were not reflected for the affected processing.
Re-executing the same file under identical conditions completed without errors and created the expected line items.
Before the Kaizen change, import history was deleted or overwritten after ODI package execution, leaving insufficient historical data for root-cause investigation.

The deployed Kaizen archives TOB and D2S import history, including order number/asset number, import status, source file name, and package name, and sends email notifications to the support team when import fails.
No reproducible defect or confirmed root cause was identified; stakeholders did not accept the archival change as a recurrence-prevention solution.

investigation_summary: Sales Quotation BIP displayed an incorrect Branch Manager Name because its mapping logic did not use the branch associated with the quotation. Earlier logic derived Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position, which could return the wrong branch manager when the creator moved between branches. The logic was revised in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, then deployed to Production through the June 2 emergency release.
important_findings: The initial BIP mapping for Branch Sales Manager name was incorrect.
The prior BIP logic displayed the Last Name of the Sales Rep's Parent Position as Manager Name.
The required logic is to display the Branch-Head of the branch from which the quotation originated, rather than the quotation creator's current branch or position hierarchy.
Using the creator/Sales Rep as the reference could display a different branch manager when the creator moved from branch A to branch B.
After the Production deployment, BIP displays blank when no branch manager exists in the target organization hierarchy.
root_cause: Incorrect Sales Quotation BIP mapping logic derived Branch Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position instead of the branch associated with the quotation.
resolution: Changed the BIP logic to display the Branch-Head of the quotation's originating branch, validated the change in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, and deployed it to Production via the June 2 emergency release.

investigation_summary: An error screen occurred when users clicked an approval notification email link after the related approval request had already been approved from the inbox. The approval request was moved to the "Completed Items List", while the email URL continued to reference the original pending request. The behavior was replicated in UAT1 and confirmed as expected system behavior; the incident was closed.
important_findings: The issue occurs when an approval request is approved directly from the inbox before the notification email link is opened.
Approved requests are automatically moved from the inbox pending list to the "Completed Items List".
The notification email URL still references the original pending approval request after approval.
Opening the stale email URL after approval results in the error screen.
The behavior was replicated in UAT1 and determined not to be a bug.
root_cause: The notification email link references a pending approval request that is no longer available after the request has been approved and moved to the "Completed Items List".
resolution: Confirmed the behavior as expected system behavior, rejected the incident, and closed it.

investigation_summary: D/N prices were not reflected across FDPs because D2S price master files contained Cost Price but omitted list price, and the old package therefore did not set D/N price in PT_Price_List. Recovery completed and prices were reflected across all FDPs. The Bulk Price batch was scheduled on Production for all FDPs and its execution times were adjusted so price updates complete before 07:00 JST.
important_findings: D2S price master files contained Cost Price but were missing list price.
The old package did not set D/N price in PT_Price_List when list price was absent.
Recovery completed and D/N prices were reflected across all FDPs for the affected part numbers.
Bulk Price batch was scheduled for all FDPs on Production to process price files received from D2S.
Job timings were changed to 04:30 JST and 05:00 JST so updates complete before 07:00 JST.
Price updates were confirmed as working correctly on all FDPs, including FDP-OKAYAMA.
root_cause: Price master files received from D2S omitted list price; during execution of the old package, this prevented D/N price from being set in PT_Price_List.
resolution: Completed recovery, scheduled the Bulk Price batch for all FDPs on Production, and adjusted job timings to 04:30 JST and 05:00 JST to complete price updates before 07:00 JST.

investigation_summary: Financial information creation failed because user-entered financial information field values were not correctly transferred to Service Request Details. As a result, AP and AR were not created. The affected record could not be recovered from task execution details because those details were not stored at the DB level; the user was asked to create a new SR and provide all entered values for further field-level analysis.
important_findings: The task execution intended to create the SR was not triggered correctly because of incorrect input conditions.
Inappropriate user-entered financial information field values were not transferred to Service Request Details.
AP and AR were not created after the financial information transfer failed.
Task execution details were not stored at the DB level.
An unknown functional error was recorded in DB logs during record writing related to AR/AP information creation.
The issue could not be reproduced because many possible input fields made identification of the invalid value impractical.
root_cause: Inappropriate field values entered by the user for financial information were not correctly transferred to Service Request Details, preventing creation of AP and AR.
resolution: The user was asked to create a new SR for the required account registration and to share values entered for all fields at each step before submission for further analysis. The incident was then closed.

investigation_summary: BIP reports generated through the Siebel "Submit" button included only the selected order line when a user selected a specific line item. This was identified as standard behavior of the vanilla BIP; selecting the Sales Order Header before submission included all line items. The issue was fixed in FDP UAT-1 and the changes were deployed to Production on April 07 after business hours.
important_findings: The Siebel standard (vanilla) BIP invoked through the "Submit" button cannot be modified.
When a specific order line item is selected, the "Submit" BIP report includes only that selected line item.
Selecting the Sales Order Header before using "Submit" causes the BIP report to include all line items.
The custom BIP accessed through the "Generate" button was provided as an alternative to avoid the line-item selection behavior.
The same behavior was observed in the SC UAT-1 environment for Reference Order #: A027129251.
The issue was fixed in FDP UAT-1 for NV Sales Order#: A001297322 and A001256624, then deployed to Production.
root_cause: The standard Siebel vanilla BIP generated through the "Submit" button scopes the report to the selected order line item when a line is selected.
resolution: Changes were validated in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to the Production environment on April 07 after business hours; users were advised to use the custom "Generate" BIP or select the Sales Order Header before using "Submit".

investigation_summary: LUMF part prices were received in D2S files dated 20 and 25 March but were not processed while the daily batch execution was temporarily stopped. The batch was paused because D2S was sending high-volume bulk files and validation could not be completed before execution. Prices were subsequently created in all FDP environments.
important_findings: LUMF part prices were received in files from D2S dated 20 March and 25 March.
Daily batch execution was temporarily stopped during the period when D2S sent bulk files daily.
High file volume prevented proper data validation before batch execution.
Prices were created on all FDP environments.
root_cause: Daily batch execution was temporarily stopped due to high-volume bulk files from D2S, preventing processing of the received LUMF part prices.
resolution: Created the LUMF part prices on all FDP environments.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed for the affected parts, and an additional sheet was shared. The incident was proposed for closure, but the comments do not document the underlying issue or corrective actions.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the affected parts.
An additional sheet was shared.
No technical investigation details, root cause, or specific remediation steps were provided.

investigation_summary: Duplicate chassis orders and pool cost orders were created when the same D21A chassis information was processed before and after its model code became available in master data. D21A_19112025200850 (TOB) created chassis order B000303862 without model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 because the code was absent from master data; after TCH01 created the code, D21A_17122025200816 (TOB) created B000332117 with the model code. The behavior matches the current system design, but a permanent corrective measure was not agreed or completed.
important_findings: D21A processing created a chassis order even when the received model code was not present in system master data.
Model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was created by TCH01 on 17 December 2025 after a business request, rather than through normal daily file processing.
When the same chassis information was re-received through D21A after the model code became available, the system created a new chassis order instead of updating the existing order.
The duplicate chassis orders resulted in duplicate pool cost orders.

The requested automatic upsert of a newly available model code to an existing chassis order is not possible within the current D21A/Siebel design because D21A creates both vehicle data and chassis order data and changes may affect dependent systems and business processes.
Including MC-9 model codes in daily TCH01 processing was proposed as a future prevention option, but it was rejected as not being a solution.
root_cause: The model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was unavailable in system master data during the initial D21A processing, so the system created a chassis order without the model code. After TCH01 created the model code, re-receipt of the same D21A information was processed as a new chassis order rather than an update, causing duplicate chassis and pool cost orders.

investigation_summary: A recycle fee order was not created in the Chugoku Production environment because the received D21F file was not executed. The failure was attributed to a temporary server-related issue during D21F ODI package execution on 03-Mar-2026. The affected record was recovered, and Cubastion email notifications were implemented to detect failed TOB file executions and enable prompt recovery and investigation.
important_findings: The D21F file for the affected recycle order was successfully received on 03-Mar-2026.
A temporary server-side issue in the Chugoku Production environment prevented D21F ODI package execution, so the recycle fee order was not created.
Execution logs were unavailable because the log retention period had passed, preventing further detailed root-cause analysis.
Subsequent FDP executions did not show the same issue.
Cubastion implemented automatic email notifications to the support team when TOB file execution fails.
The affected record recovery was completed.
root_cause: A temporary server-related issue in the Chugoku Production environment caused the D21F ODI package execution to fail or not occur after the D21F file was received, preventing creation of the recycle fee order. Further detailed cause analysis was not possible because execution logs were no longer retained.
resolution: Recovered the affected record and implemented Cubastion email notifications for failed TOB file executions so unprocessed or failed files can be detected and recovered promptly.

investigation_summary: All UV 2-05 FDP reports failed to display data because a hidden SO# filter applied during the 2025 deployment of Profit column logic caused backend queries to process unnecessary data and exceed resource limits. The filter was removed/fixed, and the reports are now correctly visible. Future deployments will include Power BI filter validation and post-deployment report checks in UAT and PROD.
important_findings: A hidden SO# filter was applied to the reports during the 2025 deployment of Profit column logic.
The filtered SO# is not available in any FDP except Okinawa.
The mismatch caused backend queries to process unnecessary data, exceed resource limits, and return an error when displaying data.
The issue affected all UV 2-05 FDP reports.
Power BI filters and report visibility will be revalidated after deployments in UAT and PROD.
root_cause: A hidden SO# filter applied during the 2025 Profit column logic deployment referenced an SO# unavailable in FDPs other than Okinawa, causing backend queries to process unnecessary data and exceed resource limits.
resolution: The report issue was fixed and all UV 2-05 FDP reports are correctly visible. Post-deployment Power BI filter validation and report-display sanity checks in UAT and PROD will be added to release communication.

Templates for the Approval Request result "Rejected" were implemented and Production approval was received. Templates were implemented for Approval Request results with status "Rejected".
Production approval was provided by e-mail.
The FDP Production release was planned for July 23.

investigation_summary: Sales Order A050609736 was not synchronized to the latest Quote Revision and remained at revision 2. Error monitoring showed that the Sales Order synchronization failed because an order line record was modified by another user/session after retrieval. The affected record was recovered; no product fix was required because the process was functioning normally, including in UAT.
important_findings: The failure occurred in step 'Sync Sales Order' using service 'EAI Siebel Adapter' and method 'Synchronize' (SBL-BPR-00162).
'WriteRecord' for business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' and integration component 'MF Order Item' returned SBL-DAT-00523 and SBL-EAI-04451.
Accessories line item Part#: QZ034500 with Total List Price ¥57,100 was being updated from another browser tab or session during Quote-to-Sales-Order synchronization.
The concurrent modification prevented the Sales Order from being synchronized to the latest Quote Revision.
Recovery was completed for the affected Sales Order record; no fix was required.
root_cause: Concurrent modification of the Accessories line item Part#: QZ034500 from another browser tab or session while the user synchronized the quote to the Sales Order caused a record-lock/concurrency error (SBL-DAT-00523), leaving Sales Order A050609736 at revision 2.
resolution: Recovered the affected Sales Order record. No product fix was implemented because the issue was attributed to rare simultaneous user operations and the process was operating normally.
technical_entities: MF RF Order Entry - Line Items

investigation_summary: The incident was determined to be the same issue as incident 5539. The team proposed marking this incident as fixed and providing the RCA and fix plan through the related incident.
important_findings: The issue was assessed as identical to incident 5539.

investigation_summary: The incident involved inconsistent behavior when setting the "Bill to Basic Account Code" field in Siebel. Analysis identified missing explicit sequencing of field-value setting, similar to a prior issue involving "Bill to Basic Account Name". The sequencing fix was implemented at the Business Component level, validated in UAT, and released to production on the 23rd.
important_findings: AR and AP Account Ids depend on the User Account Id being set first.
Incorrect field-value setting order previously caused failures when fetching AR and AP Account Ids for "Bill to Basic Account Name".
The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field did not have equivalent explicit sequence handling and was identified as the cause of inconsistent results.
The fix was implemented at the Business Component level, covering MF Job Card Detail Applet, MF JC List Applet (@JC), and MF Job Card List Applet (@Vehicle Master).
MF JC Change Order Payment Form Applet (@Change Order) already had the required sequencing and required no change.
The change was deployed to all FDP-PRODs and applied to the production environment in the release on the 23rd.
root_cause: The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field lacked explicit sequencing to set the User Account Id before retrieving dependent AR and AP Account Ids, resulting in inconsistent behavior.
resolution: Implemented the required field-value sequencing at the Business Component level, tested it in UAT, and deployed the change to all FDP-PRODs.
technical_entities: MF Job Card List Applet (@Vehicle Master)
MF JC Change Order Payment Form Applet (@Change Order)

The incorrect recovery caused an issue during delivery completion of Sales Order#: A050343405.
A total of 296 records were affected and their recovery was reviewed.

root_cause: A manual recovery mistake caused the line item for Pool Cost Order#: B050613266 to be recovered incorrectly.
resolution: Completed recovery, reviewed all 296 affected records, and updated and checked the AMS Recovery Manual.

investigation_summary: Good Will account item code processing was corrected through Account Code Master changes and validation in UAT-1. A subsequent issue left the JV account item code (CSJS201) blank for “Free cost of outsourcing: parts (53: Good will)” because of an Account Code Master overlap for the GWNC case. After the UAT fix, an Account Code Master overlap in the GWNC case caused the JV account item code (CSJS201) to be blank.
