resolution: The GWNC Account Code Master overlap was handled, the fix was validated in UAT-1, and it was applied to the production environment in the regular release on the 23rd.
technical_entities: Free cost of outsourcing: parts (53: Good will)

investigation_summary: Consumption Tax on the BIP invoice is sourced from the NV Quote field "Registration Commission Fee Tax," which is calculated as 10% of "Registration Total Commission Fee." Testing in UAT-1 and code/UI regression testing reported that the calculated value displays and updates correctly unless the editable field is manually changed, and changed values propagate to subsequent Quotes and Sales Orders. However, the discussion did not provide conclusive evidence that a user manually changed the affected production record, and the proposed read-only change was not approved.
important_findings: "Registration Commission Fee Tax" is automatically calculated as 10% of "Registration Total Commission Fee."
Consumption Tax in the invoice/Expense BIP is derived from "Registration Commission Fee Tax" in the NV Quote.
The field is editable in the UI by design for FDP, allowing manual value changes.
A changed "Registration Commission Fee Tax" value is synchronized to subsequent Quote revisions and Sales Orders, then reflected in BIP invoices.
The behavior was reproduced in FDP UAT-1 using Quote# 1-85UN3O and Sales Order# A001303334.
Testing reported no calculation or screen-refresh defect, but no conclusive production-record evidence of manual user modification was provided.

investigation_summary: Vehicle base price was blank on NV Order Sheet-3 for NV Sales Order# A000413141. The initial assumption that blank output was expected for non-Bus vehicles was corrected after identifying that Trailer and Forklift Product Classes were not handled by NV Order Sheet-3. A fix was validated in UAT-1 and deployed to Production in the March 25 FDP planned release.
important_findings: NV Sales Order# A000413141 has Product Class of Vehicle set to 'Trailer'.
Trailer and Forklift Product Classes were not handled in NV Order Sheet-3, causing the vehicle base price to remain blank.
The initial BRD-based explanation that Order Sheet-3 output should be blank for non-Bus vehicles did not meet the required behavior equivalent to specification 2.
The fix was implemented and verified in UAT-1 using NV Sales Order# A001301436.
The fixed changes were applied to the Production environment in the March 25 FDP regular release.
root_cause: NV Order Sheet-3 did not handle Trailer and Forklift Product Classes, resulting in a blank vehicle base price for Trailer sales orders.
resolution: Updated NV Order Sheet-3 to handle Trailer and Forklift Product Classes; validated the change in UAT-1 and deployed it to Production on March 25.

investigation_summary: A recovery was completed and the requester was asked to validate the result. The requester subsequently requested ticket closure. No technical investigation details, root cause, or specific corrective actions were documented.
important_findings: Recovery was reported as completed.
Requester was asked to validate the recovery.
Requester requested closure after recovery completion.
resolution: Recovery was completed; no further technical resolution details were documented.

investigation_summary: Recovery of the affected records was completed, and no additional impacted records were identified. The incident was determined not to be a Siebel system issue. Monitoring would continue, with recovery to be performed if further affected records were detected.
important_findings: Recovery of the affected records was completed.
No additional impacted records were identified.
The incident was not a Siebel system issue.
Continued monitoring was planned for any further affected records.
resolution: Recovered the affected records; continued monitoring was planned and incident closure was requested.

investigation_summary: Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Planned Delivery Date in the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order. This caused an incorrect invoice payment date when the Quote and Sales Order planned delivery dates differed. The mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation was changed to use the Sales Order and was validated in UAT-1 before deployment to PROD in the May 13 release.
important_findings: The affected invoice showed PaymentDueDate 2026-03-31 because Payment Term was 1 and the Quote Planned Delivery Date was 2026-02-25.
As an immediate recovery, the Quote Planned Delivery Date was updated to 2026-03-17, matching the Sales Order date, and the invoice displayed the correct value after regeneration.
The confirmed defect was that Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate/Planned Payment Date was sourced from NV Quote rather than NV Sales Order.

UAT1 tests confirmed that when the Sales Order Planned Delivery Date was present, PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Sales Order date; the test response was sent to KB for invoice report generation.

Holiday handling was clarified to include Saturdays, Sundays, and defined public holidays; adding holiday-aware Planned Payment Date calculation was identified as a separate Project Change Request requirement.
The mapping fix was released to PROD in the May 13 release.
root_cause: The Planned Delivery Date used to calculate Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was mapped from the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order.
resolution: Updated the Planned Delivery Date mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation from Sales Quote/NV Quote to Sales Order/NV Sales Order, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to PROD on May 13.

investigation_summary: Amounts differed between the SV_SIEBEL and KB reports because the KB Bip report showed incorrect UnitPrice values for some line items. When an existing JCO was updated or synchronized after a user changed List Unit Price in Quote Line Items, JCO retained and forwarded the old price. The fix was implemented and validated in UAT-1, then deployed to production in the regular release on the 23rd.
important_findings: The KB Bip report displayed incorrect UnitPrice values for some line items, causing differences from SV_SIEBEL.
Updating List Unit Price in Quote Line Items did not update the price selected by JCO.
The issue occurred only when an existing JCO was updated/synced.
The previous price was saved and sent forward despite the user-entered price change.
The fix was verified successfully in UAT-1 before production approval.
The fix was applied to production during the regular release on the 23rd.
root_cause: For updates/synchronizations of an existing JCO, JCO picked up the old List Unit Price instead of the newly updated price in Quote Line Items.
resolution: Fixed the JCO price-selection behavior in UAT-1, validated the result, and deployed the fix to production in the regular release on the 23rd.

investigation_summary: Profit values between the UV Sales Order and the latest UV Sales Quote revision became misaligned when a Sub Quote was synced after the Sales Quote had already completed approval and been synced to the Sales Order. The issue was reproduced in FDP UAT-1 using UV Quote#: 1-6UW1UZ and UV SO#: E001303159. A validation preventing post-approval Sub Quote updates was released to Prod on 9th April, and recovery was completed.
important_findings: Sub Quote 1-7DUHTZ was synced to the UV Sales Quote after the Sales Quote had been approved and synced to the Sales Order.
The "Update Customer Quote" button remained active in the Sub Quote detail view when the UV Sales Quote status was "Initial Approval Completed".
Service items synced to the UV Sales Quote after approval were not synced to the UV Sales Order.
The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 with UV Quote#: 1-6UW1UZ and UV SO#: E001303159.
Recovery was completed before the production fix release.
root_cause: The "Update Customer Quote" button allowed Sub Quote updates after the UV Sales Quote reached "Initial Approval Completed" and had already been synchronized to the UV Sales Order, causing later Service items to update the quote but not the order.
resolution: Added validation to display "Sales Quote has already been completed." when "Update Customer Quote" is selected after the UV Sales Quote reaches "Initial Approval Completed". The change was released to Prod on 9th April.
technical_entities: Sales Quote has already been completed.

investigation_summary: List Price in Siebel was incorrectly updated with Cost Price during Price Master automation on Iwate and Wakayama prod. Investigation identified an ODI Data Mapping defect; the mapping was corrected, PT_Price_List master was recovered, and Price Master was re-executed successfully using new batch logic.
important_findings: Cost Price was being updated to both List Price and Cost Price in Siebel.
The issue was caused by a miss in ODI Data Mapping.
Price Master automation was initially implemented only on Iwate and Wakayama prod, where the issue was detected.
Other environments were unaffected because Price Master was executed manually.
After updating the ODI mapping, Price Master was re-executed on Iwate and Wakayama using new batch logic and prices were updated correctly.
root_cause: A miss in ODI Data Mapping caused Cost Price to be mapped and updated as both List Price and Cost Price in Siebel.
resolution: Recovered and updated List Price in PT_Price_List master, corrected the ODI mapping, and re-executed Price Master on Iwate and Wakayama using new batch logic.

investigation_summary: The issue affected Purchase Orders with no Parent Order. A fix was implemented and validated in UAT1 using test record N001302802. After confirmation that the issue was working correctly, the fix was deployed to production in the March 12, 2026 emergency release.
important_findings: The issue occurred for Purchase Orders with no Parent Order.
The fix was applied in UAT1 and tested with record N001302802.
UAT validation confirmed the fix was working correctly.
The fix was deployed to production in the March 12, 2026 emergency release.
root_cause: The issue was triggered when processing Purchase Orders with no Parent Order.
resolution: Implemented a fix for Purchase Orders with no Parent Order, validated it in UAT1 with test record N001302802, and deployed it to production in the March 12, 2026 emergency release.

investigation_summary: Duplicate vehicle records were created when a vehicle was initially registered without a model code because the model code was unavailable in the Production environment. After the model code was added, the update process searched by model code and could not match the original record, so it created a new record. Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles were recovered, and monitoring was deployed across all FDP environments to detect and recover similar records promptly.
important_findings: The initial vehicle record was created without a model code because the code was not available in the Production environment.
The update process uses the model code to locate an existing vehicle record.
Because the original record lacked the model code, the system could not identify it and created a duplicate vehicle record with the correct model code.

Example impacted record: Hakodate Production vehicle MS06GP-20085; initial record created on 19 Dec 2025, model code added on 23 Dec 2025 under SR MFTBCFFR-5162, and duplicate creation occurred during the 24 Dec 2025 update.
Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles required recovery; recovery of the Hakodate vehicle was completed.
A monitoring script was deployed across all FDP environments to send email alerts for similar records so they can be recovered immediately.
root_cause: The model code was unavailable when the original vehicle record was created, leaving that record without a model code. After the code was added, the system's model-code-based update lookup could not find the original record and created a duplicate vehicle record.
resolution: Recovered impacted Sales Orders and vehicle records, and deployed a monitoring script across all FDP environments that sends email alerts for records matching this condition, enabling immediate recovery.

investigation_summary: The reported Customer Name Print 1 and Customer Name Print 2 values for account code 0000T08492 were compared between Account Receivable/Account and the data sent to KB. Engineering confirmed that the values in the KB files matched the account information updated on 3 March 2026. The incident was closed temporarily because no response was received from the vendor; a new ticket will be raised if further investigation is required.
important_findings: The records for account code 0000T08492 in chuKRCIF0012026030402160200486.csv and chuASAIF0032026030403313500482.csv showed Customer Name Print 1 and Customer Name Print 2 values matching the UI.
The data sent to KB on 3 March 2026 matched the current values in Account Receivable and Account.
No discrepancy between Account information and KB-linked data was identified during the investigation.
The vendor had not responded before closure, so the incident was closed pending any future need to reopen through a new ticket.

investigation_summary: Registration Request tax-related line items were not created when the Vendor Code derived from the Registration Request Master had no Account Payable Information. This prevented required values from being maintained and could prevent tax finalization/JV creation. The solution was aligned with the SC version, tested in UAT-1, and released to PROD on 13 May.
important_findings: In NV Sales Order, the Vendor Code for a Registration Request is derived from the Registration Request Master based on the Registration Location.
When the derived Vendor Code lacked Account Payable Information, tax-related Registration Line Items were not generated.
JV creation requires tax Registration Items with Part# S02, S03, or S06 and an actual amount greater than zero.
Before tax finalization, mandatory vendor payment fields are required when the actual amount including tax is greater than zero.
The fix was changed to match the SC version by making Customer Code, Customer Payment Date, and Customer Payment Method editable in Registration Request line items.
The changes were implemented in UAT-1, tested with SO# A001302470 and A001303987, and released to PROD on 13 May.
root_cause: The system did not create tax-related Registration Request line items when the Vendor Code derived from the Registration Request Master lacked Account Payable Information, leaving users unable to maintain required information for tax finalization.
resolution: Updated Registration Request line-item behavior in accordance with the SC version, including editable Customer Code, Customer Payment Date, and Customer Payment Method fields; the change was released to PROD in the 13 May release.

investigation_summary: Invoices could not be issued because the Payment Date was blank when the source Payment Date was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote. The investigation established that the system lacked the required fallback logic to derive the invoice payment date from delivery-related dates under the configured payment-deadline conditions. The logic was iteratively corrected and tested in UAT-1, then released to PROD in the 13th May release.
important_findings: Payment Date on the Invoice was blank because the corresponding value was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote.
The original behavior required a manually entered Payment Date after selecting a month in Payment Term Type, which did not satisfy the required invoice behavior.
For Payment Due Date (Baseline Type) Vehicle = "After Delivery", a null Payment Date must use the planned delivery date before Sales Posting and the Actual Delivery Date after Sales Posting.
The required fallback behavior was expanded beyond Payment Due (Term) Vehicle = "00"; dates also had to be displayed for terms other than "00".
For Payment Due Date (Baseline Type) Vehicle = "After Deadline", the proposed behavior was to display Payment Scheduled Date when Payment Date was null and make the field mandatory at Quote.
The proposal to replace the Actual Delivery Date with the system-generated actual sales date was rejected.
root_cause: When Payment Date was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote, the Invoice logic did not derive a payment date from the required delivery-related dates and payment-deadline conditions.
resolution: Implemented the corrected payment-date derivation logic based on user feedback, completed UAT-1 testing, and released the change to PROD in the 13th May release.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Journal Voucher (JV) records required recovery, and the recovered data was linked to KB through the night batch. The initial investigation attributed the issue to concurrent "Tax Finalize" actions from separate unrefreshed sessions, but this cause was explicitly rejected. A logic change to prevent multiple JV creation was tested on UAT1 and deployed to production in the 2026-04-23 FDP release.
important_findings: Recovery for the affected record was completed using reverse Journal Voucher data, and the data was linked to KB in the night batch.
The initially reported cause was duplicate JV creation when "Tax Finalize" was clicked from list applet and Line Item applet in separate sessions without refresh.
The reported root cause was challenged as incorrect by the requester.
The corrective logic was fixed and validated on UAT1 using test record A001303745.
The fix was deployed to production in the 2026-04-23 FDP release.
resolution: Updated logic to prevent Journal Voucher (JV) creation multiple times; the fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to production in the 2026-04-23 FDP release.

investigation_summary: Sales Price in Quote Line Items was not set to zero for non-chargeable YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A line items. Investigation found that the existing zero-price condition for non-chargeable line items excluded these parts. The condition was updated, validated in UAT1 using JC Number I001303010, and deployed to production in the March 25 regular FDP release.
important_findings: The issue affected Sales Price in Quote Line Items for non-chargeable YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A line items.
Existing logic set Sales Price to 0 for non-chargeable line items but did not include YS4A, YS5A, or YS6A parts.
The fix added YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A parts to the existing zero-price condition.
The fix was validated in UAT1 with test record JC Number I001303010; Sales Price could be controlled by Line Item Type.
The fix was applied to the production environment through the March 25 FDP regular release.
root_cause: The existing condition that sets Sales Price to 0 for non-chargeable line items excluded YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A parts.
resolution: Updated the existing non-chargeable line-item condition to include YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A parts, validated the change in UAT1, and deployed it to production in the March 25 FDP release.

investigation_summary: Sales Orders were displayed in the logged-in user's 'My' view even when the user was not the sales person in charge. Investigation determined that visibility was granted to all members listed in the Other Team Members/Sales Order team context. The visibility logic was changed so that only the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association can view the order in 'My'; the change was deployed to Production on 23/04/2026.
important_findings: Entity Transfer added users to the Sales Order team, causing multiple users to be associated with an order.
The issue occurred because Sales Orders were visible in 'My' view for all members shown in the Other Team Members applet.
The required behavior was that selecting 'My' must not display orders belonging to other sales representatives.
The final visibility rule uses the logged-in user as the Primary Employee of the primary position association with the order.
The same correction was applied to the NV Quotes tab.
The production deployment was completed in the release on 23/04/2026.
root_cause: The 'My' view visibility logic allowed all users associated through the Other Team Members/Sales Order team to view a Sales Order, instead of restricting visibility to the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association.
resolution: Implemented code-level visibility logic restricting Sales Order and NV Quotes tab 'My' view results to the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association, then deployed the fix to Production on 23/04/2026.

investigation_summary: An incorrect approval flow was triggered for an NV Quote revision because the backend field "Profit Amount High Flag" was set to "Y" incorrectly. The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 using multi-browsing activity, while other approval-flow scenarios operated correctly. A code-level fix was implemented to recalculate the field from the latest Quote revision updates and was deployed to Production in the April 23 FDP release.
important_findings: The incorrect value "Y" in "Profit Amount High Flag" caused the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to be triggered incorrectly.
"Profit Amount High Flag" is a backend field used in approval-flow conditions for NV Quote revisions based on Sales Profit changes.
For revised NV Quotes, the flag should be "Y" when Sales Profit remains the same or increases, and "N" when Sales Profit decreases.
The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 using multi-browsing activity; other tested approval-flow cases were reported as working correctly.
The implemented fix recalculates "Profit Amount High Flag" based on the latest updates made during Quote revision.
The fix was deployed to Production through the FDP release on April 23.
root_cause: During NV Quote revision, "Profit Amount High Flag" was incorrectly updated to "Y" due to multi-browsing activity, causing the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to trigger instead of the applicable flow.
resolution: Implemented a code-level fix to recalculate "Profit Amount High Flag" using the latest Quote revision updates, validated the NV Quote approval process in FDP UAT-1, and deployed the change to Production in the April 23 FDP release.

investigation_summary: Incorrect hierarchy/sequencing display was traced to an incorrect LOV migration to production for CR-2902. The old LOV was migrated instead of the new LOV required by the added search-condition logic. Production LOV values were corrected, the affected order was recovered, and validation found no other affected orders in FDP environments.
important_findings: CR-2902 introduced a new LOV for hierarchy control and logic that uses the LOV as a search condition.
The old LOV was migrated to production instead of the new LOV, causing hierarchy display to be incorrect.
Production LOV values were updated outside business hours, after which the hierarchy displayed correctly.
Recovery was completed for affected order B050663847; all details were included and correctly linked to TOB.
Checks of FDP production environments found no remaining affected records or orders beyond the reported order.
root_cause: During migration of CR-2902 to production, the old LOV was deployed instead of the new LOV required for hierarchy-control search logic.
resolution: Updated the LOV values in production, completed recovery for the affected order, and verified that all details were correctly linked to TOB with no remaining affected records in FDP environments.

investigation_summary: Actual expense invoice line items were not being created correctly for affected sales orders. Existing affected sales orders were recovered while a permanent fix was tested in UAT-1. The fix was deployed to the production environment in the regular release on March 25, 2026.
important_findings: All sales orders listed in the attached Excel sheet were recovered before the permanent fix was deployed.
The issue was resolved in UAT-1 for UV Sales Order E001302581, where Actual Invoice line items were corrected.
The required line items will be created in actual expense invoices after the change.
New affected sales orders and invoices were to be recovered until the production release.
The production fix was applied in the March 25, 2026 regular release.
resolution: Implemented changes to create all required line items in actual expense invoices, validated the fix in UAT-1, and deployed it to the production environment on March 25, 2026.

investigation_summary: This ticket was identified as a duplicate of MFTBCFFR-4150, “CR_NV_Specification changes.” Engineering discussion and requested changes are being tracked in MFTBCFFR-4150, and this ticket was proposed for closure.
important_findings: The incident discussion was moved to MFTBCFFR-4150.
MFTBCFFR-5443 is a duplicate ticket.
Requested changes and future updates are tracked in MFTBCFFR-4150.
resolution: Close MFTBCFFR-5443 as a duplicate and track the requested changes under MFTBCFFR-4150.

investigation_summary: Consumption tax was not calculated when a Shipment Detail response was received from IBOS, resulting in incorrect or missing tax Journal Vouchers. The missing calculation logic was traced to the Siebel IBOS component during CR-4194 development. A fix was validated in UAT, affected records were recovered using reverse and corrected JVs, and the fix was deployed to PROD in the release on the 11th.
important_findings: IBOS JV creation is triggered when a Shipment Detail response is received from IBOS.
Consumption tax calculation logic was missing from the Siebel IBOS component during CR-4194 development.
All FDPs were checked and no additional cases were found where a Tax JV was not created.
Affected records were corrected through reverse JVs with negative amounts and corrected JVs; recovery JVs were linked to KB through the regular KB night batch.
The UAT fix added logic for creation of the “ConsTax - Body Building IBOS” type Journal Voucher; UAT1 test record was B001302440.
Monitoring and recovery were continued until the production deployment.
root_cause: The logic to calculate Consumption tax was missed in the Siebel IBOS component during CR-4194 development, causing incorrect or missing tax Journal Voucher creation for IBOS Shipment Detail responses.
resolution: Added Consumption tax calculation logic for “ConsTax - Body Building IBOS” Journal Voucher creation, validated the fix in UAT, recovered affected records with reverse and corrected JVs, and deployed the fix to PROD in the release on the 11th.
technical_entities: ConsTax PO - Body Building Order - IBOS

investigation_summary: The incident affected order records and required recovery of the initially affected record and additional records identified in an attached Excel file. Investigation determined the issue matched MFTBCFFR-5446 and was caused by an incorrect LOV. LOV values were corrected in all FDP production environments, and recovery was completed for all affected records.
important_findings: Recovery was initially incomplete, then completed for the affected record.
Additional orders with the same issue were identified and recovered.
The issue was the same as MFTBCFFR-5446: VO_Chassis order details outline number wrong_China.
An incorrect LOV caused the error to appear.
LOV values were corrected across all FDP production environments.
Recovery was completed for all affected records.
root_cause: An incorrect LOV was present, causing the error to appear.
resolution: Corrected LOV values in all FDP production environments and recovered all affected records.
technical_entities: VO_Chassis order details outline number wrong_China

investigation_summary: A delivery approval error occurred for an NV Sales Order after the associated Chassis Order was moved to "Pending" through an SR and then reprocessed to "Ordered." The system attempted to create another Vehicle record; because a Vehicle already existed, the existing Vehicle was unmapped from the Chassis Order and Sales Order. The issue was replicated in UAT-1, the affected record was recovered on February 27, and the user subsequently completed Sales Posting.
important_findings: Approving an NV Sales Order with Product Class "Trailer" automatically created a Chassis Order.
Setting the Chassis Order to "Ordered" created a Vehicle that was mapped to both the Chassis Order and Sales Order.
After the Chassis Order was set to "Pending" through an SR and reprocessed to "Ordered," the system attempted to create a new Vehicle record.
Because a Vehicle record already existed, no new Vehicle was created and the existing Vehicle was unmapped from both related orders.
The behavior was replicated in UAT-1 using SO# A001302411 and Chassis Order# B001302412.
root_cause: Recovery performed under an SR changed the Chassis Order status to "Pending" after a Vehicle had already been created. Reprocessing the order to "Ordered" caused the system to attempt Vehicle creation and unmap the existing Vehicle from the Chassis Order and Sales Order.
resolution: Recovered the affected record on February 27; the user successfully completed Sales Posting for the Sales Order.

investigation_summary: The Tax exemption/Non Tax Flag was always set to "Y" because the corresponding flag was disabled in Siebel configuration, preventing its logic from executing. An initial UAT1 configuration fix did not cover the "Both" case for new registration of accounts receivable and payable when the Tax exemption flag was unchecked. Additional changes were made and verified in UAT1, then deployed to production through an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
important_findings: The Consumption Tax Exempt flag/Non Tax Flag was inactive in Siebel configuration, so its logic processing did not execute and the field defaulted to "Y".
The initial configuration change resolved part of the issue in UAT1 but failed for "New registration of both accounts receivable and payable" when the Tax exemption flag was unchecked.
Necessary changes were made for the "Both" case on UAT1, and user testing confirmed that everything was working as expected.
The validated fix was applied to the production environment in an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
root_cause: The Consumption Tax Exempt flag/Non Tax Flag was disabled in Siebel configuration, preventing logical processing and causing the field to default to "Y".
resolution: Updated the required configuration, including changes for the "Both" accounts receivable and payable registration case; the fix was verified in UAT1 and deployed to production via an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
technical_entities: New registration of both accounts receivable and payable

investigation_summary: The incident involved duplicate Chassis Orders/Purchase Orders and Recycle Fees, plus blank Pool Cost items in NV Pool Cost Order. Duplicate Purchase Orders were traced to duplicate Vehicle records in Chugoku production for chassis# MS06GP-20140, caused when a Vehicle Model Code update created records with different model codes. Pool Cost Master End Date values were corrected in FDP Chugoku and affected records were recovered, but the recurrence-prevention fix for the duplicate-order issue remained pending deployment to FDP.
important_findings: Receiving multiple D21A files from TOB is normal and was not the confirmed cause of the duplicate-order issue.
Chugoku production contained two Vehicle records for chassis# MS06GP-20140 with different Model Codes, resulting in duplicate Purchase Orders.
Updating the Model Code on a Vehicle was identified as causing duplicate Purchase Order and Vehicle records; a similar issue was recorded in MFTBCFFR-4952.
Pool Cost Master End Date values in FDP Chugoku remained set to 2025, causing blank Pool Cost items; the End Date was corrected and affected records were recovered.
The SC fix changes Model Code matching to use the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record and synchronously updates the Vehicle Model Code from the incoming TOB file.
The duplicate-order fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871, but deployment to FDP required SC approval.
root_cause: A Vehicle Model Code update created duplicate Vehicle records with different Model Codes for the same chassis#, which generated duplicate Purchase Orders/Chassis Orders. Separately, Pool Cost Master End Date values in FDP Chugoku had not been updated and remained set to 2025.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned differing amounts for three lubrication line items printed on the KB Invoice Sheet. Siebel Orders, related logic, and Invoice JSON were rechecked and showed no discrepancy; the transmitted values were correct. The issue could not be reproduced, and the bug was closed with investigation results retained for future recurrence.
important_findings: Siebel transmitted UnitPrice/Sub-totalAmountwithoutTax values of 7,840 for ServiceItemNumber 18930001, 3,512 for 30109001, and 4,257 for 17460001.
KB Invoice Sheet showed different standard amounts: 10800 for 18930001, 3520 for 30109001, and 4110 for 17460001.
KB confirmed that it prints data linked from SIEBEL as is.
Re-investigation of Siebel Orders, processing logic, affected records, and Invoice JSON found no discrepancy.
The issue could not be reproduced.
resolution: The bug was closed because the issue could not be reproduced after confirming correct SIEBEL processing and Invoice JSON values; investigation results were to be retained for future recurrence.

important_findings: The issue was caused by a Hakodate login issue.

important_findings: IDOCs sent to Siebel can fail during downtime.

investigation_summary: A fix was completed in UAT-1 and approved for production deployment via Teams. The change was released to the production environment on 11 March 2026, and verification was requested before closure.
important_findings: The issue was fixed in UAT-1.
Production approval was provided via Teams.
The fix was deployed to Prod on 11 March 2026.

investigation_summary: When a new Assessment Request reused a VIN from a cancelled previous Assessment Request, approving Stock In Verification activated the "Previous Assessment Flag". The flag prevented UV Body Building POs for that VIN from being mapped to a new sales order. Data was recovered, making the BB POs available on the "Map" screen, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Reusing a VIN from a cancelled previous Assessment Request triggered the "Previous Assessment Flag" after Stock In Verification approval for the new assessment number.
The "Previous Assessment Flag" indicates that the VIN and its associated UV BB POs already exist in a previous assessment.
The flag prevented UV Body Building POs associated with the VIN from being mapped to a new sales order.
Data recovery restored availability of the BB POs on the "Map" screen.
root_cause: The "Previous Assessment Flag" was activated because the VIN and associated UV BB POs were already present in a previous Assessment Request, blocking PO mapping for the new sales order.
resolution: Recovered the data so that the BB POs became available on the "Map" screen.

investigation_summary: Automatic print functionality was investigated and determined not to be related to Siebel configuration. The issue was attributed to the printer; reverting the test user to original values restored automatic printing. Canon is conducting further analysis, and the incident remains On Hold pending Canon's RCA and printer change request completion.
important_findings: The issue was confirmed to be related to the printer rather than Siebel configuration.
The test user was reverted to original values, after which automatic print functionality worked as expected.
Print requests will continue to be monitored while proceeding with the printer change request advised by Terui-san.
No system issue or pending action was identified from the Cubastion side.
Canon is analyzing the issue and will provide the RCA after its investigation is complete.
root_cause: Printer-related issue; no Siebel configuration issue was identified.
resolution: Reverted the test user to the original values, restoring automatic print functionality. A printer change request is planned, with final closure pending assignment of new printers and Canon's RCA.

investigation_summary: A UV Quote approval record was affected when the approver and alternative approver updated the Action simultaneously from multiple browsers. The concurrent Approved and Rejected actions caused other approvals to become Auto Rejected while the first approval remained Approved. The behavior was replicated in UAT-1 and classified as user miss-operation rather than a system defect. The affected record was recovered by changing the UV Quote status to In Progress so the approval process could continue.
important_findings: Approval history timestamps indicated concurrent user actions.
The approver set Action to Approved while the alternative approver simultaneously set Action to Rejected.
The concurrent actions caused other approvals to become Auto Rejected and retained the first approval as Approved.
The scenario was replicated in UAT-1 using UV Quote "1-7XXRK3".
The affected UV Quote was recovered by setting its status to In Progress.
root_cause: Simultaneous Action updates by the approver and alternative approver from multiple browsers, resulting in conflicting Approved and Rejected actions.
resolution: Recovered the affected record by changing the current UV Quote status to In Progress, allowing the user to continue the Quote Approval process.

investigation_summary: The issue was fixed and verified in UAT-1. Validation confirmed that behavior matched SC, and deployment to FDP-PROD was requested.
important_findings: The fix was applied in UAT-1.
UAT-1 verification confirmed the behavior was working correctly and matched SC.
Deployment to FDP-PROD was requested after UAT-1 validation.
resolution: The issue was fixed in UAT-1 and validated as functioning correctly; deployment to FDP-PROD was requested.

investigation_summary: A report-printing issue occurred only in the Chugoku production environment; other FDP environments were unaffected. Investigation identified random LOV behavior associated with SR MFTBCFFR-4676 and duplicate backend LOV entries. The LOV was corrected in the Chugoku production backend, and the user confirmed report printing worked afterward.
important_findings: The issue was isolated to Chugoku production; functionality worked in other FDP environments.
The affected functionality was report printing.
The issue was associated with random LOV behavior created for SR MFTBCFFR-4676.
Duplicate LOV entries existed in the backend.
Fixing the LOV in the Chugoku production backend restored report printing and was user-confirmed.
root_cause: Duplicate backend entries in the LOV caused random LOV behavior associated with SR MFTBCFFR-4676, preventing report printing in Chugoku production.
resolution: Fixed the LOV and its duplicate backend entries in Chugoku production; the user confirmed that report printing worked.

investigation_summary: In NV FDP China, trade-in vehicles were not displayed on the Sales Order Sheet, and Stamped Model Code, Registered Year, and C/# number were blank in NV quotations and sales orders. Investigation confirmed that Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0, while Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are sourced from the Product ID of the linked Model Code. The observed values were blank in FDP production and SC production; C/# number is designed to remain blank in both environments.
important_findings: Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0.
The target NV quotation had Trade-In Amount set to 0 on the trade-in vehicle detail line, so the trade-in item was not displayed.
Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are populated from the Product ID of the linked Model Code.
The applicable Model Code had blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code values in both FDP production and SC production.
C/# number is always blank by design in both SC and FDP environments.
SC production SO# A037817024 also had Trade-In Amount of 0 and therefore did not display the trade-in item in Order Sheet BIP.
root_cause: The trade-in vehicle was not displayed because its Trade-In Amount was 0, which does not meet the Order Sheet BIP condition of Trade-In Amount greater than 0. Blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code resulted from blank values on the applicable linked Model Code; C/# number is blank by design.
resolution: No corrective change was applied. The behavior was confirmed as existing Order Sheet BIP logic and existing data/configuration; updating C/# number was offered if requested.

investigation_summary: EC Orders created toward Siebel printed the wrong BIP report because the production default report configuration was set to PT Delivery Note instead of the EC-specific report. The configuration was corrected in UAT to use EC Delivery Sheet for EC Orders and was approved after validation. The fix was deployed to Production in the release on the 11th.
important_findings: For EC Orders created toward Siebel, the production default print report was configured as PT Delivery Note.
The incorrect default configuration caused the wrong BIP report to print.
The UAT fix changed the EC Order report setting to EC Delivery Sheet.
The UAT fix was approved and subsequently applied to Production.
root_cause: The production configuration selected PT Delivery Note as the default report for EC Orders created toward Siebel, rather than the EC-specific report.
resolution: Changed the report setting for EC Orders to EC Delivery Sheet, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it to Production.

investigation_summary: The Eligible Business Number field in EC BIP displayed the Dealer code for the respective FDP Production environment. The field depends on a backend column in the Dealer master record that supports a join used to retrieve the Dealer code. The backend data was corrected, and EC BIP now shows the correct Dealer code value.
important_findings: The Eligible Business Number field in EC BIP retrieves the Dealer code through a join with the Dealer master record.
A backend column in the Dealer master record was created before the Okayama go live to enable this join.
The required backend column value needed to be updated in other FDP Production environments.
After the backend data was fixed, EC BIP displayed the correct Dealer code value.
root_cause: The backend column value in the Dealer master record, required for the join that retrieves the Dealer code in EC BIP, was not updated in the affected FDP Production environment.
resolution: Updated the backend data in the Dealer master record so EC BIP retrieves and displays the correct Dealer code value.

investigation_summary: In FDP UAT-1, cancelling a Work Order line item after Quote customer approval updated the Quote price but left the JCO price unchanged when the Job Card was closed without creating and approving a new Quote. The issue was compared with SC behavior and a synchronization fix was implemented in UAT-1. The fix was released to the production environment on March 11.
important_findings: The issue was reproducible in UAT-1 when a labor, parts, or lubrication line item was cancelled after the Quote was customer approved.
Cancelling a Work Order line item immediately updated the Quote total, but did not update the corresponding JCO price.
JCO pricing was previously refreshed only when a new Quote was created and customer approved after the line-item cancellation.
The resulting mismatch affected Labor List Price between the Quote and JCO when the Job Card was closed without re-syncing the Service Quote.
In FDP, the JCO Subtotal price is sent to KB, making JCO price synchronization required.
The fix was tested in UAT-1 using SC behavior as the reference and then deployed to production.
root_cause: The FDP JCO price was not synchronized when Work Order line items were cancelled after Quote customer approval; JCO was updated only after a subsequent Quote creation and customer approval.
resolution: Implemented a JCO price synchronization fix in FDP UAT-1, aligned with the SC reference behavior, and released it to production on March 11.

investigation_summary: A print status error occurred when the print button was clicked because a connection to the Canon server could not be established. Review of FDP production records found the issue affected only one record; requests before and after it completed successfully. No related record was found in monitoring, and the incident was closed after normal operation was confirmed.
important_findings: The print status error was caused by failure to establish a connection to the Canon server when the print button was clicked.
The issue occurred for only one FDP production record.
Requests before and after the affected record were processed successfully.
No related record was found in monitoring at the time of review.
Printing was confirmed to be working normally before closure.
root_cause: The connection to the Canon server could not be established when the print button was clicked.
resolution: No corrective action was documented; the issue was isolated to one record, normal processing was confirmed, and the incident was closed.

investigation_summary: An Assessment Request for an Unstock Vehicle could not be updated to "Completed" because it became read-only after reaching "Vehicle for Quotation". The request was created by user D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role, for which existing functionality permits editing only specific statuses. Recovery was completed on February 3 by updating the Assessment Request to "Cancelled", and a logic change was planned for UAT to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable.
important_findings: The Assessment Request was created by user ID D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role.
The "Quotation Vehicle Allocation" flag was set to "Y", causing the request to be treated as an Unstock Vehicle case.
For Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff, statuses outside the configured editable-status list are read-only.
When the request status became "Vehicle for Quotation", UV staff could not update it to "Completed" because the status was read-only.
A review of the FDP production environment found no other similar incidents.
root_cause: Existing editability logic made Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff read-only when their status was set to "Vehicle for Quotation", preventing UV staff from changing the status to "Completed".
resolution: On February 3, the affected Assessment Request status was updated to "Cancelled". A follow-up change was planned in the UAT environment to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable even when the request was created by Branch-Sales-Staff.

investigation_summary: An incorrect value was manually corrected. The issue was caused by a different sequencing order of files received in Iwate and Chugoku compared with other environments. The user manual was updated with precise processing steps to prevent recurrence.
important_findings: The affected value was manually corrected.
File sequencing order in Iwate and Chugoku differed from other environments.
The differing file order caused the issue.
The user manual was updated with precise steps to prevent similar mistakes.
root_cause: The sequencing order of files received in Iwate and Chugoku differed from the sequencing order in other environments.
resolution: The incorrect value was manually fixed, and the user manual was updated with precise steps to prevent recurrence.

investigation_summary: UV Sales Quote profit calculation mismatched for production record AR#: H000522508, Quote#: 2-AJ8LJK, an Unstock Vehicle case. A blank Vehicle ID on the Model Code line item caused it to be classified as a Non-Vehicle Line Item and its price to be deducted twice. The affected record was recovered, and the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification was corrected, validated in UAT1, and released to Production on February 19.
important_findings: The affected record was an Unstock Vehicle, where the chassis number was not mapped to the assessment.
Vehicle and Non-Vehicle line item prices in UV Sales Quote are calculated separately based on the Vehicle ID in the Model Code line item.
For Unstock Vehicle cases, the Model Code line item has no chassis and its Vehicle ID remains blank.
The blank Vehicle ID caused the Model Code line item to be treated as a Non-Vehicle Line Item, resulting in its price being deducted twice during Sales Profit calculation.
The corrected Non-Vehicle Line Item search condition identifies records with blank Vehicle ID only when Product Type is not 'Model Code'.
The fix was implemented in UAT1 using AR#: H000052299 and UV Quote#: 1-7WLRVD, then released to Production on February 19.
root_cause: For an Unstock Vehicle, the Model Code line item had a blank Vehicle ID because no chassis was present. The Non-Vehicle Line Item search logic therefore misclassified the Model Code line item as non-vehicle, causing the Model Code price to be deducted twice during UV Sales Quote profit calculation.
resolution: Recovered the affected record and updated the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification to exclude records with Product Type 'Model Code' when Vehicle ID is blank. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Production on February 19.

investigation_summary: A Total List Price mismatch occurred between SV Quote and UV Quote labor line items because the quotes used different pricing logic. SV Quote directly stored Adjusted List Price for specified Labor Billing Types, while UV Quote multiplied by Qty in all cases. The SV Quote logic was implemented in UV Quote, validated in UAT-1, and released to Production on February 19.
important_findings: The mismatch affected Total List Price between SV Quote and UV Quote.

For Shaken, 3-month Inspection, 6-month Inspection, 12-month Inspection, 24-month Inspection, MPC Shaken, PDF Shaken, MPC + PDF Shaken, and Spare Tire – Toolbox, SV Quote stores Adjusted List Price directly.
UV Quote applied multiplication by Qty for all Labor Billing Types, including types requiring directly stored Adjusted List Price.
The updated UV Quote pricing behavior was validated in UAT-1 using UV Sales Quote# 1-7VR5H1 and SV Quote# 1-7VR5I9.
The fix was released to Production in the February 19 FDP release.
root_cause: UV Quote did not implement the SV Quote pricing logic for specified Labor Billing Types and instead multiplied the price by Qty in all cases.
resolution: Implemented the SV Quote pricing logic in UV Quote so that Adjusted List Price is stored directly for the affected Labor Billing Types; validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on February 19.

investigation_summary: Parts added through the “ASENT”/“Ascent” button in Parts Internal Order did not receive a Sales Order ID, causing the incident. The issue was replicated in UAT using Parts Internal Order M001301558, fixed and tested in UAT-1, and deployed to production in the 19/02/2026 regular release.
important_findings: When parts or other line items were added using the “ASENT” button in Parts Internal Order, the Sales Order ID was not populated on the line items.
The issue was replicated in UAT with Parts Internal Order M001301558.
The same issue had been identified and fixed in SC under incident INC5623286, and the fix was planned for FDP.

UAT-1 testing used sales orders A001301627 and A001301641 with Parts Internal Orders M001301628 and M001301642; Registration and Delivery completed with no error during final approval for sales posting.
Testing of the Ascent function requires a parts-staff user; SSO login availability initially prevented user validation.
root_cause: The Sales Order ID was not populated on Parts Internal Order line items when parts or other line items were added through the “ASENT”/“Ascent” button.
resolution: Implemented the fix to populate the Sales Order ID for line items added through Ascent, validated it in UAT-1, and applied it to the production environment in the 19/02/2026 regular release.

investigation_summary: AR/AP details were not visible in Accounts for migrated SC accounts 0000H37697 and 0000G14513, although the accounts were Active and linked to KB. Investigation found that the UI filter condition for displaying AR/AP was inactive due to a data migration issue from SC. The inactive condition was updated for all affected records, restoring AR/AP visibility; no application logic fix or KB linkage was required.
important_findings: Affected accounts 0000H37697 and 0000G14513 were Active and had AR/AP data present.
The accounts were already linked to KB, and Account data had already been sent to KB.
AR/AP details were hidden because the UI filter condition to display AR/AP was inactive.
The inactive condition resulted from data migration from SC, not from application logic.
All FDPs were checked and no similar records were found.
Recovery was completed for all affected records, and AR/AP details became visible in Accounts.
root_cause: During data migration from SC, the filter condition controlling AR/AP visibility on the UI became inactive for affected accounts.
resolution: Updated the inactive UI filter condition for all affected records, restoring AR/AP visibility in Accounts. No code fix or KB linkage was required.

investigation_summary: UOE Order Type was not transferred from Quote Line Items to Sales Order Line Items, preventing automatic purchase-order creation. The issue was traced to join logic used for the transfer. The logic was corrected in all UAT environments and validated in UAT-7 using Quote No. 1-MWLB5 and Sales Order No. M000034549.
important_findings: The join logic transferring values from Quote Line Items to Sales Order Line Items was incorrect.
UOE Order Type did not appear on Sales Order Line Items.
Because UOE Order Type was not passed downstream, the purchase order was not created automatically.
The corrected logic was deployed to all UAT environments.
The fix was verified successfully in UAT-7 for UOE Quote 1-MWLB5 and Sales Order M000034549.
root_cause: Incorrect join logic for transferring UOE Order Type from Quote Line Items to Sales Order Line Items.
resolution: Corrected the join logic in all UAT environments, restoring UOE Order Type on Sales Order Line Items and automatic purchase-order creation.

investigation_summary: Adding AR or AP from the Finance Info tab of Accounts failed when the account had a value in DUNS No. Non-null DUNS No values existed only for Chugoku accounts migrated from SC, where TSR functionality from CR-0574 had existed but was removed in FDP. DUNS No was removed from account 0000U08057 to allow AR creation, and the incident was closed with a wait-and-see approach because the case was considered rare.
important_findings: The error occurred when adding AR or AP from the Finance Info tab of Accounts with a non-null DUNS No field.
Accounts with non-null DUNS No values existed only in the Chugoku region and were migrated from SC.
TSR functionality implemented in SC under CR-0574 had been removed in FDP and was identified as causing the issue.
Removing DUNS No from account 0000U08057 allowed the user to proceed with AR creation.
Removal of TSR logic was proposed, but no permanent correction was implemented; the case was classified as rare and closed.
root_cause: TSR logic related to DUNS No remained applicable to Chugoku accounts migrated from SC, despite the TSR functionality from CR-0574 having been removed in FDP.
resolution: Removed DUNS No from account 0000U08057 to enable AR creation. No permanent TSR-logic change was made; the issue was closed for observation.

investigation_summary: Quote revisions failed when the copied 'Promissory Note Due Date' was earlier than the quote revision/creation date and triggered validation. The underlying cause was an incorrect backend date-field format that made date values non-comparable. The date format was corrected, successfully tested in UAT-1 on Quote '1-2MZIQ2', and deployed to PROD in the 5-Feb-2026 regular release.
important_findings: Validation requires 'Promissory Note Due Date' to be greater than or equal to the quote creating date.
During quote revision, historical promissory-note dates caused validation errors for quotes including 1-6YMFWCN, 1-6Z3N4YR, and 1-6Z3N60P.
Temporary recovery changed affected promissory-note due dates to the current date so users could complete quote revisions, then restored the original dates.

Existing quote-revision behavior creates the revised quote with a blank 'Promissory Note Due Date' when the original date is earlier than the quote revising date; the user can then enter a new date manually.
Quote copy does not copy the 'Promissory Note Due Date'; it is entered manually and must satisfy the quote-creation-date validation.
The proposed change to disable validation during quote revision was not required after identifying the backend date format defect.
root_cause: The backend date field format was incorrect, making 'Promissory Note Due Date' values non-comparable and causing validation errors during quote revision.
resolution: Corrected the backend date field format, validated the fix in UAT-1 using Quote '1-2MZIQ2', and deployed the fix to PROD in the 5-Feb-2026 regular release.

investigation_summary: An error occurred while creating an Assessment Request when multiple Assessment Requests existed for the same Chassis#. The issue was replicated in UAT-1 and traced to an incorrect code-level Search Specification that queried Purchase Quote using the wrong Assessment Request number. The corrected Search Specification was deployed to UAT-1, verified by successful creation of a new Assessment Request, and released to Production on February 5, 2026.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced in UAT-1 for Chassis# Test-60VX using Assessment Requests H000052187, H000052188, and H000052190.
Purchase Quote associated with Assessment Request H000052187 was incorrectly selected when processing another Assessment Request.
The affected Production records had the same root cause as the UAT-1 reproduction.
Recovery for the affected records was completed before the permanent code fix.
After the UAT-1 fix, users could create a new Assessment Request for the same Chassis#.
root_cause: An incorrect code-level Search Specification queried Purchase Quote using the wrong Assessment Request number, causing the Purchase Quote for Assessment Request H000052187 to be selected incorrectly.
resolution: The Search Specification was corrected to query Purchase Quote using the correct Assessment Request number. The fix was deployed to UAT-1 on January 27, 2026 and released to Production in the February 5 FDP regular release.

investigation_summary: The VECT button transition was affected because the PR object in the manifest management screen was inactive. The inactive configuration originated during CR-4982 testing in the development environment and was migrated to RT2 and production. The configuration was corrected in all production and UAT environments, restoring VECT integration.
important_findings: During CR-4982 testing, the PR object in the manifest management screen was changed to inactive in the development environment.
The inactive PR configuration was migrated from the development environment to RT2 and production.
An inactive PR file affected the transition triggered by pressing the "VECT" button.
The configuration was fixed in all production and UAT environments.
Preventive actions include migration checks for unnecessary production configuration changes and adding VECT verification to the daily morning sanity check.
root_cause: The PR object in the manifest management screen was set to inactive during CR-4982 testing and that configuration was migrated to RT2 and production, causing the PR file to be inactive and affecting VECT button transitions.
resolution: Corrected the PR object configuration in all production and UAT environments.

investigation_summary: A recovered record showed that the price master data was correct for the model code, but the price had not updated correctly in the quote. The issue could not be replicated in FDP UAT, where all tested cases succeeded. Analysis found required conditions were satisfied when the model code and price were changed, but no reproducible defect or confirmed root cause was identified.
important_findings: The affected record was recovered.
Price master data was correct for the corresponding model code, but the quote did not update correctly.
Investigation was requested across SC and all FDP environments.
The issue could not be replicated in the FDP UAT environment; all test cases were successful.
Required conditions were correctly satisfied at the time of the model-code change and price update.
Limited information for the affected record prevented further root-cause tracking.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned Responsible Service Shop Code becoming null without creating another SR. Engineering could not reproduce the behavior using an identical record, AR Shop Code updates, or Customer Update in Service Request. Logic and recovery processing reviews found no discrepancy, so the incident was closed as an unconfirmed, extremely rare event.
important_findings: Once Responsible Service Shop Code is populated, testing indicated it cannot become null without creating another SR.
An identical record was created and Shop Code was updated in AR; the functionality operated normally.
Updating values through Customer Update in Service Request did not reproduce the issue.
Review of the related process logic found no defect or discrepancy that could cause the behavior.
No recovery processing issue was identified that could lead to the incident.
resolution: Incident closed without a corrective change because the issue could not be reproduced and no logic or recovery-processing discrepancy was identified; re-investigate if the behavior recurs.

investigation_summary: A recurring slowness issue was reported and was confirmed improved after database statistics were gathered. Engineering identified database statistics collection as the corrective measure and scheduled it to run every Sunday to prevent recurrence.
important_findings: The incident involved a recurring slowness issue.
Gathering database statistics resolved the slowness on 2026-01-21.
The user confirmed that the improvement was observed.
Database statistics will be gathered every Sunday as a preventive measure.
root_cause: Outdated or insufficient database statistics causing slowness.
resolution: Database statistics were gathered to resolve the immediate slowness, and a weekly Sunday database-statistics collection schedule was established to prevent recurrence.

investigation_summary: Branch sales manager/director names displayed in BIP were sourced from the corresponding department configuration. Incorrect personnel-change settings affected Department 7020 and other departments under base 70. The department values were corrected in Prod, and the updated names were reflected in BIP reports.
important_findings: The branch sales manager name in BIP is derived from the corresponding department configuration.
The reported issue was attributed to omitted settings during personnel changes.
Department 7020 was updated and the corrected value was reflected in BIP.
All director names for base 70 departments were updated.
The corrected data was confirmed in Prod and reflected in the BIP report.
root_cause: Department configuration values for branch sales manager/director names were not updated during personnel changes.
resolution: Updated the name values in all base 70 department configurations, including Department 7020, in Prod; the corrected values were reflected in BIP reports.

investigation_summary: BIP delivery-slip reports inserted blank pages for shipments with more than 90 line items and reports exceeding 15 pages. Investigation found that BIP configuration and alignment did not handle the higher line-item volume correctly. The BIP changes were updated for the new delivery-slip format, validated on UAT-1 for shipment O000181209, and confirmed to work for up to 96 line items; production release was approved for the FDP release scheduled for 2026-07-23.
important_findings: Reports with 88 and 90 records generated correctly, while shipment O000181209 with 93 records generated blank pages.
The blank-page issue occurred when shipments had more than 90 line items and the BIP report exceeded 15 pages.
BIP configuration and alignment were not aligned for reports containing more than 90 items.
The initial UAT-1 changes had to be applied to the new delivery-slip format implemented under CR-0869.
The PDF-generation error in the new format was resolved, and the bottom-page feed names Delivered and Quantity Delivered were corrected to display on one line.
The BIP report was confirmed to work correctly for up to 96 line items.
root_cause: BIP configuration and alignment did not correctly support delivery-slip reports with more than 90 line items, causing blank pages in reports exceeding 15 pages.
resolution: Updated the BIP changes for the new delivery-slip format, resolved the PDF-generation error and bottom-page feed-name wrapping, and validated the report on UAT-1 for up to 96 line items. Production release was approved and planned for the FDP release scheduled for 2026-07-23.

investigation_summary: The incident involved incorrect approval flows for the Bus-Staff position. Corrected approval flows were implemented and validated using Assessment Request# H000052108 in UAT-1. The changes were subsequently completed in the Okayama Production environment, and affected records were recovered.
important_findings: Incorrect approval flows affected the Bus-Staff position.
Corrected approval flows were implemented in UAT-1.
Assessment Request# H000052108 was provided as a UAT-1 verification record.
Testing used User ID D0X20903 with the Bus-Staff position.
Approval flow changes were completed in the Okayama Production environment.
Affected records were recovered in production.
root_cause: Incorrect approval flows for the Bus-Staff position.
resolution: Implemented corrected approval flows in UAT-1 and Okayama Production, and recovered the affected records.

investigation_summary: Records corresponding to Hinmoku were not uploaded because its field mapping in the backend master was configured incorrectly. The Hinmoku field configuration was corrected and the process was verified to be working on all production environments.
important_findings: A backend master stores file columns that are mapped to Siebel columns.
The Hinmoku field was incorrectly configured in the backend master.
Records corresponding to Hinmoku were not uploaded as a result of the incorrect mapping.
After correcting the Hinmoku field configuration, the process worked on all production environments.
root_cause: The Hinmoku field was not configured correctly in the backend master that maps file columns to Siebel columns.
resolution: Corrected the Hinmoku field configuration in the backend master and verified the process on all production environments.

investigation_summary: An error occurred when creating a clothing order from order details. A fix was deployed to FDP Okoyama UAT and UAT-1, where it was tested using record 'A001301251'. Power BI reports were refreshed, and the change was applied to production through the PBI release on 24 January 2026.
important_findings: The reported issue was an error when creating a clothing order from order details.
The fix was deployed to FDP Okoyama UAT and confirmed resolved on UAT-1 using record 'A001301251'.
Power BI was updated and the reports were refreshed.
The code fix was scheduled for all FDPs Prod and was applied to production in the PBI release on 24 January 2026.
resolution: The code fix and Power BI update were deployed to production in the PBI release on 24 January 2026 after UAT validation.

investigation_summary: Option codes appeared in Japanese in the VC UI. Backend verification found no Japanese characters in VC database data, and no recovery was performed. The behavior was reproduced by using the Explorer option to translate the VC to Japanese; the translation affected only the UI.
important_findings: No Japanese characters were present in VC data at the database level.
Correct option names were displayed when the investigation began, and no recovery was performed.
The issue was reproduced by opening the VC and selecting the Explorer option to translate to Japanese.
Explorer translation converts some option values on the UI only and does not modify backend data.
All VC data on FDP Production was verified and no Japanese characters were found.
root_cause: User operation: the Explorer option was used to translate the VC UI to Japanese, causing some option codes to appear in Japanese on the UI only.
resolution: No system correction was required. The incident was dismissed and closed after confirming the behavior was caused by user operation and did not affect database data.

investigation_summary: Sales prices in PowerBI reports did not consistently match Siebel for JC records, including special labor and billing-type scenarios. Investigation identified mismatched sales-price logic in ODI, including Net Operation Time handling and report-specific logic differences. ODI logic was modified for reports 1-10A, 1-15A, and 1-12A, but final release validation for all affected reports was not confirmed in the comments.
important_findings: The issue affected sales-price discrepancies between Siebel and PowerBI across reports, not only SV 1-12 Report.
Special scenarios included labor code .004330 and Billing Type "Spare tire toolbox".
PBI-UAT initially included Net Operation Time in the Special Sales Price calculation, although this was reported as incorrect for the tested Billing Type.
Testing in UAT1 (FDP Okoyama) found mismatches for JC I001301489: Siebel 43,200 versus differing values in reports 1-01, 1-10A, 1-12A, 1-15A, and no update in 1-02.
ODI code was modified to correct Sales price values in PowerBI Report 1-10A and to align sales-price logic in reports 1-10A, 1-15A, and 1-12A.
root_cause: ODI sales-price calculation logic in PowerBI did not match Siebel logic for special labor and Billing Type scenarios, including incorrect Net Operation Time handling and inconsistent report logic.

investigation_summary: Printing of the FDPC_A1 Acceptance Sheet was investigated for USER-UW's primary printer, CFUSO-07-LBP006, after an issue was reported affecting three printers. A test print on Chugoku prod using a Canceled Job Card succeeded, and the print request also succeeded on Canon Server. The issue was therefore not attributed to Siebel, and users were subsequently able to print successfully.
important_findings: The reported issue affected three printers, including USER-UW's primary printer, CFUSO-07-LBP006.
FDPC_A1 Acceptance Sheet printing was successfully replicated on Chugoku prod using a Canceled Job Card.
The print request was successful on Canon Server.
The investigation concluded that this was not a Siebel issue.
Canon logs were shared with the IT team.
Users were later able to print successfully.
resolution: Printing functionality was confirmed to be working successfully for users; the incident was proposed for closure.

investigation_summary: The incident was caused by the JPN screen cache not being cleared after master data upload because the JPN screen was unavailable for maintenance during the holiday period. The ENU screen cache had been cleared. The incident was confirmed not to be a Siebel issue and was dismissed after preventive operational steps were defined.
important_findings: The ENU screen cache was cleared during the holiday period.
The JPN screen was down for maintenance, preventing its cache from being cleared.
The issue was reported before the JPN screen cache was cleared the following morning.
Cache clearing for the JPN screen will be prioritized in post-master-data-upload verification and morning sanity checks.
The incident was confirmed not to be a Siebel issue.
root_cause: The JPN screen cache was not cleared because the screen was unavailable for maintenance during the holiday period.
resolution: Add JPN screen cache clearing as a priority post-master-data-upload verification item, perform it during morning sanity checks, and confirm execution with relevant teams.

investigation_summary: A Tax amount finalization error was replicated in UAT-1 using UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882. The issue occurred after a user manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax'; the affected YN6M line item was not updated to Invoiced when the invoice was created. The incident was classified as user misoperation, with no affected cases found in any FDP Production Environment; users should revise the UV Sales Quote and restore the correct expense line items.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in UAT-1 with UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882.
Creating an invoice automatically updates standard line items with Type 'Tax' to status Invoiced.
The manually changed line item with Part Number YN6M and Type 'Tax' was not updated to Invoiced.
Tax Finalization requires all line items with Type 'Tax', including manually updated lines, to be Invoiced.
No cases of manually changing an Expense Line item to 'Tax' were found in any FDP Production Environment.
root_cause: User manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax', causing the YN6M line item to remain outside the expected invoicing-status update and not be set to Invoiced before Tax Finalization.
resolution: No system fix or recovery was required. The user should revise the UV Sales Quote and update the correct expense line items.

investigation_summary: The issue was reproduced for JC# I001300905 on FDP - UAT1: a Quote Item showed Line Discount % as 0% after manually entering List Unit Price for Dummy Lubricant (..999999), while the synced JCO Order Item showed 100%. Investigation identified differing Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item, associated with a null Lubrication Price. A JCO-side fix was implemented in UAT and deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.
important_findings: The issue was replicated on FDP - UAT1 for JC# I001300905.
When List Unit Price was manually entered for Dummy Lubricant (..999999) while the Quote was In Progress, Quote Item Line Discount % was 0%.
After the Quote became Customer Approved and the JCO was created/synced, the Order Item Line Discount % became 100%.
Quote Item and Order Item used different Line Discount % calculation behavior.
The issue was associated with Lubrication Price being null.
The initially proposed approach to make List Unit Price read-only was rejected; the fix was changed on the JCO side.
root_cause: Different Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item when Lubrication Price was null caused the JCO Order Item Line Discount % to become 100% while the Quote Item remained 0%.
resolution: A JCO-side fix was implemented and validated in UAT, then deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.

investigation_summary: Chassis Orders were created with a blank/missing model code because the relevant model code was not registered when the TOB/D21A processing occurred. The model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025 after the chassis order had been created on 10-Dec-2025. Impacted records were recovered after model-code creation was restored across FDP environments; the investigation also identified that not all TOB master files are automatically updated.
important_findings: The affected chassis order was created on 10-Dec-2025, while model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025.
Model code "MS06GPQUCV-9" was missing from the Chugoku, Wakayama, and Okayama Model Master, preventing chassis-order creation in those environments.
Affected Chassis Orders were recovered by correcting master data and reprocessing the relevant records; recovery was reported complete for all impacted records.
Model codes with MC "9" were manually updated in Chugoku and Wakayama on 26-Dec-2025 after receipt of the required TCH01 file.

TCH01 is the TOB PC Master 2 - Model Master inbound batch interface to Siebel via SFTP and is scheduled as a daily package run in Siebel PROD; not all TOB master interfaces are scheduled for daily PROD processing.
The proposed preventive control is to prevent Chassis Order creation when a model code is absent, notify the AMS team by email, correct data, and reprocess the record.
root_cause: The required model code was not registered in the system when the TOB/D21A file was processed. Specifically, "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created after the corresponding Chassis Order, and TOB master updates were not configured so that all master files were automatically updated.
resolution: Model-code creation was restored and missing model codes were manually updated in the affected FDP environments. The impacted Chassis Orders were recovered and reprocessed after the required master data was available.

investigation_summary: The reported amount mismatch between the order form and sales estimate was initially observed as different discount mappings between Quotation BIP and Order Sheet BIP. The final investigation determined that the Quote price was changed after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approval, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order. This was classified as a user mis-operation rather than a product defect.
important_findings: Quotation BIP showed a Discount amount of -819798 from MF Vehicle Discount Amount, while Order Sheet BIP showed -60000 from MF UV Discount.
The Quote price was changed after the Quote had been approved and the Sales Order had been created.
A price change made after Quote approval without re-approval is not reflected in the Sales Order.
The incident was determined not to be a bug and was proposed for rejection.
root_cause: The user changed the Quote price after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approving the Quote, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order.
resolution: Users should avoid changing the Price after Quote Approval; the incident was rejected as a user mis-operation rather than a bug.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed on all FDP-PROD environments. The requester confirmed that the issue was resolved and requested closure.
important_findings: Recovery was completed on all FDP-PROD.
The requester confirmed that all systems were functioning normally after recovery.
No root cause or recovery procedure was documented in the comments.
resolution: Recovery completed on all FDP-PROD; requester confirmed resolution.

investigation_summary: The incident involved PO Shipments becoming stuck in the "In Progress" status in Shikoku PROD. The issue was confirmed to be the same as SC Version INC4055209. The corrective fix schedules two Job Instances to submit shipments stuck in "In Progress" status, and it was released through the regular FDP release on 9 January.
important_findings: PO Shipments could become stuck with status "In Progress".
The issue was identified as the same issue addressed by SC Version INC4055209.
Recovery for the immediate issue was completed on Shikoku PROD.
Two Job Instances were scheduled in FDP-UAT1 to submit Shipments stuck in "In Progress" status.
The fix was released in the regular FDP release on 9 January.
