root_cause: PO Shipment processing could get stuck, leaving Shipments in the "In Progress" status.
resolution: Implemented and released two Job Instances across FDP-PROD to submit Shipments that are stuck in the "In Progress" status.

investigation_summary: Column sequences were incorrect across all FDPs following the SV Sales Price lubrication prod release. The issue was recovered by correcting the column sequence for all FDPs.
important_findings: The incident affected column sequence across all FDPs.
The issue occurred following the SV Sales Price lubrication prod release.
Column sequences were corrected for all FDPs.
The issue was recovered.
root_cause: SV Sales Price lubrication prod release caused the column sequence issue.
resolution: Corrected the column sequence for all FDPs.
technical_entities: SV Sales Price lubrication prod release

investigation_summary: The PO Invoice BIP in Service Purchase Order did not handle tax-exempt line items correctly. The BIP logic was updated in FDP-UAT1 so SV_Invoice displays a 0% tax rate when the Tax Exempt flag is Y. UAT1 validation completed without issues, and the fix was released through the regular FDP release on 9 January.
important_findings: Tax rate configuration in PO Invoice BIP did not handle tax-exempt line items.
The corrected logic sets the SV_Invoice tax rate to 0% when the Tax Exempt flag is Y.
The fix was validated successfully in FDP-UAT1 using JC# I001300757 and PO# J001300758.
The fix was released in the regular FDP release on 9 January.
root_cause: Tax rate configuration in PO Invoice BIP in Service Purchase Order did not handle tax-exempt line items.
resolution: Updated the PO Invoice BIP logic to handle tax-exempt line items and return a 0% tax rate in SV_Invoice when the Tax Exempt flag is Y; released in the regular FDP release on 9 January.

investigation_summary: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation compared the entered Branch Code with the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, preventing invoicing when the codes differed. For I000111578 (D8YOOSEK), the relevant Primary Location Code was "70"; for I000111572 (D8MICSAS), it was "00". CR MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code filter, allowing Individual Invoice issuance from Branch Code "00"; Bulk Invoice was unaffected because it selects Branch from the JC Header.
important_findings: The entered Branch Code was validated against the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, which can be checked in the employee Location Code.
I000111578 (D8YOOSEK) had Primary Location Code "70", while I000111572 (D8MICSAS) had Primary Location Code "00".
Before the MFTBCFFR-4379 release, I000111578 could be invoiced using Branch Code "70".
MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice, allowing invoice issuance from Branch Code "00".
Bulk Invoice was not affected because Branch is selected from the JC Header.
root_cause: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation/filter required the entered Branch Code to match the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, causing failures when the codes differed.
resolution: Deployed CR MFTBCFFR-4379, which removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice.

investigation_summary: Department Code values CSJS200 and CSJS300 in PO - Trailer & Forklift JV were sourced from the Purchase Order creator instead of the intended Sales Order Location Code. The mapping was corrected and validated in UAT1. The change was released to FDP prod in the 17 December planned release; no recovery Journal Vouchers were created.
important_findings: Department Code in PO - Trailer & Forklift JV was mapped from the Purchase Order's Creator.
The required mapping source was Sales Order's Location Code.
UAT1 validation included Sales Order Location Code 10 and Last Approver's Location Code 50.
Recovery through reverse and corrected Journal Vouchers was not required.
The mapping correction was released to FDP prod on 17 December 2025.
root_cause: Department Code mapping for PO - Trailer & Forklift JV incorrectly sourced the value from the Purchase Order's Creator rather than the Sales Order's Location Code.
resolution: Changed the Department Code mapping to use Sales Order's Location Code, validated the change in UAT1, and released it to FDP prod on 17 December 2025. No recovery was performed.

investigation_summary: The Expense Invoice BIP report displayed the value from "Integrated Address(J)" instead of "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)". The issue affected all FDP Production environments and resulted from a required BIP report update not being completed after the code changes associated with MFTBCFFR-4625. The report mapping was corrected, validated in UAT, and released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
important_findings: Expense Invoice BIP report used "Integrated Address(J)" rather than "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)" for the address value.
For Invoice 1-130032159 and Account 0C00240272, the report was corrected to display "1-4-11 Minami-Shinozakicho, Edogawa-ku, Tokyo".
The issue was not specific to Chugoku; it existed in all FDP Production environments.
A necessary BIP report update was missed after code changes related to MFTBCFFR-4625.
The corrected address display was validated in UAT before production approval.
root_cause: A required BIP report update was not completed after the code changes associated with MFTBCFFR-4625, causing Expense Invoice BIP to map the address to "Integrated Address(J)" instead of "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)".
resolution: Updated the Expense Invoice BIP report to display the correct "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)" value, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it in the 17th Dec FDP release.

investigation_summary: Investigation found that Quote 1-1DCFQK (Rev11) contained an incorrect Sales Price of ¥1,596,200,000 instead of the Quote Sales Price of ¥15,900,000. The Sales Price field is editable, so the user must correct the value before proceeding with the Revise functionality. The issue was determined to be user mis-operation rather than a system defect.
important_findings: Quote 1-1DCFQK (Rev11) had Sales Price set to ¥1,596,200,000.
The Quote Sales Price was ¥15,900,000.
Sales Price is an editable field.
The incorrect Sales Price prevented the user from proceeding with Revise functionality.
The incident was classified as user mis-operation, not a system issue.
root_cause: User entered an incorrect Sales Price of ¥1,596,200,000 in Quote 1-1DCFQK (Rev11) instead of ¥15,900,000.
resolution: Update the editable Sales Price field to ¥15,900,000 and then proceed with Revise functionality.

investigation_summary: The incident involved incorrect part prices in FDP environments. Correct list-price files were received and executed, after which part prices updated correctly. The issue was determined not to be a system issue and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Files containing the correct list prices were received for all FDP environments.
The corrected file was executed on 2025-12-09.
Part prices updated correctly after file execution.
The incident was determined not to be a system issue.
resolution: Executed the received files containing the correct list prices for all FDP environments, which updated part prices correctly.

investigation_summary: Recycle fee orders were not created for impacted vehicles due to a data migration issue. Engineering recovered the missing orders and corrected the data for all identified records in Chugoku Prod.
important_findings: The incident was identified as a data migration issue.
The impacted vehicles were FBA20-611682, FBAV0-610618, FEAV0-611155, FEB50-611002, FK65F-620975, FY84HY-500017, FY84HY-500018, and FY84HY-500019.
Recovery created the recycle fee order for the initially reported vehicle.
All impacted Recycle fee orders were recovered.
Data was confirmed correct in Chugoku Prod after recovery.
root_cause: Data migration issue affecting Recycle fee order data for the listed vehicles.
resolution: Recovered all impacted Recycle fee orders and corrected the associated data in Chugoku Prod.

investigation_summary: Delivery Approval failed for NV Sales Order records A000009087 and A000011464 in the Wakayama Production environment. The failure was traced to a Vehicle ID mismatch between the automatically created Purchase Order and its corresponding Sales Order. The affected records were recovered, but the underlying reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined because required historical system information was no longer retained.
important_findings: Both affected NV Sales Orders had product class "Trailer", which automatically creates a "Trailer & Forklift" Purchase Order after Sales Order approval.
When the Purchase Order status changed to "Ordered", a new Vehicle record was created and its Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order.
Delivery Approval validates Vehicle information between the Purchase Order and Sales Order; the Vehicle ID mismatch caused the validation error and blocked Delivery Approval.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT or FDP UAT, and no similar recurrence was observed in production environments during subsequent monitoring.
The affected Purchase Orders were processed in March 2025 but the incident was reported in December 2025, after the required system-information retention period had expired.
System log retention is planned to be extended from one month to two months to support investigation of future occurrences reported within the retention period.
root_cause: The immediate cause of the Delivery Approval error was a Vehicle ID mismatch: the newly created Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order. The reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined.
resolution: Affected records were recovered. No defect was identified in the current implementation and no reproducible code fix was confirmed; continued monitoring and extension of system log retention from one month to two months were planned for future investigation and recurrence prevention.

investigation_summary: JV Base Amount for Outsource Non IBOS was mapped from the Outsource order's Total Selling Price instead of the Purchase Order Total price. Body Building Order JVs also selected incorrect account codes when Vehicle Type was null. The mapping was changed and validated on UAT1, then released to Prod in the 17th Dec FDP release; recovery reverse and corrective JVs were requested for affected BB orders.
important_findings: Outsource Non IBOS JV Base Amount was sourced from Total Selling Price in the Outsource order, which was 5000 for the investigated case.
The required mapping for both IBOS and Non-IBOS cases was Purchase Order Total price; when multiple POs exist in an Outsourcing order, a JV must be created for each PO.
For PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS, a null Vehicle Type caused selection of account code 038, rather than the required Account Code CSJS201: 031 and Subsidiary Account Code CSJS202: 60.
Incorrect Account Item Code CSJS201 records were identified for recovery through reverse JVs and corrected JVs based on the Vehicle Class.
The Purchase Order Total price mapping was fixed and validated on UAT1 using SO# A001300621, then released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
Account Item Code CSJS201 & 301 issues were being addressed through CR MFTBCFFR-4627.
root_cause: JV mapping used the Outsource order Total Selling Price rather than Purchase Order Total price, and Body Building Order JV account-code selection defaulted to account code 038 when Vehicle Type was null.
resolution: Changed the JV Base Amount mapping to Purchase Order Total price on UAT1, validated the change, and released it to Prod in the 17th Dec FDP release. Recovery required reverse and corrected JVs for affected BB orders with posting date 20251211.
technical_entities: PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS

investigation_summary: For I050366087 JC, the associated JV did not have a Re-edit Red Slip created. The JV was created before the 13 September release of CR-4039, which updated Re-edit functionality and related logic; the current logic showed no discrepancy and no similar affected records were found. A recovery Red Slip JV was created in Chugoku prod after approval and will be linked to KB through the nightly daily batch.
important_findings: The Re-edit Red Slip was not created for the JV associated with I050366087 JC.
The affected JV was created before the CR-4039 release on 13 September, which updated Re-edit functionality and related logic.
Review of the logic and all FDPs found no similar affected records.
Testing did not reproduce the issue using multiple browsers or other special cases.
The recovery Red Slip JV was created in Chugoku prod after verification and approval.
root_cause: A data issue affecting a JV created before the CR-4039 Re-edit functionality update; no discrepancy was found in the current logic.
resolution: Created the recovery Red Slip JV in Chugoku prod after approval; the data will be linked to KB in the nightly daily batch.

investigation_summary: Parts Internal Return Orders for NV and UV Order Department did not have Vehicle Id, causing VIN# and Registration# to remain blank in Siebel and PBI. The initial analysis incorrectly assessed Parts Sales Return Orders; subsequent investigation confirmed the issue also existed in the SC version. The Parts Internal Return process was changed to populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order, validated in FDP-UAT1, released to FDP-PROD on 17/12/2025, and historical records were data-patched.
important_findings: The initial analysis of Parts Sales Return Orders was not applicable because the reported issue concerned Parts Internal Return Orders.
For NV and UV Order Department, Parts Internal Return Orders did not contain Vehicle Id; the same behavior existed in the SC version.
Missing Vehicle Id resulted in blank VIN# and Registration# on both Siebel and PBI.
The corrected process populates Vehicle Id on the Parts Internal Return Order from its parent Internal Order.
The fix was validated in FDP-UAT1 using NV record M001300645 and UV record M001300655, with VIN# and Registration# populated in Siebel and PBI.
Data patching was completed for affected FDP-PROD records through 17/12/2025.
root_cause: The Parts Internal Return process did not populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order for NV and UV Order Department, leaving VIN# and Registration# blank.
resolution: Updated the Parts Internal Return process to populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order, released the fix in the 17/12/2025 FDP release, and data-patched affected FDP-PROD records.

investigation_summary: When changing the Sales Rep on a Sales Order, the Entity Transfer functionality did not initially display D8OKATAR because the Employee Applet search logic required the same Primary Position Type as the current Sales Rep. Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition allowed users from other locations to appear. The search logic was corrected to display only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code, and the fix was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
important_findings: The original Entity Transfer condition required users to be in the same organization and have the same Primary Position Type as the primary Sales Rep.
D8OKATAR was excluded because its Primary Position Type was Branch-Sales-Staff, while D8TAKOUN and D8THORIK had Branch-Sales-Manager.
The Primary Position Type condition had been added under MFTBCFFR-4341, but the requested behavior was branch-based selection without a job/position-type restriction.
Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition made positions in the Sales Rep's department visible, but also displayed users from other locations.
The Employee Applet search logic was revised so Entity Transfer displays users with the same branch as the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code.
root_cause: The Employee Applet/Entity Transfer search logic used a Sales Rep Primary Position Type condition rather than limiting eligible users solely by the Sales Order branch; after that condition was removed, the logic was still insufficiently constrained and displayed users from other locations.
resolution: Corrected the Employee Applet search logic to show only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code. The change was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
technical_entities: Sales Rep Primary position Id condition

investigation_summary: The incident blocked Delivery Approval for Recycle order B050483481. Investigation determined that, during duplicate-line-item recovery for MFTBCFFR-4952, the backend X_SALES_ORDER_ID for line item "YN5D" was not updated correctly. The affected record was recovered, the prior recovery was verified, and the user proceeded with Delivery Approval.
important_findings: The issue was related to recovery work for MFTBCFFR-4952, not a Siebel issue.
The affected business object was line item "YN5D" in Recycle order B050483481.
Duplicate-line-item recovery requires updating the backend column X_SALES_ORDER_ID.
The X_SALES_ORDER_ID for the affected line item was missed or incorrectly updated during recovery.
After the record recovery was completed, the user successfully proceeded with Delivery Approval.
The recovery performed for MFTBCFFR-4952 was subsequently verified.
root_cause: During duplicate-line-item recovery for MFTBCFFR-4952, the backend X_SALES_ORDER_ID column for line item "YN5D" in Recycle order B050483481 was not updated correctly.
resolution: Recovered the affected record, verified the MFTBCFFR-4952 recovery, and confirmed that the user could proceed with Delivery Approval.

investigation_summary: An affected record was recovered, and a planned fix was approved for production deployment. The fix was released on December 17 and the Pool Cost order All View was confirmed fixed in FDP Production.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the affected record.
Production approval was obtained for the planned fix.
The changes were scheduled for the December 17 FDP production release.
Pool Cost order All View was fixed in FDP Production.
resolution: Released the approved changes to FDP Production, fixing the Pool Cost order All View.

investigation_summary: Payment Terms were missing from Wave-3 PROD environments because the required Payment Condition master data was not available during the initial PROD deployment. UAT4–8 were corrected by uploading master data based on values in OKAYAMA-PROD and validating the PO Sheet master-to-BIP linkage. The corrected changes were deployed to production in the 30th November FDP emergency release.
important_findings: Payment Condition values displayed in BIP are based on the PO Sheet master.
Required Payment Condition master data was not provided during the initial Wave-3 setup, so Payment Terms were not reflected in Wave-3 PROD.
MFTBCFFR-4978 added the missing Payment Condition values across UAT environments using values already present in OKAYAMA-PROD.
Shikoku and Wakayama PROD displayed Payment Terms because their BIP configuration contained hardcoded Payment Condition values.
Iwate, Okinawa, and Chugoku did not contain hardcoded BIP Payment Condition values, causing differences across FDP environments.
UAT4–8 validation confirmed that the master and BIP were linked and that master values were correct.
root_cause: Required Payment Condition master data was unavailable during the initial Wave-3 PROD deployment; BIP displays Payment Terms from the PO Sheet master.
resolution: The missing master-data/BIP changes validated in UAT4–8 were deployed to production through the 30th November FDP emergency release.

investigation_summary: Users could not print the "Specification 2" BIP report because a part line item had a null price. The price for Part MK645741 became null after its quantity was edited directly in the Sales Order, rather than through the Quote. The quantity field for parts line items was made read-only in UAT-1 and released to FDP Production on 26 November.
important_findings: The "Specification 2" BIP report fails when a part line item price is null.
Part MK645741 had a null price.
Editing quantity directly in the Sales Order caused the part price to be set to null.
Quantity changes must be performed through the Quote, not the Sales Order.
Epic MFTBCFFR-3485 had made only body tab line-item quantity read-only; this incident required the same restriction for parts line items.
The parts line-item quantity field was made read-only in UAT-1 and deployed to FDP Production.
root_cause: A user edited the quantity of Part MK645741 directly in the Sales Order, causing its price to become null; BIP reports cannot process part line items with a null price.
resolution: Made the quantity field read-only for parts line items in the Sales Order, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to FDP Production in the 26 November planned FDP release.

investigation_summary: After SO Sales Posting, revising an NV/UV Quote to change the Customer Account created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV and omitted the Consumption Tax JV. The issue was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093. The logic was updated and validated on UAT1, then deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.
important_findings: The issue occurred when an NV/UV Quote was revised after SO Sales Posting and the Customer Account changed without a Sales Amount change.
Existing logic created revised Journal Voucher items only when the Sales Amount changed; otherwise, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.
The missing Consumption Tax JV was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093.
The same functionality and affected logic apply to UV and across all FDPs.
Past JVs have been affected because the logic has existed since FDP go-live.
root_cause: Existing revised Journal Voucher logic created Consumption Tax Journal entries only for Journal Voucher items with a Sales Amount change. When only the Customer Account or other non-amount values changed, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.
resolution: Updated the logic to create the Consumption Tax Journal together with the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' Journal even when the Sales Amount is unchanged and fields such as Customer Account change. The fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.

investigation_summary: The incident affecting Update AR was caused by an incorrect value in the "Customer Name(J)" field in AR. Recovery was completed by correcting the customer name, and users could proceed with Update AR functionality.
important_findings: The "Customer Name(J)" field in AR contained an incorrect customer-name value.
The incorrect value used a different Japanese corporate notation and spacing than the required value.
Recovery was completed after correcting the "Customer Name(J)" value.
Update AR functionality was available to users after recovery.
root_cause: An incorrect value in the "Customer Name(J)" field in AR.
resolution: Corrected the "Customer Name(J)" value in AR and completed recovery, allowing users to proceed with Update AR functionality.

investigation_summary: The D21A file for Fuso Reception Number 038765 contained model code MS06GPQGUCV with MC 9. This combination was not present in Shikoku Model Code Master, so no chassis order was created and the Vehicle record product Id remained null.
important_findings: D21A file for Fuso Reception Number 038765 provided model code MS06GPQGUCV with MC 9.
Model code MS06GPQGUCV with MC 9 did not exist in Shikoku Model Code Master.
No chassis order was created.
The Vehicle record product Id was set to null.
root_cause: Model code MS06GPQGUCV with MC 9 was missing from Shikoku Model Code Master.

investigation_summary: Approvals were not generated for assessment request H000030210. The issue was traced to a field configured in Approval Flow Master that was not functioning as expected. The fix was applied in the Okayama Production environment, and recovery was completed for all impacted records.
important_findings: Assessment request H000030210 completed, but approvals were initially not generated.
A field configured in Approval Flow Master was not functioning as expected.
The issue was fixed in the Okayama Production environment.
Recovery was completed for all impacted records.
Approvals for H000030210 were successfully generated after the fix.
root_cause: A field configured in Approval Flow Master was not functioning as expected, preventing approval generation.
resolution: Fixed the Approval Flow Master field issue in the Okayama Production environment and completed recovery for all impacted records.

investigation_summary: A Shipment was not processed successfully because the workflow execution crashed. Recovery for the affected Shipment was completed. No issue was identified in the shipment processing logic on the Siebel side; hourly monitoring will be added to detect similar cases.
important_findings: The affected Shipment recovery was completed.
A workflow crash caused the Shipment to remain unprocessed.
No issue was found in shipment processing logic at the Siebel side.
Regular hourly monitoring will be implemented to identify and ensure processing of affected Shipments.
root_cause: A crash occurred during execution of the workflow, preventing the Shipment from being processed successfully.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected Shipment, and regular hourly monitoring is being added for similar cases.

investigation_summary: Recovery for N000294048 on FDP-Shikoku PROD was initially completed with an incorrect destination branch, then corrected to Marugame Honko and the extra transaction was reverted. Investigation reproduced the underlying issue for Parts Purchase Return Order #N001300132 on FDP-UAT1. The fix was validated in FDP-UAT1 and released to FDP Production on 26 November 2025.
important_findings: The initial recovery of N000294048 used an incorrect destination branch and created an extra transaction.
Recovery was corrected on FDP-Shikoku PROD using destination location Marugame Honko, and the extra transaction was reverted.
The issue was reproduced for Parts Purchase Return Order #N001300132 on FDP-UAT1.
Return Good Qty and Return Defective Qty became editable after shipment processing through the “Shipped” button.
Post-shipment quantity changes created incorrect actions and transactions for the line item.
The fix was validated in FDP-UAT1 before release to FDP Production.
root_cause: Return Good Qty and Return Defective Qty were editable after a shipment was processed using the “Shipped” button, allowing users to modify quantities after shipment and create incorrect actions and transactions for the line item.
resolution: Return Good Qty and Return Defective Qty were made permanently read-only regardless of shipment status. The fix was deployed to FDP-UAT1, approved after validation, and released to FDP Production on 26 November 2025.

investigation_summary: SV master data was missing after the Wave-3 data migration because the required master file was not received from Biz. BIP report text retrieves values from this master data, causing incorrect or missing display. Master data was updated to match FDP-Okayama in FDP-UAT environments UAT4–UAT8, validated by the customer, and deployed to production in the 30 November FDP emergency release.
important_findings: SV master data was missing following the Wave-3 data migration because the required master file was not received from Biz.
BIP report text is configured to fetch values from master data.
Master data in FDP-UAT UAT4, UAT5, UAT6, UAT7, and UAT8 was updated according to FDP-Okayama/Okayama-PROD values.
The updated UAT4–UAT8 master data was validated as displaying correctly with correct values.
The production fix was deployed in the 30 November FDP emergency release.
root_cause: During the Wave-3 data migration, the required SV master-data file was not received from Biz, leaving SV master data missing.
resolution: Updated master data in FDP-UAT UAT4–UAT8 to match FDP-Okayama/Okayama-PROD, obtained validation, and deployed the fix to production in the 30 November FDP emergency release.
technical_entities: Body Purchase order sheet master data

investigation_summary: When an Account was selected from the pick applet for the "Bill To Basic Account Name" field, Payer Details were not updated correctly. Analysis identified an internal configuration conflict. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and deployed to FDP Prod in the 17th December 2025 release.
important_findings: Selecting an Account from the pick applet in "Bill To Basic Account Name" caused Payer Details to remain incorrect.
The issue was caused by an internal configuration conflict.
The affected record was recovered before the permanent fix was completed.
UAT-1 validation confirmed that Customer Info updated correctly when the Account Name changed.
The fix was deployed to FDP Prod in the 17th December 2025 release.
root_cause: An internal configuration conflict prevented Payer Details from being updated correctly when an Account was selected from the pick applet in the "Bill To Basic Account Name" field.
resolution: Fixed the configuration issue, validated the correction in UAT-1, and deployed the fix to FDP Prod in the 17th December 2025 release.

investigation_summary: A fix was developed in UAT and released to PROD in the 13 November FDP release. Recovery for Parts and Lubrication required corrected JV recovery data, including Data Set Separator (OBCD001), and was moved to MFTBCFFR-4965 for tracking. The comments do not identify a confirmed technical root cause.
important_findings: The initially supplied JV recovery data did not include Data Set Separator (OBCD001).
The recovery data was corrected and later designated as the final data for PROD.
Voucher creation date and posting date are set through CSJS005.
The fix was released to PROD in the 13 November FDP release.
Parts and Lubrication recovery was to be tracked separately under MFTBCFFR-4965 after JV data was provided.
resolution: The fix was released to PROD in the 13 November FDP release. Remaining Parts and Lubrication recovery was transferred to MFTBCFFR-4965 pending JV recovery data.

investigation_summary: An affected record was recovered, and investigation identified that approval flows did not handle cases where the Assessment Price field was null. The approval flow was corrected and deployed to Okayama Prod to support the null-value scenario.
important_findings: The affected record was recovered before the RCA was completed.
Approval flows did not handle records with a null Assessment Price field.
A corrected approval flow was implemented to handle null values in the Assessment Price field.
The corrected flow was deployed to Okayama Prod after business hours.
root_cause: Approval flows lacked handling for null values in the Assessment Price field.
resolution: Implemented and deployed a corrected approval flow in Okayama Prod to handle null Assessment Price values.

investigation_summary: In rare cases, Quote processing failed to calculate the 'Trade In Consumption Tax' after entering a Trade in Amount. Investigation identified a code-efficiency timing issue: the link updating the Quote could complete slower than the line-item tax update script, causing the update to break. The code was optimized with a more efficient link, validated on UAT-1, and released to FDP Production on 26-Nov-25.
important_findings: The issue affected calculation of 'Trade In Consumption Tax' in Quote in rare cases.
Entering a Trade in Amount triggers a tax update in the line item and a linked update in the Quote.
The Quote update failed when the link executed slower than the script; normally, the link completed faster.
The issue was not attributable to user mis-operation or functional mis-operation and could not be replicated.
A more efficient link was implemented to prevent the timing-related failure.
The fix was deployed to FDP Production in the 26-Nov-25 planned release.
root_cause: A code-efficiency timing issue caused the link that updates the Quote to run slower than the line-item tax update script, breaking the update and preventing calculation of 'Trade In Consumption Tax'.
resolution: Optimized the code by replacing the link with a more efficient link; the fix was tested on UAT-1 and released to FDP Production on 26-Nov-25.

investigation_summary: A duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee order/line items were created when the D21A ODI package processed a TOB file whose Model Code did not match the Model Code stored in the Vehicle record. The affected data was recovered in production, including JV recovery and cancellation of duplicate Chassis Order B050481404. The evidence did not conclusively establish that a user changed the Model Code through the Administration Vehicle screen. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version and proposed for FDP after approval.
important_findings: Chassis Order B050208984 and its Vehicle record were initially created with Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830; the Vehicle record later contained FBA20B21W00F-4-G830.
A TOB D21A file received on 7 November 2025 contained Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830.

Because the D21A ODI package did not match the incoming Model Code to the Vehicle record, it treated the data as new and created duplicate Chassis Order B050481404, a new Vehicle, and duplicate recycle fee order and line items.
JV recovery was completed and the duplicate order was cancelled in the production environment; recycle fee attributes became visible after recovery.
The claimed user mis-operation through the Administration Vehicle screen was disputed and was not proven by the recorded last-updated user or replication results.

The SC-version fix matches the TOB Model Code against the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record and updates the Vehicle Model Code from TOB; equivalent FDP implementation was pending approval.
root_cause: A Model Code mismatch between the incoming TOB D21A file/original Chassis Order Line Item (FBA20B21W00F-5-G830) and the Vehicle record (FBA20B21W00F-4-G830) caused the D21A ODI package to identify the data as new and create duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee records.
resolution: Completed JV recovery and cancelled duplicate Chassis Order B050481404 in production. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871; FDP implementation was proposed pending approval.

investigation_summary: Bulk Invoice records for multiple shipments were missing from month-end closing files sent to KB, requiring recovery data to be manually created and transmitted. Investigation found that the post-extraction SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag by order number instead of shipment, causing all shipments under an order to be marked as sent when only one shipment was processed. The SQL was corrected in all production environments, impacted records were recovered, and subsequent December month-end Bulk Data verification found no issues.
important_findings: The issue affected Bulk Invoice data for shipments in FDPs including Okayama, Iwate, and Shikoku that were not included in closing data sent to KB.
After data extraction, an update SQL set the sent-to-KB flag based on the order number rather than the shipment.
When one shipment under an order was selected for KB processing, the SQL updated the flag for all shipments of that order.
Missing November 30 records had X_IF_STATUS set to Y before the SQL fix, causing them to be excluded from Bulk Invoice processing.
Recovery Bulk Invoice data was created and manually sent to KB for identified impacted records.
December month-end Bulk Data was verified and no further issue was found.
root_cause: The post-extraction update SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag, X_IF_STATUS, using the order number instead of the shipment, incorrectly marking all shipments for an order as sent to KB.
resolution: The SQL was corrected in all production environments to update flags by shipment, recovery Bulk Invoice data was generated and sent to KB for impacted records, and month-end Bulk Invoice executions were monitored through December.

investigation_summary: Slowness was observed in FDP Production environments. AWR monitoring later showed no ongoing slowness after database statistics gathering over the weekend refined SQL execution. No further action was required and the incident was closed.
important_findings: AWR reports showed no further slowness in FDP Production environments.
Database statistics gathering performed over the weekend refined SQL.
No additional corrective action was required after performance stabilized.
resolution: Performed database statistics gathering over the weekend, which refined SQL and eliminated the observed slowness.

investigation_summary: The incident affected Recycle Fee Order processing and required the Recycle Fee Order status to be manually updated to 'Completed' for recovery. A fix was implemented and validated in the FDP UAT-1 environment for the Send Recycle Fee, Change Order, and Cancel Order functions, including changes associated with MFTBCFFR-4456. The fix was subsequently released to Prod.
important_findings: Recovery was performed by updating the Recycle Fee Order status to 'Completed'.
The fix was implemented in the FDP UAT-1 environment and validated using Chassis Order# B001296607 and Recycle Fee Order# B001296610.
Send Recycle Fee, Change Order, and Cancel Order functionality was confirmed to work as expected.
Change Order and Cancel Order validation was performed in accordance with changes from Jira MFTBCFFR-4456.
The changes were released to Prod on the planned FDP release.
resolution: Implemented and validated a fix in FDP UAT-1 for Send Recycle Fee, Change Order, and Cancel Order functionality, then released the changes to Prod.

investigation_summary: Report Print was verified as successful for PTMWTransferDeliveryNote BIPs on the Reports server. The issue was resolved by restarting the printer, and Canon logs showed no irregularities. The investigation concluded that the issue was network-related rather than a Siebel issue.
important_findings: Report Print was successful for PTMWTransferDeliveryNote BIPs on the Reports server.
Restarting the printer resolved the issue.
Canon logs did not show any irregularities.
The issue appeared to be network-related rather than Siebel-related.
root_cause: A network-related printer issue.
resolution: Restarted the printer.

investigation_summary: Duplicate JVs were created for insurance order processing associated with request# I050063671. Investigation found that a user could change the status back to Spreadsheet Approved, causing another JV to be created; the affected JV predated the fix delivered in MFTBCFFR-4382. Reverse JVs were recreated after an incorrect initial recovery amount, approved, and loaded to production for nightly processing.
important_findings: Request# I050063671 created three insurance orders.
Only insurance order Q050076191 had Clerical Error flag set to "N", and a JV was created only for this order.
The duplicate JV resulted from the user being able to set the status to Spreadsheet Approved again.
The affected JV was created before the release of MFTBCFFR-4382.
The MFTBCFFR-4382 fix was tested successfully in UAT.
Recovery required reverse JVs; the initial recovery amount was reported as incorrect and corrected recovery data was loaded to production.
root_cause: A user could change an insurance order status to Spreadsheet Approved again, which triggered creation of a duplicate JV. The affected JV was created before this behavior was fixed by MFTBCFFR-4382.
resolution: Created corrected reverse JVs for the duplicate JV recovery and loaded the approved recovery data to production for nightly processing. The recurrence was prevented by the fix delivered in MFTBCFFR-4382 and validated in UAT.

investigation_summary: Duplicate records recurred in PBI after recovery. Investigation identified that syncing a quote to sales order caused the issue to reoccur for records impacted by MFTBCFFR-4750. The affected duplicate IDs were permanently de-synced, and PBI reports showed no remaining duplicates.
important_findings: Recovery restored correct values in PBI, but duplicate records recurred.
The issue recurred each time a user synced the quote to sales order.
The affected records were related to MFTBCFFR-4750.
No duplicate records remained on PBI reports after the corrective activity.
Permanent de-syncing of duplicate IDs was completed for all affected records.
root_cause: Syncing a quote to sales order caused duplicate IDs/records to recur for records impacted by MFTBCFFR-4750.
resolution: Permanently de-synced the duplicate IDs for all affected records and monitored PBI reports to confirm that no duplicates remained.

investigation_summary: A screen in JPN UAT8 failed because it is backed by a database view and JPN applications use SSO database logins. The SSO users lacked permission to access the view, causing an SQL error. Access was granted to the SSO users, and the screen became visible in JPN UAT8.
important_findings: The affected screen is based on a database view rather than a table.
ENU applications access the database directly, while JPN applications use SSO logins.
SSO users did not have access to the database view, resulting in an SQL error.
The issue was isolated to JPN UAT8 and did not occur in other UAT or Prod environments.
Granting the database-view access to SSO users restored screen visibility in JPN UAT8.
root_cause: SSO users used by JPN applications lacked permission to access the database view backing the affected screen.
resolution: Granted the database-view access to SSO users, making the screen visible in JPN UAT8 applications.

investigation_summary: UV Purchase Quotes could not be transitioned from "Rejected" to "Cancelled" when the Cancel button was clicked. The issue was reproduced for UV Purchase Quote# 1-569PKE in the FDP UAT1 environment, fixed and validated in UAT-1, then released to Prod after approval. Recovery was completed for UV Purchase Quote# 1-5TC05G by setting its status to "Cancelled".
important_findings: The status transition from "Rejected" to "Cancelled" failed for UV Purchase Quotes when using the Cancel button.
The issue was reproducible in the FDP UAT1 environment for UV Purchase Quote# 1-569PKE.
Recovery was completed for UV Purchase Quote# 1-5TC05G by changing its status to "Cancelled".
The fix enabled the "Rejected" to "Cancelled" transition in UAT-1 without error.
The approved fix was released to Prod.
root_cause: A system issue prevented UV Purchase Quote status from transitioning from "Rejected" to "Cancelled" when the Cancel button was clicked.
resolution: Implemented and validated a fix in UAT-1 to allow cancellation of UV Purchase Quotes in "Rejected" status, then deployed the fix to Prod after approval. The affected UV Purchase Quote# 1-5TC05G was recovered by setting its status to "Cancelled".

investigation_summary: Duplicate Insurance Orders were created when a Policy Number was manually entered in Siebel rather than returned through the Ejibai interface. Testing on UAT4 reproduced the behavior: manual entry left the backend User Key null, so a subsequent Ejibai policy response could not match the original record and created a duplicate. The issue was determined to be user mis-operation rather than a system defect; users should not manually update the policy number.
important_findings: Insurance Orders are created in Siebel and Policy Numbers are generated through the Ejibai interface.
When the Ejibai response populates the Policy Number, the backend User Key is updated automatically.
Manually updating the Liability Insurance Policy # leaves the User Key null.
A later Policy Number response from Ejibai cannot locate the original record without the User Key and creates a duplicate Insurance Order.
The issue was replicated on UAT4 using Insurance Order Q000037255 and duplicate Q000037256.
root_cause: The Liability Insurance Policy # was manually updated instead of being populated through the Ejibai interface, leaving the backend User Key null and preventing subsequent Ejibai responses from matching the original Insurance Order.
resolution: Instruct users to avoid manual updates to the Liability Insurance Policy # and allow the Ejibai interface response to populate the Policy Number and User Key.

investigation_summary: The okoyama load plan failed on the night of 1 Nov 2025, preventing 1 Nov 2025 data from being populated in PBI. Recovery was completed by updating db last upd for records created or updated on 1 Nov 2025, and data was confirmed to be correct afterward. Weekend and holiday monitoring of load plans was added as a preventive measure.
important_findings: The okoyama load plan failed on Saturday night, 1 Nov 2025.
PBI did not contain data for 1 Nov 2025 as a result of the load-plan failure.
Recovery updated db last upd for all records created and updated on 1 Nov 2025.
Data was confirmed to be correct after the recovery action.
Night resources will monitor load plans on Saturdays, Sundays, holidays, and weekends to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: The okoyama load plan failed on the night of 1 Nov 2025.
resolution: Updated db last upd for all records created and updated on 1 Nov 2025, restoring the missing PBI data; added weekend and holiday load-plan monitoring.

investigation_summary: Users experienced slowness that prevented quote creation. Backend checks and hourly AWR report monitoring did not identify a long-running SQL query; SQL tuning was performed after business hours, after which no slowness was observed and users confirmed improvement.
important_findings: No SQL causing the reported slowness was detected in backend checks or hourly AWR reports.
Navigation testing in Shikoku Production did not reproduce the slowness.
Shikoku Production SQL queries were compared with Chugoku Prod SQL queries during the investigation.
SQL tuning was performed after business hours as a precautionary measure.
DB statistics were gathered on Shikoku Prod, and subsequent Production checks showed normal performance.
Users confirmed that performance had improved.
resolution: Performed precautionary SQL tuning after business hours and gathered DB statistics on Shikoku Prod; subsequent monitoring and user confirmation indicated that the slowness was resolved.

investigation_summary: Investigation confirmed there was no issue with the gateways. Some members were not reachable or were offline, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Gateways were not affected.
Some members were not reachable or not online.
The requester asked to close the incident.
root_cause: Some members were not reachable or were offline.
resolution: Incident closed.

investigation_summary: The Sales Order report was not visible because its query used the Delivery approval date rather than the Sales posting completed date. Updating the Delivery Completion Approved Date to the Sales Posting Completion Date made the report visible. A fix was implemented, validated on UAT-1, approved for Prod, and released.
important_findings: The Sales Order query filters based on Delivery approval date, not Sales posting completed date.
The Delivery Completion Approved Date was updated to the Sales Posting Completion Date, after which the Sales Order report became visible.
The implemented fix updates the Delivery Completion Approved Date to the current timestamp when status changes to Sales Posting Done.
The change was deployed to UAT-1 for testing and subsequently released to Prod.
root_cause: The Delivery Completion Approved Date was not being updated when the Sales Order status changed to Sales Posting Done, while the report query relied on the Delivery approval date.
resolution: Updated the workflow so that the Delivery Completion Approved Date is set to the current timestamp when the status changes to Sales Posting Done; the change was released to Prod.

investigation_summary: An error occurred when Liability Insurance Information entered by the user did not match a Liability Insurance record in the master. The existing behavior could not resolve the insurance name and displayed an error instead of handling the unmatched master data as a zero-cost item. The fix was implemented in UAT-1 and released to Prod to create a zero-price Liability Insurance Quote Line Item when no matching master record exists.
important_findings: The entered liability insurance information was not maintained in the master for the applicable combination of MD Classification 'M', Insurance Vehicle Type 'Omnibus', and Mainland Category 'Mainland'.
Liability Insurance Term values 1 through 13 were identified as available for the applicable master-data combination.
The initial error message occurred because the system could not find the insurance name, rather than because no insurance information had been entered.
The required behavior was to retain the expense name and display a zero amount when master data does not match, consistent with Taxes and other expenses behavior.
The implemented fix creates a Liability Insurance record in the Quote Line Item with zero price when Liability Insurance is not maintained in the master.
The change was completed on UAT-1 and subsequently released to Prod.
root_cause: No Liability Insurance master record matched the user-entered Liability Insurance Information, and the existing logic treated the unresolved insurance name as an error instead of creating a zero-price item.
resolution: Modified the logic to create a dummy Liability Insurance in the Quote Line Item with zero price when no matching Liability Insurance master record is found; the change was tested on UAT-1 and released to Prod.

investigation_summary: The Order Detail BIP report failed to generate for Trailer and Forklift sales orders. Investigation found that a missing Planned Delivery Date in the Sales Quote resulted in a null Tax rate being passed to the Sales Order. A fix was deployed to UAT1, approved for production, and released to Prod.
important_findings: The affected function was generation of the Order Detail BIP report.
Tax rate is calculated in the Sales Quote based on the Planned Delivery Date and is passed to the Sales Order.
Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes did not validate Planned Delivery Date before approval.
When Planned Delivery Date was empty, Tax rate remained null in both the Sales Quote and Sales Order.
The null Tax rate caused the BIP report generation failure.
The affected sales order was recovered, allowing BIP to be printed.
root_cause: Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes lacked Planned Delivery Date validation, allowing approval with an empty date. This prevented Tax rate calculation and passed a null Tax rate to the Sales Order, causing the Order Detail BIP report to fail.
resolution: A fix addressing the issue was deployed to UAT1 and then released to Prod after approval; the affected sales order was recovered so BIP could be printed.

investigation_summary: A slowness issue occurred in Shikoku Production. Investigation determined that a SQL operation was taking an unusually long time. The issue was fixed and post-fix monitoring showed no recurrence.
important_findings: The incident affected Shikoku Production.
Slowness was caused by SQL taking a long time.
The behavior was identified as a rare issue.
Post-fix production monitoring showed no recurrence.
root_cause: A SQL operation was taking a long time, causing system slowness.
resolution: The slowness issue was fixed in Shikoku Production and monitored after deployment with no recurrence observed.

investigation_summary: NV Quote and NV Sales Order contained different model codes because users could directly edit fields in the Chassis & Options tab of NV Sales Order line items. Affected records were recovered, and the editability issue was corrected and validated in FDP-UAT1 before release to PROD. The fix was released to PROD on 13 November.
important_findings: The Chassis & Options tab in NV Sales Order line items was editable for some responsibility categories.
Users changed the model code directly in NV Sales Order instead of changing it in NV Quote and synchronizing the Quote to the Sales Order.
The correct business process is to update the model code in NV Quote and then sync the Quote to NV Sales Order.
The before-fix condition was available in FDP-RT2, where SO# A000055765 had editable Chassis & Options line-item fields.
In FDP-UAT1, fields in NV Sales Order were made read-only, including Product Name, Line#, and C#.
Recovery was completed for the shared affected records; no additional affected records were found in other FDP environments.
root_cause: The Chassis & Options tab of NV Sales Order line items was editable for some responsibility categories, allowing users to directly modify model codes in NV Sales Order and create mismatches with NV Quote.
resolution: Made NV Sales Order Chassis & Options fields read-only, including Product Name, Line#, and C#, validated the change in FDP-UAT1, and released the fix to PROD on 13 November.

investigation_summary: System slowness was observed in the Shikoku production environment. The DBA team identified blocking sessions in production as the cause of the delays. The blocking session was deleted, and monitoring through month end found no recurrence; the incident was closed.
important_findings: The issue was reported for Shikoku, with no additional inquiries reported from other FDPs.
DBA identified blocking sessions in the production environment causing system delays.
Deleting the blocking session restored normal system operation.
Regular monitoring through month end found no further slowness in Shikoku production.
root_cause: Blocking sessions in the production environment caused system slowness.
resolution: The DBA team deleted the blocking session and monitored Shikoku production through month end with no recurrence.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Payment Information was identified in the Registration Location master following execution of SR MFTBCFFR-4690. Investigation determined that the operator created additional Payment Information for UV Type instead of updating Payment Recipient details. The affected Registration Location records were recovered and corrected, and a manual validation step was added for future SR executions.
important_findings: During SR MFTBCFFR-4690 execution, additional Payment Information for UV Type was created instead of updating Payment Recipient details.
The incorrect manual update caused duplicate values in the Payment Information master.
Recovery was completed for all affected Registration Location records.
The Registration Location master now contains correct Payment Information details with no duplicate Payment Information values.
The SR execution master manual was updated to verify Payment Information updates and check for duplicates after SR completion.
root_cause: Manual SR MFTBCFFR-4690 execution error: the operator created new Payment Information rather than updating the existing Payment Recipient details, causing duplicate Payment Information.
resolution: Recovered and corrected all affected Registration Location master records, removed duplicate Payment Information values, and updated the SR execution master manual to validate Payment Information updates and post-execution duplicates.

investigation_summary: The 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field in WO was defaulting to 'N' for dummy lubrication parts in UAT-1. Investigation confirmed that the executed Lubrication Master file for MFTBCFFR - 4830 contained Generic Flag = 'N', which directly drove the field's pre-default value. The Generic Flag was reset to 'Y' for the dummy parts, and the issue was confirmed as incorrect master data rather than a system defect.
important_findings: The 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field is pre-defaulted from the Generic Flag in Lubrication Master data.
The default logic was the same in UAT and prod; the discrepancy between UAT-1 and UAT-8 was caused by master data values.
The Lubrication Master file executed for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama under MFTBCFFR - 4830 contained Generic Flag = 'N'.
For dummy lubrication parts ..888888 and ..999999, the Generic Flag must always be 'Y' to default the Carry-in Flag correctly.
Price-only updates must use Lubricant Price Master; Lubrication Master additions or information changes must use SVC_LUBR_00_209 with only changed records.
root_cause: Incorrect master data: the Lubrication Master file executed for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama contained Generic Flag = 'N' for dummy lubrication parts, causing 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' to default to 'N'.
resolution: Recovery was completed by resetting the Generic Flag to 'Y' for the dummy lubrication parts. The SOP will be updated to validate the Generic Flag for dummy parts whenever a Lubrication Master file is received.

investigation_summary: Retrofit order B050024442 could not progress from Ordered to Completed because Actual Completion Date 01 was not registered in the TOB Logistics Info tab. Investigation confirmed that TOB did not send the Actual Completion Date via the D21Z file. The order status was manually recovered to Completed, and no further action was required for this Jira.
important_findings: Actual Completion Date 01 is a mandatory condition for updating the order status.
The Actual Completion Date registered through D21Z files is displayed as Actual Completion Date 01 in the TOB Logistics Info tab.
Order B050024442 did not have an Actual Completion Date registered.
TOB confirmed that the Actual Completion Date was not sent for order B050024442.
The status was recovered by changing the order from Ordered to Completed.
root_cause: TOB did not send the Actual Completion Date for retrofit order B050024442 through the D21Z file, leaving Actual Completion Date 01 unregistered and preventing the status update.
resolution: Manually changed order B050024442 status from Ordered to Completed; the ticket was closed after TOB confirmed the missing Actual Completion Date transmission.

investigation_summary: The issue was fixed and validated on FDP-UAT1/UAT-1. The specifications were changed to match the SC version, then the change was approved for deployment to FDP-PROD and released to Prod. The comments do not state the underlying root cause.
important_findings: The issue was fixed on FDP-UAT1 and validated in UAT-1.
Specifications were changed to be the same as the SC version.
The validated change was approved for deployment to all FDP-PROD.
The incident was released to Prod.
resolution: Changed the specifications to match the SC version, validated the change on FDP-UAT1/UAT-1, and deployed the release to FDP-PROD/Prod.

investigation_summary: The issue was fixed in FDP-UAT1 but could not be reproduced in the UAT environment, consistent with the SC version. The fix was subsequently deployed and released to PROD.
important_findings: The issue was fixed in FDP-UAT1.
The issue could not be reproduced in the UAT environment.
The UAT behavior was reported to match the SC version.
The incident was released to PROD.
resolution: The fix was deployed and released to PROD after validation in FDP-UAT1/UAT.

investigation_summary: A garbage character had been manually entered into an editable Description field for the affected Product. The Description field was corrected, and the correct value was confirmed to be reflected in the master. The incident was resolved and closed.
important_findings: The issue was caused by a garbage character entered through manual update of the editable Description field.
The affected business object was a Product.
After correcting the Description field, the correct value was reflected in the master.
The scenario was identified as rare.
root_cause: A garbage character was manually updated in the editable Description field of the affected Product.
resolution: The Description field of the affected Product was updated with the correct value, which was reflected in the master.

investigation_summary: The Sales Order Owner field was changing based on Ship To Account, Bill To Account, or Payer Account updates made during Sales Quote revision. Analysis confirmed that Sales Order Owner was expected to retain the Sales Quote Customer Name value. The Owner-field mapping was corrected in UAT-1, approved for production, and released to Prod on 13 November.
important_findings: On Sales Quote revision, changes to Ship To Account, Bill To Account, and Payer Account caused the Sales Order Owner value to change.
Sales Order Owner is expected to match the Customer Name field on the Sales Quote.
The issue was reproduced on UAT1 using Assessment# H000050988, Sales Quote# 1-6Q119Q, and Sales Order# E001299696.
The mapping for the Sales Order Owner field was updated to use Sales Quote Customer Name.
The fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to Prod.
root_cause: The Sales Order Owner field mapping was influenced by Ship To Account, Bill To Account, and Payer Account values during Sales Quote revision instead of being mapped to the Sales Quote Customer Name field.
resolution: Updated the Sales Order Owner mapping to match the Sales Quote Customer Name field, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to Prod.

investigation_summary: In UAT-1, modifying or cancelling a PO changed the associated external-mechanic WO to "Not Work", but subsequent WO update and creation of a Customer Approved quote did not transition the WO status as expected. The issue was reproduced using JC I001299776 and fixed in UAT-1. Validation confirmed PO statuses changed correctly to "Modify" and "Cancel", and the fix was released to Prod.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced in UAT-1 for JC I001299776 with external-mechanic WO 1-6QIIYZ.
After PO J001299779 was modified, the associated WO status changed to "Not Work".
Following a WO update and creation of Customer Approved quote 1-6QIJ2K, WO 1-6QIIYZ remained "Not Work" instead of changing status in the next step.
The same behavior occurred for both PO modification and PO cancellation scenarios.
The fix was deployed to UAT-1 and validated before release to Prod.
resolution: Fixed in UAT-1, validated for PO "Modify" and "Cancel" status handling, and released to Prod on the FDP release scheduled for 13 November 2025.

investigation_summary: Incorrect sales prices were identified on JC line items with Line Item Type "51: Claim" and Item Status "Lubrication Shipped", where the required sales price was 0. Recovery of the affected records was completed, and new sales price logic was added to workflows 1-01, 1-10A, 1-12A, and 1-15A. The change was validated in UAT and released successfully to PROD on 13 December 2025.
important_findings: Affected JC line items were "51: Claim" with Item Status "Lubrication Shipped" and Customer Pay Amount 0, while List Price values were populated.
The required sales price for the identified problematic line items was 0.
Affected JCs were identified across Okayama, Wakayama, Hakodate, and Shikoku.
Recovery of the affected records was completed before the production deployment.
New sales price logic was implemented in workflows 1-01, 1-10A, 1-12A, and 1-15A, validated in UAT, and approved for PROD deployment.
root_cause: The sales price logic required an update to ensure sales price was set to 0 for the affected "51: Claim" and "Lubrication Shipped" line items.
resolution: Recovered the affected JC records and deployed new sales price logic in workflows 1-01, 1-10A, 1-12A, and 1-15A to PROD on 13 December 2025 after UAT validation.

investigation_summary: The Map button was inactive for lot Sales Order A000181823 with Requested Quantity 2. Investigation confirmed that its Purchase Orders were mapped to child sales orders A000181829 and A000181830, both in "Sales Posting Completed" status, rather than to the parent sales order. This was determined to be expected behavior, not a system issue.
important_findings: Lot Sales Order A000181823 has Requested Quantity 2.
The lot Sales Order has child sales orders A000181829 and A000181830.
Both child sales orders were in "Sales Posting Completed" status.
Purchase Orders are mapped at the child sales order level rather than the parent sales order for this lot Sales Order.
The Map button is inactive because Purchase Orders are mapped to the child sales orders.
root_cause: For the lot Sales Order, Purchase Orders were mapped to child sales orders A000181829 and A000181830 rather than parent sales order A000181823, causing the Map button to be inactive.
resolution: No corrective action was required; the inactive Map button was expected behavior for this lot Sales Order configuration.

investigation_summary: Power BI export failed for JPN when two columns had identical Japanese translations, producing duplicate alias names in the export query. English exports succeeded because Power BI automatically appended suffixes such as _1 and _2. A fix to make the Japanese field titles unique was deployed to UAT and then released to production.
important_findings: Two columns with the same Japanese translation generated the same alias name in the Power BI export query.
Duplicate column names made the export query invalid and caused the error: “File creation failure – An error occurred while executing the query for the data export operation.”
English Power BI exports handled duplicate aliases by appending suffixes such as _1 and _2.
For JPN, adding _2 to one duplicated field title prevented title duplication.
The fix was deployed to UAT and subsequently released to production.
root_cause: Duplicate Japanese translations caused two exported columns to receive the same alias name, resulting in an invalid Power BI export query with duplicate column names.
resolution: Updated one of the duplicate Japanese field titles by adding _2, then deployed the fix to UAT and production.
technical_entities: File creation failure – An error occurred while executing the query for the data export operation.

investigation_summary: The incident was acknowledged for investigation. It was subsequently closed and tracking was moved to MFTBCFFR:4849; no technical findings, root cause, or corrective action were documented in the comments.
important_findings: The incident was closed and tracking was transferred to MFTBCFFR:4849.

investigation_summary: The issue affected population of the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field for Job Cards created from UV Inventory. Investigation found that the program logic did not correctly update the field during UV Inventory JC creation and, after initial remediation, did not update it when "Update JC" was clicked for a Request for Reservation-only scenario. The logic was updated, validated in UAT-1 for both Quote Request and Reservation Request scenarios, and released to PROD.
important_findings: For a JC created from UV Inventory with Department set to "UV", "Internal Order (Charge To)" should be populated with "UV".
The current program did not properly update "Internal Order (Charge To)" when a Job Card was created from the UV Inventory side.
After the initial UAT fix, the field still did not update when "Update JC" was clicked in an Only Request for Reservation scenario.
The logic was updated to populate "Internal Order (Charge To)" on button click.
UAT-1 validation confirmed that "Internal Order (Charge To)" had a value for both Quote Request and Reservation Request scenarios.
The fix was released to PROD.
root_cause: The program logic did not update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field for UV Inventory Job Cards, including when "Update JC" was clicked for an Only Request for Reservation scenario.
resolution: Updated the "Internal Order (Charge To)" logic for UV Inventory Job Cards and for the "Update JC" button flow; validated in UAT-1 and deployed to PROD.

investigation_summary: In UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW", using Change Records to update Manual Discount% after selecting all quote line items with Ctrl+A changed the editable field initially clicked by the user. The behavior was reproduced in Service Quotes and parts quote and was identified as a Siebel Vanilla functionality defect rather than a business-process configuration issue. Users were instructed to initiate the operation from a read-only field or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.
important_findings: The issue occurred when a user clicked an editable field, selected all lines with Ctrl+A, and used Change Records to update Manual Discount%.
After confirming Change Records, the editable field initially selected in step 1 was changed.
The behavior was reproduced on Service Quotes and parts quote, including UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW".
The current business process configuration was confirmed to be correct.
Change Records is a Siebel Vanilla functionality, and the behavior was identified as a Siebel bug.
As a workaround, users should click a read-only field before using Ctrl+A and Change Records, or manually select records if the cursor is in an editable field.
root_cause: A Siebel bug in the vanilla Change Records functionality causes the initially selected editable field to be changed when all records are selected with Ctrl+A and a bulk update is performed.
resolution: Communicate the operational workaround to Hakodate branch users: start the Change Records operation from a read-only field, or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.

investigation_summary: A BIP was updated on FDP_UAT1 according to conditions provided in an Excel sheet. Testing was confirmed successful, and the change was released to Production in the 23 October scheduled FDP release.
important_findings: The BIP was updated on FDP_UAT1 based on the conditions in the provided Excel sheet.
A sample BIP was provided for validation.
Testing was confirmed as OK before production release.
The change was deployed to Production during the 23 October scheduled FDP release.
resolution: Updated the BIP according to the provided Excel-sheet conditions, validated it in FDP_UAT1, and released it to Production.

investigation_summary: Performance delays were reported for PO line-item operations and when returning from WO or VM to JC. The issue was no longer observed on October 16, and an SQL restriction was approved for the October 23 release. The restriction was deployed to Production in the scheduled FDP release.
important_findings: Delays were reported for PO operations: Add Parts Line Item, Add Labor Line Item, and Cancel Line Item.
Delays were also reported when returning from WO to JC and from VM to JC.
No delays were observed on October 16; the system was reported as back to normal.
An SQL restriction was approved and deployed to Production on October 23 through the scheduled FDP release.
resolution: An SQL restriction was deployed to Production in the October 23 scheduled FDP release.

investigation_summary: Duplicate JVs were created for D2S Invoice records with a blank PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) because the processing flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation. The flag-update logic was corrected and tested in UAT8 so PO-blank records are processed only once. The fix was deployed to Production in the 23rd October FDP release, and recovery data was completed for the affected duplicate JV records.
important_findings: JV creation is triggered when the D2S Invoice flag is not "S".
The existing flag-update logic required PO Num, Invoice Num, and Inv Dt to be non-null.
PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) being blank is normal for D2S invoices received by Siebel.
For PO-blank records, the flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation, allowing duplicate JVs to be created.
The issue affected three records on Chugoku.
Recovery was required for duplicate JV types D2S Inv Amt, D2S Inv CommFee, and D2S Inv CT.
root_cause: The flag-update filter required PO Num to be non-null. When PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) was blank, the D2S Invoice record was not updated to flag "S" after JV creation and was eligible for duplicate JV creation.
resolution: Updated the flag-update logic so records with blank PO Num are updated to "S" after processing, tested the change in UAT8, and deployed it to Production in the 23rd October FDP release. Created and completed Production recovery data for the duplicate JVs.

investigation_summary: The issue occurred when an Assessment Request was created for a selected Chassis with a blank Full Model Code field. The existing Assessment Request needed to be cancelled and recreated. A validation check was implemented in FDP-UAT1 and released to PROD in the 23 October scheduled FDP release to prevent processing when Full Model Code is blank.
important_findings: The selected Chassis had a blank Full Model Code value, which caused the issue.
Affected users were instructed to cancel the existing Assessment Request and create a new one.
A validation check for blank Full Model Code values on selected chassis was implemented in FDP-UAT1.
Test Assessment Request AR#: H000050796 was created in FDP-UAT1.
The approved change was released to PROD on 23 October as part of the scheduled FDP release.
root_cause: The Full Model Code field was blank for the selected Chassis.
resolution: Implemented and released a validation check that displays a validation message when the Full Model Code is blank for a selected Chassis.

investigation_summary: Affected orders required recovery in PBI Datamart because necessary updates were not made on the Siebel side. Recovery was performed manually, including A026311561 and subsequently A036540392 after it was identified as omitted. A PBI-side logic issue affecting some records was fixed in UAT, approved for PROD, and released to PROD on 8 November 2025.
important_findings: Manual removal of line items in Power BI was required during recovery.
A026311561 was recovered initially; 10 remaining records were later identified for recovery.
A036540392 was identified as omitted from the original recovery target and was subsequently recovered.
Necessary updates were not made on the Siebel side for the affected records.
Some records required a PBI fix due to a PBI-side logic issue.
The PBI logic fix was validated in UAT and deployed to PROD on 8 November 2025.
root_cause: Necessary updates were not made on the Siebel side; a subset of affected records also had a PBI-side logic issue requiring a PBI fix.
resolution: Performed manual recovery in PBI Datamart for the affected records and deployed the approved PBI logic fix to PROD on 8 November 2025.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned a user being unable to print. Support added the user to the Printer file, after which the business confirmed the user could print. The ticket was closed following confirmation.
important_findings: The affected user was unable to print.
The user was added to the Printer file.
Business confirmed that the user could print after the update.
root_cause: The user was not present in the Printer file.
resolution: Added the user to the Printer file.

investigation_summary: A Sales Order did not synchronize to the latest of 9 approved Quote revisions and remained at revision 7. Error logs showed a concurrent-update conflict during the Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization, and the scenario was reproduced in UAT by modifying the same Sales Order line item while synchronization was running. The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod; no system change was implemented, and the proposed prevention was to avoid concurrent updates to the same record.
important_findings: The Sales Order remained at revision 7 after 9 Quote revisions had been created and approved.
The failure occurred in step 'Sync Sales Order' using service 'EAI Siebel Adapter' and method 'Synchronize' with error SBL-BPR-00162.
Business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' failed in 'WriteRecord' with SBL-DAT-00523 and SBL-EAI-04451, indicating the record had been modified after retrieval.

The issue was reproduced in UAT when another user modified a Sales Order line item while Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization was running; the synchronization update succeeded and the manual update received the error.
The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod.
Regression testing in FDP did not reproduce the issue; SC UAT and FDP were identified as different applications.
root_cause: A concurrent update to the same Sales Order line-item record during Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization caused a Siebel record-update conflict, preventing the Sales Order from synchronizing to the latest Quote revision.
resolution: The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod. The proposed preventive measure was to instruct users not to update the same record simultaneously from different sessions or screens.
technical_entities: MF RF Order Entry - Line Items

investigation_summary: Journal Voucher ordering was investigated for records that were grouped in an unexpected sequence. When Timestamp and Global Order Number are identical, sorting falls back to Data Set Separator, which can produce this scenario. Configuration was confirmed identical across all FDPs, and the behavior was reproduced in UAT1 and UAT2; no recovery was required, and the scenario will be monitored through daily AMS monitoring.
important_findings: Journal Voucher sorting order is Timestamp > Global Order Number > Data Set Separator.
When Timestamp and Global Order Number are the same, grouping is determined by Data Set Separator.
The issue was initially observed for a small number of records in Okayama, but no Okayama-specific configuration discrepancy was found.
The scenario was reproduced in UAT1 and UAT2 and is possible for all FDPs.
Implementing a logic fix would require significant changes to the existing logic.
Recovery was not required for the affected orders; similar occurrences will be monitored and recovered if needed.
root_cause: A Journal Voucher sorting tie occurs when both Timestamp and Global Order Number are identical; sorting then uses Data Set Separator, resulting in the observed grouping sequence.
resolution: No recovery was performed because it was not required. The Jira was closed, and the scenario was added to daily AMS monitoring for detection and recovery of future occurrences.

investigation_summary: Location number values were correct in PBI Datamart but were not synchronized in the PBI 5-02 report through its normal refresh. A manual full refresh in PBI Desktop populated the correct values, confirming this was not an ODI load plan issue. Full refreshes were completed for the 5-02 report across all FDPs.
important_findings: Location numbers are subject to change and should be updated daily.
The correct location number values were present in PBI Datamart.
The issue was isolated to PBI Report refresh behavior and was not an ODI load plan issue.
A full refresh in PBI Desktop synchronized the location number values correctly.
A full refresh of the 5-02 report was completed on all FDPs.
root_cause: The normal PBI 5-02 report refresh did not synchronize updated location number values despite the correct data being available in PBI Datamart.
resolution: Performed a full refresh of the 5-02 report on all FDPs.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed on Shikoku-PROD. The issue was identified as being on the D2S side rather than in the Siebel system, and the incident was proposed for rejection.
important_findings: Recovery was completed on Shikoku-PROD.
Hirata san and the D2S team were notified.
The issue was determined to be on the D2S side.
