The issue was not a Siebel system issue.
root_cause: Issue on the D2S side.
resolution: Recovery completed on Shikoku-PROD; D2S team was notified and the incident was proposed for rejection.

investigation_summary: Status Code values differed between SC and FDP because each environment sourced the value from a different table and represented a different status type. Changes were implemented and validated in FDP UAT, with the final Status Code LOV filter update deployed to production for Report #1-15A across all FDPs. Validation in PBI-PROD confirmed the change was correct and the incident was resolved.
important_findings: In FDP, Status Code is sourced from WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F and represents Order Status.
In SC, Status Code is sourced from W_SRVREQ_MD and represents Service Request Status.
The differing source tables caused different Status Code filter values between SC and FDP.
The Order Code LOV displayed correctly in FORCE FDP (UAT), but the line item Order Code (JC Status) was initially not displayed.
The requested LOV change for Report #1-05 was withdrawn because it was technically difficult.
The Status Code LOV for Report #1-15A was changed correctly for all FDPs in PBI-PROD.
root_cause: SC and FDP used different source tables for Status Code: WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F in FDP for Order Status and W_SRVREQ_MD in SC for Service Request Status.
resolution: Deployed the Status Code LOV filter change for Report #1-15A to production for all FDPs; the change was validated successfully in PBI-PROD.

investigation_summary: Invoice data for Parts Purchase Order line items was not inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch when the D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file. The insertion logic was corrected on FDP-UAT1, including a filter-condition update for null X_ATTRIB_02 values, and was released to Production on 23rd October. Historical mismatch records were recovered across affected FDPs and their creation dates were aligned to the invoice-received date.
important_findings: D2S Invoice Mismatch excluded invoice data when D2S SO Item Number and Product values in a PO line item did not match the D2S invoice file.
A filter condition failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null, causing incorrect values to be selected for records with blank PO numbers.
After the fix, invoice data was inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch even when PO line items differed from the D2S Invoice file.
D2S Invoice Mismatch records are stored in CX_MISM_TOB / siebel.CX_MISM_TOB.
Recovery was required for mismatch records on Iwate, Aomori, Shikoku, and FDP Chugoku; recovered records had their creation dates updated to the invoice-received date.
Creation dates for invoice 8000115382 items 000010 and 000020 in siebel.CX_MISM_TOB were corrected to August 4, 2025 to match siebel.cx_d2s_recon.
root_cause: D2S Invoice Mismatch insertion logic excluded invoice data when PO line-item D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file; a related filter condition also failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null.
resolution: Updated the insertion and filter conditions on FDP-UAT1, released the fix to Production in the 23rd October scheduled FDP release, and recovered affected mismatch records with corrected creation dates.

investigation_summary: The issue was fixed on FDP-UAT1 and could not be reproduced in UAT during validation. The program was approved for deployment, deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release, and monitoring was requested.
important_findings: The issue was fixed on FDP-UAT1.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT during SC UAT validation.
Deployment of the program was approved for Production.
The incident was deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
resolution: The program fix was deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.

investigation_summary: No incident discussion comments were provided, so the incident could not be investigated or analyzed.

The reported duplicate JVs were investigated for both referenced Job Cards. The duplicate JVs had the same price because the related External Work Order contained two parts with the same price. The behavior was determined to be expected and not a system issue, so the incident was rejected.
important_findings: Two JVs with the same price were present for both Job Cards referenced in the Jira description.
The related External Work Order contained two parts with the same price.
The duplicate JV pricing was determined to be expected behavior, not a system defect.
The incident was rejected after the investigation outcome was agreed.
root_cause: Two parts with the same price existed in the External Work Order, resulting in two JVs with the same price.
resolution: No system change was required; the incident was rejected because the behavior was working as expected.

investigation_summary: The "Internal Order (Charge To)" field was not being updated correctly by the existing program, requiring recovery of affected Internal Orders. The issue had existed for an extended period and was not caused by a recent configuration change or release. The program was corrected, validated in FDP-UAT1/UAT-01, and deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
important_findings: Data recovery was required for Internal Orders, with September JC Create Date Required orders prioritized.

For TYPE "22: NV Modification (Transfer)" and "23: NV Stock Modification (Pool)", Internal Order (Charge To) had to be recovered as NV; for TYPE "26: UV Repair (Transfer)", it had to be recovered as SV.
The existing program was not working properly to update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field.
No configuration change was identified as the cause; the issue had existed since at least SR MFRBCFFR-1824.
Orders were prevented from proceeding with JCO when the field was not populated because a validation required the field before JCO.
The fix passed testing in UAT1 and was deployed to Production on 9th October.
root_cause: The existing program did not correctly update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field. The defect was longstanding and was not attributed to a recent configuration change or release.
resolution: Recovered affected Internal Orders, updated the program that populates "Internal Order (Charge To)", validated the fix in FDP-UAT1/UAT-01, and deployed it to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.

investigation_summary: Shipment processing failed for all FDPs during the PROD release window from 25 September 11 PM JST to 26 September 12:00 AM JST. IT confirmed that interfaces were stopped during the PROD release, causing the shipment failure. Files for PO Allocation and Shipment were subsequently received from D2S.
important_findings: System downtime occurred from 25 September 11 PM JST to 26 September 12:00 AM JST.
Shipment failure affected all FDPs.
Interfaces were stopped during the 25 September PROD release.
Interface partners had been notified in advance of the release.
Future releases will require interface partners to complete pending requests beforehand and proactive coordination if support is needed.
root_cause: Interfaces were stopped during the 25 September PROD release, resulting in shipment failure in FDP.
resolution: PO Allocation and Shipment files were received from D2S. As a preventive measure, interface partners will be asked to complete pending requests before release downtime and will be proactively coordinated with for required support.

investigation_summary: Incorrect D/N prices were created for part-number records with an October 1 start date in FDP PROD. The issue was caused by execution of the D2S_PRICE_MASTER file received on September 26, which contained future-dated records. Recovery was completed, data was verified after month-end price revision activity, and price data was confirmed in sync with the SC version.
important_findings: Records with an October 1 start date had incorrect D/N prices.
The D2S_PRICE_MASTER file received on September 26 contained future-dated records and was executed.
Recovery was completed across FDP PROD.
After month-end price revision activity, recovered price data was verified to be in sync with the SC version.
Future-dated records will be removed from received price master files; a CR for Realtime interfacing for price master is intended as a permanent prevention measure.
root_cause: Execution of the D2S_PRICE_MASTER file received on September 26 despite it containing future-dated records, resulting in incorrect D/N prices.
resolution: Completed recovery in FDP PROD and verified price data was in sync with the SC version after month-end price revision activity. Future-dated records will be eliminated from incoming price master files; Realtime interfacing for price master is planned through a CR as the permanent solution.

investigation_summary: A backend retry function was implemented to allow status processing to continue through the normal process flow. The fix was released to PROD on 04/10/2025 through an FDP-emergency release, with ongoing monitoring planned to verify status consistency.
important_findings: A retry function was implemented on the backend.
The retry function enables status processing through the usual process flow.
The fix was approved for PROD release.
The fix was released through an FDP-emergency release on 04/10/2025.
Post-release monitoring was planned to ensure status consistency.
resolution: Implemented a backend retry function and released it to PROD through the FDP-emergency release on 04/10/2025.

investigation_summary: The incident was addressed through a fix deployed in the FDP-PROD release on 25th September, 2025. Post-release monitoring was planned to prevent recurrence related to PO cancellations.
important_findings: A fix was scheduled for the FDP-PROD release on 25th September, 2025.
The issue was confirmed fixed after the 25th September, 2025 release.
Future occurrences are being monitored in relation to PO cancellations.
resolution: Deployed the fix in the FDP-PROD release on 25th September, 2025.

investigation_summary: The incident involved correcting Journal Vector recovery data and identifying JVs from WO line items. Sample JV records in UAT1 were corrected, including the Parts condition code for Issue records. The validated change was deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
important_findings: A Recovery List for Journal Vector was created using Power BI to support recovery-data registration.
Recovery data was planned for Journal Vector across four days, covering February through August.
The team investigated a method to identify Journal Vectors based on WO line items.
Corrected JV logic was implemented and validated in UAT1.
For sample JC# I001299074, the Parts condition of the Issue was changed to the correct code.
The validated change was deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
root_cause: The Parts condition code on Issue records was incorrect, causing incorrect Journal Vector logic.
resolution: Updated the Parts condition of Issue records to the correct code, validated the corrected JV logic in UAT1, and deployed the change to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.

investigation_summary: Changing the customer code in the JC header did not immediately update the customer code in all child applet placeholders. The values updated correctly only after manually refreshing the child applet. Refresh functionality was added to JC More Info and other screens in FDP-UAT1, then deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
important_findings: Customer code changes in the JC header were not propagated to all placeholders in the child applet.
The correct customer code was reflected after the child applet was refreshed, based on the JC header value.
The fix added refresh functionality so changes are reflected immediately without a manual applet refresh.
The fix was implemented in FDP-UAT1, approved for Production monitoring, and deployed in the 9th October FDP Release.
root_cause: Customer code updates in the JC header were not updating all placeholders in the child applet until the applet was refreshed.
resolution: Added refresh functionality on JC More Info and other screens to immediately reflect JC header customer code changes; deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.

investigation_summary: The incident was associated with changes to the Department Name and Contact address. The agreed corrective action was to revert both values to their previous values, and approval was provided for deployment to PROD.
important_findings: A related past incident, MFTBCFFR-3016, "SV_Individual invoice issue(＠Iwate)", was referenced.
The Department Name and Contact address were identified as values requiring reversion.
The customer agreed to the proposed action and approved deployment to PROD.
resolution: Revert the Department Name and Contact address to their older values and deploy the change to PROD.

investigation_summary: The comments state that recovery was successfully completed in the SR. No technical investigation details, root cause, affected components, or corrective actions were documented.
important_findings: Recovery in the SR was reported as successfully completed.
The requester confirmed closure of the issue.
resolution: Recovery in the SR was successfully completed.

investigation_summary: The JV Department Code was populated from the Sales Order Creator’s Department Code, causing Department Code "05" from user D8TOSANA to appear in the JV. The mapping was changed and validated in UAT1, then deployed to Production in the 9th October 2025 FDP Release.
important_findings: Department Code in JV was mapped from the Creator’s Department Code.
The Sales Order creator user D8TOSANA had Department Code "05", which was therefore shown in the JV.
The required mapping was to populate the JV Department Code from the Primary Sales Rep’s Department Code (Current Sales Rep).
The fix was completed in UAT1 and deployed to Production in the 9th October 2025 FDP Release.
root_cause: The JV Department Code mapping used the Sales Order Creator’s Department Code instead of the Primary Sales Rep’s Department Code (Current Sales Rep).
resolution: Modified the JV Department Code mapping to use the Primary Sales Rep’s Department Code (Current Sales Rep), validated the fix in UAT1, and deployed it to Production in the 9th October 2025 FDP Release.

investigation_summary: The issue involved status values in JC Status and WO Status. Validation in UAT-1 confirmed that the "Maintenance Started" LOV was hidden in JC Status and that multiple JC and WO test cases had no issues. The change was released to PROD on 18 September, and a subsequent request was made to deploy the validated program to FDP-PROD.
important_findings: The "Maintenance Started" LOV was confirmed hidden in JC Status in UAT-1.
The expected behavior was that "Work Completed" would no longer exist in WO Status after the change.

System instability during peak traffic was investigated and linked to a timeout parameter increase from 1 hour to 2 hours. The longer session duration increased session retention and memory utilization at the web layer, amplifying existing memory leaks. Reverting the timeout parameter to 1 hour restored system stability.
important_findings: The timeout parameter was changed from 1 hour to 2 hours before the instability occurred.
During peak traffic, prolonged sessions caused higher memory utilization and session retention at the web layer.
Extended sessions amplified memory leaks in the system.
Oracle and Siebel best practices recommend synchronizing timeout settings between web and application layers and avoiding long timeout values.
Reverting the timeout parameter from 2 hours to 1 hour restored stability.
Future timeout increases should be made gradually, such as in 10-minute intervals, with stability monitoring after each change.
root_cause: Changing the timeout parameter from 1 hour to 2 hours extended user sessions during peak load, increasing web-layer session retention and memory utilization and amplifying memory leaks.
resolution: Reverted the timeout parameter from 2 hours to 1 hour, restoring system stability.

investigation_summary: The incident matched MFTBCFFR-4243 and involved a Trade-In Assessment that could not be deleted after the Trade-In Flag was manually changed from "Y" to "N" in NV Quote Header revision 2. Unchecking the flag makes related Trade-In fields read-only, preventing required backend updates during assessment deletion. The issue is resolved by rechecking the Trade-In Flag to "Y" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment.
important_findings: In revision 1, the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header was set to "Y".
In revision 2, the user manually unchecked the Trade-In Flag, changing it to "N".
When the Trade-In Flag is unchecked, related Trade-In fields become read-only.
Read-only Trade-In fields prevent backend field updates required to delete the Trade-In Assessment.
The correct process is to delete the Trade-In Assessment first, then uncheck the Trade-In Flag.
root_cause: The Trade-In Flag was changed to "N" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment, causing related Trade-In fields to become read-only and blocking the backend updates required for deletion.
resolution: Recheck the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header to "Y", delete the Trade-In Assessment, and only then uncheck the flag if required.

investigation_summary: Duplicate recycle fee orders were repeatedly created when multiple D21F files were processed for the same chassis order. The investigation determined that the recycle fee order creation logic generated a new order for each D21F processing rather than updating an existing order. A logic enhancement was documented to prevent duplicate creation, but the timeline contains no confirmation that the fix was approved or that D21F content updates, such as amount changes, are handled.
important_findings: For C# number 610083, D21F files were received on February 7 and August 4 for the same Chassis Order.
SIEBEL created duplicate recycling orders when the same D21F file or multiple D21F files for the same chassis order were processed.
The number of recycle fee orders created matched the number of D21F processing occurrences.
Repeated operational recoveries removed duplicate orders and updated recycle status/order status to completed, but did not prevent recurrence.
A CR was planned to handle multiple D21F files for the same C# number, and duplicate recycle order checks were added to daily AMS monitoring across FDP production environments.

The proposed logic change prevents subsequent processing from creating another recycle fee order when one already exists for the chassis order and dealer code; handling of D21F updates such as amount changes was queried but not answered.
root_cause: The recycle fee order creation logic was not idempotent: it created a new recycle fee order each time D21F data was processed for the same chassis order instead of identifying and updating the existing order.

investigation_summary: Button enablement in FDP used an RF status condition even though RF Status is not available in FDP, causing incorrect button behavior. The implementation was revised to control Send Recycle Fee, Modify/Change Order, and CUT/Cancel Order behavior using TOB and Recycle Fee Order statuses, including a one-day rule based on receipt of a successful TOB response. The final changes were tested in UAT1, approved for production, and released in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.
important_findings: The original button logic depended on RF STATUS = Null, but RF Status is not used in FDP.

The requested behavior was to make the Request for modification and CUT buttons unavailable from the day after a successful TOB response when the recycle order status is Completed or Recycle Order Changed.
The One Day Window requirement was corrected: CUT and Modify buttons must be enabled for the full day on which a successful TOB response is received, not the day the TOB request is sent.
For UAT1 verification, a TOB response was simulated for Chassis Order # B001217339 and Recycle Fee Order # B001217574; the record Last Modified date was used to identify the successful-response date.
The implementation also needed to preserve Send Recycle Fee availability after CUT success or a modification TOB error, rather than relying only on TOB response date and TOB status.
The incident was released to Production in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.
root_cause: Legacy RF STATUS-based button-enable conditions were retained although RF Status is not available in FDP, resulting in incorrect enablement control for the TOB-related buttons.
resolution: Reworked the FDP button-control logic to use TOB Status and Recycle Fee Order Status, with CUT and Modify enabled only on the date a successful TOB response is received; the finalized changes were released to Production on 23 October 2025.
technical_entities: Confirmation Report - Send Recycle Fee Button

Sales Quote 1-6FHJ0C and Opportunity 1-6FHIYB were used for investigation.
The Model Code was manually removed from the Vehicle.
Without a Model Code on the Vehicle, line items were not created in the UV Quote.
The corrective process is to delete the Vehicle from the UV Opportunity, add the appropriate Model Code, re-map the Vehicle, and create the Quote again.
The incident was determined to be user misoperation, not a system issue.
root_cause: The Model Code was manually removed from the Vehicle, causing UV Quote line items not to be created.
resolution: Delete the Vehicle from the UV Opportunity, add the appropriate Model Code to the Vehicle, re-map the Vehicle to the UV Opportunity, and create the Quote from the Opportunity again.

investigation_summary: The incident occurred in Aomori prod and was confirmed to be the same issue as MFTBCFFR-4179. Recovery was completed, while the D2S team continued root cause analysis and implementation of a permanent fix under the related incident. The incident was approved for rejection after recovery.
important_findings: Recovery was completed in Aomori prod.
The issue was identified as the same as MFTBCFFR-4179.
The D2S team was responsible for RCA and a permanent fix.
The incident was rejected after recovery was validated.
resolution: Recovery was completed in Aomori prod; further RCA and permanent remediation were tracked under MFTBCFFR-4179.

investigation_summary: The incident affected user D8MIHOSH when retrieving printer details from the Siebel printer master screen and printing BIP Reports. Print Server history showed the print request status as Success, while the user-side error was traced to the user not being present on the Canon server. The user was added to the Canon server, and printing was confirmed to work.
important_findings: Print Server history recorded the print request status as Success.
User D8MIHOSH received an error when clicking “get printer detail” on the Siebel printer master screen.
D8MIHOSH was not present on the Canon server.
A Printer Master SR had been completed for the user on 17th July, but the printer changes were not reflected.
After the user was added to the Canon server, the user was able to print BIP Reports.
root_cause: User D8MIHOSH was not present on the Canon server, and the completed Printer Master SR changes were not reflected.
resolution: Added user D8MIHOSH to the Canon server; printing of BIP Reports was subsequently confirmed successful.

investigation_summary: A record was reported as visible in Siebel but missing from PBI Reports; sample order Q050163081 was provided. Investigation found that the editable Request# field in the Siebel UI had been populated with an Opportunity# instead of the Insurance Quote request number. Recovery was completed, and the Request# is now displayed in the FDPC Report.
important_findings: Sample affected order: Q050163081.
The Request# field in the Siebel UI is editable.
Users can mistakenly enter an Opportunity# in the Request number field of an Insurance Quote.
The issue also occurs on SC.
After recovery, the Request# was displayed in the FDPC Report.
root_cause: User misoperation: an Opportunity# was entered in the editable Request# field of an Insurance Quote instead of the correct request number.
resolution: Completed recovery of the affected record; the Request# is now displayed in the FDPC Report.

investigation_summary: Zero-amount Journal Vouchers (JVs) were created because JV-creation filters did not consistently evaluate the same Base Amount fields used by the JV. In Okinawa prod, the fix from MFTBCFFR-3779 was ineffective for two Journal Event types because of an extra space in the deployed filter. The Okinawa fix was released on July 24, 2025, and the corrected filters for the remaining Journal Event types were validated in UAT/UAT1 and released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.
important_findings: Zero-amount JVs were found in FDP prod for multiple Journal Event types where the filter field differed from the JV Base Amount field.
The JV-creation filter is intended to prevent JV creation when Base Amount equals zero.

For Okinawa prod, the MFTBCFFR-3779 fix for "Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable" and "Service Correction Sales Amount Red Slip Non-Taxable" failed because of an extra space in the deployed filter.
The corrective logic uses the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount" and applies a "Base amount not equal to zero" condition.
The fix was validated in UAT1, where zero-amount JVs were no longer created.
root_cause: Incorrect JV-creation filter configuration: filters used fields different from the JV Base Amount fields; additionally, an extra space in the deployed filter prevented the prior MFTBCFFR-3779 fix from working in Okinawa prod.
resolution: Released a corrected "Base amount not equal to zero" filter using the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount". The Okinawa prod correction was released on July 24, 2025, and changes for the remaining Journal Event types were released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.
technical_entities: Service Correction Sales Amount Red Slip Non-Taxable
Re-Edit Red Slip Job Card Sales Amount Non-Taxable
ConsTax PO - UV Body Building Order
ConsTax PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS

investigation_summary: Users were unable to complete spreadsheet approval from the inbox. Recovery changed the item status to 'Spreadsheet Requested', after which the user could approve it. A fix was validated in UAT1 and released to production in the 13 September scheduled FDP release.
important_findings: The inbox issue prevented completion of the spreadsheet approval request.
Recovery changed the status to 'Spreadsheet Requested', enabling the user to approve the spreadsheet from the inbox.
The issue was fixed and spreadsheet approval was confirmed working in UAT1.
The approved fix was released to production in the 13 September scheduled FDP release.
resolution: Applied a fix in UAT1, validated spreadsheet approval, and released the fix to production in the 13 September scheduled FDP release.

investigation_summary: A slowness issue was monitored in the production environment. No recurrence was reported during monitoring, and the business confirmed that users had not observed further slowness. The incident was closed based on the absence of recurrence.
important_findings: Slowness was observed in the production environment.
No recurrence of slowness was reported during the monitoring period.
Business confirmed that users had not reported further slowness.
resolution: The incident was closed after monitoring confirmed no recurrence of the slowness issue in the production environment.

investigation_summary: The incident affected the Copy Quote functionality for NV Quote and was reported across multiple locations. The issue was replicated on UAT-01 and identified as being caused by the fix released through MFTBCFFR-4241. A corrective fix was implemented and validated on UAT-01, then deployed to PROD through the 15 July 2025 Emergency release.
important_findings: The issue was replicated on UAT-01.
The issue was caused by the fix released through MFTBCFFR-4241.
After the corrective fix, Copy Quote functionality for NV Quote worked correctly on UAT-01.
The fix was released to PROD via the 15 July 2025 Emergency release.
root_cause: The fix released through MFTBCFFR-4241 caused the issue with Copy Quote functionality for NV Quote.
resolution: A corrective fix was implemented and validated on UAT-01, then deployed to PROD through the 15 July 2025 Emergency release.

investigation_summary: Insurance files were not updating on the Siebel side. Failed file executions were monitored and processed manually, and affected insurance orders were recovered and updated through the received files. Monitoring later confirmed that Insurance files executed successfully at their scheduled time in Chugoku Production without errors.
important_findings: Insurance files were not updating at the Siebel side.
When file execution failed, the files were processed manually.
Affected insurance orders were recovered and updated through the received files.
IFIN009 Insurance Order files were executed through the 25th.
From 6 October, monitoring showed files executing correctly at their scheduled time.
On 10 October, Insurance files completed successfully at 10 PM JST in Chugoku Production without error.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned differing workshop and department values across JC, JCO, and JV. Investigation confirmed that the values followed existing logic based on the branch code of the user who created the Job Card and the user who customer-approved the quote. The case was classified as a rare Operation Miss; no system changes or recovery were performed, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Workshop Code in JC reflects the Branch Code of the user who created the Job Card; it was 23 in this case.
JCO Workshop Name reflects the Branch Code of the user who Customer Approved the Quote; it was 21 in this case.
JV Department Code (CSJS200) and Department Code (CSJS300) come from the JCO Site, which was 21.
JVs had already been sent to KB.
The observed behavior was confirmed as current logic rather than a defect requiring a change.
The case was considered a rare Operation Miss, so no changes were made.
root_cause: A rare Operation Miss caused different branch-derived values to be used: JC used the Job Card creator's Branch Code (23), while JCO and JV used the Customer Approved Quote user's/JCO Site Branch Code (21).
resolution: No corrective system change was made. The incident was closed after confirming the existing logic and classifying the case as a rare Operation Miss.

investigation_summary: A Service Request could not be completed because of invalid data in the Service Request Details. The issue was traced to user mis-operation when entering fields in Tasks before creating the Service Request. Support rejected the affected Service Request and instructed the user to create it again; the recreated request completed successfully and Account Receivable was created.
important_findings: A data issue in Service Request Details prevented the Service Request from reaching Completed status.
The invalid data originated from user mis-operation while entering fields in Tasks before creating the Service Request.
The affected Service Request was rejected rather than corrected in place.
Creating the Service Request again completed successfully.
Account Receivable was created after the Service Request was recreated.
root_cause: User mis-operation when entering fields in Tasks before creating the Service Request, resulting in invalid Service Request Details data that prevented completion.
resolution: Rejected the affected Service Request and had the user create it again; the new Service Request completed successfully and created Account Receivable.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned Entity Transfer behavior for Sales Rep transfers, particularly transfers within special sales. Multiple UAT issues were identified, including unavailable target users due to organization and position configuration, duplicate Position Id values, and incorrect user filtering. The final implementation restricts Sales Rep Transfer to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position, and was deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.
important_findings: Entity Transfer initially displayed only configured position types; requested additional position types were added to the Entity Transfer logic on UAT1.
A transfer between D0X20852 and D0X20851 was blocked because their primary organizations differed: D0X20852 was in Default Organization, 000000000O, while D0X20851 was in Okayama East Branch, 10.
A transfer did not reflect because both users had the same Position Id; the Position Id issue was corrected.
Person selection was unavailable for one Sales Order because no user was assigned to the current Sales Rep's position; the position was assigned to users.
The final Entity Transfer rule allows Sales Rep Transfer only to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position.
The self-approval validation was separately identified as introduced to FDP through CR-0836 and was removed from NV Quote on UAT1 for testing.
root_cause: Entity Transfer user-selection and transfer behavior did not meet the required special-sales transfer criteria; additional issues were caused by different user organizations, duplicate Position Id values, and missing user assignments for the current Sales Rep position.
resolution: Updated Entity Transfer to allow Sales Rep Transfer only among users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position; corrected duplicate Position Id configuration and assigned missing positions to users. The changes were deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.

investigation_summary: PDF generation errors were reported for Non Genuine Delivery Slip in FDP Prod. The implementation review found no code-related issues; the BIP was re-uploaded to the server. Subsequent checks found no PDF generation error records on 09/07/2025 in FDPO Prod or on 10/07/2025 across all FDP Prod environments, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: No code-related issues were identified during the implementation review.
The BIP was re-uploaded to the server.
No records with PDF generation Error were found for Non Genuine Delivery Slip on 09/07/2025 in FDPO Prod.
No records with PDF generation Error were found for Non Genuine Delivery Slip on 10/07/2025 across all FDP Prod environments.
resolution: Re-uploaded the BIP on the server and verified that no further PDF generation Error records existed in FDP Prod environments.

investigation_summary: Bulk invoice data was not sent on 30 June because the existing logic determines the send schedule from the closing date of the original account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order. The relevant account had a closing date of 20, so the data was scheduled for 20 July rather than 30 June. The behavior was confirmed as consistent with the current logic, and a change is being addressed through project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.
important_findings: Recovery was completed and the data was linked to KB again.
Bulk invoice data is fetched using "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, which represents the original Account.
The closing date used for bulk invoice processing is taken from the account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code".
The original Account closing date was 20; therefore, data was expected to be sent on 20 July, not 30 June.
Current logic does not fetch bulk invoice data using the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code".
A logic change is being tracked under project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.
root_cause: The bulk invoice workflow uses the closing date of the original Account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, rather than the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code". Because that account's closing date was 20, the data was not scheduled to send on 30 June.
resolution: Recovered the incident data by linking it to KB again. The required logic change is being handled through project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.

investigation_summary: An affected record was recovered, and the user was instructed to complete the required fields in the Sales Quote. Subsequent review found no issue with the Quote. If the user proceeds with Generate Approval, approvals are expected to process correctly; no further action was pending.
important_findings: The affected record was recovered.
The user was instructed to fill the required fields in the Sales Quote.
Investigation found no issue with the Quote.
Generate Approval is expected to process approvals correctly if the user proceeds.
The user was not proceeding with the Quote, possibly because the Quote or Opportunity was Lost.
resolution: The affected record was recovered; no defect was found in the Quote, and the user was advised to proceed with Generate Approval after completing required fields.

investigation_summary: Users could manually change a UV Purchase Quote status from "Approved" to "Order Intake" through the "My Branch" view, but could not change it back to "Approved", blocking the business process. Recovery was completed for the affected record. The Status field was made read-only in UAT and then deployed to Production in the July 24 regular FDP release.
important_findings: UV Purchase Quote status could be manually updated from the "My Branch" view.
A status change from "Approved" to "Order Intake" was permitted, while reverting from "Order Intake" to "Approved" was not possible.
The one-way status transition blocked the business process.
Recovery for the affected record was completed.
The selected fix was to make the Purchase Quote Status field read-only.
The fix was implemented in UAT and released to Production on July 24.
root_cause: The UV Purchase Quote Status field was manually editable from the "My Branch" view, allowing an "Approved" to "Order Intake" transition that could not be reversed.
resolution: Made the Purchase Quote Status field read-only, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it to Production in the July 24 FDP regular release.

investigation_summary: Incorrect posting dates were identified in Recycle invoice recovery data. The search specification in the MFT TOB Reconciliation Business Component was updated and validated in Siebel uat8, with recovery data generated for FDP Shikoku. The fix was deployed to Prod, recovery was completed, and the data was scheduled to link to KB in the nightly batch.
important_findings: Recycle invoice data initially had an incorrect posting date.
Posting date was set to 20250630 for all recovery data for both TOB Invoice JV and Recycle Invoice JV.
The search specification in the MFT TOB Reconciliation Business Component was changed in Siebel uat8 and validated through batch and job processing.
The production release was approved after UAT validation.
The fix was deployed to Prod and recovery was completed.
resolution: Updated the search specification in the MFT TOB Reconciliation Business Component, set recovery posting dates to 20250630 for TOB Invoice JV and Recycle Invoice JV, deployed the change to Prod, and completed recovery.

investigation_summary: The requested production data update was found to already be applied. The request was identified as a duplicate of SR MFTBCFFR-4332, where the recovery was completed. This incident was rejected as not being a bug and closed.
important_findings: The requested data was already updated in the production environment.
The incident duplicated SR MFTBCFFR-4332.
Additional correction work for customer code 0C00125894 was requested under MFTBCFFR-4332.
Recovery was completed through the SR rather than through this incident.
The incident was determined not to be a bug.
root_cause: The incident was a duplicate of SR MFTBCFFR-4332; the requested production data update had already been applied.
resolution: Completed recovery through SR MFTBCFFR-4332 and closed/rejected MFTBCFFR-4319 as a non-bug duplicate.

investigation_summary: A Model Price update file received from TOB on the shared part was picked up by the Okinawa production ODI package, causing incorrect price updates for 13,329 Model Code records in PROD. Recovery data and corrected data were prepared, and the affected model-price, Quote, and Sales Order records were recovered. The recovery process was ultimately confirmed complete on PROD.
important_findings: The Model Price update file received on 3/June was picked up by the Okinawa production ODI package.
Prices for some Model Codes were incorrectly updated, affecting 13,329 records.
Recovery initially addressed the affected production model-price records but did not include Quote or Sales Order records.
Affected Quote and Sales Order records were subsequently recovered.
Some Sales Orders had the status "Sales Posting Completed" during recovery; final confirmation stated that all recovery processes were completed on PROD.
root_cause: A Model Price update file received from TOB on the shared part was picked by the Okinawa production ODI package, resulting in incorrect price updates for 13,329 Model Code records.
resolution: Prepared corrected and recovery data, then recovered the affected model-price records, Quotes, and Sales Orders on PROD; all recovery processes were confirmed complete.

investigation_summary: Insurance Order Q036607132, migrated from SC, was identified as a case related to MFTBCFFR-4125. The order was missed during the MFTBCFFR-4125 data patch because its JV had already been created on 7th February 2025. The Department Code was corrected in production, the Posting Date was changed to 20250704, and the recovery data was scheduled for transmission to KB through the nightly daily batch.
important_findings: Insurance Order Q036607132 was migrated from SC and is related to MFTBCFFR-4125.
The order was excluded from the MFTBCFFR-4125 data patch because a JV had already been created on 7th February 2025.
The Department Code was updated for the affected Insurance Order.
Recovery was completed in prod with Posting Date updated to 20250704.
No additional Liability Insurance Order records with a created JV and null Department Code were found in the Chugoku production environment.
root_cause: Insurance Order Q036607132 was missed during data patching for MFTBCFFR-4125 because its JV had already been created on 7th February 2025 and was therefore not included in the patch.
resolution: Updated the Department Code for Insurance Order Q036607132 in prod, changed the Posting Date to 20250704, and sent the recovery data to KB through the nightly daily batch.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Insurance Order Journal Vouchers were identified in Chugoku Production. All affected records were recovered by creating reverse JVs, including the two orders whose recovery JVs had already been created in production. The duplicates were caused during recovery activity for MFTBCFFR-4125, not by a system issue; the recovery manual was updated to prevent recurrence.
important_findings: 21 duplicated Insurance Order JVs were reported.
Reverse JVs were created for the duplicated Insurance Order JVs.
Recovery JVs for orders I050187391 and A031016519 had already been created on production and were not recreated.
Recovery was completed for all affected records in Chugoku Production.
The duplicate records were created during recovery of MFTBCFFR-4125, not due to a system issue.
The recovery manual was updated to prevent similar incidents.
root_cause: During recovery of MFTBCFFR-4125, duplicate Insurance Order Journal Voucher records were created.
resolution: Created reverse JVs for all affected duplicated Insurance Order JVs and updated the recovery manual.

investigation_summary: The incident involved blank actual cost/option price display for affected records, including chassis options. The affected records were recovered and actual cost was corrected, but subsequent investigation found Option Pricing working correctly in Production and UAT1/UAT environments. The issue could not be reproduced, no recurrence was observed, and the incident was temporarily closed with ongoing monitoring.
important_findings: Affected records were recovered, and actual cost was corrected for those records.
Option Pricing was functioning correctly in Production, UAT1, and UAT regression testing.
No data issue was found in the price data for the reported options or in master records.
The issue involving a chassis option price not being displayed did not recur after 30 June.
Option price monitoring was added to daily AMS-monitoring; monitoring continued on FDP Production environments.
The incident remained unresolved because the cause could not be reproduced or identified.

investigation_summary: PT_PO to MWH Stock transfer slip print requests were successfully processed by Siebel in Shikoku Prod for the reported POs and printer TAK_12_P10. The failures occurred after the requests reached the Canon printer side. Monitoring shared by Terui san showed no recurrence, and the incident was closed with no AMS action required.
important_findings: Siebel reported successful print processing for PT_PO to MWH Stock transfer slips in Shikoku Prod.
Reported successful requests included POs N000169477, N000169624, N000169836, and N000169869, created by USER-50 for printer TAK_12_P10.
After successful processing in Siebel, print requests were delivered to the printer; downstream printer failures were not investigable by AMS.
The issue was identified as a Canon-side failure, not a Siebel issue.
Monitoring results indicated that the issue did not recur.
root_cause: Print requests failed on the Canon side after successful processing and delivery from Siebel.
resolution: No corrective AMS action was required; monitoring confirmed no recurrence and the Jira was closed.

investigation_summary: A recovery JV was created with a blank Client Code because the Vendor Finance Code was blank in the Body Building Order. The affected JV was recovered using branch code 7000 and was scheduled to link to KB in the nightly daily batch. The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, and monitoring of FDP production environment through July 31 found no further JVs with null Client Code.
important_findings: The Vendor Finance Code was blank in the Body Building Order, resulting in a blank Client Code in the JV.
The affected JV recovery was completed using branch code 7000 and was to be linked to KB in the nightly daily batch.
The issue could not be replicated in UAT despite checking all logic scenarios.
Daily monitoring of FDP production environment found no additional JVs with null Client Code through July 31.
The incident was treated as a one-time occurrence and closed after the monitoring period.
root_cause: The Vendor Finance Code was blank in the Body Building Order, causing the Client Code to be blank in the JV.
resolution: Recovered the affected JV using branch code 7000 and linked it to KB through the daily batch; monitored FDP production environment through July 31 with no recurrence.

investigation_summary: The issue affected editability of Line Item fields based on Actual Expense Status. A fix was implemented and verified in FDP UAT-1, where Line Item fields became read-only when Actual Expense Status was "Completed". The change was released to Prod on 10th July 2025.
important_findings: Line Item fields were required to be read-only when Actual Expense Status is "Completed".
The fix was deployed and verified successfully in FDP UAT-1.
The verified change was released to Prod on 10th July 2025.
resolution: Implemented a fix so that Line Item fields are read-only when Actual Expense Status is "Completed", verified in FDP UAT-1, and released to Prod on 10th July 2025.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Journal Vouchers were created for Body Building Orders in FDP Production, including Chugoku prod. Investigation found that the validation introduced under MFTBCFFR-3809 checked only for an existing Completed JV trigger, allowing a second trigger while the original trigger was still in progress. The validation was updated and tested in UAT1, then released to FDP Production on 27th August.
important_findings: Affected duplicate Journal Vouchers were recovered using reverse Journal Vouchers and linked to KB through the daily batch.
The MFTBCFFR-3809 validation prevented new JV triggers only when a Completed trigger existed for the Body Building Order.
A duplicate Journal Voucher was created two minutes after the original because the original JV trigger had not yet reached Completed status.
The corrected validation prevents creation of another JV trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of status.
UAT testing confirmed that multiple Shipment Details responses from IBOS send the Journal Voucher trigger only once.
The fix was deployed to FDP Production in the 27th August planned release.
root_cause: The validation check added by MFTBCFFR-3809 searched only for existing Completed JV triggers. When another trigger was received before the original trigger completed, the validation did not detect the in-progress trigger and created a duplicate Journal Voucher.
resolution: Updated the JV-trigger validation to block creation of a new trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of trigger status. The fix was implemented in UAT1 and released to FDP Production on 27th August.

investigation_summary: Cycle Count ID 1-27LEMV was recovered, and its associated cycle count batch job completed successfully on 27/06/2025. Investigation found that the required approver position was not assigned to any user in branch 02 of Wakayama Prod Employee Master, causing the approver to be blank. This was determined to be master-data configuration rather than a system or code issue.
important_findings: Cycle Count ID 1-27LEMV was created for branch 02.
User D8TDOUMO has the position SCHQ-BizMgmt-SnrMgr in branch 01 of Wakayama Prod Employee Master.
No user with position SCHQ-BizMgmt-SnrMgr exists in branch 02, causing the approver to be blank.
The cycle count batch job associated with 1-27LEMV completed successfully on 27/06/2025 after recovery.
A Service Request is required if a user with position SCHQ-BizMgmt-SnrMgr must be added to branch 02.
root_cause: No user with position SCHQ-BizMgmt-SnrMgr was configured in branch 02 of Wakayama Prod Employee Master for Cycle Count ID 1-27LEMV, resulting in a blank approver.
resolution: Recovered Cycle Count ID 1-27LEMV and completed its associated cycle count batch job. No system or code fix was required; an SR is needed to add the required position to branch 02 if needed.

investigation_summary: Duplicate recycle fee orders were created during manual recovery for Jira ticket MFTBCFFR-4173. The recovery was confirmed after the duplicate recycle fee order was removed and the correct Purchase Orders displayed in the Sales order. The incident was caused by inadvertently executing the batch scheduled for D21F during the manual recovery; an additional backend-data verification step was added to the recovery process.
important_findings: A recycle fee order for the respective chassis order was missing and was manually recovered.
The batch scheduled for D21F was inadvertently executed during recovery, creating two recycle fee orders.
The chassis order screen displayed only one recycle fee order and did not reveal the duplicate backend entry.
The duplicated recycle fee order was removed, and correct Purchase Orders were displayed in the Sales order.
Recovery procedures now require backend-data verification before completion.
root_cause: Manual error during recovery for Jira ticket MFTBCFFR-4173: the batch scheduled for D21F was inadvertently executed while manually recovering a missing recycle fee order, resulting in duplicate recycle fee orders.
resolution: Removed the duplicated recycle fee order and added a backend-data verification step to the recovery process to detect duplicate entries before completion.

investigation_summary: Part# ZC116876 was received from D2S in the Price Master file, after which its price was updated in FDP. Recovery was completed across FDP - PROD. The comments reference an RCA from D2S, but do not provide its details.
important_findings: Part# ZC116876 was received from D2S in the Price Master file.
The price for part# ZC116876 was updated in FDP.
Recovery was completed on all FDP - PROD environments.
An RCA was shared by the D2S team, but its content was not included in the incident comments.
resolution: Received part# ZC116876 through the D2S Price Master file and updated its price in FDP; recovery was completed on all FDP - PROD.

investigation_summary: The Chassis Order Shipment Date was updated from a D21Z file containing a 26 May date. Investigation confirmed that the current mapping used D21Z to update Shipment Date/Actual Shipment Date, although D21Z contains transportation information rather than shipping data. The required D21Z mapping changes were redirected to MFTBCFFR-3505, but the comments do not confirm that a fix was implemented.
important_findings: A D21Z file received on 27 May contained a 26 May date, which caused 26 May to be displayed in the Chassis Order.
The current mapping updated Shipment Date from D21Z files.
D21Z is transportation information and does not contain shipping data.
Updating Actual Shipment Date from D21Z was identified as an incorrect mapping behavior.
D21Z-related mapping changes were tracked through MFTBCFFR-3505, which was later reported as not fixed.
root_cause: Incorrect D21Z file mapping updated the Chassis Order Shipment Date/Actual Shipment Date even though D21Z contains transportation information, not shipping data.

investigation_summary: The user could not delete the UV Trade-In Assessment after manually changing the UV Trade-In Flag in the UV Quote Header from "Y" to "N" in Revision 4. Unchecking the flag made related Trade-In fields read-only, preventing required backend updates during assessment deletion. The issue was classified as user misoperation rather than a system defect; the flag must be rechecked to "Y" before deleting the assessment.
important_findings: The UV Trade-In Flag was "Y" in Revision 2 and Revision 3, then manually changed to "N" in Revision 4.
When the UV Trade-In Flag is unchecked in the UV Quote Header, related Trade-In fields become read-only.
Read-only Trade-In fields prevent backend field updates required to delete the UV Trade-In Assessment.
The required sequence is to delete the UV Trade-In Assessment first and then uncheck the UV Trade-In Flag.
The incident was determined to be user misoperation, not a system defect.
root_cause: The user unchecked the UV Trade-In Flag before deleting the UV Trade-In Assessment, causing related Trade-In fields to become read-only and blocking the backend updates needed for deletion.
resolution: Recheck the UV Trade-In Flag to "Y", delete the UV Trade-In Assessment, and only then uncheck the flag if required.

investigation_summary: For quotation 1-DOS1L, MC 6 Model Code was unavailable in the catalogue when the body type was Cabover. Cabover could incorrectly persist when the product class was changed from a truck class to LB, despite LB allowing only Other. A fix was implemented to refresh body type options when changing the product class to LB, preventing Cabover from remaining selected; it was validated in UAT and released to Prod on 10th July 2025.
important_findings: MC 6 Model Code is not displayed in the catalogue when the body type is set to Cabover.
Changing the body type to Other makes the MC 6 Model Code available.
Cabover could be retained for LB by selecting a truck class, setting body type to Cab Over, saving, and then changing the truck class to LB.
The fix automatically refreshes body type options when the product class is changed to LB, so Cabover is no longer available for LB.
The fix was applied to UAT before release to Prod on 10th July 2025.
root_cause: The system did not refresh body type options when the product class was changed to LB, allowing the invalid Cabover body type to persist for LB.
resolution: Implemented a functionality fix to automatically refresh body type options when changing the product class to LB, preventing Cabover from being available or retained; deployed to UAT and released to Prod on 10th July 2025.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned missing insurance files for insurance code 000000000000004 in FDP. Investigation confirmed that FDP received only files for insurance codes 000000000000017 and 000000000000009, and those files were processed successfully by Siebel. The issue was determined to be outside Siebel, with the IT team and Insurance Interface partner team investigating why the 04-code file was not sent through the Hitachi gateway.
important_findings: FDP received files only for insurance codes 000000000000017 and 000000000000009.
Files received for codes 17 and 09 were processed successfully on the Siebel side.
No file was received in FDP for insurance code 000000000000004.
SC Version was receiving files for 0000000000000004.
The issue was not identified as a Siebel issue; IT was checking with the Insurance Interface partner team and the Insurance side through the Hitachi gateway.
Chugoku FDP requested other company information from Tokyo Marine (Tokai San), with an update expected after the end of September.
root_cause: The file for insurance code 000000000000004 was not being sent to FDP from the upstream Insurance Interface/Hitachi gateway side.

investigation_summary: The FDP Chugoku SV_101_105_110_110A_112_112A_115_115A_132 Adhoc Reports Incremental refresh was starting at 8:30 AM JST, preventing completion by the required 7:00 AM timeframe. Investigation found that the SV incremental report refresh time was mistakenly changed during load plan and report refresh timing modifications performed after business hours on 14 June. The schedule was corrected to start at 11:30 PM JST, with correct results expected from the following morning.
important_findings: Only SV incremental reports were affected.
The refresh start time was mistakenly set to 8:30 AM JST during load plan and report refresh timing changes on 14 June.
The reports were required to complete by 7:00 AM, consistent with the SC version.
The refresh schedule was changed to 11:30 PM JST.
Chugoku HQ approved the response and confirmed the incident could be closed.
root_cause: The SV incremental report refresh start time was mistakenly configured as 8:30 AM JST during load plan and report refresh timing modifications on 14 June.
resolution: Changed the SV incremental report refresh start time to 11:30 PM JST.

investigation_summary: Users could add an Option line item through the Parts and Internal Work Applet in a UV quote by entering it in Part#. Options were not displayed in the Parts and Internal Work screen, preventing users from deleting them; saving produced an error while adding the record. A validation restricting permitted product types was implemented in the FDP UAT Environment and released to Prod on 10 July 2025.
important_findings: The Parts and Internal Work Applet allowed an Option to be entered in Part# and saved as a line item.
The Parts and Internal Work screen displayed only Parts, so Option line items were not visible and could not be deleted by users.
Saving the affected record displayed an error but still added the record; a UAT1 reference was 1-19MOBS.
Production recovery was completed before the permanent fix was deployed.
The fix restricts the Parts and Internal Work Applet to Parts, Labor, Accessories, and Lubricant product types.
root_cause: The Parts and Internal Work Applet lacked validation to prevent unsupported product types, allowing Option line items to be added even though the related screen displayed only Parts.
resolution: Implemented validation in the Parts and Internal Work Applet to allow only Parts, Labor, Accessories, and Lubricant. The fix was deployed to the FDP UAT Environment on 27 June 2025 and released to Prod on 10 July 2025.

investigation_summary: Duplicate journal entries (JVs) were identified as the same issue addressed in MFTBCFFR-4187. JVs for Segment2 Codes MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 were re-created on May 7, 2025 because manually added data under MFTBCFFR-3743 did not have its Sent Flag updated. Reverse JV recovery was completed after validation and approval for production.
important_findings: Duplicate JVs other than MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 already had reverse JVs created on June 13, 2025 through MFTBCFFR-4187.
The JVs with Segment2 Codes MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 originated from manually added data in MFTBCFFR-3743.
The Sent Flag was not updated for the manually added data, causing the JVs to be created again on May 7, 2025.
Reverse JV data for MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 was validated and approved for production.
The TOB/D2S Invoice Recovery SOP was updated to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: The Sent Flag was not updated for manually added data created under MFTBCFFR-3743, causing duplicate JVs to be re-created.
resolution: Created, validated, approved for production, and completed reverse-JV recovery for Segment2 Codes MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100; updated the TOB/D2S Invoice Recovery SOP.

investigation_summary: The incident involved Journal Vouchers that required recovery. Investigation determined that the Journal Vouchers were created as part of the MFTBCFFR-4125 recovery and were not caused by a system issue. Recovery was completed using reverse JV entries, validated, and approved for production deployment.
important_findings: Affected records required recovery through reverse JV entries.
Validation of the recovery reverse JV was completed before production deployment.
The Journal Vouchers were created as part of the MFTBCFFR-4125 recovery.
The incident was confirmed not to be a system issue.
Recovery of the Journal Vouchers was completed.
root_cause: Journal Vouchers were created as part of the MFTBCFFR-4125 recovery, not due to a system issue.
resolution: Completed recovery of the affected Journal Vouchers using reverse JV entries after validation and approval for production.

investigation_summary: MFTBCFFR-4222 was identified as a clone issue associated with MFTBCDIGISIGN-40. Further tracking and work were redirected to MFTBCDIGISIGN-40.
important_findings: MFTBCFFR-4222 is a clone issue.
The incident is being tracked under MFTBCDIGISIGN-40.
resolution: Track and continue work under MFTBCDIGISIGN-40.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned three tax amounts finalized through the Tax Finalize button not being reflected in the Sales Order Tax and Expenses amounts. Investigation established that Tax Finalize did not trigger tax-amount synchronization; synchronization occurred only when the "Actual amount including Tax" field was manually changed. A change was implemented and tested in UAT/UAT-1 to synchronize taxation line-item prices on tax finalization, then released to Prod.
important_findings: The issue was not caused by Quote revision or Registration Request creation timing; the reported issue was Sales Order values not updating after tax confirmation.
Three tax amounts are finalized by clicking the Tax Finalize button.
Before the fix, clicking Tax Finalize performed validations and froze values but did not synchronize the Tax Amount to the Sales Order.
Tax Amount synchronized only when the "Actual amount including Tax" field was manually changed.
A UAT test identified that after a Quote revision changed the three tax amounts, clicking Tax Finalize did not update the Sales Order Tax and Expenses amount.
The synchronization change was tested successfully in UAT-1 and released to Prod.
root_cause: The Tax Finalize button did not trigger synchronization of finalized Tax Amount values to the Sales Order; synchronization was only triggered by manual changes to the "Actual amount including Tax" field.
resolution: Implemented synchronization so the taxation line-item price/finalized Tax Amount is synchronized to the Sales Order/Registration Request when Tax Finalize is performed. The change was tested in UAT/UAT-1 and released to Prod.

investigation_summary: Parts were not being updated in the Siebel system from Ascent for Wave-3 Environments. Investigation found that Ascent users for Iwate, Shikoku, Okinawa, and Wakayama had expired. The users were restored and configured to never expire; other FDP users were confirmed to already be in a never-expiry state.
important_findings: Expired Ascent users prevented parts from being updated to the Siebel system.
Affected Wave-3 Environments were Iwate, Shikoku, Okinawa, and Wakayama.
Users for the affected environments were restored and marked as never expired.
Users for other FDPs—Okayama, Aomori, Hakodate, and Chugoku—were already configured as never-expiry users.
root_cause: Ascent users for Wave-3 Environments (Iwate, Shikoku, Okinawa, Wakayama) had expired, blocking part updates from Ascent to the Siebel system.
resolution: Restored the expired Ascent users for the affected Wave-3 Environments and configured them as never-expired users.

investigation_summary: The reported issue concerned an unspecified *total* column, but no details, snapshot, or reproducible evidence were provided in the discussion. The ticket was later classified as not being an incident and proposed for rejection.

Manual patching was completed for H000502304 in the Chugoku Production environment.
H000502304 was confirmed synchronized to Power BI after patching.
Records created going forward are not expected to be affected.
root_cause: The affected AR record H000502304 was created or updated before the June 12, 2025 release of the synchronization fix in MFTBCFFR-4059.
resolution: Manually patched AR record H000502304 in the Chugoku Production environment, resulting in successful synchronization to Power BI. The permanent fix had already been released through MFTBCFFR-4059.

investigation_summary: Shikoku Fuso and Okinawa Fuso road plans completed at 4:30 AM JST, later than the expected completion time before 3:00 AM JST. The report refresh scheduled for 3:30 AM JST occurred before Load Plan completion and displayed incorrect data. The report was manually refreshed as recovery, and subsequent scheduled refreshes completed on time.

The report refresh was scheduled for 3:30 AM JST.
The report refreshed before Load Plan completion, resulting in incorrect data.
The report was manually refreshed to recover the correct data.
From the following day, reports refreshed on time and the issue was no longer present.
root_cause: The Load Plan completed after the scheduled 3:30 AM JST report refresh, causing the report to update with incomplete data.
resolution: Manually refreshed the report after Load Plan completion; subsequent report refreshes completed on time.

investigation_summary: Approval conditions and approval flow changes were implemented and verified in the UAT environment on June 17. After approval was received, the changes were deployed to the Production Environment on July 17. The incident was resolved through the production implementation of the approved approval-flow changes.
important_findings: Approval conditions were implemented for the mentioned position in the UAT environment.
The approval flow changes were verified in the UAT environment before production deployment.
The completion rule is handled by the Cubastion team.
Approval flow changes were deployed to the Production Environment on July 17.
resolution: Implemented the approved approval flow changes in the Production Environment on July 17.

investigation_summary: Re-edit JVs were not created for multiple Job Card JVs following the 04 June 2025 FDP emergency release. Investigation identified a data issue introduced during the release. The data was corrected, missing re-edit JVs and required reverse JVs were created, and functionality was confirmed to operate normally across all FDP environments.
important_findings: For I000377921, Re-edit was clicked multiple times; reverse JVs were created for applicable JVs except those created when the last Re-edit JC was closed.
The issue was caused by a data issue during the 04 June 2025 FDP emergency release.
The data issue was fixed and recovery was completed.
System functionality was confirmed to be working normally in all FDP environments.
The AMS manual was updated to prevent similar data issues.
root_cause: A data issue during the 04 June 2025 FDP emergency release.
resolution: Corrected the data issue, created missing re-edit JVs and applicable reverse JVs, and updated the AMS manual to prevent recurrence.

investigation_summary: Monthly invoice data showed incorrect Delta amount rounding because the batch calculation for Customer Pay Amount did not apply rounding at the required step. This caused values such as 0.5 to round to 1 in the invoice file's SMDO067 column, differing from Siebel UI logic. The Monthly Invoice logic was corrected in UAT8, validated with May 2025 bulk invoice data, and approved for release to Prod on June 26, 2025.
important_findings: The Customer Pay Amount rounding was missing at a required step in the batch logic used to fetch monthly invoice data.
Missing batch rounding caused 0.5 to be rounded to 1 during calculation.
The incorrect calculated value was populated in the SMDO067 column of the invoice file.
The corrected Monthly Invoice logic in UAT8 calculates rounding consistently with Siebel UI.
Bulk invoice data for May 2025 was recreated using the revised logic and approved for Prod release.
root_cause: The batch logic calculating Customer Pay Amount did not apply rounding at the required calculation step, causing incorrect Delta amount values in monthly invoice data.
resolution: Updated the Monthly Invoice batch logic in UAT8 to apply correct rounding consistent with Siebel UI; the fix was approved for deployment to Prod in the June 26 release.

investigation_summary: During recovery of MFTBCFFR-3884, the Revise Sales Posting JV logic was triggered during sync and created Revise Sales Posting Journal Vouchers for seven orders. Reverse JV data was prepared, verified, and recovery was completed in the FDP Chugoku production environment. The issue was attributed to an oversight in the manual recovery process, and the SOP will be updated to include Journal Voucher checks during SO Sync recoveries.
important_findings: Recovery of MFTBCFFR-3884 triggered Revise Sales Posting JV logic during sync.
Revise Sales Posting Journal Vouchers were created for orders E011550005, E005935534, E012619663, E003084633, E003425066, E008533799, and E003876474.
Reverse JV data was prepared for recovery and the recovery was completed in the FDP Chugoku production environment.
The incident was not caused by a system bug; it resulted from an oversight during manual recovery.
The SOP will be updated to include Journal Voucher checks in future SO Sync recoveries.
root_cause: An oversight during the manual recovery process for MFTBCFFR-3884 allowed Revise Sales Posting JV logic to trigger during sync, creating Revise Sales Posting Journal Vouchers.
resolution: Prepared reverse JV data and completed the recovery in the FDP Chugoku production environment; update the SOP to include Journal Voucher checks during SO Sync recoveries.

investigation_summary: Duplicate JVs were created during June invoicing for records manually recovered under MFTBCFFR-3723. The manual recovery did not update the "Sent Flag" to "Y", causing eligible DT01* records to be processed again. Reverse JV data was prepared for each affected environment and applied to Prod; the recovered data was scheduled to link to KB in the nightly daily batch.
important_findings: MFTBCFFR-3723 addressed JVs not being created for Line Type Color and was released on 12th June 2025.
During manual recovery for MFTBCFFR-3723, the "Sent Flag" was not updated to "Y".
Records with stamp code "MS06GP" and Line Type "4" in the DT01* file were created again during June invoicing.
The duplicate JVs affected manually recovered DT01 TOB Invoice records across FDP environments.
Reverse JV data was created for the affected records and recovery was completed on Prod.
The SOP will be updated to include validation of all recovery conditions, including the "Sent Flag".
root_cause: An oversight during the manual recovery process for MFTBCFFR-3723 left the "Sent Flag" unset instead of updating it to "Y", causing recovered records to be processed again in June invoicing and creating duplicate JVs.
resolution: Reverse JVs were created and applied on Prod for the affected records. The SOP will be updated to require validation of recovery conditions to prevent recurrence.

investigation_summary: A mismatch in Service Quote Header recovery fields was corrected in Okayama-PROD. Regression testing of Service Quote Header calculations found no code omissions. Because the affected Service Quote was old, the team could not determine whether the mismatch resulted from user operation or an error during Service Quote processing; the case was classified as rare and closed with monitoring.
important_findings: Recovery Fields in the Quote Header included a Price value of ¥17,502.
Recovery was completed in Okayama-PROD, and the cost was confirmed as corrected.
Regression of Service Quote Header calculations found no code omissions.
The affected record was an old Service Quote, preventing confirmation of whether the cause was user misoperation or Service Quote processing error.
Service Quote Header calculations will be monitored for recurrence.
resolution: Corrected the mismatched cost in the Service Quote Header recovery fields in Okayama-PROD and closed the incident with ongoing monitoring for recurrence.

investigation_summary: An Assessment Request with Assessment Purpose set to "User Purchase" could be directly mapped to an NV Quote as a Trade-in Vehicle, allowing a UV Purchase Order to be mapped to an NV Sales Order. The issue was replicated in UAT1 and the affected record was recovered. Validation was implemented for both NV Quote Trade-in and UV Quote Trade-in processes, validated in UAT, and released to Prod on July 24, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in UAT1 using NV SO# A001295706, PO# F001295707, and AR# H000047991.
AR# H000047991 had Assessment Purpose "User Purchase" and could be selected as a Trade-in Vehicle on an NV Quote.
The unrestricted assessment mapping allowed a UV Purchase Order to be mapped to an NV Sales Order.
The affected production record was recovered.
A validation message was added to prevent selection of irrelevant trade-in vehicles in NV Quote Trade-in and UV Quote Trade-in processes.
The fix was applied to Prod in the regular release on July 24, 2025.
root_cause: The NV Quote Trade-in process allowed Assessment Requests with non-trade-in Assessment Purpose values, including "User Purchase", to be directly mapped as Trade-in Vehicles.
resolution: Implemented validation restricting NV Quote and UV Quote Trade-in selection to assessments related to Trade-in assessment purposes only; released to Prod on July 24, 2025.

investigation_summary: PO allocation failures occurred in FDP Shikoku, Okayama, Aomori, and Chugoku for Parts Purchase Orders received from D2S; the issue was also observed in the SC version. Investigation determined that D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger for parts that had not been registered in order line items. Affected orders were recovered in the relevant production environments, and preventing recurrence requires order-line-item registration before cancellation.
important_findings: Current logic registers parts in order line items only when the received part is Norm(ZFTN) or Bans(ZFTS).
D2S sent ZFTX triggers directly to cancel parts that were not present in the order line items.
Cancellation and PO allocation failed because the target parts did not exist in the order line items.
The issue affected FDP and was also observed in the SC version.
Affected orders were recovered in FDP - PROD, FDPC - PROD, FDPA - PROD, and FDPO - PROD.
root_cause: D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger before the relevant part had been registered in the order line items. Since only Norm(ZFTN) and Bans(ZFTS) parts are registered under the current logic, the cancelled parts did not exist in the line items and could not be cancelled or allocated.
resolution: Recovered the affected orders in the applicable FDP production environments. To prevent recurrence, order line item registration must occur before the ZFTX cancellation trigger is processed.

investigation_summary: Additional affected records B000001718 and B000001722 were identified during recovery. Recovery of all affected records was completed. The incident was confirmed to be the same issue as MFTBCFFR-4157, where a permanent fix was being tracked.
important_findings: Two additional records with the same issue were identified: B000001718 and B000001722.
Recovery was completed for the affected records.
The issue matched MFTBCFFR-4157.
A permanent fix was being worked on under MFTBCFFR-4157.
resolution: Recovered the affected records and continued permanent-fix tracking under MFTBCFFR-4157.

investigation_summary: The affected record was recovered on June 07. Investigation and regression testing on UAT1 found that the sync process completed successfully and the issue could not be replicated; no related database errors were recorded. Error monitoring was added to the NV Quote syncing process in UAT and subsequently deployed to the production environment to capture diagnostics if the issue recurs.
important_findings: The affected record recovery was completed on June 07.
The sync process could not be reproduced as failing during tested scenarios and regression testing on UAT1.
No database errors related to user misoperation or system issues were found.
Error monitoring was implemented for the NV Quote syncing process in UAT on July 2.
Error monitoring was deployed to the production environment to identify the cause of any future sync failures.
