investigation_summary: Job Card JC#：I000031325 had a JCO created manually under SR MFTBCFFR-4124. Because an Admin user created the JCO, the Workshop Name was automatically set to the default organization. Recovery was completed, and the incident was confirmed not to be a code-related system issue.
important_findings: The JCO for Job Card JC#：I000031325 was created manually under SR MFTBCFFR-4124.
The JCO was created by an Admin user.
Manual JCO creation by an Admin user automatically set the Workshop Name to the default organization.
Recovery was successfully completed for the affected JCO.
Future manually created JCOs must have the Workshop Name set to the correct value.
root_cause: The JCO was manually created by an Admin user, causing the Workshop Name to be automatically set to the default organization.
resolution: Recovered the affected JCO and established that manually created JCOs must have the Workshop Name set to the correct value.

investigation_summary: IBOS estimate responses were not reflected because new body specification/bodywork records in the IBOS response were not created. The backend data map operation was configured as "update", which only modified existing records. The operation was changed to "upsert" in UAT so that existing records are updated and new records can be created; IBOS response testing and demonstration remained pending.
important_findings: The issue affected reflection of IBOS estimate responses for NV Body quotes.
The existing backend data map operation was set to "update", preventing creation of new body specification/bodywork records received from IBOS.
The configuration issue was associated with changes made when the Body Building sub-quote was removed from FDP.
Changing the data map operation to "upsert" allows both updates to existing records and creation of new records from the IBOS response.
The fix was reported as implemented and tested on UAT/UAT1, but end-to-end IBOS response testing was still pending.
Requested verification was to submit an NV quote with a body using "Submit to IBOS" and confirm that the IBOS quote response updates the relevant records.
root_cause: The backend data map operation was set to "update", which only updated existing records and prevented creation of new body specification/bodywork records included in IBOS estimate responses.
resolution: Changed the backend data map operation from "update" to "upsert" in UAT/UAT1, enabling IBOS responses to update existing records and create new body specification/bodywork records as needed.

investigation_summary: Affected records required recovery, which was completed and confirmed on 10 June 2025. Investigation identified an incorrect condition in the ODI View search specification that prevented D21N and D21F files from executing for user-created Chassis Orders and prevented correct display of Recycle Fee details. The ODI fix was validated in UAT and deployed to Prod on 28 June 2025.
important_findings: Recovery of the affected records was completed and confirmed on 10 June 2025.
Some affected records contained files needed for recovery; executing D21 files initially required changing the originating Chassis Order position Division from Branch to Headquarters.
The identified cause was a condition in the search specification of the ODI View.
The ODI-side fix was applied and tested successfully in the UAT environment.
After deployment, D21N and D21F files are expected to execute successfully for user-created Chassis Orders, with Recycle Fee details displayed correctly.
The change was deployed to Prod on 28 June 2025.
root_cause: A condition in the search specification of the ODI View caused the issue.
resolution: Applied and deployed an ODI-side fix to Prod on 28 June 2025 after successful UAT testing.

investigation_summary: The department code in the JV was null following manual JV creation during MFTBCFFR-4124 SR recovery. The manually created JV used an admin ID that does not have a branch, resulting in the missing department code. Recovery was completed and the validation was added to the recovery SOP.
important_findings: The department code in the JV was null.
The JV was manually created as part of MFTBCFFR-4124 SR recovery.
The manual JV creation used an admin ID that does not have a branch.
A check was added to the recovery SOP to prevent similar issues during future recoveries.
The issue was determined not to be a product bug.
root_cause: The JV was manually created using an admin ID without a branch during MFTBCFFR-4124 SR recovery, causing the department code to be null.
resolution: The recovery was completed, and the required check was added to the recovery SOP for future manual recoveries.

important_findings: Changes were deployed to FDP-UAT1.

The changes were released to Prod on 12 June 2025.

important_findings: Changes were deployed to FDP-UAT1.

The changes were approved for Prod release.
The incident was released to Prod on 12th June 2025.
resolution: Released the verified changes to Prod on 12th June 2025.

investigation_summary: Stock records were visible in SIEBEL/Siebel DB but missing from the PBI 5-02 report because they were excluded by ODI filtering conditions. The affected Shikoku parts were corrected by changing their item category to LUMF and creating/executing the required Price Master; recovery completed and the records became visible in PBI 5-02. For part #101244115, the remaining root cause was identified as an inventory update timestamp outside the effective date range of its price-list item.
important_findings: Shikoku Branch 42 parts HB06MS2, HB511, HD72T, HD72U, HD72V, and MB05A were present in SIEBEL but absent from PBI 5-02.
These parts were excluded from the PBI datamart by ODI because they failed the condition S_PRI_LST.SUBTYPE_CD = 'Parts Price List'.
The affected parts were incorrectly categorized as NORM instead of LUMF, so the expected LUMF price lists with List price and D/N price set to 0 had not been created.
After the item category was manually changed to LUMF, Price Master was created and executed, and the affected parts appeared in PBI 5-02.

Part #101244115 failed the ODI condition S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD BETWEEN S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_START_DT AND NVL(S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_END_DT,'31-12-9999') because its LAST_UPD timestamps were later than the configured EFF_END_DT of 2025-04-26.
root_cause: Invalid or missing price-list master data caused ODI exclusions: the affected parts were categorized as NORM rather than LUMF and lacked a 'Parts Price List'; for part #101244115, S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD was outside the S_PRI_LST_ITEM effective-date range.
resolution: Manually changed the affected parts' item category to LUMF, created and executed the Price Master, and completed recovery so the parts became visible in the PBI 5-02 report.

investigation_summary: The incident involved an affected record and incorrect master data/pricing. The affected record was recovered, and master files were executed on Prod, after which the master data was confirmed correct. The comments reference related SR MFTBCFFR-4044 and request verification of both LDT and SLDT.
important_findings: The affected record was recovered to allow the user to proceed.
Pricing required investigation and a fix.
Master files were executed on Prod.
Master data was confirmed correct after the master-file execution.
Both LDT and SLDT were identified for verification.
Related SR: MFTBCFFR-4044.
resolution: Executed the master files on Prod, correcting the master data; the affected record was also recovered.

important_findings: Accessibility was affected by an expired SSL certificate.
The ASCENT team identified and resolved the certificate issue.
Service operation was reported as normal after remediation.

resolution: The ASCENT team resolved the expired SSL certificate issue.

investigation_summary: Control logic was initially fixed and validated in FDP-UAT1/UAT-1, then released to PROD, including a correction for expense item "41: Other service expenses". A later review found that JC Type "32" allowed an amount despite requiring the same free-cost control as JC Types 22-51. JC Type 32 was added to the current logic in UAT1 so that all JCs from 22-51 use the same free-cost condition; production approval was requested.
important_findings: The initial fix was verified in UAT-1 and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
Expense item "41: Other service expenses" was subsequently found to be outside the control logic and was fixed in FDP-UAT1 under reference JC I001296258.
After the correction, the functionality was confirmed to work correctly in the production environment.
JC Type "32" contained an amount although it should have the same free-cost control as other free expense items in the JC Type 22-51 range.
JC Type 32 was added to the current logic in UAT1, and all JCs from 22-51 were configured with the same free-cost condition.
root_cause: JC Type "32" was not included in the existing free-cost control logic applied to JC Types 22-51, allowing an amount to be entered.
resolution: Added JC Type "32" to the current free-cost control logic in UAT1 so that all JCs from 22-51 have the same condition; approval for Production deployment was requested.

investigation_summary: Journal Voucher data for Liability Insurance Orders was not sent to KB because the department code was null. Investigation found that migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), which resulted in missing department code in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher. The impacted orders were patched, recovery JVs were created, and recovery data was added to Prod for transmission to KB in the nightly batch.
important_findings: On 22 May, a Journal Voucher was created after spreadsheet approval but was not sent to KB because its department code was not set.
Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id).
A null Primary Position Id caused the department code to be null in both the Insurance Order and the Liability Insurance Journal Voucher.
Liability Insurance Orders with status "Spreadsheet Approved" were excluded from the recovery.
PR_POSTN_ID was patched by mapping the Sales Rep's Primary Position for the impacted Insurance orders.
Recovery JVs were created and added to Prod for delivery to KB in the nightly batch.
root_cause: Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), causing the department code to be null in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher and preventing JV data from being sent to KB.
resolution: Patched PR_POSTN_ID for impacted Liability Insurance Orders using the Sales Rep's Primary Position, created recovery JVs, and added the recovery data to Prod for transmission to KB.

investigation_summary: A blank trade-in line item could be created in an NV Quote when the AR# was removed and the line item was saved during a quote revision. Replication in UAT confirmed that clearing the AR# cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id, resulting in the blank line item. A validation was implemented and tested in UAT to prevent saving a trade-in line item with a blank assessment number, then released to PROD on June 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in UAT using NV Quote #: 1-KHY8Z, Rev-3.
In NV Quote #: 1-IQZEL, Rev-2, removing AR#: H000001601 from a trade-in vehicle while creating Rev-3 and then deleting the record cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id.
A new trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001602 could then be added while the cleared asset_id caused a blank line item to display in the NV Quote.
The implemented validation prevents users from saving a trade-in line item when the AR# / assessment number is blank.
Users can still update the AR# through the standard process or delete the trade-in line item.
The UAT test record was UAT1, NV Quote #: 1-6AFG8S; the validation error message was changed to “Assessment No. is a required field and cannot be left blank.”
root_cause: The trade-in line item process allowed the AR# to be removed and the line item saved, which cleared asset_id and created a blank trade-in line item in the NV Quote.
resolution: Implemented validation in UAT and released it to PROD on June 26, 2025, preventing a trade-in line item from being saved with a blank AR# / assessment number.
technical_entities: Assessment No. is a required field and cannot be left blank.

investigation_summary: Invoice API field mappings were reviewed and updated in FDP UAT-1 to align CustomerName and DeliveryNumber values with billing requirements. CustomerName now uses Prospect Account Name when it is populated on the JC Header, otherwise Ship To Customer Name; DeliveryNumber uses Bill To Basic Account Name. The approved changes were released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
important_findings: The original CustomerName mapping populated the API value from Ship To Customer Name in the JC Header.
The mapping was revised after review of vehicle-name consistency for individual and monthly billing invoices, including change orders, versus Siebel delivery notes.
In FDP UAT-1, CustomerName is populated from Prospect Account Name when the field is not null; otherwise it is populated from Ship To Customer Name.
DeliveryNumber in the Invoice is populated from Bill To Basic Account Name.
The updated program was approved for deployment and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
root_cause: The existing Invoice API mapping always sourced CustomerName from Ship To Customer Name and did not use Prospect Account Name when it was available.
resolution: Updated the CustomerName mapping to use Prospect Account Name when populated and Ship To Customer Name when null, updated DeliveryNumber to use Bill To Basic Account Name, and released the changes to PROD on 12 June 2025.

resolution: Recovered the affected record; the underlying file-arrival-order issue is being tracked in Jira MFTBCFFR-3546.

investigation_summary: SV & PT Orders with Customer Code "0000328018" were omitted from the February EOM Bulk Invoice transfer to KB after the account closing was changed from 20 to EOM on 6 February. Bulk Invoice processing was limited to the last 30 days, excluding data from 20 January to 28 January. Recovery Bulk Invoice data was sent to the MDIS team, completing the recovery.
important_findings: Affected SV & PT Orders were I000012952, I000020814, and M000015656.
The account closing was changed from 20 to EOM on 6 February.
The orders were expected to be sent to KB on the 20th closing, but were instead deferred to the February EOM run.
Bulk Invoice logic included only the previous 30 days, so data from 20 January to 28 January was not sent to KB.
An ongoing CR will extend the Bulk Invoice range from 30 days to 60 days to prevent similar omissions.
root_cause: Bulk Invoice logic was designed to process only the last 30 days of data. Changing the account closing from 20 to EOM caused 20 January to 28 January data to fall outside the February EOM processing window.
resolution: Recovery Bulk Invoice data was sent to the MDIS team for delivery to KB; all recoveries were completed.

investigation_summary: Journal events of type "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM" could generate an incorrect Department Code. Investigation found that the Department Code was sourced from the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator instead of the relevant inventory name. The mapping was corrected, released to Prod on 2 June 2025, and recovery JVs were completed for Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku.
important_findings: For "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM", Department Code was fetched from the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator.
The corrected logic uses the Purchase Return Order inventory name as the Department Code and uses the inventory name for "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" JV lines.
The fix was deployed to UAT1 for testing before Prod release.
Recovery required reverse JV and correct JV data with the correct JV_Department_Code.
Recovery was completed in Prod for Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku and linked to KB through the daily batch.
root_cause: Incorrect Department Code mapping: the system used the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator rather than the applicable inventory name for "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM" journal events.
resolution: Updated the Department Code mapping to use inventory name, released the fix to Prod on 2 June 2025, and created reverse and corrective recovery JVs for affected orders in Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku.

investigation_summary: Statistics were not collected for tables in the Wakayama environment because the Oracle-recommended coe_Siebel_stats.sql script locked tables below its configured data-volume cutoff. The affected tables were unlocked and statistics were gathered, resolving the incident on 19 May 2025 at 13:45 JST. As a permanent measure, Wakayama will use monthly manual statistics collection through DBMS statistics instead of coe_Siebel_stats.sql.
important_findings: coe_Siebel_stats.sql locks tables with fewer rows, preventing statistics collection for those tables.
The Wakayama tables had insufficient data volume to exceed the script cutoff value.
The cutoff value is defined by the Oracle-provided and recommended script and cannot be changed by the support team.
A similar issue occurred in the FDP Hakodate environment in February 2025.
Unlocking statistics on the affected tables followed by gathering statistics restored collection.
root_cause: The Oracle-recommended coe_Siebel_stats.sql script locked Wakayama tables whose data volume was below its configured cutoff, preventing statistics from being collected.
resolution: Unlocked statistics for the affected tables and reran statistics gathering. Wakayama will manually collect statistics monthly using DBMS statistics rather than coe_Siebel_stats.sql.

important_findings: Service Change Order – Bulk Invoice is mapped to Job Card Order fields.
The Bulk Invoice and CO Delivery Slip use different mapping logic, causing the price difference.
Only Job Card Order was configured during initial development of the real time invoice interface.
Change Order was not included in the BRD for the real time Invoice CR.
A similar issue was tracked in MFTBCFFR-3251, with a fix deployed on UAT-1.
root_cause: The real time invoice interface was designed only for Job Card Order, and Change Order mapping was not included in the BRD for the real time Invoice CR, resulting in mapping logic differences between the Bulk Invoice and CO Delivery Slip.

investigation_summary: Recycle Invoice data was received on May 1, 2025, while the Invoice Calendar processing date was May 7, 2025. Under the current functionality, only files received on the same date as the monthly Invoice Calendar date are executed, so the file did not run in any FDP environment. Recovery was completed by manually processing the recycle invoice data on all FDP production environments.
important_findings: Recycle Invoice data was received on May 1, 2025, before the May 7, 2025 date configured in the Invoice Calendar.
Current functionality executes monthly files only when their receipt date matches the Invoice Calendar date.
The date mismatch prevented the Recycle Invoice data file from executing in FDP environments.
The behavior was determined to be consistent with the initial requirements and not a system bug.
A modification to support early file receipt would require an AMS CR.
Recovery was completed by manually processing the recycle invoice data on all FDP production environments.
root_cause: The Recycle Invoice data file was received before its configured Invoice Calendar date; the existing logic processes files only when the receipt date exactly matches the Invoice Calendar date.
resolution: Recycle Invoice data was manually processed for recovery on all FDP production environments.

Account code 1000007404 was created in April and was not sent to KB because the Account master bulk linkage had already been stopped before April.
MFTBCFFR-3040 identified incorrect mappings in some Account master data columns sent to KB; the incident fix was deployed to all FDP environments.
A further CR requested after MFTBCFFR-3040 is still pending development and Production deployment.
KB-side manual recovery is being performed while the Account master linkage remains suspended.
root_cause: The SIEBEL-to-KB Account master bulk interface in Shikoku Production was intentionally suspended for all accounts at Miyauchi's request until the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR is released to Production, following incorrect Account master column mappings.
resolution: The incident was closed as expected behavior; KB-side manual recovery is ongoing, and the Account master linkage will remain suspended until the pending CR is developed and released to Production.

investigation_summary: Chassis Orders files were processed but the corresponding orders were not created because the ODI database storage was full when the files were scheduled to execute. All previously unprocessed files were executed and impacted data was verified. Automatic ODI storage expansion was implemented, and the recovery manual was updated to improve recovery response.
important_findings: ODI database storage was completely full when the affected files were scheduled for execution, preventing file execution.
Chassis Orders were recovered after the failed files were re-executed.
All files affected by the ODI database storage limit were executed, and impacted data was verified.
Mail notification was received when files were not executed; the notification system itself had no issue.
An automatic mechanism was implemented to increase ODI database storage capacity when its limit is reached.
The recovery manual was updated to make recovery more efficient and ensure recovery proceeds while delays are communicated.
root_cause: ODI database storage was completely full when the affected files were scheduled for execution, so the files could not execute and Chassis Orders were not created.
resolution: Re-executed all unprocessed files, verified impacted data, implemented automatic ODI database storage expansion, and updated the recovery manual.

investigation_summary: Affected Vehicle records displayed the Fuso Reception Number as the Chassis Number instead of the combination of Stamped Model Code and C# number, while C# was present. Initial analysis attributed unprocessed D21G files to exhausted ODI database storage, but later analysis attributed the condition to SC-to-FDP Chugoku data migration; both explanations were challenged because affected chassis numbers were confirmed after transfer. Records were repeatedly recovered, including recurrence A050266885, but the timeline does not establish a validated root cause or confirmed permanent fix.
important_findings: The reported symptom was that the Chassis Number remained the Fuso Reception Number while C# was displayed; the expected Chassis Number format was Stamped Model Code plus C# number.
An initial finding stated that ODI database storage reached its limit, preventing D21G file execution and VIN updates; an incremental ODI storage expansion mechanism was reportedly implemented.
A later comparison of FDP Chugoku Vehicle Data with SC Production identified records where Fuso Reception Number was used as Chassis Number despite non-null Stamped Model Code and C# number.
The issue recurred for record A050266885 on 2025-08-06 and the record was manually recovered.

Support repeatedly classified the issue as SC-to-FDP Chugoku migrated data, but this was disputed because chassis-number confirmation occurs after transfer and affected May 2025 chassis were reported.
Affected Vehicle records were recovered, but the requester continued to request confirmation of the corrective action and completion date.

D21F was received before D21E, preventing Recycle Fee Order creation for the affected VINs.

Recovery was completed for all affected records in FDP environments.
Kaizen activity was in progress to monitor and proactively recover similar file-ordering events.
root_cause: D21F file receipt before D21E file caused Recycle Fee Order not to be created for the affected VINs.
resolution: Recovered all affected records in FDP environments; ongoing monitoring and proactive recovery are tracked in MFTBCFFR-3546.

investigation_summary: The March 31 Bulk Invoice file from Cubastion showed that all referenced JCs were successfully sent from Siebel to KB, so the Bulk Invoice process was operating normally. The investigation identified that the Account master linkage from Siebel to KB had been intentionally suspended for all accounts in Shikoku Production pending deployment of the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR. KB was performing manual recovery while the interface remained suspended, and the incident was closed as not being a system issue.
important_findings: All referenced JCs were included in the March EOM (March 31) Bulk Invoice file and were successfully sent to KB.
Siebel sends Bulk Invoice data to KB; no information was available regarding CSS Invoice processing.
MFTBCFFR-3040 addressed incorrect mapping in some Account master data columns sent to KB; the incident fix was deployed to all FDP environments.
A further CR requested after MFTBCFFR-3040 remained pending for Production deployment.
Under MFTBCFFR-3149, the complete Account master interface was stopped in Shikoku Production for all accounts, not only specific account codes.
Account code 1000007404, created in April, was not sent to KB because Account master bulk processing had been stopped before April.
root_cause: The complete Account master linkage from Siebel to KB was intentionally suspended in Shikoku Production at Miyauchi's request until the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR is deployed to Production.
resolution: KB performed manual recovery while the Account master linkage remained suspended pending CR development and Production deployment; the incident was closed as not being a system issue.

investigation_summary: In a Payer Change Order, changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not refresh the Closed Date from the newly selected payer. The retained old Closed Date prevented the change order from being processed at EOM (31 March), and the JC lines and change order lines were instead sent to KB on 20 April. The issue was identified as similar to MFTBCFFR-3672 and was tracked through that incident.
important_findings: Bill to Basic Account and Ship to basic account values are initially fetched from JCO when a Payer Change Order is created.
Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account should update Closed Date and Payment term based on the new payer.
Closed Date retained its previous value after the payer change and was not updated to EOM (31 March).
K000076384 was output in billing data on 20 April rather than at the end of March.
The issue was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3672.
root_cause: Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not update the Closed Date value in the Payer Change Order, leaving the previous date and preventing EOM processing.

investigation_summary: Journal Voucher department code assignment for employee D8NOOSHI failed because the Employee master contained an incorrect department assignment for the employee's Branch CS Staff position. Department code 0108, a Headquarter department code, was assigned instead of the appropriate branch department. The Employee master data was corrected, and subsequent Journal Vouchers populated the correct department code.
important_findings: D8NOOSHI created Job Cards with a Branch CS Staff position, but the department code was not fetched correctly.
The Employee master had department code 0108 assigned to the Branch CS Staff position; 0108 is a Headquarter department code.
The incorrect Employee master department assignment caused the Branch CS Staff position to be created with an HQ department and caused the Journal Voucher to fail.
After correcting D8NOOSHI's Employee master department code, the correct department code was populated in Journal Vouchers.
Okinawa Prod Job Card I000035491, created by D8NOOSHI and closed on 2025/05/30 10:56:21 AM, confirmed the corrected Journal Voucher department code.
root_cause: Incorrect Employee master data assigned Headquarter department code 0108 to employee D8NOOSHI's Branch CS Staff position.
resolution: Corrected the Employee master department code for D8NOOSHI; Journal Vouchers subsequently populated the correct department code.

investigation_summary: The affected record was recovered successfully. Investigation identified several workflow steps that could be contributing to the issue, with additional error handling planned for a release scheduled for 14 May 2025. The incident was determined to be similar to MFTBCFFR-3740 and was transferred to that ticket for further handling.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the affected record.
Several workflow steps were identified as potential contributors to the issue.
Additional error handling was planned for the identified workflow steps in the 14 May 2025 release.
Further investigation and reproduction attempts in the UAT environment were planned.
The issue was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3740 because it was similar to that incident.
resolution: The affected record was recovered, and follow-up corrective work was moved to MFTBCFFR-3740.

investigation_summary: Fields missing from accounts migrated from SC to Chugoku were investigated. The fields were absent from Account Creation packages used by other FDPs and were therefore not included in the SC to Chugoku migration package. Recovery was completed for all affected accounts.
important_findings: The affected fields were not available in Account Creation packages for other FDPs.
The fields were omitted from the migration package from SC to Chugoku.
Recovery was completed for all affected accounts.
A list of recovered accounts was attached.
root_cause: The affected fields were not included in the SC to Chugoku migration package because they were not present in Account Creation packages for other FDPs.
resolution: Completed recovery for all affected accounts and provided an attached list of recovered accounts.

investigation_summary: For NV Quote 1-2KHAWY, the Branch Manager name displayed in BIP was investigated. BIP derives this value from the Department Master, specifically the record associated with Department Code 3011, rather than from Employee Master. The required correction is to update "BIP_NVUV_name" in the Department Master through a Service Request.
important_findings: BIP derives the Branch Manager name from the Department Master, not Employee Master.
For NV Quote 1-2KHAWY, the displayed value is associated with Department Code 3011.
This BIP behavior was implemented through a CR submitted by Sasaki, Takuya (575) in July 2024.
The identified data correction is to update "BIP_NVUV_name" in the Department Master.
Department Master changes require a Service Request (SR).
root_cause: The Branch Manager name in BIP was sourced from the Department Master record for Department Code 3011 rather than from Employee Master.
resolution: Correct "BIP_NVUV_name" in the Department Master by raising a Service Request (SR).

investigation_summary: The issue was reproduced in FDP UAT-4 for JC I000034940 and Invoice 1-36721159. When the Service Invoice (Planned Expense) "Expense Planning Status" was "Open", the "Bill To Account Code" field remained editable. A user cleared the field after creating the planned expense from the "Shaken Expense Creation" button on the JC header, causing the incident; it was classified as user mis-operation.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced in FDP UAT-4.
For Service Invoice (Planned Expense) records with "Expense Planning Status" set to "Open", "Bill To Account Code" was editable on the UI.
The user cleared "Bill To Account Code" after creating a planned expense using the "Shaken Expense Creation" button on the JC header.
The incident was identified as user mis-operation.
Making "Bill To Account Code" read-only was proposed to prevent similar user errors.
root_cause: User mis-operation: the user cleared the editable "Bill To Account Code" field while the Service Invoice (Planned Expense) "Expense Planning Status" was "Open".

investigation_summary: Affected records, including A000020793, were recovered, and no additional records requiring recovery were identified. Investigation confirmed that Activity statuses could be manually changed through the UI and were not automatically set to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) was set to "Closed". A fix was implemented and verified in UAT 1.
important_findings: The affected records were recovered, and no other records requiring recovery were found.
The issue was replicated during investigation.
Users could manually perform all Activity status transitions through the UI: Open → Request for Reservation → Reservation Confirmed → Work Completed → Closed.
Activity status did not automatically update to "Work Completed" when the Job Card (JC) status was set to "Closed".
The implemented fix updates Activity status to "Work Completed" regardless of its previous status and makes it read-only afterward.
The fix was implemented and confirmed to work as expected in UAT 1.
root_cause: The Activity status was not automatically synchronized to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) status changed to "Closed", while users could manually modify Activity statuses through the UI.
resolution: Implemented a fix in UAT 1 that automatically sets the Activity status to "Work Completed" when the Job Card (JC) status is set to "Closed", regardless of the prior Activity status, and makes the Activity status read-only after the update.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned activity status changes in the UI and the relationship between Activity status and Job Card (JC) status. Investigation confirmed that users could manually perform all standard Activity status transitions. A fix was implemented so that closing a JC automatically sets the Activity status to "Work Completed" and makes it read-only; it was validated in UAT 1 and released to production on 26 May 2025.
important_findings: The standard Activity status flow is "Open" → "Request for Reservation" → "Reservation Confirmed" → "Work Completed" → "Closed".
Users were able to manually change Activity status through the UI, including all standard transitions.
When Job Card (JC) status is set to "Closed", the fix updates the Activity status to "Work Completed" regardless of its prior status.
After an Activity status is updated to "Work Completed", the status becomes read-only and cannot be manually modified.
The fix was implemented and validated in UAT 1 before release to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.
root_cause: The UI allowed users to manually modify Activity status, and Activity status was not automatically set to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) status was set to "Closed".
resolution: Implemented automatic Activity status update to "Work Completed" when JC status is set to "Closed", regardless of previous Activity status, and made the Activity status read-only after that update. The fix was validated in UAT 1 and released to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.

investigation_summary: Profit values differed between Sales Quote, Sales Order, and Power BI in PROD. Investigation identified synchronization discrepancies between quote and order records, including mismatched product_id values between order_item and corresponding quote_item and line-item count mismatches. Manual data patching was completed in Siebel for affected production records, but a Power BI mismatch remained for AR# H000001001 and PBI-side validation was still in progress.
important_findings: Some production records had mismatched product_id values between order_item and the corresponding quote_item.
The affected records were attributed to synchronization discrepancies between quotes and orders.
Line-item count mismatches were identified for 91 records in Chugoku Prod and 1 record in Okayama Prod.
Manual data patching was completed in Siebel, and Sales Profit for UV Sales Orders was confirmed synchronized with the respective UV Sales Quotes.
Power BI still showed an unmatched value for AR# H000001001: Sales Quote and Sales Order were 1,105,936, while PBI was 1,107,086.
The Power BI display was also reported to be missing comma thousand separators.
root_cause: Synchronization discrepancies between quote and order records, including mismatched product_id values and line-item count mismatches.

investigation_summary: The incident involved Job Cards with mismatched Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id. A total of 47 affected Job Cards were identified. The Job Cards were recovered in Chugoku Prod using the same approach as SC prod, and verification confirmed that Chassis# and Asset# were synchronized correctly in Chuugoku-PROD VM.
important_findings: The issue was caused by a mismatch between Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id on Job Cards.
47 Job Cards had the same mismatch issue.
Recovery required changing either the Asset Id or MF Vehicle Id for the affected Job Cards.
The affected Job Cards were recovered in Chugoku Prod using the same method as SC prod.
Post-recovery verification on Chuugoku-PROD VM confirmed Chassis# and Asset# were in sync.
root_cause: Mismatch between Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id on Job Cards.
resolution: Recovered the affected Job Cards in Chugoku Prod using the SC prod recovery approach; verification confirmed Chassis# and Asset# synchronization.

investigation_summary: The Invoice CustomerName mapping was reviewed because it was selecting different customer sources based on the Cash Receipt Flag on the JC Header. An interim UAT-1 change mapped CustomerName to Prospect Account Name when the flag was Y, but the final validated requirement was to always use Ship To Customer Name. The final mapping was approved for PROD deployment, with release planned for 14 May.
important_findings: The original CustomerName logic used Vehicle Owner Name when Cash Receipt Flag was Y and Ship To Customer Name when it was N.
An interim FDP UAT-1 change mapped CustomerName to Prospect Account Name when Cash Receipt Flag was Y.
The final FDP UAT-1 mapping sets CustomerName from Ship To Customer Name regardless of the Cash Receipt Flag value.
Validation confirmed CustomerName uses the JC customer even when the Vehicle Owner in the vehicle master differs from the JC customer.
The final Xlms value was validated and approved for PROD deployment.
root_cause: CustomerName was mapped conditionally to Vehicle Owner Name or other sources based on the Cash Receipt Flag, instead of consistently using Ship To Customer Name.
resolution: Updated the CustomerName tag mapping in FDP UAT-1 to use Ship To Customer Name regardless of Cash Receipt Flag, validated the results, and approved the change for PROD release on 14 May.

investigation_summary: The issue involving UV Sales Quote#: 1-M9530 could not be reproduced in the UAT/UAT5 environment despite code-level investigation. No recovery was performed. The user was instructed to proceed using a Revised Quote, while recurrence will continue to be monitored.
important_findings: The issue could not be reproduced in the UAT environment using UAT5 reference record UV Sales Quote#: 1-M9530.
The investigation included code-level analysis, but no confirmed cause was reported.
The proposed recovery and update of the UV Sales Quote status to "Rejected" was declined.
The user was instructed to respond using a Revised Quote.
The team will monitor for recurrence of similar events.
resolution: No recovery was performed; the user was instructed to proceed with a Revised Quote.

investigation_summary: Users could not create an account from Landscape and the system became unresponsive when using the Customer & Company Name "K-Design Co., Ltd.". Investigation identified an Account Name validation that requires full-width characters and rejects half-width characters in the submitted name. The incident was classified as a user operational error and closed after the cause was confirmed.
important_findings: Account Name validation requires full-width characters.
Creating an account from Landscape with the Customer & Company Name "K-Design Co., Ltd." caused the system to become unresponsive.
Creating an account with "K-Design Co., Ltd." produced a validation error because half-width characters are not allowed.
The incident was determined to be caused by user input/operation rather than a system defect.
root_cause: The Account Name contained half-width characters, which violated the validation requiring full-width characters.
resolution: The cause was communicated and the Jira incident was closed as a user operational error.

investigation_summary: A Consumption Tax JV line was missing for the "Job Card Sales CT" journal event because a search specification evaluated a consumption tax amount of 0.8 as zero. The search specification was corrected to use the proper rounding behavior, validated in UAT-1/UAT-01, and released to Production on 14 May.
important_findings: JV line creation uses a Search Specification to prevent creation of zero-amount JV lines.
The consumption tax amount of 0.8 should have been rounded to 1.
Incorrect rounding in the Search Specification treated 0.8 as 0.
As a result, no JV line was created for the "Job Card Sales CT" journal event.
The affected JC was recovered and the Consumption Tax JV was added in Production.
The corrected Search Specification was tested in UAT-1/UAT-01 and released to Production on 14 May.
root_cause: The Search Specification used to determine whether a tax amount was zero applied incorrect rounding, causing consumption tax amount 0.8 to be treated as 0 and suppressing creation of the "Job Card Sales CT" JV line.
resolution: Corrected the Search Specification rounding behavior, validated the fix in UAT-1/UAT-01, released it to Production on 14 May, and recovered the affected JC by adding the Consumption Tax JV in Production.

investigation_summary: A Sales Quote remained in Pending Approval after approval generation because the user ID was updated after the Generate Approval action. Testing in the UAT environment confirmed that approval functionality worked correctly for the same user position. Recovery was subsequently completed for the affected quote, and the user was instructed to proceed.
important_findings: The affected user ID was updated after the Generate Approval button was triggered.
A similar record was reproduced in the UAT environment, where the Generate Approval/Request Approval functionality worked correctly for the same position.
The Sales Quote was initially still in Pending Approval after the first reported recovery and required further verification.
Recovery was completed for the affected quote.
The incident was classified as user mis-operation.
root_cause: User mis-operation: the UID was updated after Generate Approval was triggered, leaving the Sales Quote in Pending Approval.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected Sales Quote, allowing the user to proceed.

investigation_summary: Department Code was null in JV records for orders whose Job Cards were created by Headquarter users without a Branch ID. The current logic derives Department Code from the Branch Code on the Job Card and Service Purchase Order. Recovery was completed by linking the correct JV to KB and adding the correct Department Code before the night batch; the permanent fix was transferred to MFTBCFFR-3920.
important_findings: Department Code became null in JV when a Headquarter user without a Branch ID created the Job Card.
Current logic sets Department Code from the Branch Code on the Job Card and Service Purchase Order.
Recovery involved linking the correct JV to KB and adding the correct Department Code from the JC or SPO before the night batch.
The required permanent logic for records created by non-branch users was moved to MFTBCFFR-3920.
The branch or Department Code to assign for Headquarter users required confirmation.
root_cause: A Headquarter user without a Branch ID created the Job Card, while the existing logic derives Department Code from the Job Card and Service Purchase Order Branch Code, resulting in a null Department Code in JV.
resolution: Completed recovery by linking the correct JV to KB and populating the Department Code before the night batch. Permanent fix work was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3920.

investigation_summary: The incident affected the same user repeatedly and required recovery actions so the user could proceed with approval. Engineering attempted to reproduce the issue, reviewed code, and examined runtime events and signals, but could not reproduce it in the UAT environment. The ticket was closed as unresolved after discussion with the business side because Cubastion could not identify the cause.
important_findings: Recovery actions were completed, allowing the user to proceed with approval.
The issue recurred for the same user after recovery.
Engineering could not reproduce the incident despite repeated investigation attempts.
Investigation included code review and examination of runtime events and signals.
The incident could not be reproduced in the UAT environment.
Cubastion could not identify the cause; the ticket was closed unresolved.

investigation_summary: The RCA was shared via email, but its technical content is not present in the Jira comments. The Sales Order was expected to reflect after load completion, and the ticket was requested to be rejected.
important_findings: The RCA was communicated outside Jira via email.
The Sales Order was expected to reflect after load completion.
A request was made to reject the ticket.

investigation_summary: The NV Quote process stopped because loading the Parts and Internal Work View was delayed. Investigation found no code issue; a database-level query delayed data retrieval. The data retrieval process was optimized, significantly reducing view load time and resolving the issue.
important_findings: The NV Quote process was impacted.
No issue was identified in the code.
A database-level query caused delays fetching the Parts and Internal Work View.
Optimizing data retrieval significantly reduced loading time for the Parts and Internal Work View.
root_cause: A database-level query caused delayed retrieval of the Parts and Internal Work View.
resolution: Optimized the data retrieval process for the Parts and Internal Work View.

investigation_summary: Incorrect Total PO Cost on the Service Purchase Order (SPO) was investigated in UAT1 for SPO J001294885 and JC I001294884. The behavior was caused by the configured labor-line quantity calculation logic for labor code .004330, not a system defect. Changing the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N corrected the SPO value, and the incident was withdrawn.
important_findings: For labor code .004330, Quantity Requested defaults to 1 when Zero Effort Flag is Y, Billing Type is not Customer, and PO Cost Flag is N.
The Quantity Requested default of 1 is applied regardless of actual labor effort or operation time.
The resulting Total PO Cost can be higher than the actual cost because it is calculated using the default quantity of 1.
The behavior is designed according to the existing validation rules.
Changing the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N caused the correct value to be reflected in the SPO in UAT1.
root_cause: Labor code .004330 was configured with Zero Effort Flag = Y, Billing Type other than Customer, and PO Cost Flag = N, which triggered designed logic that defaulted Quantity Requested to 1 and produced an incorrect Total PO Cost.
resolution: Changed the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N in UAT1, which corrected the value in the SPO. The incident was withdrawn as a flag-setting issue rather than a system issue.

investigation_summary: Users encountered an error when using "Go To Account" from the "Search in Siebel" view, affecting multiple FDP environments. The issue was fixed and validated in UAT-01/UAT-1, where "Go To Account" correctly navigated users to the All Accounts view in the Accounts screen. After UAT approval, the fix was released to Prod on 14 May.
important_findings: Users had access privileges to the relevant view; the issue occurred when using "Go To Account" from "Search in Siebel".
The previous behavior produced an error when users clicked "Go To Account" after searching for an Account Name.
The corrected behavior navigates users to the All Accounts view in the Accounts screen.
The same issue affected other FDPs and the release was planned for all FDPs.
UAT-1 validation confirmed that the error no longer occurred before production approval.
resolution: Implemented the fix in UAT-01/UAT-1, obtained UAT approval, and released the fix to Prod on 14 May.

investigation_summary: JCO Payment Term values were affected when Payer Basic Account Code did not align with the Bill To account after account changes. Investigation confirmed that Payment Term and Payer Basic Account Code are populated from the Bill To Basic Account Code in the JC Header. The mapping was corrected so Payer and Sold To values synchronize with Bill To, validated in FDP UAT-1, and released to PROD.
important_findings: Payment Term and Payer Basic Account Code are populated based on the Bill To Basic Account Code selected in the JC Header.
JCOs with missing Payment Term had a different Payer Basic Account Code than JCOs without the issue.
If the Payer Account Code is invalid, Payment Term can be blank because the value cannot be referenced from Account Code (AR).
Payer Code and Name are sourced from Bill To Customer.
All Sold To values also needed to be mapped to Bill To because Sold To fields are hidden in the FDP version.
The fix could not be reproduced in UAT after deployment and was released to PROD on 26 June.
root_cause: Payer Basic Account Code and Sold To values were not consistently mapped/synchronized to the Bill To account in the JC, causing Payment Term lookup failures when the Payer Account Code differed from or was invalid for the Bill To account.
resolution: Updated the FDP UAT-1 mapping so Payer To and Sold To values synchronize with Bill To of the JC; the validated fix was released to PROD on 26 June.
technical_entities: Payer Mapping Change(Bill To Customer Code).xlsx

investigation_summary: Individual invoice generation failed for JCO# I050019559 because the Branch Code used for issuance did not match the creator's Primary Branch Code. The behavior was confirmed as consistent with current functionality and similar to MFTBCFFR-3534. The incident was rejected as no product defect was identified.
important_findings: JCO# I050019559 was created by user D8TKANEM.
The creator's Primary Branch Code was UG.
Individual invoice issuance used Branch Code 7331, mapped to UF, which did not match UG.
The Branch Code mismatch caused individual invoice generation to fail.
A blank Closed Date does not affect individual invoice issuance.
The behavior is consistent with current functionality and similar to MFTBCFFR-3534.
root_cause: The Branch Code used to generate the individual invoice (7331 → UF) did not match the JCO creator's Primary Branch Code (UG).
resolution: No system change was made; the incident was rejected because the behavior was working as per current functionality.

investigation_summary: The incident was identified as a data migration issue that occurred after the FDPC go-live. The affected records were recovered and the issue was closed.
important_findings: The issue was attributed to data migration after the FDPC go-live.
Affected records were successfully recovered.
root_cause: Data migration issue occurring since the FDPC go-live.
resolution: Recovered the affected records.

investigation_summary: Affected quote records were recovered, allowing users to continue the quote process by clicking "Generate Approval". Investigation confirmed that user "D8TDAINO" invoked the button for all affected quote numbers, but the user's position was "SCHQ-BizMgmt-Staff" rather than the required "Branch-Sales-Staff". Users must perform the operation with a valid user ID assigned the required position.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the affected quote records.
"Generate Approval" was invoked by user "D8TDAINO" for all affected quote numbers.
User "D8TDAINO" had the "SCHQ-BizMgmt-Staff" position.
Approval flow conditions require the "Generate Approval" operation to be performed by a user with the "Branch-Sales-Staff" position.
root_cause: The "Generate Approval" button was executed by user "D8TDAINO", whose position was "SCHQ-BizMgmt-Staff", while the approval flow requires "Branch-Sales-Staff".
resolution: Recovered the affected quote records and instructed users to click "Generate Approval" using a valid user ID with the "Branch-Sales-Staff" position.

investigation_summary: Duplicate journal vouchers (JVs) were created when IBOS returned duplicate responses for a single record. Affected JVs were recovered using reverse JVs, with daily monitoring in Chugoku until a permanent fix was deployed. The fix was deployed and tested in UAT-01, where JVs were created only once, and was released to PROD through an emergency release on May 19.
important_findings: Duplicate responses from the IBOS system for a single record caused duplicate journal vouchers (JVs) to be created.
Affected duplicate JVs were corrected by creating reverse JVs.
Daily monitoring was performed in the Chugoku environment, with duplicate JVs removed before the daily night batch when detected.
The fix was deployed to UAT-01 and testing showed that a JV was created only once.
The production fix was released through an emergency release completed on May 19.
root_cause: IBOS returned duplicate responses for a single record, resulting in duplicate JV creation.
resolution: A fix was deployed and validated in UAT-01, then released to PROD through an emergency release on May 19. Duplicate JV records were recovered using reverse JVs while daily monitoring continued until the permanent fix was deployed.

investigation_summary: During migration to FDP-Chugoku, duplicate vehicle records with the same VIN/Fuso Reception Number caused the first matching vehicle to be mapped to Purchase Orders instead of the correct vehicle. The incorrect mapping to Chassis Orders prevented creation of Recycle Fee Orders and Pool Cost Orders. Recovery required correcting vehicle mappings, executing TOB files, restoring related Chassis, Sales, and Body Orders, and resolving a duplicate recycle fee order; final verification reported no further recovery required.
important_findings: SC data was confirmed correct; the issue occurred during migration to FDP-Chugoku.
Serial numbers were identified from Purchase Orders, and duplicate vehicle data caused the first vehicle with the same VIN to be selected regardless of SC data.
Incorrect vehicle-to-Chassis Order mapping resulted in missing Recycle Fee Orders and Pool Cost Orders.
Recovery initially updated only Chassis Orders; affected Sales Orders and Body Orders also required recovery.
A remaining record had conflicting model codes FK62FK4J, FQ62FU6B, and FK65FK4, with product code 012 identified as invalid/garbage data.
A duplicate recycle fee order was identified and recovered.
root_cause: A data-migration matching issue: duplicate vehicle records with the same VIN/Fuso Reception Number caused the first matching vehicle to be linked to Purchase Orders and Chassis Orders instead of the correct vehicle.
resolution: Correct vehicle records were re-linked to affected Chassis Orders, TOB files were executed, related Sales Orders and Body Orders were recovered, and the duplicate recycle fee order was recovered. The recovered records were subsequently verified and reported as requiring no further recovery.

investigation_summary: Recoveries were completed for the FDP environments, including wakayama and chugoku prod for the referenced order. The environments were monitored for additional affected orders, and the incident was closed at the requester’s direction.
important_findings: Recoveries were completed for the FDP environments.
wakayama and chugoku prod were referenced as recovered environments.
Monitoring continued for other potentially affected orders.
The incident was closed after recovery completion.
resolution: Completed recoveries for the FDP environments and monitored for any additional affected orders.

investigation_summary: Purchase Orders were created by user D8NOOSHI, who belongs to the Headquarter division and therefore had no Branch Code. Because the Journal Voucher Department Code is derived from the Branch Code, it was blank. Recovery was completed by setting Branch Code to 10, and the user was to update the employee master.
important_findings: User D8NOOSHI is part of the Headquarter division and did not have a Branch Code.
The Journal Voucher Department Code is populated from the Branch Code.
Blank Branch Code caused the Department Code in the Journal Voucher to be blank.
Recovery was performed by setting Branch Code to 10 for the affected records.
The issue was determined not to be a system issue; the employee master required updating.
root_cause: User D8NOOSHI's employee master did not contain a Branch Code because the user belongs to the Headquarter division, resulting in a blank Journal Voucher Department Code derived from that Branch Code.
resolution: Set Branch Code to 10 for the affected records and update the user's employee master.

investigation_summary: Investigation found that 10 JVs associated with the provided Segment2 codes were affected: 5 were created from Chassis orders migrated from SC, and 5 were mapped to dummy Chassis orders. The issue resulted from duplicate vehicles created during data migration. Recovery for the affected JVs was completed, and the underlying duplicate-vehicle issue had already been handled in MFTBCFFR-3538.
important_findings: 10 JVs were identified for the provided Segment2 codes.
5 JVs were created from Chassis orders migrated from SC.
5 JVs were mapped to dummy Chassis orders, which was identified as incorrect.
Duplicate vehicles were created due to a data migration issue.
Recovery for the affected JVs was completed.
The underlying issue was handled through MFTBCFFR-3538.
root_cause: A data migration issue created duplicate vehicles, causing JVs to be associated with dummy Chassis orders.
resolution: Completed recovery for the affected JVs; the duplicate-vehicle data migration issue was fixed through MFTBCFFR-3538.

investigation_summary: Journal vouchers (JV) were missing for Chassis Orders migrated from SC to Chugoku Production. The Siebel Job that creates JVs did not select the migrated orders because their Batch RF Status was "Sent to Create RF", which is not included in the job's filter criteria. The affected orders were recovered, and JVs will be created automatically for remaining orders once their status becomes "Shipment Instructed".
important_findings: The JV creation process is executed by a Siebel Job for Chassis Orders.
The Siebel Job selects orders with Status = "Shipment Instructed" and Batch RF Status in ("Send Shipment to RF", "Send Create to RF", "").
Orders migrated from SC to Chugoku Production had Batch RF Status "Sent to Create RF", so they were excluded from JV creation.
383 missing-GR JV records were identified and provided in the recovery attachment.
JV creation under the existing logic applies only to orders with Status = "Shipment Instructed".
root_cause: Migrated Chassis Orders from SC to Chugoku Production had Batch RF Status "Sent to Create RF", which did not match the Siebel Job filter values for JV creation.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected orders. Remaining orders will generate JVs automatically after their status is updated to "Shipment Instructed".

investigation_summary: A user's editable responsibility and editable view access were assigned by employee master execution on the night of 10 April, but the changes were not reflected because the employee had not logged out. The user later confirmed the screen was operational and editable. The AMS procedure will be updated to require a system restart after employee master execution.
important_findings: Employee master execution assigned the editable responsibility to the user on the night of 10 April.
The updated employee responsibility and editable view access were not reflected while the employee remained logged in.
The issue was not identified as a system bug.
The user confirmed that the screen became operational and could be edited.
A system restart after employee master execution can prevent recurrence.
root_cause: The employee did not log out after employee master execution, so the updated responsibility and editable view access were not reflected.
resolution: The user was able to edit the screen after the access changes became effective. The AMS procedure will be updated to perform a system restart after employee master execution.

investigation_summary: The investigation confirmed that users can select more than 10 records, but the current functionality limits selection to a maximum of 20 records. The same limit applies in both FDP and SC. The requester accepted the documented behavior and requested incident closure.
important_findings: More than 10 records can be selected.
Selection is limited to a maximum of 20 records under the current functionality.
The 20-record limit is consistent in both FDP and SC.
Changing the selection limit would require an AMS-CR.
root_cause: The current functionality enforces a maximum selection limit of 20 records.
resolution: Confirmed the existing 20-record selection limit; no system change was made, and the incident was closed at the requester's approval.

investigation_summary: Vehicle PFB34118-8055 generated an error when the Done button was pressed because its deregistration data was inconsistent. The Date of Deregistration was blank while the De-registration flag was set to 'Y'. The De registration Flag was updated to 'N' to allow processing to continue, and an SR was requested to track the master-data change.
important_findings: Vehicle PFB34118-8055 had a blank Date of Deregistration with the De-registration flag set to 'Y'.
This data mismatch caused an error when pressing the Done button.
Multiple vehicles in Chugoku Prod had the same blank Date of Deregistration and De-registration flag 'Y' condition.
For the same vehicles in FDP, the SC version had a non-null De registration Date and the flag set to 'Y'.
The De registration Flag for the affected vehicle was updated to 'N'.
root_cause: Inconsistent master data: the De-registration flag was set to 'Y' while the required Date of Deregistration field was blank.
resolution: Updated the De registration Flag for vehicle PFB34118-8055 to 'N' and requested a service request (SR) to track the master-data change.

investigation_summary: TOB transmissions triggered after 5:00 PM JST could receive no TOB response, preventing Siebel from identifying the asynchronous transaction as failed and retrying it the following morning. The issue was observed across multiple FDP records and had a similar incident in SC. A countermeasure was developed in UAT1 to retrigger records with completed interfaces but no TOB response, but no completed UAT, production deployment, or final resolution was confirmed.
important_findings: Normally, TOB triggers sent after 5:00 PM JST are not accepted and result in a Siebel asynchronous-transaction failure.
For affected records, TOB did not return a response, so Siebel did not mark the record as failed and the next-day batch job did not retrigger it.
The behavior was observed across multiple records in all FDP environments and was also associated with an incident in SC: INC4990796.
The proposed countermeasure is to retrigger records for which the interface is completed but no TOB response is received.
The retrigger logic must avoid resubmission on days when TOB is not open, such as Sundays.
Development of the proposed fix was completed in UAT1, but UAT completion and deployment were not confirmed.
root_cause: TOB did not return a response for requests triggered after 5:00 PM JST. As a result, Siebel did not classify the asynchronous transaction as failed, so its next-day batch job did not resend the affected records.

investigation_summary: The incident involved Journal Vector (JV) creating non-taxable line items when the related Sales Price was "0", including after Change Order processing. Initial UAT1 fixes addressed re-edit and Price Change scenarios, but validation found the issue persisted for Payer Change and Price and Payer Change scenarios. The additional fix was validated in UAT-1, and the incident was deployed to PROD on 12 June 2025.
important_findings: For taxable Account Codes, all line items are taxable, but Change Order (Price Change) could generate Non-Tax Line Items with a value of "Zero" in the Journal Vector.
The initial UAT1 correction passed JC Close, JC Close And Re-Edit, and JC Close And Change Order (Price Change) scenarios for both Tax and Non-Tax cases.
UAT-1 validation found [Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable] line items were still created when Sales Price was "0" for Payer Change and Price and Payer Change scenarios.
After the follow-up fix, Payer Change scenarios no longer created a JV line item when Sales Price was "0".
UAT was completed and the fix was released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
root_cause: The zero-value line-item suppression did not cover Change Order workflows involving Payer Change or Price and Payer Change, allowing [Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable] JV line items to be created when Sales Price was "0".
resolution: Updated the UAT1/UAT-1 fix to suppress JV line-item creation for zero Sales Price in Payer Change scenarios; the correction was validated in UAT and deployed to PROD on 12 June 2025.

investigation_summary: The "Create PO" button remained inactive for item #1 because a PO already existed for the item. PO F000072028 was linked to item #1 and had reached the "Acceptance Verification Done" status, preventing creation of another PO. The incident was classified as user mis-operation and rejected.
important_findings: The "Create PO" button is intended to become active after sales are recorded for specified sales positions.
A PO already existed for item #1: F000072028.
The user manually corrected the bodywork unit price while processing PO F000072028.
PO F000072028 was linked to item #1 and had status "Acceptance Verification Done", which prevented creation of a new PO for that item.
The required corrective action was to cancel the existing PO before creating a new PO.
root_cause: User mis-operation: an existing PO, F000072028, was already linked to item #1 and was in "Acceptance Verification Done" status, preventing a new PO from being created.
resolution: Cancel existing PO F000072028 and then create a new PO for item #1.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed on @FDPC-PROD. The requester was asked to verify the recovery outcome. The comments do not identify the underlying incident cause or recovery procedure.
important_findings: Recovery was completed on @FDPC-PROD.
Verification of the completed recovery was requested.
No root cause, error details, or recovery steps were documented.
resolution: Recovery was completed on @FDPC-PROD; verification was requested.

investigation_summary: Chassis Price was not displayed in Aomori Production while pricing was available in UAT2. Investigation confirmed that the affected Production pricing/master data was absent because the final Production model-code file did not include the required model code. The affected Production record was recovered and a file was executed to align Production pricing with UAT; subsequent UAT2 alignment with Production was identified as requiring a separate SR.
important_findings: The initial issue was caused by the absence of the Price Master for the affected Chassis in Aomori Prod.
The affected Production record was recovered; model code FED90K74S00H could not be found in the files previously executed on Aomori Prod.
The January 2024 UAT setup file included model code FED90G73S00H, but the final Production file shared in July 2024 did not include it.
The file executed in Aomori Production through SR MFTBCFFR-3780 contained updated model-code pricing, creating a pricing difference with UAT2.
Production setup files were agreed to be applied only to Production; applying them to UAT requires a separate service request.
root_cause: The final model-code file supplied for the Aomori Production setup did not include the required model code/pricing data, while the earlier UAT setup file did.
resolution: The affected Aomori Production record was recovered and the relevant file was executed, aligning Production model-code pricing with UAT. Any subsequent UAT2 update to match Production was to be requested through a separate SR.

investigation_summary: The request concerned applying the "Do Not Print" feature to real-time invoices. Analysis confirmed that "Do Not Print" was deployed to FDP during FDP Okayama sprint development, but no requirement was provided to apply it to Cubastion real-time invoice functionality. The request was classified as an additional requirement rather than a defect and requires a Change Request (CR).
important_findings: The "Do Not Print" feature was applied to FDP during FDP Okayama sprint development.
The business team was coordinating Cubastion and real-time invoice capabilities at the time of deployment.
No requirement was provided to apply "Do Not Print" functionality to real-time invoices.
The reported behavior was confirmed not to be a bug.
Implementing the feature for real-time invoices requires a Change Request (CR).
root_cause: "Do Not Print" functionality was not included in the requirements for Cubastion real-time invoices.
resolution: Ticket rejected as not a bug; submit a Change Request (CR) if "Do Not Print" functionality is required for real-time invoices.

investigation_summary: Invoice CustomerName population was investigated for Job Cards where the Cash Receipt Flag on the JC Header is Y. The expected source was the Vehicle Owner Name, but the invoice mapping referenced a different field. The mapping was corrected in FDP UAT-1, approved for production, and released on April 24.
important_findings: For Cash Receipt Flag = Y on the JC Header, Invoice CustomerName must be populated from the Vehicle Owner Name.
For Cash Receipt Flag = N, Invoice CustomerName is populated from the Ship To Customer Name.
The existing mapping for Cash Receipt Flag = Y was mapped to a different field instead of Vehicle Owner Name.
The corrected mapping was validated in FDP UAT-1 using JC# I001293791.
The approved mapping change was released to the production environment on April 24.
root_cause: For Job Cards with Cash Receipt Flag = Y, the Invoice CustomerName mapping referenced an incorrect field rather than the Vehicle Owner Name.
resolution: Changed the Invoice CustomerName mapping to use the correct Vehicle Owner Name field when the Cash Receipt Flag on the JC Header is Y, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to production on April 24.

investigation_summary: Orders were created without line items when the Material master file from D2S contained an unusually high record count. Processing of the file was delayed, and the order-creation job executed before all parts had been released to siebel. The teams discussed a workaround with IT and D2S, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: The Material master file from D2S contained 82,876 records.
The increased Material master file volume caused the package execution to take longer.
The order-creation job ran before all parts were released to siebel.
The issue occurs when a high number of Material master records are sent from D2S.
root_cause: A high-volume Material master file from D2S delayed package processing, allowing the order-creation job to run before all parts were released to siebel, resulting in orders without line items.
resolution: A workaround was discussed with the IT team and D2S team; no specific corrective action was documented.

investigation_summary: Commission fee and tax calculations were triggered when "Create Spreadsheet" was selected for a Liability Order. The button could be enabled through the Clerical Error workflow before "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" had a valid value, creating incorrect commission details. The enablement logic was updated in UAT, recovery JVs were processed and linked to KB, and the fix was released to production on April 24.
important_findings: Commission calculation occurs when the "Create Spreadsheet" button is clicked within an order.
"Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" is populated when "Liability Insurance Policy #" is entered on the order.
The issue was reproduced on UAT8 using liability order Q050023214 by setting the order to "Liability Clerical Error", clearing the Clerical error flag, and then creating a Liability Spreadsheet.
The "Create Spreadsheet" button was enabled without requiring a valid "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date".
Recovery required creation of Reverse JV and Correctr JV with the posting date set to the current date; the JVs were linked to KB through the nightly batch.
"Create Spreadsheet" is visible only in the My Branch and All Insurance Orders views under Liability Order, and testing used user D0X20922.
root_cause: The "Create Spreadsheet" button could be enabled through the "Liability Clerical Error" workflow while "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" was not valid, allowing commission calculation to run with incomplete order data.
resolution: Updated the "Create Spreadsheet" enablement condition to require a valid "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date". The fix was validated in UAT, recovery Reverse JV and Correctr JV entries were linked to KB, and the change was deployed to production in the April 24 scheduled release.
technical_entities: Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date

investigation_summary: Negative-amount TOB invoice JV records were present but were not processed or created in the system. Investigation identified an overlap between RCR and KB batch processing on Chugoku caused primarily by high data volume. Affected records were recovered, and the FDP-Chugoku DT-01 processing schedule was moved earlier to provide sufficient time for DT-01 processing and JV creation.
important_findings: JV for negative-amount TOB invoices was not created although the underlying data existed in the system.
The unprocessed records were associated with overlapping RCR and KB batch processing on Chugoku.
The overlap was primarily driven by a large volume of data.
Affected records were recovered and shared through email and the night batch.
FDP-Chugoku DT-01 file processing was changed from 7:00 PM JST to 6:00 PM JST.
root_cause: RCR and KB batch processing overlapped on Chugoku due primarily to large data volume, preventing timely processing and JV creation for negative-amount TOB invoices.
resolution: Recovered the affected records and moved FDP-Chugoku DT-01 file processing from 7:00 PM JST to 6:00 PM JST to allow sufficient time for DT-01 processing and JV creation.

investigation_summary: An affected Sales Order was recovered and synchronized with Revision 3 of NV Quote/Quote 1-ENPAF, and the revised amount was linked to KB. Engineering attempted to reproduce the incident in UAT but could not do so and classified it as a rare occurrence. Potential contributing workflow steps were identified and additional error handling was planned for the 14 May 2025 release, but the comments do not confirm implementation or effectiveness. The incident was closed as unresolved after discussion with the business side.
important_findings: The Sales Order recovery was completed and synchronized with Revision 3 of the NV Quote, identified as Quote 1-ENPAF.
The revised amount was linked to KB after recovery.
Engineering was unable to reproduce the issue in UAT environments despite repeated investigation.
Several workflow steps were identified as possible contributors, and additional error handling was planned.
The planned 14 May 2025 release outcome was not confirmed in the comments.
The issue was closed as unresolved because analysis and reproduction were not possible with Cubastion.
resolution: The affected Sales Order was recovered, synchronized with Revision 3 of Quote 1-ENPAF/NV Quote, and the revised amount was linked to KB. The broader incident was closed unresolved.

investigation_summary: The user was unable to edit a work order. The issue appeared to be related to cache behavior and was resolved when the user started a new session. The incident was rejected after the problem no longer occurred.
important_findings: The affected function was editing a work order.
The issue was considered a cache issue.
Starting a new user session resolved the issue.
The user was able to edit the work order after starting the new session.
root_cause: Cache issue affecting the user's session.
resolution: The user started a new session, which cleared the issue and restored work order editing.

investigation_summary: The incident occurred because UID D8NABUKU was present in the Employee Master but absent from the Canon print server file. Investigation found that the UID registered in the March 31 Employee Master run was D8TABUKU, which was subsequently changed to D8NABUKU, leaving no corresponding Canon server entry. The requested resolution was to register the missing UIDs on the Canon server.
important_findings: D8NABUKU did not exist on the Canon server/Canon print server file.
The March 31 Employee Master run registered D8TABUKU, and the printer was updated for D8TABUKU on March 31.
D8TABUKU was changed to D8NABUKU, causing the Canon server file to lack the updated user.
D8FURUTM also required addition to the server.
Additional Employee Master UIDs were missing from the Canon print server file for Aomori, Hakodate, and Okinawa FDPs.
root_cause: The UID was changed from D8TABUKU to D8NABUKU after the March 31 Employee Master/printer update, but the Canon print server file was not updated with D8NABUKU.
resolution: Register D8NABUKU, D8FURUTM, and the other identified missing Employee Master UIDs on the Canon server.

investigation_summary: The affected user could not be found in the Canon server file. Investigation of the employee master file run on 31st March found that the registered UID was changed from D8TABUKU to D8NABUKU, while D8TABUKU did not exist in the master. Additional UID discrepancies between the employee master and Canon print server file were identified across FDPs; updating the missing UIDs on the server was proposed.
important_findings: D8NABUKU was not present in the Canon server file.
The employee master file run on 31st March registered UID D8TABUKU, and the printer was updated for D8TABUKU on 31st March.
UID D8TABUKU was changed to D8NABUKU, causing the user to be absent from the Canon server file.
Additional employee-master UIDs missing from the Canon print server file were identified for Aomori, Hakodate, and Okinawa FDPs.
The proposed corrective action was to update the missing UIDs on the server after business hours.
root_cause: A UID change from D8TABUKU to D8NABUKU was not reflected in the Canon server file, leaving D8NABUKU unavailable on the server.

investigation_summary: AR# H000109757 and multiple other AR# records were excluded from aggregated Power BI visuals because X_REPAIR_COST was null in both Warehouse DB and Siebel DB.
