Power BI SUM aggregation ignored null values rather than treating them as zero. Power BI logic was updated to replace null X_REPAIR_COST values with 0, validated in UAT1 for the PBI UV2_01 report, and released to production on April 14.
important_findings: X_REPAIR_COST for AR# H000109757 was null in both Warehouse DB and Siebel DB.
Multiple AR# records had null X_REPAIR_COST values.
Power BI SUM aggregation ignored null values, causing affected AR# records to be absent from aggregated visuals.
The implemented Power BI logic replaces null X_REPAIR_COST values with 0.
The fix was resolved in UAT1 and applied to production in the April 14 release.
root_cause: Null X_REPAIR_COST values in Warehouse DB and Siebel DB were ignored by Power BI SUM aggregation, excluding affected AR# records from aggregated report visuals.
resolution: Updated Power BI logic to replace null X_REPAIR_COST values with 0; validated in UAT1 for PBI UV2_01 and deployed to production on April 14.

investigation_summary: Power BI displayed duplicate AR entries because Sales Posting Date values differed between line items of the same order, causing unintended row duplication during PBI aggregation. Recovery was performed for the affected Wakayama AR records, and no additional affected records were found across production environments. The issue could not be reproduced in UAT or production, so the underlying root cause was not identified; daily monitoring was continued and the incident was proposed for closure.
important_findings: Duplicate AR entries in Power BI were associated with differing Sales Posting Date values at line-item level for the same order.
Recovery was completed in Wakayama for AR# H000000801, H000001401, and H000001901.
No affected records were confirmed in any production environment after the initial occurrence.
The issue was considered rare and could not be reproduced in the UAT environment.
The Sales Posting Date discrepancy was observed, but the technical root cause for the differing dates was not identified.
Records continued to be monitored daily, with planned same-day investigation and reproduction attempts if the issue recurs.
resolution: Recovered all identified affected AR records in Wakayama and continued daily monitoring; the incident was proposed for closure because the issue could not be reproduced or further analyzed.

investigation_summary: Profit values in the UV Report (2-06 - Used car details (profit and loss)) did not consistently match Siebel. The investigation identified an inconsistency in the profit calculation formula, and corrected logic was deployed to UAT and then all FDP Prod environments. A remaining discrepancy in FDP Iwate showed that PBI 2-06 Report Profit still differed from Siebel Sales Quote and Order Profit due to rounding/overall-profit logic requiring further change.
important_findings: The profit calculation formula contained an inconsistency that caused UV Report profit values to differ from Siebel.
Corrected profit logic was deployed to UAT Okayama and verified against Siebel UAT1, except for identified garbage-data orders E001192564, E001261152, and E001187324.
FDP UAT1 SO# E001294027 was reported as an additional profit mismatch after the initial UAT release.
The corrected logic was released to all FDP Prod environments, but FDP Iwate AR# H000003201 still showed PBI 2-06 Report Profit 1020811.90 versus Siebel Sales Quote and Order Profit 1,020,813.
Logic similar to the SC Power BI 2-06 report was implemented, but additional logic changes were required to round the overall profit and align all profit values.
Further corrective work was requested through an AMS CR; the timeline does not confirm that the remaining discrepancies were resolved.
root_cause: An inconsistency in the profit calculation formula, with remaining mismatches requiring additional overall-profit rounding logic.

investigation_summary: A gap occurred because Journal Vouchers (JVs) were not created for certain Color records across multiple FDPs. The issue was confirmed to affect line type "4"; a fix was developed, validated on UAT8, and recovery data was prepared for previously unprocessed records. After JV creation was verified on UAT8, the fix was released to Production on 12 June 2025.
important_findings: Some JVs were not created, causing an amount gap.
The issue occurred for Color records and affected records on multiple FDPs.
The defect specifically prevented JV creation for line type "4".
Target recovery data was prepared to create JVs that had not been created earlier.
Sample January TOB Invoice data from Shikoku and March TOB Invoice data from Chugoku were used for UAT8 verification.
JV creation was confirmed on UAT8 before release to Production.
root_cause: A defect affecting Color records prevented Journal Voucher (JV) creation for line type "4".
resolution: The defect was fixed and validated on UAT8, recovery data was prepared for previously uncreated JVs, and the fix was released to Production on 12 June 2025.

investigation_summary: Price updates were missing for material ZC116610 and several other parts in FDP Okayama. ZC116610 was absent from the D2S Material Master file for FDPs that had been updated on SC-PROD on March 13. The missing part was exported from SC, all FDP environments were updated with prices, and the remaining affected prices were updated in Okayama-PROD.
important_findings: ZC116610 was not displayed in Material master because it was missing from the D2S Material Master file for FDPs.
The affected D2S Material Master file had been updated on SC-PROD on March 13.
Only FDP Okayama had not updated prices for the reported list of parts.
The missing D2S part was exported from SC and all FDP environments were updated along with prices.
Remaining affected part prices were updated in Okayama-PROD.
root_cause: Part ZC116610 was missing from the D2S Material Master file for FDPs, preventing its display in Material master and application of its price.
resolution: Exported the missing D2S part from SC, updated all FDP environments with the part and prices, and updated the remaining affected prices in Okayama-PROD.

investigation_summary: A sales report associated with sales order A000023860 was reported as not sent to TOB after recycling, causing sales-result discrepancies. Investigation confirmed that the DJ2L transaction from Siebel on 28/March/2025 had a TOB error response and that the record existed in both JMS logs and the TOB Request/Response Screen; the unresolved concern was why it was not displayed when filtering by Interface ID DJ2L.
important_findings: Sales order A000023860 sent DJ2L from Siebel on 28/March/2025 and received an error response from TOB.
The displayed error response was identified as an error during recycling send/receive processing.
The sales report sent after recycling was reported as not TOB-sent, causing sales results not to match.
The relevant record was confirmed in both JMS logs and the TOB Request/Response Screen.
The record was reported as visible in the UI when checked using Interface ID DJ2L, although the user reported it was not displayed using only that Interface ID filter.
IT and business teams planned further discussion, but no confirmed final finding or corrective action was documented.

investigation_summary: A JV was not sent to KB because its credit and debit Department Code was set to "10V1", derived from the order Shop Code. "10V1" was absent from KB Department Code Mapping, preventing the JV from linking to KB. The required mappings were added, remaining attached shop codes were mapped to 0001, and the recovery JV was sent through the KB batch.
important_findings: The credit and debit Department Code "10V1" was derived from the order Shop Code.
"10V1" was not present in KB Department Code Mapping, so the JV was not linked to KB.
SR MFTBCFFR-3727 was created and completed to add the required mapping in Prod.
All remaining attached shop codes were mapped to 0001.
The recovery JV for "10V1" was processed through the KB batch with posting date 04/APR/2025.
root_cause: The order-derived Shop Code "10V1" was used as the credit and debit Department Code but did not exist in KB Department Code Mapping, preventing the JV from being linked and sent to KB.
resolution: Added the required Department Code/shop-code mappings in Prod, mapped the remaining attached shop codes to 0001, and reprocessed and sent the "10V1" recovery JV to KB.

investigation_summary: Bulk files received after 28-FEB-2025 were not processed. Investigation identified an issue in the code that executes bulk files. All pending files through 04-APR-2025 were manually processed in receipt order, and the automation script was modified and verified by successfully processing the following day's bulk files.
important_findings: Files had not been processed since 28-FEB-2025.
All pending files through 04-APR-2025 were processed manually in the order received.
An issue was found in the code that executes bulk files.
The automation script was modified after the code issue was identified.
The modified automation processed the previous day's bulk files as expected.
root_cause: An issue in the code that executes bulk files prevented automated processing.
resolution: Manually processed pending files in receipt order, modified the automation script, and verified that automation subsequently processed bulk files as expected.

investigation_summary: A D21F file was received and executed before the corresponding D21E file for an order. Because the chassis order had not yet been created, the recycle order was not generated. The affected record was recovered, and a Kaizen activity was initiated to provide AMS Team email notifications when a D21F file is received without an order for a VIN#.
important_findings: The D21F file was received before the D21E file for the affected order.
The chassis order did not exist when the D21F file was executed.
The missing chassis order caused the recycle order not to be generated.
The affected record was recovered and recovery was confirmed.
A Kaizen activity is being implemented to notify AMS Team by email when a D21F file is received without an order for a VIN#.
root_cause: The D21F file was processed before the D21E file had created the chassis order, preventing recycle order generation.
resolution: The affected record was recovered. A Kaizen activity was initiated to add AMS Team email notifications for D21F files received when no order exists for a VIN#.

investigation_summary: The issue was attributed to cached data in the JPN environment. Clearing the JPN cache resolved the incident. For prevention, cache clearing in both JPN and ENU environments and a SIEBEL restart will be planned after bulk data imports in production.
important_findings: Cached data caused the issue.
Clearing the cache in the JPN environment resolved the issue.
After production bulk data imports, caches should be cleared in both JPN and ENU environments.
A SIEBEL restart should also be planned after bulk data imports.
The restart procedure was shared internally before incident closure.
root_cause: Cached data in the JPN environment.
resolution: Cleared the cache in the JPN environment.

investigation_summary: A job card of type "51: Complaint" could become linked to a new vehicle order by first creating it as "22: New car modification (movement)", linking the order, and then changing the JC Type before completion. The investigation confirmed that the relevant internal-order fields were retained when the JC Type changed. A Service Job Card fix was implemented in FDP UAT1, validated, and released to Production on 13 September.
important_findings: "51: Complaint" job cards cannot be directly linked to a new car order by design.

New vehicle order A000121450 was linked by creating a "22: New car modification (movement)" job card, setting the new car order in the internal order field, and changing the JC Type to "51: Claim" before completion.
The system allowed the linkage because internal-order values persisted after the JC Type was changed.
The fix resets "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type is changed.
UAT-1 validation confirmed that changing JC Type from "22" to another type, including "26", correctly resets the values.
The fix was released to Production in the 13 September scheduled FDP release.
root_cause: Service Job Card did not reset the internal-order fields when the JC Type was changed, allowing a new car order linked under JC Type "22: New car modification (movement)" to remain linked after changing the job card to "51: Claim".
resolution: Implemented a Service Job Card change to reset "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type changes; validated in FDP UAT1/UAT-1 and deployed to Production on 13 September.

investigation_summary: Sales approval was blocked because no Recycle Fee order was mapped to the Sales Order for C# 10360. Investigation confirmed that TOB did not send the D21F file, so no Recycle Fee order was created; only D21A, D21R, and D21N files were received. Recovery was completed and Sales Posting was completed without a recycling order. The reported “major component is missing” message was considered inappropriate for this rare scenario and will be monitored for recurrence.
important_findings: No D21F file was received for C# 10360.
Only D21A, D21R, and D21N files were received for C# 10360.
Without a D21F file, no Recycle Fee order was created or mapped to the Sales Order.
During Generate Approval/Request Approval, Siebel validates whether a Recycle Fee order is mapped to the Sales Order; this behavior is the same as SC.
The “major component is missing” error message was reported as incorrect when the Recycle Fee order does not exist.
The case was considered rare; corrective measures will be considered if similar incidents recur.
root_cause: TOB did not provide the D21F file for C# 10360, so no Recycle Fee order was created or mapped to the Sales Order.
resolution: Recovery was completed, allowing delivery approval and Sales Posting to complete without a recycling order. The incident was closed with monitoring for recurrence.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed, and a new JV was planned to be sent to KB that night. The incident was identified as the same issue as MFTBCFFR-3631 and was tracked under that incident.
important_findings: Recovery was completed.
A new JV was scheduled to be sent to KB.
MFTBCFFR-3694 was determined to be the same issue as MFTBCFFR-3631.
resolution: Recovery was completed; a new JV was scheduled to be sent to KB.

investigation_summary: A Payer Change Order retained the previous Closed Date after the user changed the Bill to Basic Account, causing bulk invoice data to be excluded from the expected closing-date processing and sent to KB at EOM instead. The issue was reproduced and fixed in FDP UAT-1, where Closed Date and Payment Term now update based on the newly selected payer. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
important_findings: For Account 0000205096, Change Order K000065493 retained an EOM closing date although the account closing date was 25.
In a Payer Change Order, Bill to Basic Account and Ship to Basic Account are initially retrieved from JCO.
Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not refresh Closed Date or Payment Term; the prior values remained on the change order.
Because Closed Date remained EOM rather than 25, the change order was not sent to KB with the expected bulk invoice data; JC lines and change order lines were sent on 31 March.
The corrected behavior was verified in UAT-1 for Payer Change and Payer and Price Change scenarios.
root_cause: When the payer was changed in Bill to Basic Account on a Payer Change Order, the system did not update Closed Date and Payment Term from the newly selected payer, leaving the previous EOM Closed Date on the change order.
resolution: Updated FDP so that changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account on a Service Change Order refreshes Closed Date and Payment Term according to the new payer. The fix was deployed to FDP UAT-1, validated, and released to PROD on 12 June 2025; recovery bulk invoice data was also shared with MDIS after approval.

investigation_summary: Incorrect accounting-date formatting during recovery of two Journal Vouchers caused the nightly batch process to fail and prevented Journal Voucher file generation. Recovery was completed, and the March 24 Journal Voucher was sent to MDIS. The recovery process was updated to validate date formats before processing recovered data.
important_findings: Two Journal Vouchers were recovered with an incorrectly formatted accounting date.
The incorrect date format caused the nightly batch process to fail.
The batch failure prevented Journal Voucher files from being generated.
Recovery was completed and the March 24 Journal Voucher was sent to MDIS.
The recovery process now includes pre-validation of date formats for recovered data.
root_cause: The accounting date was formatted incorrectly during recovery of two Journal Vouchers.
resolution: Completed the recovery, sent the March 24 Journal Voucher to MDIS, and updated the recovery process to pre-validate date formats of recovered data.

investigation_summary: Replenishment orders were not created because the stock order creation process followed an incorrect path and terminated. The issue was fixed and validated in FDP UAT-1 by executing the batch job, which successfully created replenishment orders. The fix was deployed to the production environment through an urgent release on March 27.
important_findings: A missing logic in the stock order creation process caused the process to follow an incorrect path and terminate without creating orders.
The issue was not detected during UAT because the batch job completed with a success status despite replenishment orders not being created.
After the fix in FDP UAT-1, batch-job testing successfully created replenishment orders.
UAT1 reference N001293397 was used for validation.
The fix was applied to the production environment in an urgent release on March 27.
root_cause: Missing logic in the stock order creation process caused it to follow an incorrect path and terminate instead of creating replenishment orders.
resolution: Added the missing stock order creation logic, validated replenishment-order creation through a batch-job test in FDP UAT-1, and deployed the fix to production in an urgent release on March 27.

investigation_summary: The incident involved incorrect Credit and Debit Department Code assignment in PO GR JV for Trade-In purchase orders. The existing logic used the NV Sales Order Last Approver, but the required logic for NV Trade-In is to derive the Branch Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep. The fix was validated in UAT1, affected JVs were recovered, and the change was released to Production on April 24.
important_findings: The original PO GR JV logic assigned Credit and Debit Department Code based on the NV Sales Order Last Approver/PO creator.
For NV Trade-In, both Credit and Debit Department Code must be set from the Branch Code of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep.
The fix was implemented in UAT1 and UAT passed with AR#H000046387 and PO# F001294580.
Alternate approver D0X20883 received the NV Sales Order approval request for Sales Rep D0X20897; approving the order created the Trade-In PO with D0X20883 as creator.
UV Trade-In does not require this fix because the department code on the JV Trade-In line is derived from the Assessment request, not the UV Sales Order final approval.
Affected JVs were recovered before the Production release.
root_cause: The NV Trade-In PO GR JV department-code logic incorrectly derived Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Last Approver instead of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code.
resolution: Updated the NV Trade-In PO GR JV logic to set Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code, validated the change in UAT1, recovered affected JVs, and released the fix to Production on April 24.

investigation_summary: A recycle fee order could not be sent to TOB because the TOB response received in the JMS queue was not reflected in Siebel. The order was recovered, allowing the user to resend it to TOB. Investigation could not reproduce the issue in UAT, and later code-level verification reported expected functionality with no observed recurrence. No confirmed root cause or preventive fix was documented.
important_findings: The recycle fee order was recovered so it could be resent to TOB.
A TOB response was received in the JMS queue but did not update the status in Siebel, with no error reported in the scenario.
An initial finding stated that Siebel could not read half-width katakana in the TOB response; this was challenged because half-width kana is standard for TOB error messages.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT.
Code-level verification reported that the implementation and functionality were working as expected.
No recurrence was observed during subsequent monitoring in Siebel.
resolution: The recycle fee order was recovered, enabling the user to resend it to TOB. No permanent corrective change or preventive fix plan was documented.

investigation_summary: Sales Posting approval failed for Sales Orders whose associated account address lacked a city code, causing Falcon-side validation errors. The failure could leave approval history marked "Approved" and create a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order even though the final Inbox approval was not completed. Recovery removed the existing shipment order and required completion of customer address data; the MFTBCFFR-3641-equivalent fix was deployed to UAT and production on April 14.
important_findings: The root cause matched MFTBCFFR-3641: the account used by the Sales Order had no city code in its address.
Error logs reported: "The following fields are required: Account, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Postal Code, Primary Postal Code Date (SBL-BPR-00131)".

During second Sales Posting approval in Inbox, a pop-up error prevented the Inbox item from becoming "Approved," while approval history could show "Approved" and the order could move to "Sales Posting Completed."
Rejecting and regenerating approval after the failure could create duplicate Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders.
Orders with null account address information error on the Falcon side; mandatory customer address fields, including "City County Name" and "OOAZA Name", must be populated before processing.
The existing Pool Cost Shipment was removed during recovery, and a reverse JV was created.
root_cause: Missing city code/address information in the customer account associated with the Sales Order caused Falcon-side mandatory-field validation errors during Sales Posting approval.
resolution: Applied the MFTBCFFR-3641-equivalent fix in UAT and deployed it to production on April 14. The recovery removed the existing Pool Cost Shipment, created a reverse JV, and required the customer account address details to be completed before regenerating and approving Sales Posting.

investigation_summary: Incomplete address data on the account used by the NV Quote/Sales Order caused an approval-processing error while downstream processing still marked approval as completed and generated duplicate Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and JVs. The affected account address is the account selected in the Contractor Name field, whose address is sent to Falcon. Duplicate JVs and Falcon records were recovered, and validation was implemented in NV Quote to prevent approval generation when the selected contractor account has incomplete address data. The validated fix was released to PROD on April 14.
important_findings: The original failure was reproduced on UAT 6 with Sales Order A000026083 and customer code 0000032930.

During the second Sales Posting approval from Inbox, an error prevented Inbox approval, but approval history showed Approved, the order moved to Sales Posting Completed, and a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order was created.
Rejecting the Inbox approval and regenerating approvals could create multiple Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and duplicate JVs.
The account address data used by the Sales Order was incomplete; missing city code/address fields, including Oaza/Common Name for account 0000029653, triggered the issue.
Validation checks only the address of the account selected in the Contractor Name field because Falcon sends that account's address data.

Recovery included unmapping Pool Cost Shipment orders, creating reverse JVs for duplicate JVs, resolving a Data set separator-related JV error for KB transmission, and completing Falcon recovery after customer master updates.
root_cause: Incomplete or null address fields on the account selected in the Contractor Name field for the NV Quote/Sales Order, including missing city code and Oaza/Common Name, caused the approval-processing error.
resolution: Implemented NV Quote validation on the Request Approval/Generate Approval action to block processing when the Contractor Name account has incomplete address information, with the message: "Please check the business partner master of the user selected in the business partner name. The customer address in the business partner master is a required field." The fix was validated in UAT and released to PROD on April 14; duplicate JVs were reversed and Falcon recovery was completed.
technical_entities: Last name of primary shipping destination

investigation_summary: Duplicate JVs were created for a JC linked to Sales Order#: Q050057080 because a spreadsheet could be approved, later manually changed to "Cancelled", and replaced with another approved spreadsheet. JV creation is triggered when "Spreadsheet Status" changes to "Spreadsheet Approved". A reverse JV was created for the JV generated from the cancelled spreadsheet, and the UI validation was deployed to production on April 14.
important_findings: A JV for Liability Orders is created when "Spreadsheet Status" changes to "Spreadsheet Approved".
The "Spreadsheet Status" field remained editable after approval, allowing an approved spreadsheet to be manually changed to "Cancelled".
Spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01 was approved and later cancelled; its approval had already created a JV.
Spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-02 was subsequently created and approved for the same JC, creating another JV.
A reverse JV was created for the JV generated by spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01.
The fix restricts editing of "Spreadsheet Status" to records whose status is "Spreadsheet Created".
root_cause: The "Spreadsheet Status" field was editable after "Spreadsheet Approved", allowing an approved spreadsheet to be cancelled and replaced with another approved spreadsheet, which triggered duplicate JV creation.
resolution: Created a reverse JV for the JV generated by cancelled spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01 and changed the UI so "Spreadsheet Status" is editable only when its value is "Spreadsheet Created". The fix was validated in UAT and deployed to the production environment on April 14.

investigation_summary: A Body Building Order could be manually transitioned without required vendor information, resulting in a blank Vendor Finance Account Code on the Journal Voucher (JV). Initial UAT1 validation covered the "Pending" to "Ordered" transition, but testing identified that "Order changed" could still be selected without a bodybuilder/Vendor Name. Validation for both required vendor details was corrected, verified, and deployed to production in the April 14 urgent release.
important_findings: The affected Body Building Order had a blank Vendor Finance Account Code, which caused the corresponding Journal Voucher (JV) value to be blank.
The issue was reproduced in UAT by manually changing a Body Building Order status from "Pending" to "Ordered" while "Vendor Finance Account Code" was null.
The initial UAT1 fix added a pop-up validation when changing status from "Pending" to "Ordered" with a blank "Vendor Finance Account Code".
Validation testing found that status "Order changed" could still be selected without a bodybuilder/Vendor Name for both Non-IBOS and IBOS workflows.
The final fix added Vendor Name validation equivalent to the validation used when executing "Generate Approvals" without Vendor Code.
root_cause: Manual status changes for Body Building Orders lacked validation for required vendor information, allowing transitions with blank Vendor Finance Account Code and, in the "Order changed" path, missing Vendor Name.
resolution: Recovered the affected order and deployed validation preventing status changes when required Vendor Finance Account Code or Vendor Name is missing. The corrected validation was verified and applied to production in the April 14 urgent release.

investigation_summary: Part prices were not updated in FDP environments because the affected parts were absent from the D2S files received on 19/03/2025. D2S resent the parts, and MX951393, MX958726, and MX962198 were updated immediately. ML351609 required an after-hours price update due to its effective start date, and all part prices were updated after the price revision activity.
important_findings: The affected parts were not present in the D2S files received on 19/03/2025, so they were not updated in FDP environments.
ML351609 had an effective start date of 01/04/2024 and was scheduled for an after-hours price update on all FDPs.
After the price revision activity, all affected part prices were updated in FDP-PROD.
root_cause: The affected part records were missing from the D2S files received on 19/03/2025.
resolution: D2S resent the missing parts, and the prices were updated in FDP environments; ML351609 was updated through an after-hours price revision activity. All part prices were confirmed updated.

investigation_summary: On 19/March/2025, a D2S-side network failure caused affected Parts Purchase order allocations to be received in reverse, reverting Confirmed Qty to null and leaving D2S Shipments in Allocation Pending. The root cause was identified as an outbound idoc failure caused by an Internet communication error. All affected records were retriggered, including reprocessing the latest D2S allocations and pending shipments.
important_findings: Affected Parts Purchase order responses from D2S for 19/March/2025 were delayed.
A D2S-side network failure caused allocations to be received in reverse order.
Reverse allocation processing caused Confirmed Qty to revert to null.
The outbound idoc failed due to an Internet communication error.
Affected records were retriggered; latest D2S allocations and D2S Shipments with Allocation Pending were reprocessed.
root_cause: The outbound idoc failed due to an Internet communication error.
resolution: All affected records were retriggered, including reprocessing the latest D2S allocations to update Confirmed Qty and reprocessing D2S Shipments with Allocation Pending.

investigation_summary: Parts Internal Order list prices became null when parts were added through Sub Quote in NV Quote. Investigation reproduced the issue on UAT1 and established that the related NV Sales Order Start Price was set to null during Sub Quote completion. A fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.
important_findings: Parts Internal Order list price is fetched from NV Sales Order.
Adding a part through Sub Quote in NV Quote caused the NV Sales Order Start Price to be set to null.
The issue was reproduced on UAT1 with NV Sales Order A001293389, part ###600SILVER, resulting in null list price on Parts Internal Order M001293390.
When parts are added through Parts and Intenal Work in an NV Quote line item, the list price is displayed; the issue occurred when creating the part order through Sub Quote.
The fix was verified on UAT1 using NV Sales Order A001293480 with parts ###600BLACK-5K and ###1003, creating Parts Internal Order M001293481.
The fix was applied to PROD in the April 14 release.
root_cause: During Sub Quote completion in NV Quote, the Start Price for the added part in NV Sales Order was set to null. Since Parts Internal Order list price is sourced from NV Sales Order, its list price also became null.
resolution: Fixed the Sub Quote processing issue that set NV Sales Order Start Price to null; the fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.

investigation_summary: A JV was created for Sales Order # Q050020683 but was not linked to KB because its Credit Department Code was set to "INTERNAL" from the Insurance Order. Investigation found that the Ejibai-created order inherited incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details from its linked existing order because it was created before Sales Rep recovery for migrated orders completed. Recovery JVs were created with Credit and Debit Department Code 3011 and sent to KB, and the affected order was recovered.
important_findings: The JV was not linked to KB because its Credit Department Code was "INTERNAL", sourced from the Insurance Order.
Sales Rep recovery for all migrated orders was completed on February 17, 2025.
Sales Order # Q050020683 was created through Ejibai on February 13, 2025, before the Sales Rep recovery completed.
Ejibai order-creation logic retrieves Sales Rep details from the linked existing order, causing incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details to be inherited.
Recovery JV processing used Credit Department Code 3011 and Debit Department Code 3011.
root_cause: Sales Order # Q050020683 was created through Ejibai before Sales Rep recovery for migrated orders completed, so it inherited incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details from its linked existing order; the resulting JV had Credit Department Code "INTERNAL" from the Insurance Order and could not link to KB.
resolution: Created recovery JVs using Credit Department Code 3011 and Debit Department Code 3011, sent them to KB, and recovered the affected order.

investigation_summary: The affected record was recovered, but the incident was rare and could not be reproduced in UAT. Investigation identified that the Billing Status Code on sales order items associated with an invoice was not updated to "Invoiced," preventing Registration Request completion. A preventive workflow-based correction was deployed to Production on 24 April 2025, with increased logging and ongoing monitoring.
important_findings: When an invoice is created, the associated sales order items are normally updated with Billing Status Code "Invoiced."
For the incident, the Billing Status Code update did not occur, which blocked completion of the Registration Request.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, so error handling was added to the invoice creation workflow and monitored.
The preventive correction checks order line items associated with completed invoices and updates unprocessed Billing Status Code values to "Invoiced" during Registration Request completion.

The intended business flow remains that a Registration Request can be completed only after invoice completion; canceled invoices and subsequently created replacement invoices are handled based on invoice status.
The correction was implemented in Production on 24 April 2025, with log levels increased for continued monitoring.
root_cause: The Billing Status Code on sales order items associated with an invoice was not updated to "Invoiced," preventing the Registration Request from being completed.
resolution: A temporary preventive workflow-based correction was deployed to Production to identify order line items linked to completed invoices whose Billing Status Code was not updated and set the status to "Invoiced" during Registration Request completion. Error logging and monitoring were also increased.

investigation_summary: An additional invoice could be created because the Billing Status Code on the associated sales order item/order line was not updated to "Invoiced" after invoice completion. The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, and the underlying reason for the missing status update remained under investigation with error logging. A temporary preventive workflow was planned for Production, with ongoing monitoring transferred to MFTBCFFR-3616.
important_findings: Invoice completion normally updates the Billing Status Code of associated sales order items to "Invoiced".
In the affected case, the Billing Status Code update did not occur and remained "Blank", allowing an additional invoice to be created.
The issue was not reproducible in UAT, and error logging was added to capture recurrence details.
The proposed preventive measure triggers a workflow from the "Automatic Billing" button to identify order lines that should be "Invoiced" and update their Billing Status Code.
The temporary fix was scheduled for implementation in the Production environment on 24 April 2025; subsequent monitoring was to continue under MFTBCFFR-3616.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed for the affected Service Purchase Order. The underlying issue will be tracked and fixed under MFTBCFFR-3619.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the mentioned Service Purchase Order.
The permanent fix was deferred to MFTBCFFR-3619.
resolution: Completed recovery for the affected Service Purchase Order; follow-up remediation is tracked in MFTBCFFR-3619.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed for the affected Service Purchase Order. The underlying issue will be tracked and fixed under MFTBCFFR-3619.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the mentioned Service Purchase Order.
The permanent fix is being tracked in MFTBCFFR-3619.
resolution: Completed recovery for the affected Service Purchase Order.

investigation_summary: A D2S price discrepancy occurred across FDP production environments for Part Number MK658033. The D2S Price master file contained duplicate records for the part number, and one record was manually removed, resulting in inconsistent processing. Recovery was completed in all PROD environments, and the data-loading procedure will be improved to ensure correct price updates across all FDP Prod environments.
important_findings: The D2S Price master file contained two records with the same Part Number: MK658033.
One duplicate record was manually deleted, which caused the issue.
D2S price master must be processed using the same file across all FDPs; using different files causes values to differ between FDPs.
Recovery was completed on all PROD environments.
Data-loading procedures will be improved to verify that price updates are correct and consistent across all FDP Prod environments.
root_cause: The D2S Price master file had duplicate records for Part Number MK658033, and manual deletion of one record caused inconsistent results across FDP environments.
resolution: Recovery was completed on all PROD environments. The data-loading procedure will be improved to ensure price updates are correctly applied and verified across all FDP Prod environments.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed for the affected Service Purchase Order/Sales Purchase Order JV. The incident was identified as a Work Completion Date issue in the service purchase order. The related posting-date issue was separated for tracking and correction under MFTBCFFR-3619.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for the affected Service Purchase Order.
The incident was identified as a Work Completion Date issue in the service purchase order.
The posting-date-related issue is being tracked and fixed under MFTBCFFR-3619.
root_cause: Work Completion Date issue in the service purchase order.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected Service Purchase Order; the posting-date-related correction was assigned to MFTBCFFR-3619.

investigation_summary: The JV posting dates were reviewed against Service Purchase Order data and matched the Work Completion Date. For Job Card JC# I050038554, JV posting dates followed the defined settlement-date logic. Recovery was completed by the KB team.
important_findings: All reviewed JV posting dates matched the Work Completion Date in the Service Purchase Order.
For Job Card JC# I050038554, the Job Card posting date is set to the Original JC Settlement Date/Time.
For re-edit and re-edit close, the posting date is set to the JC Settlement Date/Time.
The KB team completed recovery.
resolution: Recovery was completed by the KB team.

investigation_summary: An unnecessary D2S Ship to LOV (7904VD) was identified in FDP Prod. The LOV was inactivated, and the requester confirmed the issue was resolved and requested closure.
important_findings: D2S Ship to LOV (7904VD) was unnecessary in FDP Prod.
The unnecessary LOV was inactivated.
The requester verified the result and approved closure.
root_cause: An unnecessary D2S Ship to LOV (7904VD) was active in FDP Prod.
resolution: Inactivated D2S Ship to LOV (7904VD) in FDP Prod.

investigation_summary: The incident was attributed to updates to Finance Accounts records that left the X_IDEN_CAT_PARTS field blank. The planned recovery was to update the db_last_upd field on Sales Account type records. Although recovery was reported complete, the requester confirmed that the problem remained unresolved and reopened the incident.
important_findings: Updates to Finance Accounts records left the X_IDEN_CAT_PARTS field blank.
The proposed corrective action was to update db_last_upd for Sales Account type records.
Recovery was reported as completed, but the requester confirmed the issue was still present and reopened the incident.
root_cause: Updates to Finance Accounts records left the X_IDEN_CAT_PARTS field blank.

investigation_summary: The ASCENT screen was inaccessible because ASCENT could not send responses to Siebel. The ASCENT team identified an expired SSL certificate on their side as the cause. After the ASCENT-side issue was rectified, the screen was confirmed to be working normally and the incident was closed.
important_findings: The ASCENT screen was not accessible during the incident.
ASCENT was unable to send a response to Siebel.
The ASCENT team's RCA identified expiration of an SSL certificate on the ASCENT side.
The ASCENT-side issue was rectified and the service was working normally.
root_cause: Expiration of the SSL certificate on the ASCENT side, preventing ASCENT from sending responses to Siebel.
resolution: The ASCENT team rectified the ASCENT-side SSL certificate issue, restoring ASCENT screen accessibility and responses to Siebel.

investigation_summary: The approval flow was incorrectly configured for profit ratio values between -1 and 0. An initial UAT-05 fix generated the correct Approval flow, but a missed test case left the approver invisible. The additional issue was corrected, validated with reference Quote 1-LI6DJ, and released to production on 2025-03-26.
important_findings: Approval flow configuration failed for profit ratio values between -1 and 0.
The initial fix was deployed to UAT-05 and generated the correct Approval flow for reference NV Quote 1-LFOUR.
Post-fix validation found that the approver was not visible.
The missing approver issue resulted from a missed test case and was corrected using reference Quote 1-LI6DJ.
The completed fix was released to production on 2025-03-26.
root_cause: The approval flow was not configured correctly for profit ratio values between -1 and 0; an additional missed test case caused the approver to remain invisible after the initial fix.
resolution: Corrected the approval-flow configuration and the missed test-case issue affecting approver visibility, validated in UAT-05, and released the fix to production on 2025-03-26.

investigation_summary: Vehicles from the common TOB TCB-01 file were synchronized to SC and all FDP environments, causing vehicles outside the intended dealer scope to be registered in the China region. Investigation confirmed that TCB-01 processing has no dealer-code-based filtering in either SC or FDP. The incident was closed as an IT issue after discussion with the business; no implementation change was recorded.
important_findings: TOB sends the same TCB01 file, containing all TOB-managed vehicles, to SC and all FDP environments.
Vehicles with dealer codes other than 7306 were registered as China-region vehicles, although dealer code 7306 was the intended update scope.
TCB-01 processing in SC and FDP has no record filter based on dealer code; all file data is synchronized.
No dealer-code filter was configured during FDP initial setup, and no related business change request had been received.
Applying a filter to TCB-01 processing requires a change request (CR).
The case was considered a rare occurrence and closed following discussion with the business.
root_cause: TCB-01 processing in both SC and FDP environments was configured without dealer-code-based record filtering, so all vehicles in the common TOB file were synchronized to all environments.

investigation_summary: The incident affected replenishment processing, including PO N000016079 and related Sales Orders 1018174950 and 1018174929, requiring recovery and D2S Shipment processing. The identified fix automated replenishment jobs to stop on Sundays. The fix was deployed to UAT-6, approved for production monitoring because it was not testable, and released to production on March 26, 2025.
important_findings: PO N000016079 had the same issue: Sales Order 1018174950 was allocated in Siebel, while N000017986 was created for Sales Order 1018174929.
Recovery was required and the received D2S Shipment needed to be processed.
The corrective change automates replenishment jobs so they automatically stop on Sundays.
The Sunday-stop functionality had already been implemented in the SC version.
The fix was deployed to UAT-6 but required production release and monitoring because it was not testable in UAT.
The production release was completed successfully on March 26, 2025.
root_cause: Replenishment jobs did not automatically stop on Sundays.
resolution: Automated replenishment jobs to stop on Sundays and released the fix to production on March 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: Stock IN processing was hindered for VINs used in UV purchase orders after migration from SC to FDP Chugoku. The affected VINs had Scrap Flag set to "Y" while Scrap Date was NULL. Recovery was completed through data patching and updates to affected records and related orders.
important_findings: The affected VIN# was migrated from SC to FDP Chugoku.
Scrap Flag was set to "Y" while Scrap Date was NULL, which hindered Stock IN processing.
Multiple VIN#s with the same Scrap Flag and Scrap Date condition were identified.
Scrap Date was patched in the FDP Chugoku environment.
Assessment number, Purchase Type, Transmission Type, and Inspection Status were updated for affected records.
Recovery was completed for affected Stock IN requests, UV purchase orders, and UV pool cost procurement orders.
root_cause: During VIN# migration from SC to FDP Chugoku, affected VINs retained Scrap Flag = "Y" with Scrap Date = NULL, causing Stock IN processing to be hindered.
resolution: Patched Scrap Date in the FDP Chugoku environment and updated affected record attributes, including Assessment number, Purchase Type, Transmission Type, and Inspection Status; recovered the affected Stock IN requests, UV purchase orders, and UV pool cost procurement orders.

investigation_summary: Purchase orders were incorrectly visible in UV Inventory after vehicle restock, allowing users to change the associated Sales Order # and disrupting the sales process. Data migration had not set the FDP "Previous Assessment Flag" to Y for qualifying orders, and the editable "Sales Order #" field permitted the change without creating a KB Map/Unmap trigger. Recovery was completed for migrated orders, the field was changed to read-only, and the fix was released to production on March 26, 2025.
important_findings: The affected PO was unmapped from UV Sales Order# E050064869 and mapped to Sales Order# E020841755 as recovery.
In FDP, "Previous Assessment Flag" must be set to Y when the parent UV Sales Order is Sales Posting Completed, preventing prior purchase orders from appearing after vehicle restock.
During data migration, "Previous Assessment Flag" was not set to Y, so previous purchase orders remained visible in UV Inventory.
"MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View" was editable for 10 responsibilities, allowing authorized users to edit the UI "Sales Order #" field.
Editing "Sales Order #" for a purchase order associated with a stocked-in vehicle does not create a KB Map/Unmap trigger.
Recovery was completed for migrated orders, and no similar issue was found in NV.
root_cause: During data migration, FDP "Previous Assessment Flag" was not set to Y for qualifying orders, leaving prior purchase orders visible in UV Inventory. Users with access to the editable "MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View" could then change the editable "Sales Order #" field without generating a KB Map/Unmap trigger.
resolution: Recovered migrated orders so prior purchase orders no longer appear in UV Inventory after restock, and changed the "Sales Order #" field to read-only in UV Inventory. The change passed UAT and was released to PROD on March 26, 2025.
technical_entities: MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View

investigation_summary: The incident concerned self-approval behavior in the FDP version, where the requester and approver were the same person and no error message was displayed. Investigation confirmed that the Self-Approval Restriction CR exists in the SC version but is not implemented in FDP. The approval flow rules were reviewed and were functioning as expected; no system change was required.
important_findings: In the SC version, the Self-Approval Restriction CR displays an error and prevents the approval email when the requester and approver are the same.
In the FDP version, approval email is expected to be sent to the approver even when the requester and approver are the same.

root_cause: The Self-Approval Restriction CR functionality implemented in the SC version is not implemented in the FDP version.
resolution: No corrective system change was required; the approval flow rules were verified as functioning correctly and the incident was requested to be dismissed.

investigation_summary: A UV Pool Cost Order remained incomplete although the related Stock-In verification was approved and the UV Purchase Order processing otherwise completed successfully. The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, code review found no issue, and historical logs were unavailable because the Stock-In Verification was approved in January 2024.
important_findings: A UV Purchase order is completed after its Stock-In verification reaches "Approved" status.
After Stock-In Approval, the process updates the vehicle, creates the UV Pool Cost order, and completes the UV Purchase Order.
For the affected case, all processing completed successfully except the UV Pool Cost Order status.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, and code review indicated the relevant code was working correctly.
No logs were available for the incident because the Stock-In Verification was approved in January 2024.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record by manually changing the PO status to "Completed" and creating a Journal Voucher; Journal linkage to KB was to be handled in batch.

investigation_summary: In FDP, Sales Posting was possible when no JCO existed because the Service Quote had not been progressed to "Customer Approved". The investigation confirmed that FDP had no Sales Posting validation for missing JCOs, while JCO creation after "Customer Approved" already required the corresponding Job Card to be closed before Sales Posting. A validation was implemented in UAT, approved for production, and released on March 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced on UAT1: a Sales Order could be completed while the JCO activity was not completed.
In FDP, Sales Posting was allowed when no JCO was created because the Service Quote was not "Customer Approved".
Changing the Service Quote to "Customer Approved" creates a JCO; after that, Sales Posting is blocked until the corresponding Job Card is closed.
The existing FDP behavior resulted from a missing validation check, potentially triggered when the user did not progress the Service Quote to "Customer Approved".
SC includes a validation message when changing a Delivery Request status to "Completed" in the equivalent missing-JCO scenario.
A similar validation was implemented in FDP, validated in UAT, approved for Prod, and released on March 26, 2025.
root_cause: FDP did not validate the presence of a JCO during Sales Posting when the Service Quote was not "Customer Approved", allowing Sales Posting without JCO creation or Job Card closure.
resolution: Implemented a validation in FDP to prevent the missing-JCO Sales Posting scenario; the change was deployed to UAT, approved for Prod, and released to production on March 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: Price master updates were missing in specific FDP environments for two separate groups of part numbers. In FDP Chugoku, the required morning-process file was not executed. In FDP Okayama, Hakodate, and Aomori production environments, files executed on March 6 did not insert new-record data; rerunning the files completed recovery in all affected environments.

FDP Okayama, Hakodate, and Aomori did not receive price master updates for five new part-number records despite files being executed on March 6.
For the second issue, the executed files did not insert data into the system.
Recovery was completed in all affected environments after the required files were run again.
root_cause: Two independent failures caused the missing updates: the morning-process file was not executed for FDP Chugoku, and files executed for new records in FDP Okayama, Hakodate, and Aomori production environments did not insert data into the system.
resolution: Reran the required files for the affected part numbers; recovery was completed in all affected environments.
technical_entities: Okayama, Hakodate and Aomori production environments

investigation_summary: In the Chugoku Production environment, recycle fee orders were not created because the TOB D21F file was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file. D21A creates the chassis order, which is a prerequisite for D21F to create the recycle fee order. The initially reported D21E dependency was corrected: the relevant sequence is D21A and D21F. Affected records were recovered by re-executing D21F after D21A processing; monitoring was implemented to identify similar cases for recovery.
important_findings: The root sequence issue was TOB processing D21F before the corresponding D21A file for the same order.
D21A creates the chassis order, while D21F creates the recycle fee order; without the chassis order, D21F cannot create the recycle fee order.
The initial reference to D21E in March 2025 was incorrect; the correct prerequisite file is D21A.
Re-executing D21F after successful D21A processing created the missing recycle fee orders.
The issue was identified as a TOB file sequencing issue rather than a Cubastion Siebel system defect.
Monitoring and email notifications were implemented to identify failed, unprocessed, or sequencing-related cases and enable recovery.
root_cause: The corresponding TOB D21F file was received and processed before the D21A file. Because D21A had not yet created the prerequisite chassis order, D21F could not create the recycle fee order.
resolution: Recovered affected records by re-executing D21F after the corresponding D21A process completed, creating the recycle fee orders. Monitoring was implemented to detect similar cases and trigger recovery actions.

investigation_summary: An intermittent Siebel issue caused Trade-in Consumption Tax not to be correctly reflected in the NV Quote header after entering a Trade-in Amount. Impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered. The code was corrected in UAT and released to production on March 26, 2025, with continued monitoring planned.
important_findings: The issue occurred intermittently and had no specific reproducible steps.
The affected behavior occurred when entering a Trade-in Amount: Trade-in Consumption Tax should populate in both the Trade-in subtab and the Quote Header.
All impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered; no recovery was required for other FDP environments.
The code did not follow Siebel best practices because Link Specification was not set to TRUE.
The UAT validation was intended to confirm that NV quotation and trade-in functionality continued to operate normally after the code change.
The production release of the fix was completed on March 26, 2025.
root_cause: Link Specification was not set to TRUE in the Siebel code, contrary to Oracle-recommended Siebel best practices, causing intermittent failure to reflect Trade-in Consumption Tax in the NV Quote Header.
resolution: Set Link Specification to TRUE in UAT, validated that existing NV quotation and trade-in functionality was not impacted, released the fix to production on March 26, 2025, and recovered affected records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments.

investigation_summary: A user revised a quote after creating an order, a Parts Internal Order, and Return order records for two part items. When the old part items were deleted and replacement part items were added, the replacement items received the same line numbers and synchronized to the existing part items instead of being created as new items. Recovery was completed for the affected record by removing the parent order ID from the affected part line items, allowing purchase-order creation to proceed.
important_findings: The order was created from a quote containing two part items, followed by creation of a Parts Internal Order and Return order records for both items.
After the quote was revised, the original two part items were deleted and two new part items were added with the same line numbers.
Quote-to-order synchronization matched the new part items to existing part items rather than creating new items.
Existing part orders for the old items caused the operation to stop and prevented purchase-order creation.
The incident was identified as a rare scenario and future occurrences should be monitored.
root_cause: After quote revision, replacement part items were assigned the same line numbers as deleted part items. During quote and order synchronization, they matched existing part items that already had Parts Internal Order and Return order records, leaving the parent order ID unchanged and causing the operation to stop.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record by removing the parent order ID from the line items associated with the parts; the user was then instructed to create the purchase order.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned incorrect chassis date display and an initial analysis attributed it to D21Z processing of MMDD date values without a year. The documented logic added the current year and converted MMDD to YYYYMMDD, resulting in incorrect dates for records requiring a prior year. Later comments disputed that D21Z contained the relevant actual shipping date, and the issue was not reproducible; only a temporary workaround was reported, with no permanent fix confirmed.
important_findings: Initial analysis identified D21Z_03032025113216 as containing Chassis Shipment Date and Actual Assembly Date in MMDD format without a year.
The configured D21Z processing logic adds the current year and converts MMDD values to YYYYMMDD; this caused an affected date to be updated as 04/12/2025.
Recovery was completed for the initially affected record.

Proposed corrective options included ODI logic to select the prior year when the MMDD date is greater than the file execution date, stopping Shipment Date updates from D21Z because D21N already updates it, or having TOB provide the year.
Later feedback stated that D21Z has no actual shipping date and that the issue was not D21Z-related, leaving the original source attribution unresolved.
As of 2026-04-07, IT reported that only a temporary workaround had been implemented and a permanent solution had not been applied; subsequent updates stated the issue could not be reproduced.

investigation_summary: Vehicle-to-business-object migration data in FDP was inconsistent because SC Prod vehicle identifiers did not reliably align. important_findings: Vehicle records in SC Prod contain X_KEY, SERIAL_NUM, and ASSET_NUM; these values should ideally match.
For ASSET_NUM "FK62F-605267", X_KEY and SERIAL_NUM were "FU74HZ-510966".
Migration used ASSET_NUM as the unique/user key, causing mismatches when X_KEY and ASSET_NUM differed.
When multiple SC Prod vehicles had the same VIN, the correct vehicle ID was not updated during migration.
Recovery scope included Chassis# (Key#) references for JC, WO, Quote, PO, JCO, Expense, and Change Order.
There was no Registration# gap; Power BI had no SC Version and no gap, so no Power BI recovery was required.
root_cause: SC Prod vehicle master data contained duplicate VIN records and mismatched X_KEY, SERIAL_NUM, and ASSET_NUM values; using ASSET_NUM as the unique key during migration prevented the correct vehicle ID from being updated.
resolution: Completed FDP recovery based on the provided file by correcting affected Chassis# (Key#) references across JC, WO, Quote, PO, JCO, Expense, and Change Order.
