The incident was cancelled after the findings were communicated to the user.
root_cause: User-initiated changes to the relevant responsible/contact codes.
resolution: Communicated the investigation findings to the user and cancelled the incident.

investigation_summary: Affected records were recovered while the issue was investigated. The incident was confirmed to be similar to MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348, where the first work order's work completion date was set on the JV. The fix was completed in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to production in the March 12 release.
important_findings: Affected records were recovered before the root-cause investigation was completed.
The issue matched prior incidents MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348.
The work completion date of the first work order was being set on the JV.
The fix was implemented in FDP UAT-1 and tracked with MFTBCFFR-3348.
The production fix was applied in the FDP release on March 12.
root_cause: The work completion date of the first work order was being set on the JV, consistent with MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348.
resolution: Recovered affected records, implemented the fix in FDP UAT-1, and deployed it to production in the March 12 FDP release.

investigation_summary: A pre-existing code issue prevented affected users from opening the VC screen. The impact began after deployment of MFTBCFFR-3329 and affected HQ users and Maintenance Staff. A code fix was validated in UAT environments and released to production on March 3, 2025 for all affected positions.
important_findings: The issue was caused by an existing code defect in the system.
The impact started after deployment of JIRA MFTBCFFR-3329.
HQ users and Maintenance Staff were affected.
The initial assessment that the issue was limited to HQ users was incorrect; VC had previously been accessible with master management privileges.
The fix was deployed and validated on UAT-01, UAT04, and UAT-08.
The code fix for all affected positions was released to production on March 3, 2025.
root_cause: A pre-existing system code defect, whose impact began after deployment of MFTBCFFR-3329, prevented affected positions from opening the VC screen.
resolution: Deployed a code fix for all affected positions to UAT-01, UAT04, and UAT-08, then released the fix to the production environment on March 3, 2025.

investigation_summary: PBI profit values differed from Siebel because deleted Siebel line items remained in the Datamart database and were included in profit calculations. The fix added DELETE_FLG handling in ODI and filtered Power BI reports to display only active line items. The changes were validated in UAT and deployed to prod across all environments.
important_findings: Deleted Siebel line items remain in the Datamart DB with DELETE_FLG = 'Y', while active line items use DELETE_FLG = 'N'.
The existing profit logic included records regardless of DELETE_FLG, causing PBI report profit discrepancies versus Siebel.
Impacted records for Iwate SO#: E000003241 and Chugoku SO#: E050024154 were recovered while the permanent fix was being developed.
DELETE_FLG was added to WC_UV_SALES_F and ODI processing was updated to set DELETE_FLG = 'Y' for inactive records.
Power BI UV reports 2_05 and 2_06 were updated with DELETE_FLG = 'N' filtering and verified by deleting a Siebel line item.
root_cause: PBI reports did not exclude Datamart line items marked DELETE_FLG = 'Y', so deleted Siebel line items were included in profit calculations.
resolution: Added DELETE_FLG to WC_UV_SALES_F, updated ODI to set DELETE_FLG = 'Y' for inactive records, and applied DELETE_FLG = 'N' filtering in Power BI UV reports 2_05 and 2_06. The changes were validated in UAT and deployed to prod across all environments.

investigation_summary: A fix was deployed to UAT-01 and UAT-08 and passed UAT validation. Following approval for release to RROD, the fix was applied to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: The fix was deployed on UAT-01 and UAT-08.
UAT validation passed.
Validation evidence referenced SO# A001292944 and Trade-In AR# H000044586.
The fix was released to RROD and applied to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
resolution: The validated fix was released to RROD and deployed to the production environment on March 12, 2025.

investigation_summary: The approval requests for two spreadsheets were reviewed. D8SENOOK approved both spreadsheets and is the manager of D8KUDOKE. The observed visibility is expected because the current process allows managers to view all approval requests from their subordinates; the item was classified as not an incident.
important_findings: Both spreadsheets were approved by D8SENOOK.
D8SENOOK is the manager of D8KUDOKE.
The current approval process allows managers to view all approval requests from their subordinates.
The reported behavior was determined to be expected and not an incident.

investigation_summary: The incident involved JV posting dates and manually editable Work Order dates. Investigation confirmed that JV posting-date logic matched MFTBCFFR-3348, MFTBCFFR-3347, MFTBCFFR-3337, and MFTBCFFR-3461, while users could set Work Start Date or Work Completion Date earlier than the Work Order creation date. The JV posting-date issue was addressed by MFTBCFFR-3348, and this incident added a control to make Work Completion Date read-only for external Work Orders, with the read-only timing changed to Acceptance Inspection.
important_findings: JV posting dates use the same logic as MFTBCFFR-3348, MFTBCFFR-3347, MFTBCFFR-3337, and MFTBCFFR-3461.
Work Start Date and Work Completion Date were editable in Work Order, allowing dates earlier than the Work Order creation date.
The JV posting-date issue was fixed in UAT by MFTBCFFR-3348.
Work Completion Date was made read-only for External work orders in UAT1 under JC# I001292913.
The requested read-only timing was changed from Work Completed to Acceptance Inspection and validated in FDP UAT-1.
root_cause: Work Start Date and Work Completion Date were editable in Work Order, allowing users to manually set dates earlier than the Work Order creation date; JV posting dates used the related common posting-date logic.
resolution: The JV posting-date fix from MFTBCFFR-3348 was applied, and Work Completion Date was configured as read-only for External work orders, with the lock applied at Acceptance Inspection. The change was validated in UAT-1/FDP UAT-1 and approved for PROD deployment.

investigation_summary: Sales recording was initially recovered successfully for the affected record. The incident was caused by the Recycle Fee order status being "Recycle Fee changed" instead of "Completed". The corrective fix was developed under MFTBCFFR-3151, applied to all UAT environments, and released to production on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: Recovery enabled sales recording for the affected record.
The Recycle Fee order status was "Recycle Fee changed" rather than "Completed".
The permanent fix was tracked under JIRA MFTBCFFR-3151.
The fix was applied in all UAT environments before production deployment.
The fix was applied to the production environment in the March 12, 2025 release.
root_cause: The Recycle Fee order status was "Recycle Fee changed" instead of "Completed".
resolution: Applied the fix developed under MFTBCFFR-3151 to all UAT environments and deployed it to production on March 12, 2025.

investigation_summary: The issue occurs after a price change because Siebel continues to use cached price data instead of querying the database for the updated value. New prices are retrieved correctly because no corresponding cache record exists. A custom solution to clear the cache after price changes was being investigated.
important_findings: Siebel stores price data in cache to improve performance.
After a price change, cached price data can prevent retrieval of the updated database price.
New prices are retrieved from the database because no cache record exists for them.
Clearing the Siebel price cache after a price change is required to force a new database query.
A custom solution for cache clearing was under investigation.
root_cause: Siebel retained outdated price data in cache after a price change, preventing a new query to the database for the updated price.

investigation_summary: A Quote remained in "GW Pending Approval" after data migration because the migration logic only handled "Pending Approval" to "In Progress" status changes. The affected Quote was recovered by changing its status to "In Progress". Separately, a dummy branch code in the location code field blocked user processing; after the user corrected it, job card processing and the MGW approval flow completed successfully.
important_findings: Data migration mapped service quotes with status "Pending Approval" to "In Progress".
The migration contained no condition check for "GW Pending Approval", leaving affected Quotes unchanged after migration.
Other records with "GW Pending Approval" were identified as records from 2021.
A dummy branch code in the location code field prevented the user from proceeding.
After the location code issue was corrected, job card processing completed successfully and the MGW approval flow worked correctly.
root_cause: The migration logic did not handle the "GW Pending Approval" status, and a dummy branch code in the location code field blocked user processing.
resolution: The affected Quote status was changed from "GW Pending Approval" to "In Progress", and the user corrected the dummy branch code in the location code field; job card processing and the MGW approval flow then completed successfully.

investigation_summary: A bodywork purchase order incorrectly received synchronized quote line items after the related quote was amended. Investigation reproduced the issue when a bodywork order item had negative list price and cost: negative-price validation interrupted the Create Purchase Order workflow, leaving the sales order Quote ID on the bodywork purchase order. A fix was deployed to all FDP UAT environments and released to production on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced by creating a bodywork order item with negative list price and cost, approving the quote and order, and using Create Purchase Order.
Negative-price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by Create Purchase Order.
The interrupted workflow caused the sales order Quote ID to be saved on the bodywork purchase order.
When the quote was amended, synchronization selected all sales orders with the same Quote ID, including the bodywork purchase order.
The issue was reproduced in UAT 1 with bodywork order B001292881 and Sales Order A001292880.
The fix was validated across all FDP UAT environments and deployed to production on March 12, 2025.
root_cause: Negative-price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by Create Purchase Order, causing the sales order Quote ID to remain saved on the bodywork purchase order. Quote amendment synchronization then updated that bodywork purchase order because it shared the Quote ID.
resolution: A fix was applied across all FDP UAT environments and released to the production environment on March 12, 2025.

investigation_summary: Tax Finalization in Registration request failed when creating expense items after a UV Sales Quote was revised and synchronized with its UV Sales Order. The issue was reproduced in UAT-01 for reference order E001292965 and attributed to user changes that interchanged Additional Body and Liability insurance line-item product types before invoice creation. Recovery for the affected record was completed.
important_findings: The user created a UV Sales Order from a UV Sales Quote.
The product type was changed from Additional Body to Liability insurance and then mistakenly changed back to Additional Body, interchanging the line items.
An Expense invoice was created from the Sales Order while the line items were interchanged.
Revising and syncing the UV Sales Quote restored the Additional Body and Liability Insurance line items to their original positions.
Because the invoice had been created from the interchanged line items, Tax Finalization in Registration request returned an error to create the expense for the items.
The issue was replicated in UAT-01 using reference order E001292965.
root_cause: User mis-operation caused Additional Body and Liability insurance line-item product types to be interchanged before Expense invoice creation; a subsequent UV Sales Quote revision and synchronization restored the original line-item positions, creating a mismatch that caused the Tax Finalization expense-creation error.
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record.

investigation_summary: Incorrect product IDs were assigned to migrated quote line items containing specific option codes, affecting NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders in the Chugoku environment. Investigation identified duplicate product-name records in the product master with different product types. All identified impacted records were recovered after business hours, and the issue was reported not to recur when processing migrated data or copying migrated NV Quotes.
important_findings: Product master contained duplicate records for product names "AE", "AD", "AF", "4A", "FD", and "BB".
For each duplicate product name, one record had product type "Parts" and the other had product type "Options".
Migrated quote line items containing the affected option codes received incorrect product IDs.
The issue could also occur when a user copied a migrated NV Sales Quote and created a new record in Chugoku.
A list of impacted NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders was identified, and recovery for all impacted records was completed.
root_cause: Duplicate product-name records in the product master for "AE", "AD", "AF", "4A", "FD", and "BB", with conflicting product types "Parts" and "Options", caused incorrect product IDs to be populated on migrated quote line items containing those option codes.
resolution: Recovery was completed for all identified impacted NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders. The issue was confirmed not to recur when users process migrated data or copy from migrated NV Quotes.

investigation_summary: The incident affected sales-order processing for SO# A034532427 and NV Sales Order A028536611. Investigation found that the same vehicle ID had been updated to two NV Sales Orders during data migration; Map/Unmap processing during delta data migration was identified as a possible contributor. Recovery required reprocessing the D21G file for the chassis order.
important_findings: The same vehicle ID was updated to two NV Sales Orders during data migration.
Map/Unmap processing between delta data migrations was identified as a possible cause of the duplicate vehicle-ID update.
No other NV Sales Orders with the same issue were identified.
The initially reported recovery status was later corrected as not completed.
The D21G file for the chassis order was reprocessed as part of recovery.
root_cause: During data migration, the same vehicle ID was updated to two NV Sales Orders; Map/Unmap processing during delta data migration may have contributed.
resolution: Reprocessed the D21G file for the chassis order as part of the recovery.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned FDP behavior for parts internal orders, including an error when creating a parts order and incorrect inventory name field editability. Investigation confirmed that FDP logic differed from SC. The corrected logic was validated in FDP UAT-1 and released to production on March 26, 2025.
important_findings: FDP logic differed from SC for parts internal order inventory name field editability.
The inventory name field must be non-editable when Already Issued, Already Reserved, or Processed Qty is not 0.
The inventory name field must be editable only when Already Issued, Already Reserved, and Processed Qty are all 0.
Initial FDP UAT-1 fixes did not pass confirmation; additional feedback was addressed before the final UAT fix.
The final fix was applied to FDP UAT-1, approved for PROD deployment, and released to production on March 26, 2025.
root_cause: FDP logic for parts internal order inventory name field editability was not aligned with SC specifications based on Already Issued, Already Reserved, and Processed Qty values.
resolution: Corrected the FDP logic in FDP UAT-1 to match SC behavior and released the approved fix to production on March 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: Impacted records were recovered successfully. The incident was caused by mismatched Vehicle Id values between the Parent NV Sales Order and one or more Child Purchase Order records during delta data migration.
important_findings: All impacted records were successfully recovered.
Vehicle Id values were mismatched between the Parent NV Sales Order and one or more Child Purchase Order records.
The mismatch occurred during delta data migration.
root_cause: Vehicle Id in the Parent NV Sales Order and one or more Child Purchase Order records was mismatched during delta data migration.
resolution: Recovered all impacted records.

investigation_summary: The incident involved duplicate recycle fee orders for Iwate, including record A000015816. The affected records were recovered, and users were instructed to proceed. The case was identified as similar to MFTBCFFR-3403 and will be tracked under that incident.
important_findings: Duplicate recycle fee orders occurred for Iwate.
Record A000015816 was added as an affected item.
Recovery of the affected records was completed.
The incident is similar to MFTBCFFR-3403 and is being tracked there.
resolution: Recovered the affected duplicate recycle fee order records; subsequent tracking moved to MFTBCFFR-3403.

investigation_summary: Invoice data generation was affected when shipment O000126395 contained Part# MH000931 twice with the same Line # 14 in its shipment lines. The invoice-data query was improved and deployed to FDP Prod. The updated query handles monthly invoice creation on the 10th, 20th, and end of month, as well as Sales Return scenarios involving duplicate part numbers and shipment/return charges.
important_findings: Shipment O000126395 had duplicate shipment lines for Part# MH000931 with the same Line # 14.
The duplicate shipment-line data caused the invoice-data query issue.
The query used to provide invoice data was improved to handle duplicate part number and line-number scenarios.
The change was deployed to FDP Prod.
Monthly invoice queries run on the 10th, 20th, and end of month are confirmed to handle the issue.
Sales Return creation with duplicate part numbers in shipment lines and shipment charge/Return charge is handled.
root_cause: Part# MH000931 appeared twice with the same Line # 14 in the shipment lines for shipment O000126395, which the invoice-data query did not handle correctly.
resolution: Improved the query used to provide invoice data to handle duplicate shipment lines, then deployed the change to FDP Prod.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Recycle Fee orders were mapped to a Sales order after two D21F files were received for the same VIN. The affected records were recovered in all FDP environments. Recurrence prevention is being handled under related issue MFTBCFFR-3357.
important_findings: Two D21F files were received for the same VIN, creating duplicate records.
The duplicate records resulted in duplicate Recycle Fee orders mapped to the Sales order.
The duplicate files were D21F_10012025143156 and D21F_21022025093442.
Recovery of the affected records was completed in all FDP environments.
The issue is tracked as similar to MFTBCFFR-3357 for further handling and recurrence prevention.
root_cause: Duplicate D21F files received for the same VIN created duplicated data and duplicate Recycle Fee orders mapped to the Sales order.
resolution: Recovered the affected records in all FDP environments; further recurrence-prevention work is tracked under MFTBCFFR-3357.

investigation_summary: An approval request was generated with a NULL approver after the user selected "Generate Approval" from the "Branch-CS-Staff" position. The spreadsheet status was reverted and the "Generate Approval" button was enabled on both affected spreadsheets. Users must generate approvals from the correct position.
important_findings: The user pressed "Generate Approval" while in the "Branch-CS-Staff" position.
The resulting approval request had a NULL approver.
The spreadsheet status was reverted following the incorrect approval generation.
The "Generate Approval" button was enabled on both affected spreadsheets.
The incident was identified as user mis-operation.
root_cause: User generated the approval request from the "Branch-CS-Staff" position instead of the correct position, resulting in a NULL approver.
resolution: Reverted the spreadsheet status and enabled the "Generate Approval" button on both affected spreadsheets; instructed the user to proceed from the correct position.

investigation_summary: A bodywork purchase order incorrectly retained the originating sales order's Quote ID when created from a quote containing negative list price and cost. Negative price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order", causing later quote amendments to synchronize sales-order line items to the bodywork purchase order. A fix was validated across FDP UAT environments and deployed to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced in UAT1 with Bodywork order B001292881 and Sales Order A001292880.
A bodywork order item with both negative list price and negative cost triggered the failure path.
The "Create Purchase Order" workflow was interrupted by negative price validation.
The interrupted workflow saved the sales order's Quote ID on the bodywork purchase order.
When the quote was amended, line-item synchronization selected all sales orders sharing the Quote ID, including the bodywork purchase order.
The fix was applied to all FDP UAT environments and released to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
root_cause: Negative price validation broke the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order" for a bodywork order with negative cost and list price, causing the sales order's Quote ID to be saved on the bodywork purchase order. Subsequent quote amendments synchronized line items to that bodywork purchase order because it shared the Quote ID.
resolution: A fix was deployed across all FDP UAT environments and then applied to the production environment in the March 12, 2025 release.

investigation_summary: A trigger sent from siebel FDP Wakayam Prod (FDPW) did not receive a response from D2S Side. Recovery was completed and verified by the requester. D2S shared an RCA, and the discussion confirmed that no action was pending from the siebel side.
important_findings: The trigger was sent from siebel FDP Wakayam Prod (FDPW), but no response was received from D2S Side.
The affected transaction was PO# N000010548 with Siebel Id 1-SW0NV, timestamped 2025/02/25 11:58:42 AM.
Recovery was completed and confirmed as correct by the requester.
D2S shared an RCA, and no pending issue remained on the siebel side.
resolution: Recovery was completed and verified; no further action was pending from the siebel side.

investigation_summary: Invoices were reprocessed in the night batch following a manual bulk invoice recovery performed on 21 February 2025. Investigation found that the "Sent to KB" flag remained set to N during the recovery. No product fix was required; the manual recovery SOP will be updated with the missing validation step.
important_findings: The issue occurred after manual bulk invoice recovery performed on 21 February 2025.
The "Sent to KB" flag was set to N.
Because the flag was N, the invoices were processed again in the night batch.
The incident resulted from a recovery-process oversight rather than a product defect.
An additional validation step will be added to the manual recovery SOP.
root_cause: During manual bulk invoice recovery, the "Sent to KB" flag was left set to N, causing reprocessing in the night batch.
resolution: Update the manual recovery SOP to include the additional step for validating or setting the "Sent to KB" flag; no product fix was required.

investigation_summary: The incident affected sales processing and required recovery of affected records. A fix was applied to UAT-01 and was reported as working correctly, while affected records were recovered. Further root-cause analysis could not continue because required user-side logs were unavailable, and the ticket was closed.
important_findings: Affected records were recovered on 2025-02-26 and again confirmed recovered on 2025-03-13.
The issue caused the Sales Process to stop.
A fix was applied on UAT-01 and reported as working correctly.
Further analysis required logs from the user side, but the user was unavailable to provide them.
The ticket was closed without a documented root cause.
resolution: Affected records were recovered, and a fix was applied and validated as working on UAT-01.

investigation_summary: For Account 0000T01468, Siebel sent the updated AR address to KB through the nightly batch and also returned the correct address for real-time billing. The issue was identified as occurring on the KB invoice address-printing side, with KB BIP mapping suspected of using the Account file address. A fix was validated on UAT8 and deployed to Prod on 2025-03-03.
important_findings: The address for Account 0000T01468 was changed on 2025-02-17 and transmitted from Siebel to KB during the nightly batch process.
The Customer file sent to KB contained only the AR address: 411-1 Minori-cho, Yonago City, Tottori Prefecture.
Siebel also sent the correct address in the API response for the job card used in real-time billing.
The suspected issue area was KB invoice BIP mapping, potentially using the Account file address instead of the AR address.
The fix passed UAT on UAT8 and was deployed to Prod on 2025-03-03.
resolution: A fix was validated on UAT8 and deployed to Prod on 2025-03-03.

investigation_summary: Tax confirmation could not be completed for an affected order after data migration. Investigation found that completed invoices retained an old SC environment line number on PO lines of type "Tax" instead of the new China environment line number. The affected record was corrected, enabling the user to proceed with tax confirmation; no additional impacted records were found.
important_findings: The issue affected tax confirmation for order code 0000U05007, with customer payment method Transfer and customer payment date 2025/02/14.
For invoices with status "Completed", the invoice line number in the China environment must be associated with the "Tax" type PO line.
Migrated invoices were registered as "Completed", but "Tax" type PO lines remained associated with the old line number from the SC environment.
The affected record was recovered by linking the "Tax" type PO line to the new China environment line number.
A review found no other records impacted; no additional recovery was required.
root_cause: A data-migration configuration error left the old SC environment invoice line number associated with "Tax" type PO lines for invoices registered as "Completed", rather than associating the new China environment line number.
resolution: Corrected the affected record by linking its "Tax" type PO line to the new China environment line number, allowing tax confirmation to proceed.

investigation_summary: The incident affected records including A027550319. Analysis determined that the issue resulted from improper recovery of the affected records. Both records were subsequently recovered correctly, and users were instructed to proceed.
important_findings: A027550319 was added as an affected item.
Both affected records required recovery.
The records had been recovered improperly.
The affected records were correctly recovered as the final corrective action.
root_cause: Improper recovery of the affected records.
resolution: The affected records were correctly recovered.

investigation_summary: The issue was fixed in UAT8, where the team prepared test records for JV creation and planned to run the kb script to generate a file for confirmation. All impacted records were recovered, and the fix was released to Chugoku Prod (China production environment).
important_findings: The issue was fixed in UAT8.
Test records were being created for JV creation.
The kb script was to be run to create a file for confirmation.
All records impacted by the issue were recovered.
The fix was released to Chugoku Prod / the China production environment.
resolution: The issue was fixed in UAT8, impacted records were recovered, and the fix was released to Chugoku Prod.

investigation_summary: UV Quote and UV Sales Order showed differing Sales Profit values after quote creation or revision. Investigation identified inconsistent additional-cost calculation logic and rounding behavior in UV Quote, resulting in profit discrepancies, including 1-yen differences. The UV Quote calculation was aligned with UV Sales Order, validated in UAT-01 for AR#: H000045187, and deployed to production on April 14.
important_findings: Initial UAT validation failed for AR#: H000037289, where Sales Quote# 1-5LHJS7 Rev.2 had Profit 526,340 and SO# E001281570 had Profit 552,740.
Data patches were completed in FDP environments except for two records in FDP Okayama; a remaining discrepancy was also reported for FDP Chugoku AR#: H000147553.
UV Quote rounded values during Sales Profit calculation, causing profit differences between UV Quote and UV Sales Order.
The fix aligned additional cost price calculation logic in UV Quote with UV Sales Order and removed rounding from the UV Quote Profit Amount calculation.
The fix is independent of Consumption Tax Rounding configured in Administration – Sales – Consumption Tax Master.
UAT passed for the rounding issue on AR#: H000045187 before production deployment.
root_cause: UV Quote used different rounding and additional cost price calculation logic than UV Sales Order when calculating Sales Profit, causing inconsistent Profit Amount values.
resolution: Updated UV Quote Sales Profit calculation to use the same additional cost price logic and no-rounding behavior as UV Sales Order. The change passed UAT-01 validation for AR#: H000045187 and was deployed to production in the April 14 release.

investigation_summary: A Service Request created by USER: D8ISATAK generated an approval request with no approver. The approval flow requires a Branch-CS-Staff user's manager to have Branch-Parts-Mgr as the primary position; USER: D8YUJISA had Branch-Service-Mgr as the primary position. The issue can be resolved by correcting the manager primary position and staff parent position, deleting the existing approval request, and creating it again.
important_findings: USER: D8ISATAK is a Branch-CS-Staff and created the Service Request.
USER: D8YUJISA had the Branch-Parts-Mgr role but its primary position was Branch-Service-Mgr.
The approval flow sends approval requests to Branch-Parts-Mgr, resulting in no approver when the manager primary position is Branch-Service-Mgr.
Only Branch-CS-Staff whose manager is Branch-Parts-Mgr can create an SR for approval under the current approval flow.
Existing approval requests must be deleted and recreated after updating the manager primary position and staff parent position.
root_cause: USER: D8YUJISA's primary position was Branch-Service-Mgr rather than Branch-Parts-Mgr, so the approval flow could not identify an approver for the Service Request created by USER: D8ISATAK.
resolution: Change USER: D8YUJISA's primary position to Branch-Parts-Mgr and update the staff parent position, delete the current approval request, then create the approval request again.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Premium Payment records with blank PPR# were identified for multiple orders in FDP and also in SC. Investigation found that SonpoWeb triggers IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) during daily settlement processing, and Siebel creates records from the decoded interface payload when the received Policy Number exists. The behavior was confirmed as functioning as expected; duplicate records were cancelled and the ticket was dismissed.
important_findings: Duplicate Premium Payment records with blank PPR# were found for orders Q019496832, Q034399511, and Q036345352.
The duplicate records were created through SonpoWeb calls to IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation).
Daily settlement processing triggers IFIN010 (Daily Settlement) from Siebel to SonpoWeb and IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) from SonpoWeb to Siebel.
Siebel decodes the IFIN011 payload, extracts settlement and premium values, and creates a record when the received Policy Number exists.
SC has the same functionality and contained 18 duplicate records; Chugoku had no new duplicate records since March 3, 2025.
The functionality was determined to be working as expected, with no interface-process change identified.
root_cause: SonpoWeb triggered IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) with additional clearance-data details, and Siebel created Premium Payment records from the decoded payload when the received Policy Number existed.
resolution: Duplicate Premium Payment records were updated to "Cancelled". No functional change was made; the behavior was accepted as expected and the ticket was dismissed.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed for the affected JCs. Investigation determined that a manual emergency recovery mistake caused the Account Code to be null in the JV for the emergency recovery requested by Yoshihara San. The issue was not identified as a product bug.
important_findings: The affected JCs were recovered successfully.
The emergency recovery was performed manually.
A manual recovery mistake resulted in a null Account Code in the JV.
The affected emergency recovery was requested by Yoshihara San.
The incident was classified as not being a bug.
root_cause: A manual emergency recovery mistake caused the Account Code to be null in the JV.
resolution: Completed recovery for the affected JCs and committed to verify recovery actions more carefully in future emergency recoveries.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Recycle Fee Orders were created for vehicles and affected delivery approval processing. Investigation identified duplicated D21F file processing and confirmed that users entering recycling confirmation in VOW triggered the issue. All affected duplicate orders were recovered across FDP environments; prevention requires users to stop entering recycling confirmation in VOW or a Change Request affecting Siebel and ODI.
important_findings: Two D21F files were received for the same VIN, creating duplicate records: D21F_08012025113917 and D21F_10022025113525.
Under the current specification, receipt of a D21F file creates a Recycle Fee Order for the respective vehicle.
The issue was determined to occur when users entered recycling confirmation from VOW.
Duplicate Recycle Fee Orders were recovered in all FDP environments.
If VOW recycling confirmation cannot be discontinued, a Change Request is required for changes to both Siebel and ODI.
root_cause: Users entered recycling confirmation in VOW, resulting in duplicated D21F file processing and duplicate Recycle Fee Orders mapped to the Sales order.
resolution: Recovered all affected duplicate Recycle Fee Orders in all FDP environments. Users were to be instructed to stop entering recycling confirmation in VOW; otherwise, a Change Request is required for Siebel and ODI changes.

investigation_summary: An issue related to LOV was addressed and fixed in the UAT8 environment. After UAT approval, the LOV-related changes were deployed to the Chugoku Prod environment.
important_findings: The incident was related to LOV.
The LOV fix was implemented and validated in UAT8.
UAT passed and approval was provided for production release.
The LOV-related changes were implemented in the Chugoku Prod environment.
resolution: Implemented the LOV-related changes in the Chugoku Prod environment after UAT8 validation and approval.

investigation_summary: During data migration, an unpopulated backend column on the Siebel side caused missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report. All records affected by the migration issue were recovered. Two Sales Orders, A003403571 and A017304950, had a separate trade-in amount issue caused by FDP ODI logic; the code fix was applied in all UAT environments and production release was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3470.
important_findings: A backend column on the Siebel side was not populated during data migration, causing missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report.
Multiple impacted Sales Orders were recovered for the data-migration issue.
Sales Orders A003403571 and A017304950 remained at Trade-in Price Total 0 because they did not meet ODI logic conditions.

The issue can be reproduced when an NV Sales Order with a trade-in is posted, the related UV Purchase Order is stocked in, and the stocked-in UV Purchase Order is used for a new UV Sales Order; the NV sales order trade-in amount becomes 0 in PBI report NV_3-06.
The ODI behavior was common across FDPs and had been resolved in SC through Incident INC4242736.
Required FDP ODI code changes were applied across all UAT environments and UAT was approved.
root_cause: A backend column on the Siebel side was not populated during data migration, resulting in missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report.
resolution: All records impacted by the data-migration issue were recovered. The separate FDP ODI logic fix was applied in all UAT environments, approved for release to PROD, and tracked under MFTBCFFR-3470.

investigation_summary: Chassis orders were not created for affected VINs because required D21A/D21C/D21E files were missing from files received from TOB, while D21N and, for some cases, D21F were present. The initial two records were recovered after the D21A file was provided. Additional affected records were handled through recovery/individual chassis-order creation after validating whether an order already existed; three recoveries were confirmed.
important_findings: BE740E-400168 and BE740E-400173 received D21N but no D21A/D21C/D21E, preventing chassis-order creation.
D21A was subsequently provided and recovery was completed for the initial affected records; both chassis orders were confirmed.
A review of TOB files identified BE740G-400668, BE740G-400689, BG740G-400212, and FU85HZ-500015 with D21N and D21F received but no D21A or D21C.
Before recovery, engineers were instructed to verify that no chassis order already existed.
Recovery was completed for four additional VINs, and three recoveries were confirmed.
root_cause: Required D21A/D21C/D21E input files were not received from TOB, so chassis orders were not created.
resolution: After the required file was provided, the initial records were recovered. Additional affected records were recovered/handled by creating individual chassis orders after checking for existing chassis orders.

investigation_summary: A re-edited External WO caused the JV Posting Date for SPO J000192078 to remain at 2025/01/30 while the related work completed on 2025/02/19. Investigation confirmed that the work completion date/time for External WO 1-F9HQT was not updated in the JC Header before JV creation; the JC Header was only updated after Generate Approval was clicked in the MF Job Card Detail Applet. A fix was validated in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to PROD on March 12.
important_findings: SPO work start date/time and work completion date/time are sourced from the JC Header.
A JV is created when an SPO reaches "Completion of Acceptance Inspection", and its Posting Date is based on the SPO work completion date/time.
For re-edited External WO 1-F9HQT, the JC Header retained the previous completion date, causing the JV for SPO J000192078 to use Posting Date 2025/01/30.
The JC Header work completion date/time was updated to 2025/02/19 14:05:04 only after Generate Approval was clicked in the MF Job Card Detail Applet.
Updating the JC Header after JV creation caused a date/time mismatch between the JV and the SPO screen.
The issue was reproduced and fixed in FDP UAT-1 before production deployment.
root_cause: The work completion date/time of re-edited External WO 1-F9HQT was not correctly set in the JC Header before the JV was created, so the JV used the prior JC Header/SPO completion date of 2025/01/30.
resolution: A fix was implemented and validated in FDP UAT-1, then deployed to PROD in the March 12 release.

investigation_summary: The SPO JV Posting Date was derived from the Job Card Work Completion Date. For Service Purchase Orders, the JV was created before the Work Completion Date was changed, causing the SPO JV to retain the old date. The shared fix for MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348 was completed in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to production on March 12.
important_findings: JV Posting Date is sourced from the Job Card field Work Completion Date.
For Service Purchase Orders, the JV is created before the Job Card Work Completion Date is changed.
The sequence caused the SPO JV Posting Date to use the previous Work Completion Date.
MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348 required the same fix and were tracked under MFTBCFFR-3348.
The fix was completed in FDP UAT-1 and applied to production in the March 12 release.
root_cause: For Service Purchase Orders, the JV was created before the Job Card Work Completion Date was updated, so the SPO JV Posting Date retained the old Work Completion Date.
resolution: Implemented the shared fix in FDP UAT-1 and deployed it to the production environment in the March 12 release.

investigation_summary: The incident involved missing chassis and option asking prices and costs on the NV Quote. Initial investigation could not reproduce the one-time Production occurrence in UAT, but later testing in RT2 identified pricing issues when the RWD date was removed and re-entered while updating chassis and options. A validation requiring the Desired shipping date before chassis selection was implemented, the error-message wording was corrected, and the fix was released to Production on 12 August 2025.
important_findings: The original Production occurrence was recovered, including the actual cost of options, but could not initially be reproduced in UAT.
When the RWD date was null, the selected chassis price was not displayed on the NV Quote.
In RT2, removing the RWD date and updating the chassis, then re-adding the date and updating the chassis, resulted in chassis pricing being displayed while option pricing became null.
The reported issue concerned missing asking price and cost for both chassis and option prices, not only blank chassis pricing.
Backend investigation attributed the zero-cost issue to the selected line options.
The validation message was corrected to use "Desired shipping date" rather than "scheduled shipping date".
root_cause: A null RWD date caused selected chassis pricing not to display; the zero-cost condition was attributed to the selected line options.
resolution: Added validation requiring users to enter the Desired shipping date before selecting a chassis, corrected the validation-message wording, and released the changes to Production on 12 August 2025.

investigation_summary: Order A028094368 was not visible in the Power BI report. Investigation confirmed that the report filter displays only records with required quantity equal to '1'; this order has required quantity '4'.
important_findings: The Power BI report filters records to required quantity '1'.
Order A028094368 has required quantity '4'.
Records with required quantity other than '1' are excluded from the report.
root_cause: The Power BI report filter excludes records whose required quantity is not '1', including order A028094368 with required quantity '4'.

investigation_summary: The Unit Price mapping in the Siebel response was sending the List Price amount instead of the Sales Price amount across all FDP environments. The mapping was corrected on UAT1 and validated using Parts Sales Order M001292036, where the correct amount was sent from the Shipment. The validated fix was deployed to Prod on 2025-03-03.
important_findings: The issue affected all FDP environments; impacted FDPs were updated from "Chugoku" to "Common".
The Siebel Unit Price response mapping sent the List Price amount instead of the Sales Price amount.
The fix was deployed to UAT1 and validated with Parts Sales Order M001292036.
After the fix, the correct amount was sent from the Shipment.
The fix was deployed to Prod on 2025-03-03.
root_cause: Incorrect Unit Price mapping in the Siebel response, which sent the List Price amount instead of the Sales Price amount.
resolution: Corrected the Unit Price mapping to send the correct amount from the Shipment, validated the change on UAT1, and deployed the fix to Prod on 2025-03-03.

investigation_summary: Customer AR records in UAT8 and Chugoku Production had incorrect module open flags after AR data updates. The issue occurred when one NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department code was blank while the remaining codes were "9999", preventing module flags from being updated. Recovery was completed in UAT8 and then in Chugoku Production.
important_findings: Affected customers were identified in UAT8 and Chugoku Production.
During Customer AR data updates, module flags were not updated when one NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department code was blank and the others were "9999".
If a module's responsible department is "9999", its corresponding module open flag must be removed; this applies to NV and the other modules.
Recovery was completed in UAT8 before being performed in Chugoku Production.
Recovery was completed in Chugoku Production.
root_cause: During Customer AR data updates, module flags were not updated when one of the NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department codes was blank and the remaining codes were "9999".
resolution: Corrected the affected Customer AR module open flags through recovery in UAT8 and subsequently in Chugoku Production, removing each module's open flag when its responsible department was "9999".

investigation_summary: A recovery JV was created for the affected record, and recovery of the PO was completed. MFTBCFFR-3337 was determined to require the same fix as MFTBCFFR-3347 and MFTBCFFR-3348, with ongoing tracking consolidated under MFTBCFFR-3348. The fix was completed in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to the production environment in the March 12 release.
important_findings: A recovery JV was created for the affected record.
Recovery of the PO was completed.
MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348 required the same fix and were tracked under MFTBCFFR-3348.
The fix was completed in FDP UAT-1 before production deployment.
The fix was applied to production in the March 12 release.
resolution: The shared fix tracked under MFTBCFFR-3348 was completed in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to the production environment on March 12; recovery JV and PO recovery were completed.

investigation_summary: TOB responses were not reflected in the UI because JMS connections were disconnected during response processing. JMS logs recorded a connection reset error, SBL-JCA-00303. The JMS connection pool size was increased from 60 to 90 and deployed to production on 26/02/2025; no Siebel changes were required.
important_findings: Affected records were recovered before the root-cause investigation was completed.
TOB responses were not reflected in the UI.
JMS connections were lost during response processing.
JMS logs showed: "parseResponse\{"Error":"Logon Request 18 was abandoned after 1739853464288 ms. Connection: e00080 due to connection shutdown request Connection reset(SBL-JCA-00303)"}"
The JMS connection pool was increased from 60 to 90 to accommodate requests from all FDPs.
The change was released to production on 26/02/2025 and required no Siebel changes.
root_cause: JMS connections were disconnected during TOB response processing, preventing TOB responses from being reflected in the UI.
resolution: Increased the JMS connection pool size from 60 to 90 and deployed the JMS-level change to production on 26/02/2025.

investigation_summary: The incident behavior was attributed to code changes made during FDP Chugoku UAT. Code was corrected for both UAT8 problem statements and validated as working in UAT. The fix was released to the production environment on February 26, 2025.
important_findings: The behavior was caused by changes made during FDP Chugoku UAT.
Code was fixed for both UAT8 problem statements.
The corrected code was confirmed as working in UAT.
The fix was released to production on February 26, 2025.
root_cause: Code changes made during FDP Chugoku UAT caused the observed behavior.
resolution: Modified the code to address both UAT8 problem statements, validated the fix in UAT, and released it to production on February 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: The issue occurred across all FDPs when users with the "Planning Staff" position encountered positions removed by NV-14 CR changes. Positions listed in "MFTBCFFR-3329_MissingPositions_20250218.csv" were absent following NV-14 CR changes.
The issue affected users assigned the "Planning Staff" position.
The fix was validated successfully in UAT.
The same correction was released to the production environment on 19 February.
No recovery was required.

investigation_summary: Inbox recovery for the specified inbox data was completed. Unlike SC, FDP had no scheduled activity for periodic inbox recovery/deletion. A Weekly SR was subsequently filed for FDP to perform the activity regularly.
important_findings: The recovery process was successfully completed for the given inbox data.
SC had a weekly SR for inbox recovery, but no corresponding scheduled activity existed in FDP.
Periodic deletion/recovery activity was requested for FDP to match the process used in SC.
A Weekly SR was filed against this JIRA for the recurring FDP activity.
root_cause: FDP did not have a weekly SR or scheduled activity for periodic inbox recovery/deletion, unlike SC.
resolution: A Weekly SR was filed for FDP to perform periodic inbox recovery/deletion activity.

investigation_summary: Okinawa experienced spreadsheet creation failures caused by duplicate spreadsheet serial numbers, despite having only one agency. Investigation found that serial numbers were generated from 0001 for each Ejibai ID, which could collide with an existing spreadsheet having the same insurance company code, year, and serial number in Completed or Approved status. Tokyo Marine was requested to add codes individually so each branch can create spreadsheets separately.
important_findings: The suspected extra-zero issue in the ID was ruled out; the Siebel configuration matched the provided Excel configuration.
Unlike Shikoku and Wakayama, where multiple agency codes caused serial-number overlap, Okinawa had one agency but received multiple requests with the same serial number.
For each Ejibai ID, the spreadsheet serial number was generated starting from 0001.
A new spreadsheet creation fails when a spreadsheet with the same insurance company code, year, and serial number already exists in Completed or Approved status.
The E column in the E-JiBAI Web ID Master file was blank for Okinawa; confirmation was requested regarding bulk-settlement authorization for registered users.
root_cause: Spreadsheet serial numbers were generated from 0001 per Ejibai ID, resulting in duplicate serial-number collisions with existing spreadsheets for the same insurance company code and year.
resolution: Tokyo Marine was requested to add codes individually so that each branch can create spreadsheets separately.

investigation_summary: The response omitted data because the Planned Payment Date became null for the affected record. With Payment term "00", Payment term type "Month", and Payment date "01" earlier than the Job Card Delivery Date, no Planned Payment Date was generated. The Payment date was changed to "20".
important_findings: Payment term was "00".
Payment term type was "Month".
Payment date "01" was less than the Delivery Date of the Job Card.
When the Payment date was earlier than the Job Card Delivery Date, Planned Payment Date became null and no data was sent in the response.
The affected record's Payment date was updated from "01" to "20".
root_cause: For Payment term "00" with Payment term type "Month", a Payment date earlier than the Job Card Delivery Date caused Planned Payment Date to become null, resulting in no response data.
resolution: Updated the affected record's Payment date to "20".

investigation_summary: Affected records were recovered, and recovery was confirmed. Investigation identified issues in JMS server logs while processing TOB responses; interface request volume was considered a possible contributing factor and was being reproduced in UAT. The issue was subsequently resolved under Jira MFTBCFFR-3336, where the RCA and fix plan were documented.
important_findings: Affected records were recovered and recovery was confirmed.
JMS server logs showed issues while processing TOB responses.
Interface request volume was identified as a possible contributing factor during initial analysis.
The interface behavior was being reproduced in UAT to determine whether parameter changes were required.
FDPs were monitored for TOB responses not populated on orders so they could be recovered.
The final resolution, RCA, and fix plan were handled under MFTBCFFR-3336.

investigation_summary: Vehicle records in FDP Chugoku had FUSO reception # populated in the VIN# field despite correct VIN# values being available in SC PROD. The affected vehicles were included in the December initial migration but omitted from the export program's delta data. Recovery was completed for all affected records.
important_findings: Affected records were vehicles in FDP Chugoku with FUSO reception # in the VIN# field.
Correct VIN# values existed in SC PROD for the affected vehicles.
The vehicles were part of the December initial migration.
The affected vehicles were not included in the export program's delta data.
All records in the attached affected-vehicle list were recovered.
root_cause: Vehicles included in the December initial migration were omitted from the export program's delta data, resulting in FUSO reception # remaining in the VIN# field for affected FDP Chugoku vehicle records.
resolution: Recovered all affected vehicle records.

investigation_summary: Report data was missing after the IKM was changed in ODI under MFTBCFFR-3269. The initial full load behavior deleted records from the DataMart table. The DataMart backup was used to recover affected data across environments, and reports now display the recovered records; Aomori remains empty because it has no records with qualifying report statuses.
important_findings: The IKM in ODI was changed from IKM Insert Global to IKM Incremental Update under MFTBCFFR-3269.
After the IKM change, the IKM initially ran as a full load rather than an incremental load.
The full load deleted records from the DataMart table, causing missing report data.
A backup of the DataMart table containing the old records was available during recovery.
Recovery was completed for all environments and data became visible in reports.
The Aomori report has no records because it only includes records with status code "Internal Posted" or "Expired", and no Aomori records meet those conditions.
root_cause: Changing the ODI IKM from IKM Insert Global to IKM Incremental Update caused the IKM to initially run as a full load, deleting records from the DataMart table.
resolution: Recovered the DataMart table records from the available backup and completed recovery across all environments.

investigation_summary: The user could not create a new UV Bodybuilding PO for line items that already had an existing PO and were not cancelled. The existing PO must be cancelled before a new PO can be created for the same line items.
important_findings: An existing UV Bodybuilding PO was already created for the affected line items.
The existing PO had not been cancelled.
The system prevents creation of a new PO for line items with an active existing PO.
Cancelling the existing PO is required before creating a replacement PO.
root_cause: An active, uncancelled UV Bodybuilding PO already existed for the same line items.
resolution: Cancel the existing UV Bodybuilding PO before creating a new PO for the same line items.

investigation_summary: Insurance-order records migrated from SC were not filtered correctly because Staff ID was not properly resolved during migration. A subsequent issue affected visibility of new My Branch records. Because FDP and SC filter functionality differs, the solution added a "Daily Settlement Process" button and a multiple-select flag to the "All records" Applet; UAT passed and the change was released to Production for all FDP.
important_findings: During migration, Staff ID was not properly resolved for insurance orders, causing filters to fail.
Impacted records were recovered so users could view records according to the filter.
Users could view records migrated from SC but could not view new records in My Branch.
FDP and SC use different filter functionality.
The "Daily Settlement Process" button and multiple-select flag were added to the "All records" Applet.
UAT passed, and the change was released to Production on 2025-02-18 for all FDP.
root_cause: During migration, Staff ID was not properly resolved for insurance orders, so filters did not work.
resolution: Added the "Daily Settlement Process" button and multiple-select flag to the "All records" Applet to accommodate differences between FDP and SC filtering; the change passed UAT and was released to Production.

investigation_summary: Journal vouchers were not sent to KB because required department-code mappings were missing. The missing mappings were added based on the attached Excel in the Chugoku production environment.
All applicable affected records were extracted and their dates were updated for KB transmission during the nightly batch.
A list of journal entry slips subject to recovery was attached.
root_cause: No mapping records existed in the "KB Department Code Mapping Master" for the department-code values in the affected journal vouchers.
resolution: Added the required mappings to the "KB Department Code Mapping Master" in Chugoku production and updated the affected record dates so they would be sent to KB in the nightly batch.

The received D2S invoice data was created and processed in Okinawa Prod.

A missing Expenses Payee Code causes the Credit Client Code to appear blank on the JV.

resolution: No product fix was required; the issue was identified as user mis-operation requiring the Expenses Payee Code to be provided in the Service Expense Request.

investigation_summary: An ODI package IKM issue caused updated records to be inserted into the fact table rather than updated, resulting in duplicate Security No.# values and incorrect commission fees. The fix was validated in FDP UAT and deployed to PROD in all environments, after which duplicates were removed and commission fees were corrected. A separate 6_10 report issue was traced to an ODI X_INS_TYPE filter that excluded records from insertion into the DataMart table.
important_findings: The ODI package IKM processed record updates as inserts into the fact table.
This behavior created duplicate Security No.# records and affected commission fee values.
The ODI fix was validated in FDP UAT, where duplicate Security No.# records were no longer present.
Changes were deployed to PROD in all environments, correcting duplicate Security No.# records and commission fees.
Data was visible in the 6_02 report.
The 6_10 report omitted records because the ODI X_INS_TYPE filter only included 'Voluntary Automobile', 'Voluntary Other', 'Voluntary Fire', and 'Life Insurance' values.
root_cause: The ODI package IKM inserted updated records into the fact table instead of updating existing records. Separately, the ODI X_INS_TYPE filter excluded non-matching records from the DataMart table, preventing them from appearing in the 6_10 report.
resolution: The ODI changes were validated in FDP UAT and deployed to PROD in all environments, eliminating duplicate Security No.# records and correcting commission fees.

investigation_summary: The issue was analyzed and required approval flow changes were implemented in the UAT4 environment. After approval, the changes were migrated to the Iwate Production Environment.
important_findings: Required changes affected the approval flow.
The changes were implemented in the UAT4 environment before production deployment.
Production deployment was requested and completed in the Iwate Production Environment.
resolution: Migrated the approval flow changes from UAT4 to the Iwate Production Environment.

investigation_summary: Assessment-request approval behavior was caused by user D8TSAWAM being assigned the Branch NV/UV Sales Staff position rather than Branch Sales Staff. The assignment originated from the Shikoku employee master file shikoku_Employee Master0110, executed on 14/01/2025. The CMVM team completed an SR to correct the issue; changing the Japanese role name was requested to prevent recurrence.
important_findings: D8TSAWAM created the assessment request while assigned to Branch NV/UV Sales Staff.
Branch Sales Manager and Branch Manager expected approvals apply to records created by Branch Sales Staff or Branch Sales Managers, not Branch NV/UV Sales Staff.
The employee master file shikoku_Employee Master0110 assigned D8TSAWAM to Branch NV/UV Sales Staff on 14/01/2025.
The master mapping distinguished Branch Staff → Branch-Staff, Branch Sales Staff → Branch NV/UV Sales Staff, while the intended Branch Sales Staff value was Branch Sales Staff.
The CMVM team completed an SR and corrected the assignment issue.
root_cause: An incorrect position mapping/assignment in the Shikoku employee master file shikoku_Employee Master0110 assigned D8TSAWAM to Branch NV/UV Sales Staff instead of Branch Sales Staff, resulting in a different approval flow.
resolution: The CMVM team completed an SR to correct the issue. A change to the Japanese role name was requested to prevent the same incorrect role selection from recurring.

investigation_summary: Duplicate UV Purchase Orders were created for Trade-in cases when a revised NV quote was approved, using the same assessment number. The defect was fixed and validated in UAT1 and UAT8, and the FDP production release was completed on February 18, 2025. Duplicate purchase orders identified during recovery were canceled after confirmation.
important_findings: In Trade-in cases, approval of a revised NV quote incorrectly created a new UV Purchase Order with the same assessment number.
Multiple UV Purchase Orders with the same assessment number can also be valid when an NV quote contains multiple quantities or when an NV order is canceled.

The quote-revision duplicate-PO fix passed UAT using the flow: create Trade-In Quote and SO, approve SO, create revised quote, approve revised quote, and verify no duplicate UV Purchase Order is created.
The fix was deployed to UAT1 and UAT8 before release to the FDP production environment.
The multiple-quantity scenario required separate process changes and was not included in the completed quote-revision fix.
The SC version required a separate release planned for February 25, 2025 and SNOW incident tracking.
root_cause: A defect in the Trade-in quote-revision flow created an additional UV Purchase Order after approval of a revised NV quote, reusing the same assessment number.
resolution: Canceled confirmed duplicate UV Purchase Orders and deployed a fix preventing duplicate UV Purchase Order creation after revised quote approval to the FDP production environment on February 18, 2025.

investigation_summary: For NV Quote Rev.4, approval requests were not generated because the Sales Rep position was Branch Head. NV Quote approval generation is determined by the Sales Rep position ID rather than the user updating the record. The affected record was recovered, allowing the user to proceed.
important_findings: Approvals for NV Quotes are generated based on the Sales Rep position ID, not the person updating the record.
Approval generation requires the user's Generate Approvals button to be active.
Approvals are generated when the Sales Rep position is Branch NV/UV Sales Staff or Branch-Sales-Staff.
The affected NV Quote Rev.4 had Sales Rep position Branch Head, so approvals were not generated.
Recovery for the affected record was completed.
root_cause: The NV Quote Rev.4 Sales Rep position was Branch Head, which is not a position eligible to generate approvals; approval generation requires a Branch NV/UV Sales Staff or Branch-Sales-Staff Sales Rep position.
resolution: Recovered the affected record so the user could proceed.

investigation_summary: Sales orders appeared in the 'My' view for user 'D8AKIHIK' because that user was included in the 'Sales Rep' field on the affected records. In Siebel, records are displayed in the 'My' view for every user listed in the 'Sales Rep' field. Recovery removed 'D8AKIHIK' from the affected sales orders, and the user confirmed the orders no longer appeared.
important_findings: All affected records had both 'D8AKIHIK' and 'D8KANEMT' in the 'Sales Rep' field.
Siebel 'My' view displays a record for each user present in the 'Sales Rep' field.
'D8AKIHIK' is a vehicle manager and should not have been assigned as a sales person.
Removing 'D8AKIHIK' from the affected sales orders stopped the orders from appearing in that user's 'My' view.
root_cause: 'D8AKIHIK' was incorrectly included in the 'Sales Rep' field of the affected sales orders.
resolution: Removed 'D8AKIHIK' from the 'Sales Rep' field for all affected sales orders.

investigation_summary: Stock details for specific vehicles were missing or incorrect in PowerBI Report 2-01 Used car details (inventory). The team compared stocked-in vehicle data with SC Prod and identified data differences for three vehicles. The affected data was corrected and linked to PowerBI.
important_findings: Stock details for H000139486 and H000146678 were confirmed visible in PowerBI Report 2-01 Used car details (inventory) after correction.
Comparison with SC Prod identified a vehicle arrival date discrepancy for H000139486.
H000145996 and H000146678 had discrepancies in direct sales price and vehicle arrival date.
The corrected data was linked to PowerBI overnight.
root_cause: Differences in stocked-in vehicle data compared with SC Prod, affecting vehicle arrival date and direct sales price for the identified vehicles.
resolution: Corrected the affected vehicle data and linked the updated data to PowerBI.

investigation_summary: Power BI showed blank receipt dates for two items due to duplicate versions of the same data records being created in Power BI. The specified record was recovered, and a full load was performed on chugoku powerbi to correct the data and prevent recurrence. Corrected data was expected to appear in Power BI after the nightly batch.
important_findings: Two items had blank receipt dates in Power BI.
Duplicate versions of the same data records were created in Power BI.
The specified affected record was recovered.
A full load on chugoku powerbi resolved the issue and was stated to prevent recurrence.
Power BI data is reflected after the nightly batch.
root_cause: Duplicate versions of the same data records were created in Power BI.
resolution: Performed a full load on chugoku powerbi and recovered the specified record; corrected data was reflected after the nightly batch.

investigation_summary: The Item Category Group field was editable across all FDPs for certain positions, including UID:D0X20883. The initial UAT change did not fully enforce read-only behavior, so the field was updated to be read-only for all positions on both the list applet and form applet of the affected View. The validated fix was released to production on February 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue existed across all FDPs.
Item Category Group remained editable for UID:D0X20883 after the initial UAT implementation.
The field was changed to always read-only for any position on the affected screen.
Read-only behavior was implemented on both the list applet and the form applet for the View.
The change was validated in UAT and released to production on February 26, 2025.
root_cause: Item Category Group read-only restrictions were not consistently applied for all positions and applets in the affected View.
resolution: Configured Item Category Group as read-only for all positions on both the list applet and form applet; released the validated change to production on February 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: Values for affected records were unavailable in PowerBI after data migration. Investigation identified that the Siebel "Login ID" field, which is linked to PowerBI, had not been populated during migration. Correct values were updated for all affected records and linked to PowerBI, restoring availability.
important_findings: Affected record values were unavailable in PowerBI.
The Siebel "Login ID" field is linked to PowerBI.
"Login ID" was not populated during data migration.
All affected records were recovered with corrected values.
Corrected values were linked to PowerBI and became available.
root_cause: The Siebel "Login ID" field linked to PowerBI was not populated during data migration.
resolution: Updated the correct "Login ID" values for all affected records and linked them to PowerBI.

investigation_summary: The Sales Order quantity was confirmed as 2. The referenced buttons could not be clicked on the Parent Sales Order, and investigation was directed to the Child Sales Order. No confirmed root cause or final resolution was documented.
important_findings: The Sales Order quantity was confirmed as 2.
The referenced buttons were unavailable on the Parent Sales Order.
Verification was requested on the Child Sales Order.

investigation_summary: A fix affecting BIPs was implemented across all UAT environments and validated by the requester. Following UAT approval, the fix was deployed to production on February 12, 2025. The incident was then ready for closure.
important_findings: Changes were implemented in all UAT environments.
All BIPs were verified as changed correctly during UAT validation.
Production deployment was scheduled after UAT approval.
The fix was released to production on February 12, 2025.
resolution: Implemented the fix in all UAT environments, obtained validation that all BIPs were changed correctly, and deployed the fix to production on February 12, 2025.

investigation_summary: The recycle-fee submission issue to TOB was caused by duplicate vehicle records with the same recycle fee ticket number. The duplication was reproduced in UAT and traced to a VIN# change occurring after the vehicle had already been migrated, causing the vehicle delta-data import program to create a new record because VIN# is its user key. All identified affected records were recovered under MFTBCFFR-3168.
important_findings: The issue occurs when a vehicle is duplicated with the same recycle fee ticket number, preventing correct recycle-fee processing to TOB.
Vehicle "BE740G-400580" was initially created in SC Prod from a TCB01 file with both Fuso reception # and VIN# set to "046754".
The vehicle was migrated to FDP Chugoku before D21A from TOB updated its VIN# to "BE740G-400580".
During vehicle delta-data migration, the import program treated the updated VIN# as a user key and created a new vehicle record.
The user submitted the recycle fee to TOB before the duplicate-vehicle recovery was completed.
All impacted records, not only the reported order, were recovered as part of MFTBCFFR-3168.
root_cause: A vehicle was migrated while its VIN# was "046754", then D21A updated the VIN# to "BE740G-400580". During subsequent vehicle delta-data migration, the import program used VIN# as its user key and created a duplicate vehicle record.
resolution: Recovered all identified impacted duplicate-vehicle records under MFTBCFFR-3168, including the reported order.

investigation_summary: The "Branch Head Name" update from CR MFTBCFFR2-208 was not applied to the UV Purchase Quote BIP. The Purchase Quote BIP logic was updated to align with the existing logic used by other Quote BIPs in FDP environments. The fix was deployed to UAT-01 and UAT-08, passed UAT, and was released to production for all FDPs on February 18, 2025.
important_findings: CR MFTBCFFR2-208 changed the BIP reports NV Purchase Plan, NV Quotation, and UV Quotation.
The "Branch Head Name" field update was missing from the UV Purchase Quote.
In FDP environments, the MF UV Employee Name field is null, unlike SC where it stores the employee last name.
Purchase Quote BIP logic was updated to match the current logic used by other Quote BIPs in FDP environments.
The fix passed UAT after deployment to UAT-01 and UAT-08.
root_cause: The "Branch Head Name" update from CR MFTBCFFR2-208 was not applied to the UV Purchase Quote BIP.
resolution: Updated the Purchase Quote BIP logic to align with other Quote BIPs in FDP environments, deployed the fix to UAT-01 and UAT-08, completed UAT validation, and released it to production for all FDPs on February 18, 2025.

investigation_summary: After the UVIS outbound batch was scheduled, no data was sent from China FDP to UVIS. The outbound logic was confirmed to send created data using code 7306. The issue was determined to have occurred during migration work and was accepted as non-recurring.
important_findings: No data was sent from China FDP to UVIS after scheduling the UVIS outbound batch.
The outbound logic sends created data with code 7306.
The incident occurred during migration work.
The issue was considered non-recurring after migration work.
root_cause: The issue occurred during migration work.

investigation_summary: During recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicles. Because all duplicates were in Pending status with null TOB status and message, recovery selected orders based on Created date and unmapped older orders. An older recycle fee order was mapped to a Sales Order, so unmapping it from the vehicle also unmapped it from the Sales Order. The attached records were recovered, and the SOP will be updated to check Sales Order mappings when processing duplicate recycle fee orders.
important_findings: Duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicles during recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159.
All duplicate recycle fee orders were in Pending status and had null TOB status and message.
The only observed difference between duplicate orders was the Created date; older orders were unmapped and latest orders retained for the chassis order.
The older recycle fee order was mapped to a Sales Order, which was overlooked during recovery.
Unmapping the older recycle fee order from the vehicle also unmapped it from the Sales Order.
root_cause: During duplicate recycle fee order recovery, an older order mapped to a Sales Order was unmapped based solely on its older Created date, causing it to be unmapped from the Sales Order.
resolution: Recovered the records attached to this Jira and added a planned SOP check to verify whether duplicate recycle fee orders are mapped to any Sales Order before unmapping them.

investigation_summary: MFTBCFFR-3229 grouped three separate incidents: PT_CR-0790 Reservation auto print issue, PT_Reservation slip JC/WO issue, and PT_Add Order Staff. The items were scheduled for synchronization on FDP in the second March 2025 release on 26 March 2025. Separate FDP Jira tickets were created for each item, and this Jira was approved for rejection.
important_findings: The three items were scheduled for FDP synchronization in the 26 March 2025 release.
PT_CR-0790 Reservation auto print issue was moved to MFTBCFFR-3272.
PT_Reservation slip JC/WO issue was moved to MFTBCFFR-3273.
PT_Add Order Staff was moved to MFTBCFFR-3274.
MFTBCFFR-3229 was approved for rejection because the work would be handled in the separate FDP Jira tickets.
resolution: Rejected MFTBCFFR-3229 and tracked the three incidents separately in FDP Jira tickets MFTBCFFR-3272, MFTBCFFR-3273, and MFTBCFFR-3274.

investigation_summary: Spreadsheet creation failed because agency code 09700036212P10000000000000000 was not registered in the Siebel system. The required agency-code master update was identified as a master-data change rather than a Siebel defect. The agency code master was subsequently updated in Siebel using the latest ejibai list.
important_findings: Agency code 09700036212P10000000000000000 was not registered in the Siebel system.
The agency codes mapped in Siebel were listed in the ejibaiID sheet of OD_PROD_EmployeeWithHitachiGW_IDs_20250116_final.xlsx.
The issue required an SR to track the agency-code master change.
The agency code master in the Siebel system was updated according to the latest file.
root_cause: Agency code 09700036212P10000000000000000 was missing from the agency code master in the Siebel system.
resolution: Updated the agency code master in the Siebel system using the latest ejibai list.

investigation_summary: Invoice C050006192 did not trigger the approval flow because it inherited a Dummy primary position from sales order A030793563. The sales order primary position was Dummy because position mapping for the primary position in the order's SC was not provided. The required corrective action is to change the missing position mapping through a service request.
important_findings: Sales order A030793563 had a Dummy primary position.
Position mapping was not provided for the primary position in the sales order's SC.
Invoice C050006192 copies its primary position from the sales order.
Invoice C050006192 had position type Dummy, which prevented the approval flow from being triggered.
The position mapping must be changed through a service request.
root_cause: Missing business-provided position mapping for the primary position in the sales order's SC caused sales order A030793563 to use a Dummy primary position, which was copied to invoice C050006192 and prevented approval-flow triggering.
resolution: Raise a service request to change the missing position mapping.

investigation_summary: Recovery for the affected record was completed, and the user was notified to proceed. The incident was identified as related to MFTBCFFR-3193, where the RCA will be shared.
important_findings: Recovery for the affected record was completed.
The user was notified that recovery was complete.
The issue is related to Jira MFTBCFFR-3193.
RCA will be provided through MFTBCFFR-3193.
resolution: Completed recovery of the affected record and notified the user.

investigation_summary: The incident affected Planned Expenses with "Open" and "Pending Approval" statuses. Investigation identified 647 affected records, all of which were recovered. The issue occurred when users processed or copied a Planned Invoice of a Job Card migrated from SC Prod because its "BranchId" had not been updated.
important_findings: Chugoku's Approval Matrix handles approval requests from "Branch-Assistant-Staff" in the same way as SC.
The requested Planned Expense status changes included "Pending Approval" to "Cancelled" for I036763022/2-432343562 and I036678507/2-433752822(Add).
