A total of 647 records with "Open" and "Pending Approval" status had the same issue.
The issue was reproduced/investigated in the UAT environment.
The "BranchId" was not updated on Planned Invoices of Job Cards migrated from SC Prod.
Processing or copying a migrated Planned Invoice triggered the issue.
root_cause: "BranchId" was not updated in the Planned Invoice of a Job Card migrated from SC Prod; processing or copying that migrated Planned Invoice caused the issue.
resolution: Recovered all 647 affected records, including changing the requested Planned Expense statuses from "Pending Approval" to "Cancelled".

investigation_summary: The incident involved a UV SO and Delivery Request requiring recovery of their statuses. Cubastion changed the UV SO status to 'Approved' and the Delivery Request status to 'Pending Delivery', after which the user was instructed to create a Registration Request and complete the Delivery Request. Investigation found that the Delivery Request screen remains editable after completion, including allowing dates to be removed; this behavior was considered normal functionality.
important_findings: Cubastion changed the UV SO status to 'Approved' and the Delivery Request status to 'Pending Delivery' as recovery actions.
The user was instructed to create a Registration Request and complete the Delivery Request.
The Delivery Request screen remains editable after the Delivery Request is completed.
Users can remove dates after completing a Delivery Request.
The functionality was reported as operating normally; the observed issue may have resulted from user error.
resolution: Cubastion restored the UV SO to 'Approved' and the Delivery Request to 'Pending Delivery'; the user was instructed to create a Registration Request and complete the Delivery Request.

investigation_summary: The incident was acknowledged and investigated. Recovery was completed, and validation was requested to confirm that no further concerns remained. The comments do not document the underlying issue, root cause, or specific recovery actions.
important_findings: Recovery was completed.
Post-recovery validation was requested.
No technical symptoms, root-cause findings, or corrective-action details were recorded in the comments.
resolution: Recovery was completed.

investigation_summary: Records were recovered so processing could continue. Investigation found that a batch of records had not had their previous quote ID updated. The affected records were identified in an attached Excel list, and their previous quote IDs were updated to prevent recurrence.
important_findings: A batch of records was missing updated previous quote IDs.
The affected record list was provided in an attached Excel file.
The records were recovered before the root-cause analysis was completed.
Previous quote IDs were updated for the affected records, preventing the issue from recurring.
root_cause: The previous quote ID was not updated for a batch of records.
resolution: Updated the previous quote IDs for the affected records and recovered the records.

investigation_summary: A duplicate spreadsheet-number conflict occurred because spreadsheet 26SC000000000S-17-24-00002 had been created by a Shikoku Fuso Ehime Headquarters user under the Shikoku Fuso Kagawa Headquarters agency-code prefix. The existing spreadsheet was renamed to the Ehime prefix, resolving the duplicate-number conflict. A subsequent error was caused by the user retriggering the wrong, already closed spreadsheet; the user was able to link with the correct spreadsheet.
important_findings: D8TEKONO, mapped to Ejbai-ID 09740020262A002, belongs to Shikoku Fuso Ehime Headquarters but selected the Shikoku Fuso Kagawa Headquarters agency code.
After MFTBCFFR-3116, spreadsheet 26SC000000000S-17-24-00002 retained the 26SC0000000S prefix, although a Shikoku Fuso Ehime Headquarters spreadsheet should use the 11SC0000000S prefix.
The existing spreadsheet with Internal Posted status caused an error when another spreadsheet with serial number 00002 was created.
The recovery changed the conflicting spreadsheet prefix from 26SC000000000S-17-24-00002-01 to 11SC000000000S-17-24-00002-01.
Later errors for 26SC000000000S-17-24-00003 occurred because policy 61HLW8910 was added to a spreadsheet that had already been completed and closed.
The user retriggered the wrong spreadsheet and was subsequently able to link with the correct spreadsheet.
root_cause: User selected the Shikoku Fuso Kagawa Headquarters agency code for a spreadsheet created by a Shikoku Fuso Ehime Headquarters user, leaving the spreadsheet with an incorrect 26SC0000000S prefix and causing a duplicate spreadsheet-number conflict.
resolution: Renamed the conflicting spreadsheet from the 26SC prefix to the 11SC prefix. The later linking error was resolved by using the correct spreadsheet instead of retriggering the closed spreadsheet.

investigation_summary: A data patching issue affected vehicle field updates after an import program completed. The investigation compared column values between SC and FDP and recovered all vehicles in the provided list. The affected vehicle fields were not updated after import completion.
important_findings: The issue was identified as a data patching issue.
Column values in SC and FDP were compared during the investigation.
All vehicles listed in the incident were recovered.
Affected vehicle fields were not updated after the import program completed.
root_cause: Vehicle fields were not updated after the import program completed.
resolution: Compared SC and FDP column values and recovered all vehicles in the provided list.

investigation_summary: A recycle fee order associated with a sales order was unintentionally unmapped during recovery of duplicate recycle fee orders for Jira MFTBCFFR-3159. All duplicate orders were Pending with null TOB status and message, so the recovery decision was based only on Created date. The affected record was recovered in Iwate Prod and remapped to the sales order; no product fix was required.
important_findings: Duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicle during recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159.
All duplicate recycle fee orders had Pending status and null TOB status and message.
The duplicate orders differed only by Created date; older orders were unmapped while the latest-created order remained mapped to the chassis order.
The older recycle fee order was mapped to a sales order, but this relationship was not checked before unmapping it from the vehicle.
Recovery of the attached record was completed in Iwate Prod, and the recycle fee order was remapped to the sales order.
The SOP will be updated to verify whether duplicate recycle fee orders are mapped to Sales Orders before unmapping.
root_cause: During duplicate recycle fee order recovery, an older-created recycle fee order was unmapped based on Created date without checking that it was mapped to a Sales Order. Unmapping it from the vehicle also unmapped it from the sales order.
resolution: Recovered the affected record in Iwate Prod and remapped the recycle fee order to the sales order. No product fix was required; the SOP will add a Sales Order mapping check for duplicate recycle fee orders.

investigation_summary: The issue was reproduced in UAT-8 and UAT-1, then fixed in UAT-01. Validation covered creating an NV Sales Order with a Model Code line item and more than 10 option lines before selecting "Create Chassis Order". Following confirmation, the fix was released to production in the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was reproducible in both UAT-8 and UAT-1.
The fix was deployed to UAT-01 for validation.
Validation required an NV Sales Order with a Model Code line item and more than 10 option lines, followed by selecting "Create Chassis Order".
The UAT-01 fix was confirmed before production deployment.
The fix was released to production through the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
resolution: A fix validated in UAT-01 was deployed to production in the FDP release on February 8, 2025.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned inability to map PO# F000194343 and proceed with Sales Posting. Investigation found that PO# F000209715 had already been mapped to SO# E000210402 and was unmapped as recovery. For the trade-in case, PO# F000194343 was already mapped to NV SO# A000194337, where Sales posting had been completed; this was confirmed as normal SC and FDP behavior.
important_findings: PO# F000209715 was mapped to SO# E000210402, preventing mapping to SO# E000215214.
PO# F000209715 was unmapped from SO# E000210402 as part of recovery.
PO# F000194343 was initially mapped to NV SO# A000194337 for a Trade-in vehicle case.
Sales posting for NV SO# A000194337 had already been completed.
The UV PO remained mapped only to the NV SO, which is normal system behavior for SC and FDP.
Recovery was completed for the affected record and the Jira was rejected as expected behavior.
root_cause: PO# F000194343 was already mapped to NV SO# A000194337 and its Sales posting was completed, so the UV PO could only remain mapped to the NV SO under normal SC and FDP behavior.
resolution: Unmapped PO# F000209715 from SO# E000210402 and completed recovery for the affected record; the remaining PO mapping behavior was confirmed as expected.

investigation_summary: The issue was replicated in the UAT environment. It occurred when Siebel batches were activated before Go-Live for FDP while transaction data existed for Chugoku and the batch start date was set in the past. The batch process ran concurrently with D2S material master execution.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in the UAT environment.
Siebel batches are activated before Go-Live for FDP.
Other FDP instances did not exhibit the issue because they had no transaction data.
For Chugoku, transaction data was present and the batch start date was set to a past date.
The Siebel batch process ran at the same time as D2S material master execution.
root_cause: Manual mistake: a Chugoku Siebel batch with transaction data was activated before Go-Live with a past start date, causing it to run concurrently with D2S material master execution.

investigation_summary: IBOS requests failed because the Azure flux pipeline used to update server configuration could not run after the configured user's password expired. Azure provided no notification of the expired password. The password expiration was removed and custom alerts were added for pipeline execution failures; functional interface testing was identified as necessary to detect similar issues before go-live.
important_findings: Azure flux pipeline updates server configuration.
The password for the user configured in the Azure flux pipeline had expired.
No notification was received from Azure when the pipeline was affected.
A ping test does not validate interface data or detect this failure.
Functional testing of the interface was required to detect the issue but was not part of pre-production activities.
Password expiration was removed and custom alerts were implemented for pipeline execution failures.
root_cause: The password for the user configured in the Azure flux pipeline expired, preventing the pipeline from updating server configuration; Azure did not provide a notification.
resolution: Removed the password expiration date and implemented custom alerts for Azure flux pipeline execution failures.

investigation_summary: The Intranet URL was working in all live environments but was not the required URL for Chugoku. IT requested a change to the Internet URL, and the change was implemented in the Chugoku FDP.
important_findings: The Intranet URL was working in all live environments.
Chugoku required the Internet URL following an IT change request.
The requested URL change was implemented in the Chugoku FDP.
root_cause: The Chugoku FDP was using an Intranet URL while IT required an Internet URL.
resolution: Changed the URL to the Internet URL in the Chugoku FDP.

investigation_summary: On the morning of the 24th, D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing did not run because a database-related error stopped processing. Database memory usage became high while FDP Chugoku transaction data was being loaded concurrently. After IT approval, database parameters were adjusted; the affected Okinawa Prod Chassis order was recovered to "Shipment Instructed" with its pool cost order and recycle fee order created and mapped, and the issue did not recur.
important_findings: D21N, D21R, and D21F files did not run on the morning of the 24th.
Logs showed that file processing stopped because of a database-related error.
Concurrent loading of FDP Chugoku transaction data caused database memory usage to reach a high state.
Database parameters were adjusted after IT approval to address the memory issue.
The Chassis order on Okinawa Prod was recovered to "Shipment Instructed", with pool cost order and recycle fee order created and mapped.
No recurrence was reported after the database parameter adjustment.
root_cause: High database memory usage caused by concurrent loading of FDP Chugoku transaction data, resulting in a database-related error that stopped D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing.
resolution: Adjusted database parameters after IT approval and recovered the affected Okinawa Prod Chassis order, including creation and mapping of its pool cost order and recycle fee order.

investigation_summary: The incident involved inconsistent vehicle visibility in the "UV Inventory" screen, where the number of records differed between the initial open and refresh. The fix was validated in UAT/UAT-8, then released to FDP Chugoku PROD on February 6, with deployment to remaining FDP PROD environments planned for February 12.
important_findings: The reported behavior showed only one vehicle on the first open, while additional vehicles appeared after refresh.
UAT verification required confirming that all vehicles appear in the "UV Inventory" screen and that, without a search, only "Stocked In" vehicles are visible through the last record.
After the fix, UAT confirmed that the record count was the same on the first open and after refresh.
Five vehicles were reported with blank purchase type: H000112159, H000147745, H000147498, H000147497, and H000147406.
The fix was released to FDP Chugoku PROD on February 6; remaining FDP PROD environments were scheduled for February 12.
resolution: Implemented and released a fix that restored consistent vehicle record visibility between the initial "UV Inventory" screen load and refresh. The fix passed UAT and was deployed to FDP Chugoku PROD.

investigation_summary: Incorrect mapping logic in the import program contained multiple fields and was incorrect for Parts Quotes. Parts Sales Orders created from affected Parts Quotes inherited the wrong Sales Staff Field value. Recovery was completed for the Sales Staff Field on all affected Parts Quotes and Parts Sales Orders.
important_findings: The import program mapping logic contained multiple fields and was incorrect in Parts Quotes.
Affected Parts Quotes had incorrect Sales Staff Field values.
Parts Sales Orders created from problematic Parts Quotes also had incorrect values.
Recovery was completed for the Sales Staff Field in all affected Parts Quotes and Parts Sales Orders.
root_cause: Incorrect mapping logic in the import program for Parts Quotes, caused by multiple fields being present in the mapping logic.
resolution: Recovered the Sales Staff Field for all affected Parts Quotes and Parts Sales Orders.

investigation_summary: Data was not reflected in the PBI report for FDP China Fuso due to duplicate ORDER_NUM entries in W_ORDER_F. Other FDP reports were unaffected because they did not have the duplicate entries. The data became visible in the NV_3_21B report, and display was confirmed.
important_findings: Duplicate ORDER_NUM entries existed in the W_ORDER_F table for FDP China Fuso.
The duplicate entries prevented data from being reflected in the PBI report and caused an error.
Other FDP reports functioned correctly because they did not contain the duplicate ORDER_NUM entries.
Proposed remediation was to remove duplicates from W_ORDER_F or perform a full load.
Data was subsequently visible in the NV_3_21B report and the screen display was confirmed.
root_cause: Duplicate ORDER_NUM entries in the W_ORDER_F table for FDP China Fuso prevented data from being reflected in the PBI report.
resolution: Data became visible in the NV_3_21B report; screen display was confirmed. The specific corrective action performed was not stated.

investigation_summary: On the morning of the 24th, D21N, D21R, and D21F files did not execute because file processing halted on a database-related error. Concurrent transactional-data loading in FDP Chugoku caused high database memory usage. Database parameters were adjusted after IT approval, and ODI-level monitoring with email alerts for failed or unexecuted Production files was implemented.
important_findings: D21N, D21R, and D21F files were not executed on the morning of the 24th.
Log analysis identified a database-related error that stopped file processing.
Concurrent transactional-data loading in FDP Chugoku increased database memory usage and halted processing.
Database parameters were adjusted after IT approval to address the memory-related issue.
An alert function was added to notify the AMS team when an ODI package fails.
ODI-level monitoring and email notifications were configured for files that do not run in Production.
root_cause: Concurrent loading of transactional data in FDP Chugoku caused high database memory usage, leading to a database-related error and halted file processing.
resolution: Adjusted database parameters after IT approval to address the memory-related issue, and implemented ODI-level monitoring with email alerts to the AMS team for ODI package failures or unexecuted Production files.

investigation_summary: Orders required recovery because receipt processing occurred before recovery actions were completed. Engineering recovered all identified affected orders, corrected flat inventory quantities for three specified orders, and resynced additional affected attachment orders. Recovery was completed for all such cases.
important_findings: Receipt processing occurred before recovery for orders N036484662, N036474368, and N036474349.
The receive action and transaction needed to be reverted before resynchronization to allow the order to update to complete.
Recovery was completed for 70 initially identified orders.
Flat inventory quantities were corrected according to transactions for N036484662, N036474368, and N036474349.
An additional 18 potentially affected orders were identified and recovery was subsequently completed for all such cases.
root_cause: Receipt processing was performed before the required recovery, causing affected orders to require receive-action/transaction reversal and resynchronization to reach complete status.
resolution: Recovered all affected orders, corrected flat inventory quantities for N036484662, N036474368, and N036474349 based on transactions, reverted applicable receive actions and transactions, and resynced the orders.

investigation_summary: Approval flows were not applied to records with MF Fleet Flag = 'Y', and the "Special Sales Manager" approver was initially missing in UAT-8. Corrected approval flows were deployed and validated in UAT-8, then applied to PROD. Recovery was completed for affected quote 1-9RJIX2E by returning its status to In Progress.
important_findings: Records with MF Fleet Flag = 'Y' did not have approval flows applied.
The "Special Sales Manager" was not displayed as an approver during initial UAT-8 validation.
Corrected approval flows were deployed and tested in UAT-8 using reference quote 2-2VCQ03.
After confirmation, the approval-flow changes were applied to PROD.
The affected quote 1-9RJIX2E was recovered by changing its status back to In Progress.
root_cause: Approval flows were not maintained for records where MF Fleet Flag = 'Y', resulting in missing approval routing, including the "Special Sales Manager" approver.
resolution: Corrected the approval flows, validated the fix in UAT-8, deployed the changes to PROD, and recovered quote 1-9RJIX2E by returning its status to In Progress.

investigation_summary: A new Ejibai mapping file received from IT was executed. Tokyo Marine subsequently reported that the mapping data was incorrect and is preparing corrected data for delivery. No final resolution is documented.
important_findings: The Ejibai mapping file received from IT was executed.
Tokyo Marine identified the mapping data as incorrect.
Corrected mapping data had not yet been provided at the time of the latest comment.
root_cause: Incorrect mapping data supplied by Tokyo Marine.

investigation_summary: A configuration error during data migration caused an unplanned D21L file to be received in SC PROD on 2025-02-01. The file removed links between Chassis Orders and NV Orders; after import into FDP Chugoku, the affected orders were identified as mismatches and deleted. Affected records, including duplicate vehicles created after D21A receipt in Chugoku PROD, were recovered and no recovery work remained.
important_findings: 758 orders were affected.
The D21L file received in SC PROD removed the link between Chassis Orders and NV Orders.
After import into FDP Chugoku, the unlinked orders were treated as mismatches and deleted.
A D21A file received in Chugoku PROD for the same approximately 750 vehicles created duplicate vehicles.
The incident was attributed to a configuration error during data migration and was stated not to recur.
Recovery was completed for all affected records and duplicate vehicles.
root_cause: A configuration error during data migration caused an unplanned D21L file to be received in SC PROD, removing links between Chassis Orders and NV Orders.
resolution: Recovered all affected records and duplicate vehicles; no outstanding recovery work remained.

investigation_summary: A total of 2,734 Work Order Item records were affected by inconsistent Work Order and Labor Status combinations. Recovery was performed using the provided WO Status/Labor Status combination table, including updates to Labor Items with status "Customer Approved". The issue was attributed to LOV cache behavior affecting one batch of Job Cards.
important_findings: 2,734 Work Order Item records were affected.
A recovery mapping for WO Status and Labor Status combinations was provided.
Labor Items with status "Customer Approved" were updated according to the recovery table.
The issue affected one batch of Job Cards.
LOV cache was identified as the cause.
root_cause: LOV cache caused incorrect status combinations for one batch of Job Cards.
resolution: Updated the affected Labor Items, including those with status "Customer Approved", according to the WO Status/Labor Status recovery table.

investigation_summary: Siebel received multiple PO Allocation messages from D2S for PO N000006382. Parts were initially processed using the latest Open allocation received on 2025/01/29, but a further Open allocation with an older D2S timestamp was received on 2025/01/31 and became the basis for processing. The reason D2S sent this allocation late was being investigated, but no final D2S finding or corrective action was recorded.
important_findings: Siebel received three PO Allocations for PO N000006382 on 2025/01/29; the latest Open allocation had D2S timestamp 20250129232648.7677280.
Parts were processed according to the 2025/01/29 latest Open PO Allocation.
Siebel received another Open PO Allocation on 2025/01/31 09:46:48 AM with D2S timestamp 20250129232627.7536910.
The PO Allocation received on 2025/01/31 had a D2S timestamp earlier than the latest allocation received on 2025/01/29.
The D2S team was requested to investigate why the allocation was sent to Siebel on 2025/01/31.

investigation_summary: Vehicle Recycle Ticket fee# values were not updated correctly for affected records. The impacted records were identified and patched. The issue was caused by recycling ticket numbers from a previously shared vehicle list not being updated after import.
important_findings: A complete list of vehicles with incorrectly updated Recycle Ticket fee# values was extracted.
All identified impacted records were patched.
Previously shared vehicle recycling ticket numbers were not updated after import.
A TOB error was not displayed and the send button could not be pressed.
root_cause: Vehicle recycling ticket numbers from the previously shared list were not updated after import.
resolution: Patched all affected vehicle records after extracting the complete impact list.

investigation_summary: The incident involved an intermittent connection-pooling error, "Exception when releasing connection to pool," during a load. The load completed successfully after ODI was restarted. The comments do not confirm a specific underlying database or resource issue.
important_findings: The reported error was "Exception when releasing connection to pool."
The issue was considered potentially related to a temporary resource constraint or database connectivity, but this was not confirmed.
Restarting the load allowed it to run successfully.
ODI was restarted as the final operational action.
resolution: Restarted ODI and reran the load successfully.

investigation_summary: The incident was identified as related to JIRA# 3117, Issue-1. The issue was planned to be fixed together with that related Jira issue; no technical cause or completed resolution was documented.
important_findings: MFTBCFFR-3158 is related to JIRA# 3117, Issue-1.
The planned approach was to fix this issue together with JIRA# 3117, Issue-1.

investigation_summary: During migration to FDP Chugoku, eight assessment requests were omitted from the export script and related UV Inventory fields were not updated for the final migrated batch. The omitted assessment requests and impacted listed records were recovered, and verification passed. SC Name blank behavior was confirmed as expected based on the assessment-request creator, while visibility of Cancelled and other statuses in UV Inventory was identified as a separate FDP-wide issue replicated in UAT1.
important_findings: Eight assessment requests did not appear in the export script for FDP Chugoku: H000054333, H000147406, H000147498, H000147745, H000106694, H000147497, H000145314, and H000112159.
Recovery was completed for all records in the previously shared impacted-record list.
In UV Inventory, SC Name is visible when an Assessment Request is created by a branch user and is not visible when created by an HQ user; this logic is the same for all FDPs.
Records with Cancelled or other statuses visible in UV Inventory occur across all FDPs and were replicated in the UAT environment/UAT1; a separate JIRA was requested for that issue.
root_cause: Eight assessment requests were omitted from the export script during migration to FDP Chugoku.
resolution: Recovered the eight missing assessment requests and completed recovery/patching for all records in the impacted-record list; verification passed.

investigation_summary: Receipt of 11,000 parts from D2S delayed part release from the normal 2–3 minutes to 25 minutes. During the delay, the replenishment order batch ran before the parts were released and created 184 purchase orders with no line items. The affected orders were recovered by updating their status to "Cancelled".
important_findings: D2S delivered 11,000 parts, causing part release processing to take 25 minutes instead of the normal 2–3 minutes.
The replenishment order batch was triggered while the parts had not yet been released.
The system created purchase orders with no line items because the parts were unavailable at batch execution time.
A total of 184 orders were affected.
Affected orders were recovered and their status was updated to "Cancelled".
root_cause: Delayed release of 11,000 parts received from D2S allowed the replenishment order batch to run before the parts were released, resulting in purchase orders with no line items.
resolution: Recovered the 184 affected orders by updating their status to "Cancelled".

investigation_summary: D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing stopped because of a database-related error, making the Chassis order unavailable on FDP-Aomori. The failure was attributed to high database memory usage during concurrent transactional-data loading in FDP Chugoku. Database parameters were adjusted with IT approval, and the production fix was applied through MFTBCFFR-3174; no recurrence was reported.
important_findings: D21N, D21R, and D21F files were not executed on the morning of the 24th.
Log analysis identified a database-related error that stopped file processing.
Concurrent transactional-data loading in FDP Chugoku caused high database memory usage and processing halts.
Database parameters were adjusted to address the memory-related issue, using the same analysis approach as 3184.
An alert function was added to notify the AMS team if an ODI package fails.
The fix was deployed to prod through JIRA MFTBCFFR-3174.
root_cause: Concurrent loading of transactional data in FDP Chugoku increased database memory usage, causing a database-related error and halting D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing.
resolution: Database parameters were adjusted with IT approval to resolve the memory-related issue, and the fix was applied to prod through MFTBCFFR-3174. An alert function was added to notify the AMS team when an ODI package fails.

investigation_summary: Sales Order approval failed when the associated Recycle Fee Order had the status "Recycle Order Changed", which occurs after using "Change Order" in the Recycle Fee Order Applet. The approval logic was updated and verified in UAT1 using a designated chassis order. The fix was deployed to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: Using "Change Order" in the Recycle Fee Order Applet changes the Recycle Fee Order status to "Recycle Order Changed".
Sales Orders could not be approved while the associated Recycle Fee Order was in "Recycle Order Changed" status.
CR-0697 was reported as deployed to SC on December 19, 2022; its availability in FDP/Okayama Fuso was disputed during the investigation.
The updated UAT logic allowed approval of Sales Orders with Recycle Fee Order status "Recycle Order Changed".
UAT1 chassis order B001249837 was provided for validation, with associated Recycle Fee Order B001249897.
The fix was applied to PROD in the March 12 production release.
root_cause: The Sales Order approval logic did not support approval when the associated Recycle Fee Order status was "Recycle Order Changed".
resolution: Updated the approval logic to allow Sales Order approval for Recycle Fee Orders in "Recycle Order Changed" status, validated it in UAT1, and deployed it to PROD on March 12, 2025.

investigation_summary: The affected JV line was recovered. Investigation found that repeated Map and Unmap attempts on the Purchase Order, combined with edits to fields in the Sales Order, resulted in the Department Code becoming null. Regression testing in UAT1 found no issue in the Siebel system.
important_findings: The affected JV line recovery was completed.
The user attempted to Map and Unmap the Purchase Order multiple times.
Edits to certain Sales Order fields during the Map and Unmap process resulted in the Department Code becoming null.
Regression testing in UAT1 identified no issues within the Siebel system.
MDIS was contacted.
root_cause: Repeated Map and Unmap attempts on the Purchase Order, combined with edits to Sales Order fields, caused the Department Code to become null.
resolution: Recovered the affected JV line.

investigation_summary: A Sales Price mismatch between Siebel and FDP PBI reports was traced to ODI logic handling Billing Rate Type values. The logic did not correctly recognize the labor product 'FDP Rate' for FDP Shikoku order I00006001, causing the Sales Price to differ between Siebel and PBI. The ODI logic was corrected, validated in FDP UAT5 using order I000035271, and released to production in the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
important_findings: The incident involved mismatched Sales Price values between Siebel and the FDP PBI report.
For FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001, line item 1-1A8DK0 had labor product 'FDP Rate', which did not satisfy the ODI Sales Price logic.
The ODI logic was expected to include 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', but incorrect values such as 'FDP???' and '?????????' were observed.
Recovery was completed for the affected mismatched values, after which Siebel sales prices matched the PBI report.
The corrected logic was verified in FDP UAT5 with ORDER_NUM I000035271 and labor product 'FDP Rate'; values populated correctly in FDP PBI reports.
The ODI change was released to production with the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
root_cause: ODI Sales Price logic did not correctly match the Billing Rate Type value 'FDP Rate' due to incorrect expected values, so the labor product on FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001 was excluded from Sales Price processing.
resolution: Modified the ODI logic in FDP UAT to correctly handle 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', validated the fix in FDP UAT5, recovered the affected mismatched data, and deployed the change to production on February 8, 2025.

investigation_summary: Vehicle BE64DG-300278 was not visible in the vehicle search pick applet for UV opportunity. Investigation found its vehicle allocation flag was set to Y, which excludes the vehicle from the applet. The incident was determined to be a user-configured data condition rather than a system defect.
important_findings: Vehicle BE64DG-300278 was not visible in the vehicle search pick applet.
The vehicle allocation flag for BE64DG-300278 was set to Y.
A vehicle allocation flag value of Y prevents the vehicle from being shown in UV opportunity.
The flag was set by a user and was not identified as a system issue.
A service request is required to change the flag value through an assessment request.
root_cause: The vehicle allocation flag for BE64DG-300278 was set to Y, which prevents the vehicle from appearing in the vehicle search pick applet for UV opportunity.
resolution: Incident rejection was requested because no system issue was found; create a SR to change the vehicle allocation flag value in the assessment request if needed.

investigation_summary: The reported issue concerned spreadsheet 11SC000000000O-09-24-00002-01. Recovery from the database had already been completed through SR JIRA MFTBCFFR-3100, and no approval was made for the spreadsheet. The ticket was determined not to be an incident and was cancelled.
important_findings: Spreadsheet 11SC000000000O-09-24-00002-01 was recovered from the DB.
The recovery was handled through SR JIRA MFTBCFFR-3100.
No approval was made for the spreadsheet.
MFTBCFFR-3118 was determined not to be an incident and was cancelled.
resolution: The spreadsheet was recovered from the DB through SR JIRA MFTBCFFR-3100; MFTBCFFR-3118 was cancelled as it was not an incident.

investigation_summary: The incident covered three BIP printing issues: D21A blank output, D21N wrapped multi-line fields, and incorrect D21L-related output. D21A blank output occurred when a schedule package created a record but no file existed to generate a BIP report. All three issues were corrected on UAT1 and released to PROD across all FDP environments on 2025-02-12.
important_findings: D21A prints blank when the schedule package creates a record but no corresponding file exists, so no BIP report is generated.
The original D21N explanation that its format matched all environments, including Shikoku, was rejected; a corrected BIP report was later attached after the issue was resolved.
No D21L file existed; the BIP was being printed from the Reports Tab instead of the "Print" button.
The D21L countermeasure was to remove the report from the Reports Tab.
The fixes applied to all FDP environments, not only Shikoku.
UAT confirmation could not be performed because UAT had not received the TOB batch.
resolution: All three issues were resolved on UAT1 and deployed to PROD on 2025-02-12 as part of the planned FDP release.

investigation_summary: Spreadsheet 11SC000000000O-09-24-00003-01 was automatically cancelled after ejibai submitted another spreadsheet request with the same insurance company code, year, and serial number, creating 11SC000000000O-09-24-00003-02. A fix was validated in UAT7 and UAT5, released to production on 03/02/2025, and affected records were recovered.
important_findings: Duplicate spreadsheet requests from ejibai with the same insurance company code, year, and serial number triggered automated cancellation of the original spreadsheet.
Spreadsheet 11SC000000000O-09-24-00003-01 was cancelled and spreadsheet 11SC000000000O-09-24-00003-02 was created.
UAT7 validation was successful; UAT5 initially showed an error for uid D0X21662, then the spreadsheet linked to Siebel without error after the UAT5 setting was checked.
The production fix was released on 03/02/2025 and recovery of affected records was completed.
root_cause: An automated process cancelled the original spreadsheet when ejibai sent a duplicate spreadsheet request with the same insurance company code, year, and serial number.
resolution: Implemented and validated a fix in UAT7 and UAT5, released it to production on 03/02/2025, and completed recovery of affected records.

investigation_summary: The Return Slip did not display the Rack Location because the rack location mapping was incorrect. The mapping was corrected in UAT1 and validated by the requester. The fix was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025 as part of the planned FDP release.
important_findings: Rack location was not correctly mapped in Return Slip.
A corrected BIP showing Rack Location was provided in UAT1.
The UAT1 fix was confirmed as working.
The approved fix was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025 through the planned FDP release.
root_cause: Rack location was incorrectly mapped in Return Slip.
resolution: Corrected the Rack Location mapping in Return Slip, validated the fix in UAT1, and deployed it to Production on 12/02/2025.

investigation_summary: In UAT-1, JC I001290325 showed a mismatch between the JC Header branch/location and the Journal Voucher department code. Investigation confirmed that the initial KB functionality was designed to set the Journal Voucher Department code to the Branch Code for this Order Type. Updating it to use the Location code is an additional development requirement, so the incident was closed and a new CR was to be raised.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced in UAT-1 for JC I001290325.
JC Create Branch Code was 10 (Okayama East Branch) and Location Branch Code was 50 (Okayama West Branch).
The Journal Voucher Department Code was set to 10 (Okayama East Branch), while the expected Department Code or Branch Code required investigation was 50.
The initial KB functionality sets the Journal Voucher Department code to the Branch Code only for this Order Type.
The requirement to set the Department code from the Location code was not implemented since the first FDP and requires an AMS-CR/new CR.
root_cause: The existing KB functionality was designed to populate the Journal Voucher Department code from the Branch Code only; mapping it to the Location code was not implemented.
resolution: The Jira incident was rejected/closed as an additional requirement, and a new CR was to be raised for development to populate the Department code from the Location code.

investigation_summary: The Revise sales posting JV mapping for NV and UV had incorrect Credit taxable code, Debit Taxable code, Credit tax rate, and Debit tax rate values. The mapping was corrected in UAT1 so that the Reg Expense - NonTaxable JV line uses tax rate 0 and Taxable Code 80 for both debit and credit. Following approval, the fix was released to production on February 26, 2025.
important_findings: NV and UV Revise sales posting used incorrect JV mapping values for Credit taxable code, Debit Taxable code, Credit tax rate, and Debit tax rate.
The corrected Reg Expense - NonTaxable JV line configuration sets both debit and credit tax rates to 0.
The corrected Reg Expense - NonTaxable JV line configuration sets both debit and credit Taxable Codes to 80.
The fix was completed in UAT1 and released to production on February 26, 2025.
root_cause: Incorrect JV column mapping for Credit taxable code, Debit Taxable code, Credit tax rate, and Debit tax rate in the NV and UV Revise sales posting process.
resolution: Updated the NV and UV Revise sales posting JV mapping so the Reg Expense - NonTaxable JV line has tax rate 0 and Taxable Code 80 for both debit and credit; released to production on February 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: Parts Expense Return Orders displayed the parent order's "Expense Charge To" value in the UI while the return order backend value was based on the return creator's department. The agreed fix copies the original Parts Expense Order's "Expense Charge To" into the expense return order header and updates the UI to display the return order's own stored value. The fix was validated in UAT1 and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
important_findings: For Parts Expense Order M000004280, creator D8MAEKAT had department code 8030, but "Expense Charge To" was manually changed to 8040.
Parts Expense Return Order M000004307 retained 8030 as its backend "Expense Charge To" based on the return-order creator, while the UI displayed 8040 from the parent order.
The same parent-order UI mapping existed in SC.
JV mapping used the Expense Return Order's "Expense Charge To" value in Department Code (CSJS300), creating a mismatch with the UI display.
In UAT1, Expense Order M001290336 was changed from department 1020 to 1030 before creating Expense Return Order M001290337; the return order and its Journal Voucher used 1030.
JV recovery was confirmed as not required.
root_cause: The Parts Expense Return Order UI mapped "Expense Charge To" from the parent order, while the return order header/backend value was independently set from the return creator's department, causing UI and Journal Voucher department-code inconsistency.
resolution: Modified expense-return creation to copy the original expense order's "Expense Charge To" into the expense return order header and changed the Parts Expense Return Order UI to display the return order's own "Expense Charge To" value. The change was tested in UAT1, approved, and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.

investigation_summary: Recycle Fee Orders were not created because the D21F file received from TOB contained an incorrect Fuso Reception#. Initial checks showed no valid D21F file at the Siebel side for the affected VINs. The affected file was corrected with the proper Fuso Reception#, recovered, and the order was completed.
important_findings: For the affected VINs, D21A_17012025171558, D21N_18012025214101, and D21R_18012025214104 were received, but Recycle Fee Orders were not created.
The D21F file was sent and received by TOB, but it contained an incorrect Fuso Reception#.
The invalid Fuso Reception# prevented Recycle Fee Order creation at the Siebel side.
The Fuso Reception# in the affected D21F file was replaced with the correct value and the order was completed.
The issue was identified as a TOB-side issue.
root_cause: TOB sent an incorrect Fuso Reception# in the D21F file, preventing creation of the Recycle Fee Orders.
resolution: Corrected the Fuso Reception# in the affected D21F file, performed recovery, and completed the Recycle Fee Order.

investigation_summary: Pool Cost price was blank for Wakayama orders created at branch level because Pool Cost master lookup used only Dealer code values configured for HQ. The fix was implemented in UAT-7 and required validation through a newly created Stock-In Verification because Pool Cost Order creation occurs during Stock-In Verification approval. UAT passed, and the fix was released to the production environment on 29/01/2025.
important_findings: Pool Cost price was fetched from the Pool Cost master using Dealer code only.
Dealer codes were configured for HQ, while Wakayama orders were created at branch level.
Pool Cost Order is created at the time of Stock-In Verification approval.
Testing with a vehicle Stocked-In before the fix could not validate the change; a new Stock-In Verification was required.
UAT passed after retesting, and the emergency release was deployed to production on 29/01/2025.
root_cause: The Pool Cost master lookup used only Dealer code values configured for HQ, causing Pool Cost price to be blank when Wakayama orders were created from branch level.
resolution: A fix was implemented in UAT-7, validated through a new Stock-In Verification, and released to the production environment as an emergency release on 29/01/2025.

investigation_summary: The incident was investigated in Iwate Prod and confirmed to behave the same as SC. When the No consumption TAX flag (Vender) is Y, Consumption Tax is displayed in SPO Line items, and setting the WO Non-Tax Flag to Y affects both PO and Sales (Quote) line items. The requested scenario, where only PO is non-tax through the AP Account Non-Tax Flag while WO and Quote remain taxable, is a new business requirement and was registered as CR MFTBCFFR-3113.
important_findings: Iwate Prod behavior matches SC.
If the No consumption TAX flag (Vender) is Y, Consumption Tax is visible in SPO Line items.
Setting the WO Non-Tax Flag to Y makes both PO and Sales (Quote) line items non-tax.
The requested FDP Original case requires WO and Quote to remain taxable while only PO is non-tax.
The new requirement is to set only PO to non-tax using the AP Account Non-Tax Flag.
The incident was rejected because the existing functionality works as expected; the requested change was raised as CR MFTBCFFR-3113.
resolution: Rejected as expected functionality. The new non-tax PO-only business case was registered as CR MFTBCFFR-3113, "SV_New Purchase Order Specifications (Non-Tax Compatible)".

investigation_summary: A ¥20,000 sales-price discrepancy was identified between 'Vehicle Order Sheet 1' and 'Vehicle Order Sheet 2'. 'Vehicle Order Sheet 2' excluded the 'Service Effort' price, affecting Sales Orders (SOs) with Product Classes 'HB,' 'MB,' and 'LB.' The correction was deployed to all Wave-3 UAT environments and subsequently released through an emergency release on 29-01-2025.
important_findings: 'Vehicle Order Sheet 1' includes 'Service Effort' in sales-price calculation, while 'Vehicle Order Sheet 2' did not.
The calculation difference resulted in a ¥20,000 discrepancy between the two order sheets.
The issue affected only Sales Orders (SOs) with Product Classes 'HB,' 'MB,' and 'LB.'
The fix was applied to all Wave-3 UAT environments; UAT4 test record was A000032947.
Because the issue was related to BIP, recovery could not be completed until the fix was implemented.
root_cause: 'Vehicle Order Sheet 2' used different sales-price calculation logic from 'Vehicle Order Sheet 1' and did not include the price of 'Service Effort'.
resolution: The sales-price calculation fix was deployed to all Wave-3 UAT environments and released through an emergency release on 29-01-2025.

investigation_summary: The issue was reproduced on UAT-02 when a Sales Order was cancelled at specified workflow statuses, causing the Vehicle status and sub-status to change to "Sold", "Sold". The behavior originated from logic implemented under FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented. The logic was corrected for UV so that a Vehicle is set to "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete; the change was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
important_findings: On UAT-02, cancelling a Sales Order in Registration Completed, Sales Posting Completed, Delivery Completed, or Delivery Pending Approval updated the Vehicle status and sub-status to "Sold", "Sold".
The behavior was introduced after FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented.
The agreed rule for UV is that Vehicle status becomes "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete.
A Sales Order cancelled before Sales Posting must retain its current Vehicle status.
The initial change was applied to both NV and UV tracks, but NV changes were reverted because NV has different requirements.
The UV fix passed UAT and was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
root_cause: Cancellation logic introduced after FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented incorrectly updated the Vehicle status and sub-status to "Sold", "Sold" when a UV Sales Order was cancelled before Sales Posting was complete.
resolution: Updated the UV cancellation process so that Vehicle status is changed to "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete; cancellations before Sales Posting retain the current Vehicle status. The NV change was reverted, and the UV fix was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
technical_entities: FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented

investigation_summary: In UV Purchase Quote, the List Applet fetched Assessment number from Vehicle while the Form Applet fetched it from Assessment Request (AR). When a new Assessment Request was created for the same VIN#, the Vehicle Assessment number was updated and older Purchase Quotes displayed the newer number in the List Applet. The fix aligned both applets to fetch Assessment # from AR, was validated in UAT01, and released to production on February 12, 2025.
important_findings: UV Purchase Quotes created from different Assessment numbers but linked to the same VIN# could display an updated Assessment number in the List Applet.
The List Applet sourced Assessment number from Vehicle, whereas the Form Applet sourced it from Assessment Request (AR).
Creating a new Assessment Request for the same Vehicle updated the Vehicle Assessment number, affecting older Purchase Quotes linked to that Vehicle.
The reported behavior initially matched the SC version existing functionality.
The fix was tested on UAT01 using UV Purchase Quote 1-5WJ1LD and UAT passed.
The change was released to production on February 12, 2025.
root_cause: Inconsistent Assessment number sourcing between the UV Purchase Quote List Applet (Vehicle) and Form Applet (Assessment Request); Vehicle Assessment number updates for the same VIN# changed the value shown for older Purchase Quotes.
resolution: Changed the List Applet to fetch Assessment # from AR, matching the Form Applet; validated in UAT01 and deployed to production.

investigation_summary: The approval request was generated by user "D8ICHIIS", whose position type "SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff" is not valid for generating Approval flows. The incident was determined to be a user mis-operation. Recovery was completed for the affected record.
important_findings: User "D8ICHIIS" generated the approval request.
The user's position type was "SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff".
"SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff" is not a valid position for generating Approval flows.
Recovery was completed for the affected record.
root_cause: User mis-operation: user "D8ICHIIS" generated an approval request with the invalid Approval-flow position type "SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff".
resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record; the user was instructed to proceed.

investigation_summary: Affected registration requests were recovered for all four records, and the registration location master was updated with the correct Payment recipient account. The issue was determined to be caused by an incorrect account selected in the Payment recipient of the registration location used for the registration request, based on business-provided account details.
important_findings: A total of four affected records required recovery.
Recovery was completed for all affected registration requests.
The registration location master was updated with the correct Payment recipient account.
The incorrect account selection originated from the Payment recipient configuration of the registration location used in the registration request.
The account details were provided by the business, and the issue was not identified as a system issue.
root_cause: An incorrect account was selected in the Payment recipient of the registration location used in the registration request.
resolution: Recovered all four affected records and updated the registration location master with the correct Payment recipient account.

investigation_summary: The incident affected Power BI reporting for Real Time Service and Real Time Branch. Investigation identified missing X_RPT_JC_TYPE values in SIEBEL DB for specific locations and a required x_5sc_desc_ filter condition for Real Time Branch. The fixes were validated in FDP UAT and deployed to FDP PROD after approval.
important_findings: X_RPT_JC_TYPE existed in SIEBEL DB for Okayama, Iwate, Shikoku, and Wakayama, allowing the values to appear in the Power BI report for the selected period.
X_RPT_JC_TYPE did not exist in SIEBEL DB for Aomori, Hakodate, and Okinawa; clearing the period filter could display the value for Hakodate.
Real Time Branch required an x_5sc_desc_ filter for Iwate, Shikoku, Wakayama, and Okinawa.
The Real Time Branch filter and Real Time Service changes were validated in FDP UAT before PROD deployment.
After deployment to FDP PROD, JC Type was no longer displayed in the Power BI report for Real Time Service.
root_cause: Missing X_RPT_JC_TYPE values in SIEBEL DB for Aomori, Hakodate, and Okinawa, together with a missing x_5sc_desc_ filter condition for Real Time Branch.
resolution: Added the x_5sc_desc_ filter for Real Time Branch, fixed the Real Time Service behavior in FDP UAT, obtained validation approval, and deployed the Real Time Service changes to FDP PROD.

investigation_summary: The incident was recovered successfully. Investigation determined that the user created multiple SRs without completing existing SRs and completed them in a non-chronological order, which led to a rare validation gap where a Module flag could be selected without entering the module's responsible shop code. No further corrective action was implemented under this Jira.
important_findings: The user created multiple SRs before completing the existing SRs and completed the SRs in random order.
The SR created at 2025/01/20 06:39:44 PM was completed at 2025/01/21 09:22:17 AM, after the SR created at 2025/01/20 07:45:08 PM was completed at 2025/01/20 08:07:48 PM.
An existing SR creation validation requires responsible code details when a Module flag is selected.
In this rare completion-order scenario, the user was able to select the Module flag without entering the module's responsible shop code.
A potential future AMS-CR would add validation on the Update AP button requiring existing SRs to be completed or rejected before creating another Update AP SR.
root_cause: User mis-operation: multiple SRs were created without completing existing SRs and then completed in a random, non-chronological order, exposing a rare validation gap.
resolution: Recovery was completed. No additional action was taken in this Jira; a future AMS-CR may add Update AP button validation.

investigation_summary: A fix was developed and validated through SIT before deployment to UAT-08. UAT passed for H000504201, and the approved fix was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025. The comments do not specify the underlying incident symptoms or technical root cause.
important_findings: The fix was initially applied on UAT-01 and underwent SIT validation.
The fix was deployed to UAT-08 for UAT.
UAT passed for H000504201.
The Production deployment was planned for and completed on 12/02/2025.
resolution: The validated fix was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.

investigation_summary: The "PO - RecycleUV Purchase Order" order type JV line item had Taxable code set to 10 since the KB Process started. The required configuration was clarified to set both debit and credit tax rates to 0, including "Tax rate (CSJS320)" and "Tax rate (CSJS220)". The change was tested in UAT1, approved, and released to production on February 26, 2025.
important_findings: Taxable code for the "PO - RecycleUV Purchase Order" order type JV line item was set to 10 since the start of the KB Process.
The required fixed value for "Tax rate (CSJS320)" and "Tax rate (CSJS220)" was 0.
Both debit and credit tax rates for the JV line item were changed to 0.
UAT was completed before production deployment.
The fix was released to the production environment on February 26, 2025.
root_cause: The "PO - RecycleUV Purchase Order" order type JV line item was configured with Taxable code 10 instead of the required fixed tax rate value of 0 for debit and credit tax rates.
resolution: Set the debit and credit tax rates to 0 for the JV line item of the "PO - RecycleUV Purchase Order" order type, including "Tax rate (CSJS320)" and "Tax rate (CSJS220)", and released the change to production on February 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: The incident affected synchronization of 'Body Building Name' in FDP when revising Sales Quotes and when creating Sales Orders after Quote Approval. The implementation was aligned with SC behavior, validated for existing UAT1 data, and released to the production environment on January 29, 2025.
important_findings: Upon Sales Quote revision, 'Body Building Name' was not synced to the newly revised quote.
Body Building synchronization functionality differed between SC and FDP, causing inconsistent Sales Order synchronization after Quote Approval.
SC had no issue in either synchronization scenario.
The initial UAT1 fix failed; subsequent testing passed for existing data because UAT could not be performed on newly created data.
Testing on newly created data was blocked by the Approval WF on UAT1.
The fix was deployed through an emergency release scheduled for 29-01-2025.
root_cause: FDP used Body Building synchronization logic that differed from SC, resulting in missing 'Body Building Name' synchronization for revised Sales Quotes and Sales Orders after Quote Approval.
resolution: Updated FDP to synchronize 'Body Building Name' according to SC behavior for revised quotes and Sales Orders after Quote Approval, then released the fix to production on January 29, 2025.

investigation_summary: Siebel returned an incorrect chassis number mapping for individual invoice responses. The VehicleNumber response mapping was corrected and validated in UAT1 using JC I001289808. The fix was deployed to the production environment on January 24 and branch verification was completed.
important_findings: The individual invoice response sent by Siebel had an incorrect chassis number mapping.
After the UAT1 fix, Siebel returned the correct VehicleNumber details for JC I001289808.
The production deployment was changed from the planned FDP release to an urgent release.
The fix was released to the production environment on January 24.
Branch verification was completed before incident closure.
root_cause: Incorrect chassis number mapping in the Siebel response for individual invoices.
resolution: Corrected the Siebel VehicleNumber mapping in UAT1, validated the response, and deployed the fix to the production environment on January 24.

investigation_summary: An existing SR was rejected and the user created a new SR after the original SR was not closed correctly. The investigation determined this was a user mis-operation. The recreated SR closed correctly, and regression testing in UAT4 found no process issues.
important_findings: The existing SR was rejected because it was not closed correctly.
The issue was determined to be user mis-operation.
A newly created SR was closed correctly.
Regression testing in the UAT4 environment found no issues with the process.
The functionality was confirmed to be working correctly; the event was considered a rare case.
root_cause: User mis-operation caused the original SR to not be closed correctly.
resolution: Rejected the incorrectly handled SR and had the user create a new SR, which closed correctly.

investigation_summary: The approval issue occurred when user D8ESAKAU submitted the spreadsheet using the Branch-CS-Staff position. The Branch-CS-Staff hierarchy does not contain an Insurance Manager, so the required approver was not routed. The behavior was reproduced in UAT7 and was determined to be a user position-selection issue rather than a system defect; recovery was completed and the user was asked to submit the approval request again.
important_findings: D8ESAKAU has two positions: SCHQ-Sales-Ins-Mgr and Branch-CS-Staff.
D8ESAKAU used the Branch-CS-Staff position to generate the spreadsheet approval request.
The Branch-CS-Staff hierarchy has no Insurance Manager, preventing the required approval routing.
The issue was replicated in UAT7 on Spreadsheet# 1-30192180.
D8TAMAIH already has the Ins Manager position; no additional role was required.
No equivalent routing issue was identified in production or UAT during subsequent checks.
root_cause: D8ESAKAU submitted the approval request using the Branch-CS-Staff position, whose hierarchy does not include an Insurance Manager.
resolution: Recovery was completed under MFTBCFFR-3100, and the user was instructed to submit the approval request again using the appropriate position.

investigation_summary: An invoice upsert failed in Siebel with an EAI Siebel Adapter error, and no invoice number was generated. The reported error indicated that no user key could be used for the "MF Ejibai Invoice" Integration Component instance. Subsequent checks found the operation working normally with no further irregularities; the issue remained under production monitoring.
important_findings: The failure occurred at the "Upsert - Invoice" step when invoking the "EAI Siebel Adapter" service using the "Upsert" method.
The reported errors were "SBL-BPR-00162" and "SBL-EAI-04397": "No user key can be used for the Integration Component instance 'MF Ejibai Invoice'."
No Invoice number was generated for the failed transaction.
Invoice number generation uses EAILookupSiebel("MF_EJIBAI_SC_IDENTIFIER", ...).
The team requested the request XML sent by Ejibai to Siebel for further analysis.
Later validation found the operation functioning normally, with no additional user escalations or irregularities observed.

investigation_summary: The Address field in Service Quote BIP was not updated when the corresponding AR address was updated because the two components used different backend Siebel field mappings. The required BIP mapping changes, previously implemented in Wave 1 and Wave 2 production under MFTBCFFR-2575, were applied to FDP UAT-5 and then released to Wave 3 production on January 24. Branch verification was completed and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Service Quote BIP and AR used different backend Siebel field mappings for the Address field.
Because of the mapping discrepancy, Address in Quote BIP was not updated when AR was updated.
The same BIP mapping changes had already been deployed to Wave 1 and Wave 2 production through MFTBCFFR-2575.
The MFTBCFFR-2575 BIP changes were applied on FDP UAT-5 and deployed to Wave 3 production on January 24.
Branch verification was completed after the production release.
root_cause: Different backend Siebel field mappings for the Address field between Service Quote BIP and AR prevented Quote BIP Address updates when AR was updated.
resolution: Applied the BIP mapping changes from MFTBCFFR-2575 to FDP UAT-5 and deployed them to Wave 3 production on January 24.

investigation_summary: The incident involved an invoice upsert failure in Siebel, with no Invoice Number generated. The reported errors indicated that no user key could be used for the Integration Component instance "MF Ejibai Invoice". Request XML from Ejibai and Ejibai code/configuration verification were requested, but no confirmed root cause or corrective fix was documented; the issue was consolidated with MFTBCFFR-3045.
important_findings: The DB recorded an error during the "Upsert - Invoice" step invoking "EAI Siebel Adapter" method "Upsert".
The error was "No user key can be used for the Integration Component instance 'MF Ejibai Invoice'.(SBL-EAI-04397)".
No Invoice Number was generated for the failed transaction.
Investigation required the request XML sent by Ejibai to Siebel and revalidation of Ejibai codes/configuration.
The incident was identified as the same as JIRA MFTBCFFR-3045 and was to be tracked through that ticket.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned a Bank Info/account-name value described as "For business testing". Review of the Siebel response found that this value was not sent by SIEBEL. The issue was confirmed to originate from KB settings, and the incident was rejected as not being a SIEBEL issue.
important_findings: The Siebel response did not contain the account-name value "For business testing".
Bank Info was not an interface value received from SIEBEL.
SIEBEL was sending the correct response.
The affected Branch was asked to check the settings in KB.
The incident was confirmed as a KB-side issue rather than a SIEBEL issue.
root_cause: Incorrect or problematic settings in KB caused the Bank Info/account-name value; the value was not supplied by SIEBEL.
resolution: Branch was requested to check and correct the relevant KB settings; the incident was rejected as not a SIEBEL issue.

investigation_summary: Duplicate Recycle fee order records caused TOB responses to update a duplicate order rather than the original, leaving the correct recycling order/TOB status unupdated. The incident was initially attributed to duplicate D21F files, but CIH server logs showed no evidence that the file was sent twice and the reason duplicate files existed on the ODI server remained unknown. A VOW-related explanation was later confirmed to apply to a separate Iwate incident, not this Okinawa incident. Affected records were recovered, and the ticket was ultimately closed as a rare case without a confirmed recurrence-prevention change.
important_findings: Duplicate recycling fee orders caused TOB response data to be reflected on duplicate records instead of the original submitted order.
The same D21F file was observed twice in the system, resulting in duplicate Recycle fee order records.
CIH server logs did not show a history of the D21F file being sent twice.
The cause of two identical files being created on the ODI server was not determined.
The VOW recycling-confirmation input cause applied to a separate Iwate incident and was not applicable to this incident.
Recovery was completed for affected VINs, including updating affected recycling order statuses to Completed.
resolution: Recovered the affected recycling order records, including updating their status to Completed. The ticket was placed on HOLD pending recurrence and later closed as a rare case; no preventive system change was documented.

investigation_summary: An order-related invoice integration failure was investigated despite the spreadsheet being in Spreadsheet Approved status. The database recorded an EAI Siebel Adapter Upsert failure for the MF Ejibai Invoice integration component, and no Invoice number was generated. The issue was identified as the same as MFTBCFFR-3045 and was transferred for tracking through that ticket.
important_findings: Order Q000010091 was initially associated with a database error and referenced Jira 2964, but it was considered a different problem.

The failure occurred at the "Upsert - Invoice" step through EAI Siebel Adapter: "No user key can be used for the Integration Component instance 'MF Ejibai Invoice'."
No Invoice number was generated following the integration error.
Further analysis required the request XML sent from Ejibai to Siebel and revalidation of Ejibai Codes.
The incident was determined to be the same as MFTBCFFR-3045 and tracking continued there.

investigation_summary: The incident was tracked under AMS CR RITM1641745, with previous CR 610008042. Required changes were applied to UAT-01 and passed UAT validation. The changes were released in the FDP release on 23 January 2025.

resolution: Updated the printer driver for OKI C332 printers after validation on a Dev server, then deployed the driver change to Prod.

FALCON response slowness resulted in no records being returned and an error screen being displayed.

resolution: The incident was cancelled after confirming the error was caused by FALCON delay and not by the FORCE system.

investigation_summary: The incident involved an invoice upsert failure from Ejibai to Siebel, with no Invoice number generated. investigation_summary: A printed document for “Shikoku FUSO Kagawa Marugame” showed dealer code B77Q5001, while B77Q5000 was registered with Sompo Japan for “Shikoku Fuso Kagawa.” The discussion determined that agency-code changes were to be handled by e-jibai through coordination between Sompo Japan and Kagawa. The agency-code change was determined to be handled by e-jibai rather than Cubastion.

investigation_summary: Users could not select Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co., Ltd. for Agency Code 11SC000000000O because no corresponding insurance company code existed in the Insurance Company 10 digit master. A configuration change released on 14 January for Jira 2954 enabled selection of 11SC000000000O, exposing the missing master-data mapping. important_findings: No insurance company code existed in the Insurance Company 10 digit master for Agency Code 11SC000000000O and Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co., Ltd.
Before 13 January, users could not select 11SC000000000O in the Agency Code field.
The 14 January release for Jira 2954 changed configuration so users could select 11SC000000000O, which caused the issue to become visible.
Selecting 26SC in the Agency Code field allowed the user to select an Insurance Company.
The user subsequently confirmed that the company code could be selected.
root_cause: The Insurance Company 10 digit master lacked an insurance company code mapping for Agency Code 11SC000000000O and Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co., Ltd.; the Jira 2954 configuration change exposed this missing master data.
resolution: Company code selection was confirmed to work; the incident was closed.

investigation_summary: The issue was fixed and validated in UAT1 and UAT8. The same issue was confirmed to exist in Production, and the approved fix was deployed to all FDP Production environments in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: The fix was applied to UAT1 and UAT8 for testing and approval.
The issue also existed in the Production environment.
