resolution: The approved fix was deployed to all FDP Production environments in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_summary: This issue was identified as a duplicate of MFTBCFFR-3001. Investigation and tracking were redirected to MFTBCFFR-3001; no technical findings, root cause, or corrective action are documented in this incident's comments.
important_findings: MFTBCFFR-3011 is the same issue as MFTBCFFR-3001.
Further tracking was moved to MFTBCFFR-3001.
No technical investigation details, root cause, or resolution are recorded in the MFTBCFFR-3011 comments.

investigation_summary: An affected order record was initially updated to "Rejected", which was reported as an invalid order status. The issue was identified and a fix was released through the 17 January FDP Emergency release. The comments do not specify the underlying technical cause.
important_findings: The affected record was updated to the status "Rejected".
It was reported that "Rejected" is not a valid status for orders; "却下" was suggested as the intended status.
The issue was identified, but no root-cause details were documented in the comments.
A fix was released in the 17 January FDP Emergency release.
resolution: A fix was released through the 17 January FDP Emergency release.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned incorrect Department Code values in Journal Voucher records for payer-change Change Orders. Department Code mappings and the JC AR Service Responsible code were corrected and validated in UAT1 and UAT8. Following RF team confirmation, the program was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
important_findings: For payer changes, the JC AR Service Responsible code is set in the Journal Voucher.
Department Code mappings required correction for Change Order payer-change scenarios, including CSJS200, CSJ200, and CSJ300 values.
CSJ300 was identified as the correct Department Code for the branch code that operated the JC.
The updated Department Code mapping was implemented in UAT1 and UAT8 and reviewed by the RF team.
The Production deployment was approved and completed on 12/02/2025 as part of the planned FDP release.
root_cause: Incorrect Department Code mapping for payer-change Change Orders caused incorrect Department Code values in Journal Voucher records.
resolution: Corrected the Department Code mapping and JC AR Service Responsible code handling for payer changes in UAT1 and UAT8, then deployed the approved program fix to Production on 12/02/2025.

investigation_summary: Sales Posting JV amounts and creation behavior for outsourcing orders were inconsistent with the required IBOS and Non-IBOS pricing logic. The existing logic depended on Net Price, causing JV creation to fail when Net Price was absent despite bodywork and other billing amounts being present. The UAT1 fix changed Sales Posting JV creation to evaluate Net Price and Total Selling Price, with the Base Amount set to their sum; the change was validated and released to Prod on 14 May 2025.
important_findings: Initially, JV contained Agency Fee, PO, and CT pricing, while the invoice sent Agency Price plus Total Selling and did not send PO price, causing a JV-to-invoice price difference.
For Non-IBOS cases, Total Selling Price was mapped to JV in UAT1; subsequent changes addressed both IBOS and Non-IBOS logic.
Outsourcing Order A001292536 did not create a Sales Posting JV because Net Price was not set in Taxes & Expenses and the existing creation condition required Net Price to be non-zero.
The required behavior was to create a JV when bodywork and other billing amounts were present, regardless of whether Net Price was set.
The corrected Sales Posting JV Base Amount is Net Price plus Total Selling Price.

JV tax calculation subtracts License Plate Number Fee and Illuminated License Plate Number Fee from the taxable amount; the validated example calculated tax of 5200 from a taxable amount of 52000 at a 10% Consumption Tax Rate.
root_cause: Sales Posting JV creation and Base Amount logic relied on Net Price being non-zero, so no JV was created when Net Price was absent even when Total Selling Price or bodywork and other billing amounts required a JV.
resolution: Updated the Sales Posting JV condition to check Net Price and Total Selling Price, and set the JV Base Amount to the sum of Net Price and Total Selling Price. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Prod in the 14 May 2025 release.

investigation_summary: A mismatch between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was reproduced on UAT-4 using two browser sessions. Completing the Shaken Expense in one browser created a Journal Voucher using the original Actual Amount, while a stale second browser session could subsequently overwrite the Actual Expense amount. The fix prevents updates to Actual Amount after the Actual Expense is Completed, and the Journal Voucher difference was recovered.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced on UAT-4 with JC# I000031108 and Expense ID 1-JCL44.
Clicking Done in Browser 1 marked the Shaken Expense as Completed and created a Journal Voucher with Actual Amount 17,400.
Without refreshing Browser 2, changing Weight Tax Actual Amount to 16,800 overwrote the Actual Expense but did not update the existing Journal Voucher.
The resulting discrepancy between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was ▲600.
After the fix, users cannot update Actual Amount from another browser once the Actual Expense is Completed.
root_cause: A stale multi-browser session allowed the Actual Expense Actual Amount to be updated after the record was marked Completed and its Journal Voucher had already been created, causing the Journal Voucher and Actual Expense amounts to diverge.
resolution: Implemented a UAT-4 restriction preventing Actual Amount updates in multi-browser sessions after Actual Expense status is Completed, and added the ▲600 difference to the Journal Voucher.

investigation_summary: The incident was scheduled for production release and deployed in the 23 January 2025 FDP release. No technical investigation details, root cause, or specific corrective change are documented in the comments.
important_findings: Production release was requested.
The incident was released in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
No error details, affected systems, root cause, or implementation details were provided.
resolution: Released in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_summary: Affected records were not displayed because TOB file processing failed in an ODI package. The affected records were recovered, and an ODI patch was applied on 2025-01-19 to correct the package issue. Automation was added to send email notifications from the ODI system when files remain unprocessed, and subsequent monitoring found no further ODI-failure discrepancies.
important_findings: The incident was caused by a malfunctioning ODI package used for TOB file processing.
Recovery was completed for the affected records after the ODI package fix was applied.
An ODI patch was applied on 2025-01-19 to resolve the ODI-specific failure.
Automated monitoring now sends email notifications from the ODI system for unprocessed TOB files.
MFTBCFFR-3152 and MFTBCFFR-3350 were confirmed to be unrelated: MFTBCFFR-3152 involved data loading to FDP Chugoku, and MFTBCFFR-3350 involved a missing D21A file.
root_cause: A defect in the ODI package processing TOB files caused files to remain unprocessed and affected records not to be displayed.
resolution: Applied an ODI patch on 2025-01-19, successfully reran the package, recovered affected records, and implemented email-based monitoring for unprocessed TOB files.

investigation_summary: The affected sales order (SO) was recovered and its status was updated to 'Pending'. A corrective change was released in the 17th January FDP Emergency release to address the incident and prevent recurrence.
important_findings: The sales order had not recovered at the time of the initial escalation.
Recovery was completed by updating the SO status to 'Pending'.
The order status was subsequently confirmed.
The incident fix was released through the 17th January FDP Emergency release.
resolution: Recovered the affected SO by updating its status to 'Pending' and released the corrective change in the 17th January FDP Emergency release.

investigation_summary: In the Map/Unmap process for UV Purchase Orders, Journal Vouchers were created when Net Price was zero because the required zero-price condition was missing from the DataMap search specification. The condition was added and validated in UATs, preventing JV creation for zero-price Map/Unmap cases while retaining JV creation when Cost fields contain a non-zero value. The fix was released to FDP on 23 January 2025.
important_findings: MAP/UNMAP scenarios in UV Purchase Orders lacked a DataMap search specification condition for Net Price equal to zero.
The missing condition caused Journal Vouchers to be created for zero-price cases.
After the fix, zero-amount Journal Vouchers are not created for Map/Unmap cases.
A Journal Voucher is still created when any Cost field contains a value other than zero, even if the total amount is not zero yen.
The fix was deployed to UATs, passed UAT, and was released in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
root_cause: The DataMap search specification for MAP/UNMAP scenarios in UV Purchase Orders did not handle cases where Net Price equals zero.
resolution: Added a Net Price equals zero condition to the DataMap search specification for MAP/UNMAP scenarios, preventing Journal Voucher creation for zero-price cases; released to FDP on 23 January 2025.

investigation_summary: The incident occurred when users attempted to continue processing cancelled spreadsheets in the Ejibai portal. Processing a cancelled spreadsheet updated the order status to Liability Policy Issued but failed at the Update spreadsheet step. Recovery was completed by reverting the affected spreadsheet statuses to "Spreadsheet Created" so users could reprocess them.
important_findings: The issue was identified as user misoperation.
Users cancelled spreadsheets and then attempted to process them again through the Ejibai portal.
When a spreadsheet status was cancelled, the portal updated the order status to Liability Policy Issued and returned an error at the Update spreadsheet step.
Recovery required reverting the spreadsheet status to "Spreadsheet Created".
Recovery was completed for both affected spreadsheets, including 11SC000000000S-09-24-00003-01.
root_cause: User attempted to process spreadsheets in the Ejibai portal after the spreadsheets had been cancelled.
resolution: Reverted the affected spreadsheet statuses to "Spreadsheet Created" and instructed users to reprocess the steps.

investigation_summary: The Job Card screen took time to load when opened from the Vehicle screen. Investigation identified delayed responses from FALCON, with an estimated response time of 30 seconds to 1 minute. The issue was determined not to be on the SIEBEL side and was cancelled, with a request to raise a ticket to FALCON for the response-delay issue.
important_findings: Opening a Job Card from the Vehicle screen was delayed.
FALCON response time was estimated at 30 seconds to 1 minute.
The delayed FALCON response affected display of response results and Job Card screen loading.
The incident was determined not to be a SIEBEL-side issue.
Users were advised to wait after selecting the Job Card while FALCON responded.
root_cause: Delayed response time from FALCON caused the Job Card screen to load slowly.
resolution: The incident was cancelled as it was not a SIEBEL-side issue; a ticket was requested for FALCON to investigate the response delay.

investigation_summary: A Planned Expense Order could not generate approval because user D8KOBAYF's primary position was SCHQ-Sales-Ins-Staff rather than a Service Staff or CS Staff position. The system displayed "Please select valid Approval Requestor" when Generate Approval was selected. The behavior was replicated on UAT-5 and was determined to be an operational mistake rather than a system defect; the incident was withdrawn.
important_findings: The Planned Expense Order was updated to status "Completed."
User D8KOBAYF had positions Branch-Service-Staff and SCHQ-Sales-Ins-Staff.
When the Planned Expense was created, D8KOBAYF's primary position was SCHQ-Sales-Ins-Staff, not Service Staff or CS Staff.
The Generate Approval action displayed "Please select valid Approval Requestor".
The issue was replicated on UAT-5 for JC# I000034169 and Invoice# 1-33022839.
The incident was classified as an operation miss and withdrawn.
root_cause: User D8KOBAYF created the Planned Expense Order while assigned primary position SCHQ-Sales-Ins-Staff, which was not a valid Service Staff or CS Staff approval requestor position.
resolution: The Planned Expense Order status was updated to "Completed," and the incident was withdrawn after confirming the issue was an operational mistake.

investigation_summary: Reports were successfully sent to the Canon servers, but their record status remained "Printing" and jobs were paused on the server side. The issue was resolved after FDP PIC restarted their router, allowing the paused jobs to print. No server changes were required.
important_findings: Reports were successfully transmitted to the Canon servers.
Affected record status remained "Printing" despite successful transmission.
Jobs were paused on the server side.
Restarting the FDP PIC router allowed the paused jobs to print successfully.
No server-side changes were needed.
root_cause: FDP PIC router required a restart; its condition prevented paused server-side print jobs from completing.
resolution: FDP PIC restarted their router, after which the paused jobs printed successfully.

investigation_summary: The issue was replicated on FDP UAT-4 using JC# I000032336 and Invoice# 1-32491254. A Planned expense created in a Job card defaults to Type "Service Expense", but changing the invoice type to "Expense" from the Service Invoice screen caused the Service invoice to disappear from that screen and appear under Customer Invoice. The Type and Code fields were made read-only in the Service Invoice screen, verified in FDP UAT-1, and released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: Planned expenses created under a Job card have a predefined Type value of "Service Expense".
Changing the invoice Type from "Service Expense" to "Expense" in the Service Invoice screen moved the created Service invoice from the Service Invoice screen to the Customer Invoice screen.
The issue was replicated on FDP UAT-4 with JC# I000032336 and Invoice# 1-32491254.
Type and Code were changed to read-only fields in the Service Invoice screen and verified in FDP UAT-1.
The fix was released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
root_cause: Users could change the predefined invoice Type from "Service Expense" to "Expense" in the Service Invoice screen, causing the Service invoice to be displayed under Customer Invoice instead.
resolution: Made the Type and Code fields read-only in the Service Invoice screen and deployed the fix to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_summary: D2S was recovering the affected records under D2S Ticket# 0010012920. The issue was determined not to be related to Siebel, and the Jira ticket was closed.
important_findings: D2S was responsible for recovering the affected records.
D2S Ticket# 0010012920 was referenced for the recovery activity.
The issue was determined not to be related to Siebel.
The Jira ticket was closed after confirming it was outside the Siebel scope.

investigation_summary: In the Okinawa production environment, the Self-Contract flag was read-only for Quote# 1-8KE7V because its Contractant Code, 0000001163, was not included in the configured Own-Company codes. The required Own-Company codes were provided for multiple FDPs and configured in production, including Okinawa code 0000001163. An Own-Company code for Chugoku Fuso remained requested but was not provided in the discussion.
important_findings: The Self-Contract flag can be checked only when the Contractant Code is configured as an Own-Company code.
Quote# 1-8KE7V used Contractant Code 0000001163, which was initially not among the configured codes and therefore showed the Self-Contract flag as read-only.
The existing configuration listed 0000H00031 and 0000GZ6000 for SC use, and 0000108561 for Okayama use.
Production configuration was updated with Own-Company codes for Aomori, Hakodate, Iwate, Wakayama, Shikoku, and Okinawa, including 0000001163 for Okinawa.
The Own-Company code for Chugoku Fuso was still requested after the production configuration update.
root_cause: Contractant Code 0000001163 for Okinawa was not configured as an Own-Company code, causing the Self-Contract flag to remain read-only.
resolution: Configured the provided Own-Company codes in production, including Okinawa Contractant Code 0000001163.

investigation_summary: The MVG applet was removed from the 'Workshop Name' field on Quote List Applet to align the behavior with SC. The change was validated in UAT-7 and confirmed correct. It was deployed to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: The MVG applet was removed from 'Workshop Name' on Quote List Applet.
The updated configuration was made consistent with SC.
The change was tested and approved in UAT-7.
The fix was released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
root_cause: The 'Workshop Name' field on Quote List Applet had an MVG applet configuration that differed from SC.
resolution: Removed the MVG applet from 'Workshop Name' on Quote List Applet, validated the change in UAT-7, and deployed it to PROD.

investigation_summary: The reported behavior occurred in all FDP environments and was transferred to AMS for handling. The requested change was later determined to be unnecessary, and the Jira was rejected.
important_findings: The behavior was observed in all FDP environments.
The incident was moved to AMS for investigation/handling.
The requested change was not required at the time of closure.
The Jira was rejected rather than implementing a change.
resolution: No change was implemented; the Jira was rejected because the requested change was not required.

investigation_summary: The reported behavior was observed across all FDP environments and the ticket was routed to AMS. The requested change was later determined to be unnecessary, and the Jira was rejected.
important_findings: The behavior occurred in all FDP environments.
The ticket was moved to AMS for handling.
The requested change was not required at the time of review.
The Jira was rejected without implementing a change.
resolution: No corrective change was implemented; the Jira was rejected because the change was not required.

investigation_summary: Recovery was completed for all four affected records. An RCA was stated to be in progress, but no root-cause details or recurrence-prevention measures were documented in the comments. The incident was released through the 17 January FDP Emergency release.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for all four records.
RCA was still in progress after recovery completion.
No confirmed cause or recurrence-prevention details were provided in the documented timeline.
The incident was released on 17 January through an FDP Emergency release.
resolution: Recovered all four records and released the incident through the 17 January FDP Emergency release.

investigation_summary: Duplicate option records in the database caused duplicate options to be displayed in VC on Hakodate Prod. The duplicate data was corrected, restoring singular option display. A duplicate-record check and cleanup query was implemented after options master updates to prevent recurrence.
important_findings: Options data was duplicated in the database on Hakodate Prod.
Duplicate database records caused duplicate options to appear in VC.
No duplicate records were found in other Prod environments.
A query was implemented to detect and delete duplicate records after options master updates.
root_cause: Duplicate options data records in the database on Hakodate Prod.
resolution: Corrected the duplicate options data on Hakodate Prod and implemented a post-options-master-update query to detect and delete duplicate records.

investigation_summary: The incident was investigated in the Shikoku prod environment. The user updated the mandatory fields and was then able to link the spreadsheet, after which the incident was closed.
important_findings: The issue was checked in Shikoku prod.
Updating mandatory fields allowed the user to link the spreadsheet.
The incident was closed after the spreadsheet-linking issue was resolved.
root_cause: Mandatory fields had not been updated, preventing the user from linking the spreadsheet.
resolution: The user updated the mandatory fields and successfully linked the spreadsheet.

investigation_summary: Recycling data was not displayed because TOB files were not processed correctly by an ODI package in Hakodate prod. The affected records were recovered after an ODI patch was applied on 2025-01-19 and the package was run successfully. Automated ODI email monitoring was added for unprocessed TOB files, and subsequent checks found no further ODI-failure discrepancies.
important_findings: Vehicles were processed successfully in Hakodate prod after recovery.
The incident was caused by an ODI package issue during TOB file processing.
An ODI patch was applied on 2025-01-19, after which the package ran successfully and the issue no longer occurred.
Automation was implemented to send email notifications from the ODI system when TOB files remain unprocessed.
MFTBCFFR-3152 was caused by data loading to FDP Chugoku and MFTBCFFR-3350 was caused by a missing D21A file; neither was caused by this ODI failure.
The implemented monitoring was confirmed to be operating normally with no observed ODI-failure discrepancies.
root_cause: A defect in the ODI package prevented correct processing of TOB files, resulting in missing recycling data.
resolution: Applied an ODI patch on 2025-01-19, successfully reran the ODI package, recovered affected records, and implemented automated email monitoring for unprocessed TOB files.

investigation_summary: The user could not map or create a Purchase Order for a line item. Investigation found the target Purchase Order was in Pending status, which disables the OK button, and a Purchase Order already existed for the line item. The incident was rejected as expected functionality rather than a product defect.
important_findings: The OK button is inactive when the Purchase Order status is Pending, Pending Approval, Rejected, or Cancelled.
The Purchase Order being mapped had Pending status.
A new Purchase Order could not be created because a Purchase Order already existed for the line item.
To create a new Purchase Order, the existing order must be cancelled or completed.
root_cause: The existing Purchase Order for the line item was in Pending status, which prevented mapping, and its existence prevented creation of another Purchase Order for the same line item.
resolution: Cancel or complete the existing Purchase Order before creating a new Purchase Order; mapping is only available when the Purchase Order is not in Pending, Pending Approval, Rejected, or Cancelled status.

investigation_summary: Parts Sales return creation failed when the editable Already Returned Qty field in the shipment screen was set to a value equal to the ordered quantity. The failure was reproduced in UAT-5 and caused the Parts Sales Order screen to update its Already Returned Qty with the shipment-screen value, resulting in the validation "Please enter Return Qty." The field was changed to read-only in the shipment screen, verified in FDP UAT-1, and released to production in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: For SO M000034005 in UAT-5, setting Already Returned Qty in the shipment screen equal to the ordered quantity caused return-order creation to fail.
The displayed validation was "Please enter Return Qty."
After the validation, the Already Returned Qty on the Parts Sales Order screen was updated with the value entered in the shipment screen.
The issue was also reproduced for M000031415 in UAT5, while testing with several other orders did not reproduce it.
Previously affected shipment-line Already Returned Qty values were reset to 0 for SO M000003330 and M000007642 to allow Parts Sales return recreation.
The corrective change made Already Returned Qty read-only in the shipment screen.
root_cause: Already Returned Qty was editable in the shipment screen; entering a value equal to the ordered quantity propagated that value to the Parts Sales Order screen and prevented Parts Sales return creation.
resolution: Made the Already Returned Qty field read-only in the shipment screen, verified the fix in FDP UAT-1, and released it in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_summary: Approvers were not displayed, preventing approval requests and requiring the quote status to be returned to creating. Investigation found that the required approval flow was missing for the affected scenario in FDP-Iwate; the same issue also existed in UAT. Approval flows were reviewed and corrected across all FDP UAT and Prod environments.
important_findings: Approvers were not displayed, preventing users from submitting an approval request.
The affected quote required status recovery to creating before approval could be requested again.
The approval flow for the affected scenario was missing in FDP-Iwate.
The issue was also present in UAT.
Approval flows exist for both pre-order and post-order processes.
The issue was resolved across all FDP UAT and Prod environments.
root_cause: The required approval flow was not configured in the system for the affected scenario.
resolution: Corrected the approval flows for the affected scenario across all FDP UAT and Prod environments.

investigation_summary: FDP users in Shikoku and Wakayama could not create Liability Insurance policies or select the 11SC Agency code because the Production Pick Applet search specification did not include 11SC. UAT was configured for "= 26SC OR =11SC", while Production was configured only for "=26SC" after CR-820 changes had been migrated in FDP but not yet to Production. The Production configuration was released on 9 January 2025, and a subsequent Pick Applet search-spec data issue was corrected so both agency options became available.
important_findings: UAT search spec was "= 26SC OR =11SC", while Production search spec was "=26SC".
The configuration difference resulted from CR-820 changes being migrated in FDP while the CR had not yet been migrated to Production.
The issue affected FDPs using the 11SC agency, specifically Shikoku and Wakayama.
Users could not select the 11SC Agency code on the Insurance order screen.
A data issue in the Pick Applet search spec was corrected, after which both agency options were available.
root_cause: Production Pick Applet search-spec configuration/data restricted agency selection to 26SC and did not include 11SC. The discrepancy existed because CR-820 changes were present in FDP but had not yet been migrated to Production.
resolution: Released the required search-spec configuration to Production for Shikoku and Wakayama on 9 January 2025, then corrected the Pick Applet search-spec data so users could select both 26SC and 11SC.

investigation_summary: The incident was related to CR MFTBCFFR-2560 SV Change Service Claim Mapping(Dealer Code/Branch Code). A Branch master created for the CR had not been synchronized to WS-3 environments. The Branch master was synchronized to all Wave-3 environments, resolving the issue.
important_findings: The issue was associated with CR MFTBCFFR-2560 SV Change Service Claim Mapping(Dealer Code/Branch Code).
A Branch master was created as part of the CR.
The Branch master was not synced for WS-3 environments.
The master was synced for all Wave-3 environments.
The issue was reported as resolved after the synchronization.
root_cause: The Branch master created for CR MFTBCFFR-2560 was not synchronized to WS-3 environments.
resolution: Synchronized the Branch master to all Wave-3 environments.
technical_entities: SV Change Service Claim Mapping(Dealer Code/Branch Code)

investigation_summary: Shipments for SO# 1017885847 and SO# 1017889654 were delayed on the D2S side. The orders had been created directly in D2S and did not have a PO#. D2S initiated shipment using a dummy number, and the shipments were marked successful in Siebel.
important_findings: SO# 1017885847 and SO# 1017889654 had delayed D2S shipments.
The orders were created directly on the D2S side.
The directly created D2S orders lacked a PO#.
D2S initiated shipment with a dummy number.
The shipments were marked successful on the Siebel side.
root_cause: Orders created directly in D2S did not have a PO#, delaying shipment processing.
resolution: D2S initiated the shipments using a dummy number, and the shipments were marked successful in Siebel.

investigation_summary: The specified records were initially not sent from TOB to Siebel. Subsequent verification confirmed receipt of D21A files for records 7604 and 8803; no underlying cause or corrective action was documented.
important_findings: The specified records had not initially been sent from TOB to Siebel.
D21A_09012025223855 was received for record 7604.
D21A_13012025214201 was received for record 8803.

investigation_summary: Recycling orders were not displayed when D21F was processed before D21E due to file timing from TOB, including cases involving inter-sales company transfers. Initial recovery of an affected 8-record file was incomplete, so all FDPs were checked and recovered. Recovery was completed for all FDPs, and Shikoku Fuso confirmed that recycling was displayed.
important_findings: TOB file timing caused D21F to arrive and be processed before D21E.
Multiple affected cases involved inter-sales company transfers.
The initial recovery covered an affected file with 8 records but did not cover all affected recycling orders.
All FDPs, including the Shikoku chassis cases, required validation and recovery.
Shikoku Fuso confirmed that recycling was displayed after recovery.
root_cause: D21F was processed before D21E because of TOB file timing, preventing affected recycling orders from being displayed.
resolution: Checked and recovered affected recycling orders across all FDPs; Shikoku Fuso confirmed recycling display after recovery.

investigation_summary: The incident affected PT Sales Order M000002277 and required review of SV realtime invoice and Bulk invoice logic. Investigation identified a code-related issue; a temporary fix was tested in FDP UATs and released to production. A permanent fix was validated on UAT1 and released to the production environment on February 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was identified as code-related.
SV realtime invoice and Bulk invoice logic were identified for review.
A temporary fix passed UAT testing in FDP UATs, excluding UAT2 and UAT3.
A permanent fix was deployed to UAT1, validated, and approved for production release.
The permanent fix was released to the production environment on February 26, 2025.
root_cause: A code-related issue affecting the invoice logic.
resolution: A temporary code fix was tested and released, followed by a permanent fix validated on UAT1 and released to the production environment on February 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: Print job submission failed because printer information files contained model information instead of the required printer driver names for three printers. DiSWebAPI returned an error that the configured printer driver name did not match the Windows printer driver name. The printer information file was updated and replaced, and Wakayama Fuso confirmed the issue was resolved.
important_findings: Printer information files contained model info instead of printer driver names.
The issue affected three printers.
DiSWebAPI POST /ps/1.0/printjobs failed with: "Printer driver name and Windows printer driver name do not match."
The corrected printer information file was uploaded and replaced.
Wakayama Fuso confirmed normal operation after the update.
root_cause: Incorrect driver names in the printer information files; model information was configured instead of the Windows printer driver names.
resolution: Updated and replaced the printer information file with the correct printer driver names.

investigation_summary: Sales Posting records required recovery after the process failed to complete. The issue was replicated in UAT1 on UV Sales Order E001287415, where the order remained at Delivery Pending Approval. A code fix for the UV Sales Posting process was tested in UAT1 and released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: The affected record was recovered on 27 December 2024.
The issue was replicated in UAT1 using UV Sales Order E001287415.
In the reproduced case, Sales Posting did not complete and the status remained Delivery Pending Approval.
The behavior was identified as rare/random status-update behavior in the Sales Posting process.
The UV Sales Posting code was fixed in UAT1, approved for production, and released in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
Monitoring of Sales Posting Completed was planned for both NV and UV orders.
root_cause: A code issue in the UV Sales Posting process caused rare/random failures to update the sales order status correctly, leaving Sales Posting incomplete at Delivery Pending Approval.
resolution: The UV Sales Posting code was fixed in UAT1, approved for production, and deployed to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_summary: A rare, random code issue in the NV and UV sales posting process prevented the status from being updated to "Sales Posting Completed". The code fix was implemented in UAT1, approved for PROD, and released in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: The issue affected sales posting in both NV and UV tracks.
The status-setting code intermittently failed to update records to "Sales Posting Completed".
The fix was deployed to UAT1 and NV Sales Posting regression testing was performed.
PROD approval was received before the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
The NV and UV sales posting processes were to be monitored during month-end to confirm complete sales posting.
root_cause: Rare, random behavior in the code that sets the sales posting status to "Sales Posting Completed".
resolution: Fixed the status-setting code in UAT1 and deployed the approved fix to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_summary: Delivery Request Approval failed because vehicle information was inconsistent between related orders. The inconsistency was traced to recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834, where the Sales Order vehicle was updated but the corresponding Body Building Order was not updated for Trailer and Forklift cases. Recovery procedures were updated, and a later validation confirmed consistent Vehicle IDs across associated orders in all production environments.
important_findings: The incident occurred during Delivery Request Approval.
The Body Building Order and Sales Order had different vehicle information for Trailer and Forklift cases.
During recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834, the vehicle was updated in the Sales Order but not in the Body Building Order.
The issue was identified as a manual recovery error rather than a system defect.
Validation across all production environments confirmed that Sales Order, Chassis Order, NV Pool Cost Order, Recycle Fee Order, and NV Body Building Order had the same Vehicle ID.
The Recovery Manual was updated to require vehicle-information updates for all related orders during recovery.
root_cause: Manual recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834 updated vehicle information in the Sales Order but omitted the related Body Building Order, causing inconsistent vehicle information and the Delivery Request Approval error.
resolution: Updated the Recovery Manual so vehicle information is updated for all related orders during recovery; associated orders were subsequently validated to have consistent Vehicle IDs across all production environments.

investigation_summary: The reported inability to create a Purchase Order was investigated for the referenced order. Both line items already had Body Building Orders created and mapped, with an existing Purchase Order for each line item. The behavior was confirmed as expected functionality, and the incident was rejected as not a bug.
important_findings: The referenced order contains two line items.
A Body Building Order was created and mapped for both line items.
Purchase Orders already existed for the line items, so another Purchase Order could not be created under the current functionality.
The issue was confirmed as expected behavior and not a product defect.
root_cause: Purchase Orders had already been created for both line items; current functionality does not allow creation of another Purchase Order when one already exists.
resolution: No corrective action was required. The incident was rejected because the system was functioning as designed.

investigation_summary: The incident involved incorrect accounting configuration for Trade-In Loss transactions in NV and UV Trade In processes. The configuration was corrected in UAT1, but UAT8 initially failed for SO# E050016909 and Trade-In PO# F050016910, requiring additional changes. After validation, the fix was released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: For NV and UV Trade In processes, the Trade in Loss Fuso account code must be configured as the debit account code.
For NV and UV Trade In processes, the Bill to account code must be configured as the credit account code.
The initial UAT1 fix passed UAT approval, but UAT8 failed for SO# E050016909 and Trade-In PO# F050016910.
Additional changes were applied in UAT8 before the PROD release.
The incident was released to PROD on 23 January 2025 through the FDP release.
root_cause: Incorrect debit and credit account-code configuration for Trade-In Loss in NV and UV Trade In processes.
resolution: Configured the Trade in Loss Fuso account code as the debit account code and the Bill to account code as the credit account code, applied additional UAT8 changes, and released the fix to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
technical_entities: Trade in Loss Fuso account code

investigation_summary: The KB Department code was blank in JV (SV). Investigation confirmed that the Department code was null because the JCO Branch ID was null when the JCO was created by SADMIN for SR MFTBCFFR-2899. Recovery was completed by correcting the JV data sent to KB, and a countermeasure was planned to populate the Department code for backend-created JCOs for SRs.
important_findings: KB Department code was blank in JV (SV).
The Department code was null because the JCO Branch ID was null.
The JCO was created by SADMIN for SR MFTBCFFR-2899, and SADMIN does not have a branch.
Correct JV data was sent to KB after recovery.
A countermeasure will update the Department code when a JCO is created from the backend for an SR.
root_cause: A JCO created by SADMIN for SR MFTBCFFR-2899 had a null Branch ID because SADMIN does not have a branch, resulting in a null Department code in JV (SV).
resolution: Recovered the data and sent corrected JV data to KB; implement Department code updating for JCOs created from the backend for SRs.

investigation_summary: An AMS bug identified during Project O Migration UAT affected the Expense Invoice report. The issue was fixed and validated in UAT8, where BIP included the S07 line-item name. Because the issue also affected FDP Okayama, Aomori, and Hakodate, the fix was deployed in the 23 January 2025 FDP production release.
important_findings: The incident was identified during Project O Migration UAT.
In UAT8, the Expense Invoice report's BIP included the S07 line-item name after the fix.
The same issue existed in FDP Okayama, Aomori, and Hakodate.
UAT passed before production deployment.
The fix was released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_summary: A newly added Work Order (WO) was not included when updating the Job Card (JC) Work completion date/time because the WO was added after the JC reached "Maintenance Completed" status. Returning the JC to "Maintenance Started" and changing it back to "Maintenance Completed" updated the last WO date, including the added WO. The system was changed in FDP UAT1 so the JC header [Approval Request] action updates the last WO date, and the verified change was released to PROD on February 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue occurred when a WO was added after the JC status was "Maintenance Completed".
The "Set Acceptance Inspection" action is not active for a newly added WO when all existing WOs are already in "Acceptance Inspection" status.
Changing the JC from "Maintenance Completed" to "Maintenance Started" and back to "Maintenance Completed" updates the date of the last WO, including an added WO.
The corrective change updates the last WO date, including added WOs, when the [Approval Request] button is clicked in the JC header.
The change was implemented in FDP UAT1, verified in UAT-1 at JC Close, and released to PROD on February 26, 2025.
root_cause: A WO was added when the JC status was "Maintenance Completed", so the added WO was not included in the last WO date update.
resolution: Modified the JC header [Approval Request] action to update the date of the last WO including added WOs; the change was verified in UAT-1 and deployed to PROD on February 26, 2025.

investigation_summary: Required records were recovered in Hakodate Prod by running the D21A file, which created the associated Planned Pool Cost Procurement orders and Recycle fee orders. The incident was traced to a defect in an ODI package processing TOB files; an ODI patch was applied on 2025-01-19, and automated ODI email monitoring for unprocessed files was implemented. Subsequent incidents MFTBCFFR-3152 and MFTBCFFR-3350 were confirmed to have different causes.
important_findings: All attached records were recovered in Hakodate Prod, including their Planned Pool Cost Procurement orders and Recycle fee orders.
The incident was caused by an issue in the ODI package responsible for TOB file processing.
An ODI patch addressing the package issue was applied on 2025-01-19.
Automated monitoring now sends email notifications from the ODI system when TOB files remain unprocessed.
MFTBCFFR-3152 was caused by data loading to FDP Chugoku, and MFTBCFFR-3350 was caused by a missing D21A file; neither was caused by the ODI failure.
root_cause: A defect in the ODI package used to process TOB files.
resolution: Applied an ODI patch on 2025-01-19 and implemented automated email monitoring for unprocessed TOB files.

investigation_summary: The Revise button was disabled for Quote Revision 2 after the Sales Order associated with Quote Revision 1 was cancelled. Investigation confirmed that the button logic incorrectly picked up the cancelled Sales Order status from the prior quote revision, although no Sales Order was associated with the current quote. The logic was corrected in UAT1 and released to PROD in the 14 January FDP release.
important_findings: Quote Revision 1 had a Sales Order in "Approving" status; when Quote Revision 2 was approved, the prior Sales Order was cancelled and was not synchronized with Quote Revision 2.
The existing Revise button logic evaluated the status of the cancelled Sales Order associated with Quote Revision 1.
Because the evaluated Sales Order status was "Cancelled", the Revise button was disabled for Quote Revision 2.
The intended behavior is to disable the Revise button only when a cancelled Sales Order is associated with the current quote.
UAT1 testing confirmed that the Revise button was active for quotation 1-5SCFIB, revision 2, after the fix.
root_cause: The Revise button logic incorrectly used the cancelled Sales Order associated with the previous quote revision rather than checking for a cancelled Sales Order associated with the current quote.
resolution: Updated the Revise button logic to check whether a cancelled Sales Order is associated with the current quote and keep the button enabled when no Sales Order is associated with the current quote. The fix was deployed to UAT1 and released to PROD in the 14 January FDP release.

root_cause: The customer code associated with the Job card had a null tax exempt flag, which violated the non-nullable tax exempt flag column requirement in Service order BC during quote approval.
resolution: Updated the tax exempt flag to 'N' when it is null for a customer; the fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on December 16.

investigation_summary: For Service Change Orders, Bulk Invoice field SMDO001 was mapped to Last Updated Date. A backend process changed the Last Updated Date after approval, causing SMDO001 to differ from the Posting Date. The mapping was changed to Change Order Completion Date, tested in Okayama UAT-1 with sample order K001287931, and deployed to production on April 14.
important_findings: When a Service Change Order is set to Approved, it becomes read-only and its Last Updated Date normally matches the Posting Date.
For the affected order, a backend process changed the Last Updated Date to November 6, 2024, setting SMDO001 to 20241106.
SMDO001 in Bulk Invoice was originally mapped to Last Updated Date for Service Change Orders.
The corrective mapping uses Change Order Completion Date for SMDO001 instead of Last Updated Date.
Posting Date mapping in Journal Voucher was changed in the same manner.
The change was implemented and tested in Okayama UAT-1, then applied to production on April 14.
root_cause: SMDO001 in Bulk Invoice for Service Change Orders was mapped to Last Updated Date, which could be changed by a backend process after approval.
resolution: Changed the SMDO001 mapping from Last Updated Date to Change Order Completion Date for Service Change Orders, made the same change for Posting Date in Journal Voucher, and deployed the fix to production.

root_cause: During Order Activity creation for activities with an existing Job Card, the system populated Job Card No but set Job Card Type to null. Because Job Card Type is read-only when Job Card No is populated, users could not enter or correct the value.
resolution: Modified Order Activity creation to populate Job Card Type using the JC Type value from the Job Card. The change was validated in UAT1 and released to Production on 16 December.

resolution: An ODI patch was applied to FDP Production environments on 2025-01-19, and automated email monitoring for unprocessed or failed TOB files was implemented. Subsequent monitoring confirmed no further discrepancies caused by the ODI failure.

investigation_summary: The incident involved sales-order cancellation behavior for revised UV Quotes. resolution: Set the Sub-Quote Active Flag to "Y" and then change the status.

investigation_summary: The affected Labors were associated with an External Work Order, which caused a Service PO to be created and categorized as Outsourcing(External). investigation_summary: The quote approval behavior for a local part was investigated in UAT. important_findings: Local parts approval criteria use cost ratio, not discount rate.

The customer LPP res in the discount master is 10%, and sales price is determined from this master.
Cost rate is calculated from Sales Price and Cost price; overwritten Less or price higher than the Sales Price may bypass the approval flow.

root_cause: A data issue in the UAT environment caused the approval flow to behave incorrectly when 1% Less Overwrite was entered.

investigation_summary: For Body Building Order B000160867, Journal Voucher Lines for PO and Consumption Tax were not created because the order amount was 0 after the line item was cancelled. The Consumption Tax field retained tax calculated before cancellation because it is a column-based field and is not updated when a line item is cancelled. This behavior was confirmed as expected, and the incident was closed without a corrective change.
important_findings: Body Building Order B000160867 had an order amount of 0 because its line item was cancelled.
Journal Voucher Lines for PO and its Consumption Tax were not created when the order amount was 0.
The Consumption Tax field stores the total tax from line-item amounts when amounts are entered.
Consumption Tax is not updated when a line item is cancelled because it is a column-based field.
Body Building Orders with cancelled line items can still have the status 'Acceptance Verification Done'.
root_cause: The line item for Body Building Order B000160867 was cancelled, causing the order amount to become 0; therefore, Journal Voucher Lines for PO and Consumption Tax were not created.
resolution: No system correction was required; the behavior was explained as expected and the Jira was closed.

investigation_summary: Approval generation for an Assessment Request did not trigger the expected rule because the requesting user’s primary position was set incorrectly. User D8KOUSTA had both Branch-CS-Staff and Branch NV/UV Sales Staff Position, but Branch-CS-Staff was configured as the primary position. The Assessment Request was reverted to "In Progress" so the user could set Branch NV/UV Sales Staff as primary and regenerate approval.
important_findings: Approval processing evaluates the requesting user’s primary position.
User D8KOUSTA had both Branch-CS-Staff and Branch NV/UV Sales Staff Position.
Branch-CS-Staff was configured as D8KOUSTA’s primary position, preventing the expected approval rule from triggering.
Changing the primary position to Branch NV/UV Sales Staff allows the approval rule to trigger correctly.
The Assessment Request status was changed back to "In Progress" to enable recovery and approval regeneration.
The incident was identified as user mis-operation rather than a system issue.
root_cause: User D8KOUSTA had Branch-CS-Staff configured as the primary position instead of Branch NV/UV Sales Staff, while approval rules use the requester’s primary position.
resolution: Reverted the Assessment Request to "In Progress" and instructed the user to set Branch NV/UV Sales Staff as the primary position before selecting "Generate Approval".

During recovery of MFTBCFFR-2441, opening D21F in the Aomori Prod Inbound folder caused it to no longer be treated as the latest file on the path, so the ODI package detected no file. Recovery was completed in production and Recycle Fee data displayed correctly.
important_findings: The D21F file received on 20 Aug evening was not processed by ODI.
During MFTBCFFR-2441 recovery, D21E files were re-run in the Aomori Prod environment.
D21F was opened while present in the Inbound folder, causing it to no longer be the latest file on the path.
When the ODI package executed, it searched for the latest file and detected no file.
Recovery was completed on prod, and no pending recoveries remained.
root_cause: During D21E recovery for MFTBCFFR-2441 in Aomori Prod, opening the D21F file in the Inbound folder caused it to no longer be recognized as the latest file; the ODI package therefore detected no file and did not process D21F.
resolution: Recovered the data in prod so Recycle Fee data displayed correctly, and added a recovery step to not open additional files present in the Inbound folder.

investigation_summary: Sequence values were reviewed for MF Reservation Number, MF Sequence Number, and MF Shipment Number across Aomori and Hakodate. The RES_NUM and SR_NUM sequences were reset to 1 because no related records existed in either environment. SHIPMENT_NUM was not reset because shipment records had already been created in the Aomori environment.
important_findings: MF Reservation Number uses Reservation Request.X_RES_NUM and Oracle sequence RES_NUM; both Aomori and Hakodate values were 1200 with no records present.
MF Sequence Number uses Assesment Request.X_SEQ_NUM and Oracle sequence SR_NUM; both Aomori and Hakodate values were 6505 with no records present.
MF Shipment Number uses Parts Shipment.X_SHIPMENT_NUM and Oracle sequence SHIPMENT_NUM; its value was 106523 and shipment records existed in Aomori.
RES_NUM and SR_NUM were reset, while SHIPMENT_NUM was intentionally not reset.
resolution: Reset the RES_NUM and SR_NUM Oracle sequences to 1. Do not reset SHIPMENT_NUM because shipment records already exist in the Aomori environment.

resolution: Recovered all chassis orders and restored normal functionality; add AMS process validation to verify that manually updated PR_HELD_POSTN_ID values are correct for the target environment.

resolution: Corrected the garbage LOV and the incorrect Aomori ID, recovered affected Chassis Order records, and verified successful D21E execution in Aomori Prod and Hakodate Prod environments.

investigation_summary: Trade-In synchronization created UV Purchase Orders when revised and approved quotes synchronized to sales orders that were not in an appropriate status. In the NV flow, this occurred after an NV Sales Order approval was rejected; in the UV flow, it occurred while the UV Sales Order remained Pending. The issue was fixed in UAT1, validated with test sales orders, and released to Production in the 13 September FDP release.
important_findings: Revision 2 of NV Quote# 1-UJYUK synchronized after approval and generated PO# F000110671 although the associated order# A000109884 had been rejected.
The Trade-In synchronization process did not account for an NV Sales Order in Rejected status.
For NV Quotes, revising and approving a quote after rejecting the generated NV Sales Order triggered creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In.
For UV Quotes, revising and approving a quote triggered creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In while the UV Sales Order remained Pending.
The fix was validated in UAT1 using NV SO#A001268431 and UV SO#E001268440 before Production deployment.
root_cause: Trade-In synchronization generated UV Purchase Orders without properly accounting for the status of the associated sales order, including NV Sales Orders in Rejected status and UV Sales Orders in Pending status.
resolution: The issue was fixed in UAT1 and released to Production in the 13 September FDP release.

investigation_summary: A Delivery Request creation error occurred when purchase orders associated with a vehicle were not all mapped. Investigation found that a previously cancelled assessment for the same vehicle set a flag to 'Y' on all mapped POs; this flag was handled during sales order mapping but was not checked during Delivery Request creation. The Delivery Request logic was corrected, validated in UAT1 on AR# H000030031, and released to Prod.
important_findings: A cancelled assessment sets a flag to 'Y' for all POs mapped to the associated vehicle.
For a subsequent assessment with the same VIN#, only the newest purchase orders are mapped in the sales order.
Delivery Request creation did not check the cancellation-related PO flag, causing the error that all purchase orders were not mapped.
The condition was fixed for Delivery Request creation and deployed to UAT1.
UAT passed on AR# H000030031, and the fix was released to Prod.
root_cause: Delivery Request creation did not check the 'Y' flag set on POs mapped to a vehicle when a prior assessment was cancelled, resulting in validation that all purchase orders were not mapped.
resolution: Updated Delivery Request creation logic to check the cancellation-related PO flag; the change passed UAT1 validation and was released to Prod.

important_findings: The accounts receivable update screen displays applicable values from the customer master record.
NV responsible details are shown only when "Module open Flag NV" is marked True during "Update AR".
When the NV module flag is unchecked, the system sets the responsible values to null and makes them read-only.
The same responsible-display logic applies to UV, PT, and SV Responsible.

root_cause: The responsible information was not displayed because "Module open Flag NV" was unchecked; this intentionally nulls and makes the NV Responsible values read-only.
resolution: Implemented changes were validated in UAT-1 and released to Prod; users must set "Module open Flag NV" to True during "Update AR" to display NV responsible details.

A corrected business file updated the employee data, and a newly created SR reflected the correct values and would populate the correct Responsible shop code in account master.
important_findings: The incorrect Responsible shop code was sourced from employee details during Service Request creation.
The employee record had shop code 7203 for the Default organization; the expected shop code was 00.
The initial employee-code file contained an incorrect Location code.
A second file received from the business corrected the employee master data.
A newly created SR reflected the correct values and, upon completion, would update account master with the correct Responsible shop code.
Employee master reruns will be monitored, with validation of the Location code.
root_cause: Incorrect Location code in the initial employee-code file caused an erroneous employee master update, resulting in Responsible shop code 7203 being selected instead of 00.
resolution: The business provided a corrected employee-code file that corrected the employee master data. A new Service Request was created with correct values and would populate the correct Responsible shop code in account master upon completion; future employee master reruns will be monitored for Location code accuracy.

investigation_summary: No employee was assigned to the Branch-CS-Head position in Division 10, causing no user to appear for that role in approval flow history. Analysis of the April 1, 2024 employee master execution on Prod found that Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, so D8TMASAA received the Branch-Service-Mgr role instead. The position mapping was corrected and the employee master file was re-executed, assigning D8TMASAA to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
important_findings: D8ISHDA1 was assigned to the Branch-Head position, not the Branch-CS-Head position, in Okayama Higashi Branch with 10 Dealer Code.
The April 1, 2024 employee master file execution removed D8TOTAKE from the Branch-CS-Head position and intended to assign D8TMASAA.
The employee master file operation for D8TMASAA was specified as "Assign" although the investigation stated it should have been "Change".
Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, resulting in D8TMASAA being assigned Branch-Service-Mgr rather than Branch-CS-Head.
Because no employee held Branch-CS-Head in Division 10, no user appeared for that role in approval flow history.
root_cause: Position Type Mapping incorrectly mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr during employee master processing, leaving no employee assigned to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
resolution: Corrected the position mapping on Prod and re-executed the employee master file for D8TMASAA, which correctly assigned the user to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.

investigation_summary: The FDP PBI Settlement Date for change orders was not correctly sourced after SC SIEBEL changes to "Change Order Completion Date/Time". Investigation found that the SC Siebel changes under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel, requiring an AMS CR on the FDP Okayama Siebel side and a corresponding FDP PBI mapping update. The fix was validated in FDP UAT and deployed to FDP PROD on July 20, 2024.
important_findings: SC SIEBEL changes for "Change Order Completion Date/Time" under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel.
FDP PBI Settlement Date for change orders needed to source the "Change Order Completion date" column from Siebel.
An AMS CR was required for FDP Okayama Siebel in addition to the PBI change.
The PROD release added a new column to the ODI mapping and required a full load of Daily Load Plan.
The fix was verified in FDP UAT for reports SV_101, 1_10A, 1_12A, and 1_15A, and the issue could not be reproduced in UAT after the change.
root_cause: The "Change Order Completion Date/Time" changes made in SC SIEBEL were not reflected in FDP Siebel, so FDP PBI could not source the correct Settlement Date for change orders.
resolution: Applied the required FDP Okayama Siebel AMS CR and updated the FDP PBI ODI mapping to source change-order Settlement Date from the Siebel "Change Order Completion date" column; performed a full Daily Load Plan load and deployed the fix to FDP PROD.

investigation_summary: PBI 1_10A Report populated Settlement Date from the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date, causing dates to appear for Change Orders that were still in progress. Analysis confirmed that the PBI logic differs from Siebel, where the relevant field is Change Order Completion date and only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date. A change to PBI SV_1_10A was identified as necessary, and an AMS-CR was requested.
important_findings: The settlement date in PBI was populated using the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date.
For JC# I000097002 / Change Order# K000121869, LAST_UPD changed from March 18 to March 19 after an update, and PBI reflected March 19.
Using LAST_UPD causes in-progress Change Orders, including recently created and unapproved Change Orders, to receive a settlement date in PBI.
Siebel uses Change Order Completion date for the settlement date requirement.
Only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date and be displayed in PBI reports.
PBI SV_1_10A requires logic changes to align with Siebel.
root_cause: PBI 1_10A mapped Settlement Date to the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date instead of the Siebel Change Order Completion date, resulting in settlement dates for in-progress, unapproved Change Orders.
resolution: An AMS-CR was requested to implement Settlement Date logic changes in PBI SV_1_10A to align with Siebel and populate settlement dates only for approved Change Orders.

root_cause: The system behavior did not meet the newly requested requirement to prevent creation and KB linkage of cycle count data when the Siebel counted flag was N.
resolution: Implemented the AMS CR in UAT1, deleted the affected record sets with BDZO007 null as recovery, validated batch processing, and released the approved change to PROD on 7 June.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned changing Adjustment Amount values in Siebel. Directly changing and saving the Adjustment Amount on an existing record was identified as an incorrect operation. Users must end-date the old record and create a new record with the revised amount and corresponding effective dates.
important_findings: Directly changing and saving Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record is an incorrect operation.
The old record must have its Effective To date populated before the Adjustment Amount is changed.
A new record must be created for the revised Adjustment Amount.
The new record must have the appropriate Effective From date populated.
The required handling was classified as an operation rule rather than a system issue.
root_cause: Users attempted to directly change and save Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record instead of end-dating the old record and creating a new effective-dated record.
resolution: Users were instructed to populate Effective To on the old record, then create a new record with the updated Adjustment Amount and an appropriate Effective From date.

investigation_summary: Journal Voucher creation failed in Sales Posting and for Individual Purchase Order B000060944 because the IBOS shipment workflow did not meet the existing trigger conditions. The change was developed and tested in UAT, approved after UAT validation, and released to Prod on 8 March 2024.
important_findings: Sales Posting did not trigger a Journal Voucher when Body Building Order-IBOS was not Shipped, even though the related Sales Order status was Acceptance Verification done.
Individual Purchase Order B000060944 did not create a Journal Voucher because the Inbound Process of IBOS-Shipment could not trigger the JV.
The revised Sales Posting logic triggers a Journal Voucher when Body Building Order-IBOS is either Shipped or Acceptance Verification done.
The GR case was handled so that the Journal Voucher is triggered when the status is Shipped.
The change was tested in UAT, UAT passed, and the release was deployed to Prod on 8 March 2024.
root_cause: Journal Voucher trigger logic required Body Building Order-IBOS to be Shipped and did not handle the Acceptance Verification done status or the IBOS-Shipment inbound process scenario.
resolution: Updated Journal Voucher trigger logic so Sales Posting triggers for Body Building Order-IBOS statuses Shipped or Acceptance Verification done, and handled the GR case to trigger the Journal Voucher when status is Shipped; released to Prod on 8 March 2024.

investigation_summary: A Service round-down change exposed that BIP reports did not handle negative quotation amounts. BIP in Run Report changed correctly for the Delivery Slip Sheet, but Direct Print BIP for the Quote Sheet and Delivery Slip Sheet was reported as not changed.
The item was approved for PROD and released through the FDP release.
root_cause: BIP reports did not handle negative quotation amounts introduced by the Service round-down change because negative test cases were overlooked.
resolution: Relevant BIP changes were made to handle negative quotation amounts, the Delivery Slip was corrected, and the item was released to Production.

investigation_summary: Purchase type values were incorrect or null in PBI reports because of both report LOV inconsistencies and a Siebel assessment update defect. In Siebel, Assessment purpose remained editable after an assessment reached "Assessment Completed"; cancelling a purpose change with Esc could leave the associated purchase type as null. The fix was validated in UAT1, released to Prod, and affected Prod records were recovered; the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was subsequently rectified.
important_findings: UV_2B had different LOVs between PBI and SIEBEL, causing purchase-type discrepancies for records H000000801, H000002802, and H000003406.
UV_2_01_2_02 did not display a value in the SIEBEL UI, so the value was not reflected in the PBI report.
Assessment purpose was editable when assessment status was "Assessment Completed".
If a user began changing Assessment purpose and pressed Esc to restore the prior value, the UI restored the purpose but set the assessment purchase type to null.
UAT initially showed "UV Trade-in" for purchase classifications in 2-01, 2-02, 2-05, 2-06, and 2-01(History), rather than "Magotori".
After the Prod release, the Purchase Type filter in 2-01 and 2-02 incorrectly included "SV reception category" LOV values; this was rectified.
root_cause: In Siebel, Assessment purpose could be edited after an assessment was "Assessment Completed". Cancelling an in-progress Assessment purpose change with Esc restored the displayed purpose but left the associated purchase type set to null. Separate PBI and SIEBEL LOV differences also caused UV_2B purchase-type discrepancies.
resolution: The issue was fixed and validated in UAT1, then released to Prod. Affected Prod records were recovered, PBI reports were refreshed, and the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was rectified.

investigation_summary: An AMS CR was implemented and validated in the UAT environment, including an FDP PBI (UAT) refresh and test-data verification. Post-PROD verification confirmed that columns were removed and there were no duplicated Row ID values.

The MEMO field is a manual-entry field.
The MEMO field was made editable for the affected position type.

investigation_summary: A deleted line item in UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) caused a line-number mismatch between the quote and the UV Sales Order created through the auto order button. During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), the mismatch deleted order line items and child records, causing the sync to fail when updating Line Item# 5. The corrective change disabled deletion from the Line Items tab while retaining deletion of Liability Insurance through the Taxes and Expenses tab; the change was validated in UAT1 and deployed to PROD.
important_findings: Deleting Line Item# 4, Expense (S07), from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) removed Line Item# 4 from the Backend Column.
The UV Sales Order created through the auto order button still contained Line Item# 4 for Recycle Fee(YN5Z).
During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), Line Item# 4 and its child records were deleted from the order, which also deleted Line Item# 5.
The sync failed when UV Sales Quote Line Item# 5 attempted to update the already deleted UV Sales Order Line Item# 5.
The FDP fix disables the Delete button on the Line Items tab; Liability Insurance can only be deleted from the Taxes and Expenses tab.
The change passed UAT1 validation and was implemented on PROD.
root_cause: Deletion of Line Item# 4 from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) created a Backend Column line-number mismatch with the UV Sales Order, which retained Line Item# 4 after auto-order creation. Synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3) then deleted order lines and child records, including Line Item# 5, causing the subsequent Line Item# 5 update to fail.
resolution: Disabled the Delete button on the Line Items tab and restricted deletion of Liability Insurance to the Taxes and Expenses tab. The change was implemented in UAT1, passed UAT, and was deployed to PROD.

investigation_summary: Rejected and incomplete used-car sales orders appeared in reports because users manually populated date fields used by report filters. UV SO# E000087121 appeared in the Order Report despite Rejected status because Approval Date was manually entered; UV SO# E000037797 appeared in the sales report because Delivery Completion Approved Date was manually entered. The incident was classified as user misoperation and closed with no system fix required.
important_findings: Approval Date is normally auto-populated when an approver approves a Sales Order, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000087121 before approval was requested.
The Order Report filters approved orders based on Approval Date, so UV SO# E000087121 appeared even after rejection by the Branch Head.
Delivery Completion Approved Date is normally populated when the Delivery Request is completed, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000037797.
The Sales Order Reporting screen filters sales-posting-completed orders based on Delivery Completion Approved Date, causing UV SO# E000037797 to appear in the sales report.
Making the two date fields Read Only was confirmed as possible and not expected to affect functionality, but no change was implemented because the issue was handled through user operation.
root_cause: User misoperation: manual entry of Approval Date and Delivery Completion Approved Date caused orders to satisfy date-based report filters regardless of their actual approval or delivery-completion status.
resolution: No system fix was implemented. The incident was handled through user operation and the Jira was rejected/closed.

investigation_summary: Parts Sales Orders created from the Part dealer sale order screen did not populate fixed tax rates because a Parts Quote is not required in that flow. The implementation was updated on UAT-1 to store the fixed tax rate based on the tax type of the part at both header and detail-line level. The change was validated and released to Production on 9th February.
important_findings: Parts Sales Orders normally receive the fixed tax rate from Parts Quote.
The Part dealer sale order screen can create a Part Sales Order without a Parts Quote, leaving the fixed tax rate unpopulated.
Detail lines initially did not store the tax rate fixed value when a part was added.
The fixed tax rate was updated to populate from the tax type of the added part number in detail lines on UAT-1.
A shipment drilldown issue was also resolved during the UAT-1 update.
UAT-1 testing was confirmed successful before Production release.
root_cause: The Part dealer sale order screen creates Part Sales Orders without requiring a Parts Quote, but the fixed tax rate population depended on the Parts Quote.
resolution: Updated the logic to store the fixed tax rate based on the tax type of the added part number, including detail lines; resolved the shipment drilldown issue; validated on UAT-1 and released to Production.

investigation_summary: Records created after January 1, 2024 were not visible in Power BI reports because a report date filter limited orders to January 1, 2018 through January 1, 2024. The filter had been introduced to reduce data load time. The end date was changed to 2050 for PBI reports using a date range, and the reports displayed the previously missing records after refresh; the fix was confirmed.
important_findings: A Power BI report filter restricted order data to the period from January 1, 2018 to January 1, 2024.
The missing records were created after January 1, 2024 and were therefore excluded by the filter.
The date range was originally configured to reduce report data load time.
FDP Okayama Prod went live in August 2023; an earlier proposal was to use a range from August 2023 to August 2028.
The end year was updated to 2050 for PBI reports that use a date range.
Previously missing records appeared after the next Power BI report refresh.
root_cause: A date filter in the Power BI reports excluded orders created after January 1, 2024.
resolution: Changed the date-range end year to 2050 for applicable PBI reports and refreshed the reports.

PaymentDueDate was calculated as February 31, 2024 because of a code issue.
The fix was deployed and tested in UAT.
Validation was completed and the fix was released to Prod.
root_cause: Incorrect code logic combined MF Customer Name Print1 with MF Shop Code Name for Individual Invoice Customer Name and incorrectly calculated PaymentDueDate.
resolution: Corrected the code, deployed and tested the fix in UAT, then released it to Prod after validation and approval.

investigation_summary: PO Creation Outbound interface processing experienced duplicate triggers after CPI system timeouts caused Siebel to retry. Recovery was completed by updating affected POs with D2S SO numbers and PO dates, reprocessing allocation and shipment where required, and setting the header status to Ordered. The timeout parameter was increased from 180 to 300 seconds, after which the issue was reported resolved and monitoring was performed.
important_findings: CPI system timeouts triggered the retry mechanism in Siebel, resulting in multiple triggers despite evidence that only one trigger was initially sent from the Siebel side.
The retry mechanism was configured for other Outbound Interfaces and was reported to be operating without issues.
The PO Creation Outbound interface timeout parameter was increased from 180 to 300 seconds.
Affected POs required D2S SO number and PO date updates, allocation reprocessing, shipment creation for BANS, and header status changes to Ordered.
All recoveries were completed before the incident was closed.
root_cause: A timeout from the CPI system caused the Siebel retry mechanism to send multiple triggers for the PO Creation Outbound interface.
resolution: Increased the PO Creation Outbound interface timeout from 180 to 300 seconds and completed recovery of affected POs by reprocessing allocation and shipment as needed, then setting header status to Ordered.

investigation_summary: Profit values differed between PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 because repair fee cost was sourced from UV Inventory under the recorded transaction sequence. A UV Body Building PO was created from UV Inventory before sales posting status, while the corresponding UV Sales Quote had a repair fee cost of zero. No corrective system change was documented; the ticket was requested to be closed after the cause was identified.
important_findings: The issue was not caused by Siebel or the Sales order reporting screen calculation.
PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 fetch repair fee cost from UV Inventory.
A UV Sales Quote was created before a UV Body Building PO was created from UV Inventory.
Because the UV Body Building PO was created before sales posting status, the repair fee cost was sourced from UV Inventory.
The repair fee cost value in the Sales quote was zero, causing the reported values to differ.
root_cause: The UV Body Building PO was created from UV Inventory before sales posting status, causing PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 to use the repair fee cost from UV Inventory while the Sales quote value was zero.

investigation_summary: UV Sales Order Reporting had not been updated to match the Sales Order logic introduced by CR "FDP CR UV Inventory_01 Individual Cost for Inventory Repair". Repair fees were not deducted from the sales price, causing 70,000 to be reported instead of 64,300, and UAT also identified missing cost-field calculation in Sales Report and Order Interk Rerpot. The logic and PBI were corrected on UAT1, passed UAT, and were released to PROD without reported issues.
important_findings: UV Sales Order Reporting did not deduct the 5,700 repair fee from the 70,000 sales price.
The expected reported value after repair-fee deduction was 64,300.
Initial UAT showed profit was correct, but cost was not included in the Cost field calculation in Sales Report and Order Interk Rerpot.
PBI initially had no data and was corrected on UAT1.
UAT passed after the fixes, and the PROD check reported no problem.
root_cause: UV Sales Order Reporting logic was not updated to align with the Sales Order changes from CR "FDP CR UV Inventory_01 Individual Cost for Inventory Repair", resulting in repair fees not being deducted and incomplete cost-field calculation.
resolution: Corrected the UV Sales Order Reporting and PBI logic on UAT1 to deduct repair fees and include cost-field calculation; after UAT approval, the changes were released to PROD.
technical_entities: FDP CR UV Inventory_01 Individual Cost for Inventory Repair
