investigation_summary: BIP generation failed because the Tax Rate column in NV Sales Order was set to null. The Generate Approval logic queried Consumption Tax Master using the Sales Order Last Contract Date for FDP-Okayama orders with an acknowledgment date earlier than the current date; no matching tax-master record was found. The Consumption Tax Master start date was changed in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version, allowing tax percent to be set correctly.
important_findings: Tax percent in Sales Order originates from the sales quote but is recalculated by logic behind the Generate Approval button.
For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the logic queries Consumption Tax Master using Start Date <= Last Contract Date <= End Date.
In FDP-Okayama, the acknowledgment date was 2020/11/30 and affected orders had a Last Contract Date earlier than the Consumption Tax Master start date of 2023/07/29.
The Consumption Tax Master query returned zero records, causing tax percent and the NV Sales Order Tax Rate column to be set to null.
The same behavior was reproduced in SC UAT1 using Order A025013709 with Last Contract Date 2018/01/31 earlier than Start Date 2020/11/30, resulting in Order Sheet BIP failure.
The logic was confirmed to be the same as in SC.
root_cause: The Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama was later than the affected Sales Order Last Contract Date. For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the Generate Approval logic queried tax records by Last Contract Date and returned no result, setting tax percent to null and causing BIP generation failure.
resolution: Changed the Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version: 2019/10/01.

investigation_summary: Approval flow was not generated when a user with the UV_Mgr position attempted to submit approval requests for UV sales orders with sales type '3rd Party Auction Sales' or 'FUSO Auction Sales'. investigation_summary: Configuration was reported as consistent across UAT1, RT2, and Prod. Verification in Prod confirmed that a UV BB PO can be cancelled when its status is Ordered. The issue was not reproducible in Okayama Prod, so the incident was closed/rejected.
important_findings: Configuration was the same across UAT1, RT2, and Prod.

investigation_summary: For PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS, the Journal Voucher account item code was determined using the Vehicle product class derived from VIN. The corrected logic fetches the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen.

root_cause: The Vehicle product class was derived from VIN; when VIN was null, it defaulted to Others, resulting in selection of the class-Others account item code in the Journal Voucher.
resolution: Updated the logic to fetch the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen instead of VIN, then tested it in Uat and released it to Prod.
technical_entities: PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS

investigation_summary: Debit department code was missing for certain Journal Voucher entries because the Responsible Service Shop Code was null for account 1000004435. root_cause: Responsible Service Shop Code was null for account 1000004435, causing the mapped debit department code to be null for Parts Sales Consumption Excl and Parts Sales Consumption Tax in Journal Voucher.

investigation_summary: The Parts Quote estimation action failed because the user set the record Active flag to N before attempting estimation. An inactive record cannot be updated, so the status could not change and the system displayed "The record in not editable". The behavior was confirmed in UAT1 and is existing functionality consistent with SC; the incident was rejected as no product defect was identified.
important_findings: Parts sub-quotes created from the NV sub-quotes screen have a null branch Id, so no branch name is displayed on the Parts Quote screen.
Setting the Active flag to N makes the Parts Quote record inactive and non-editable.
The Estimate button cannot update an inactive record; therefore, the Parts Quote status does not change.
With the Active flag set to Y, the estimation process works correctly.
The behavior was replicated and confirmed in UAT1 and is consistent with SC.
root_cause: The user set the Parts Quote Active flag to N before estimation, making the record inactive and preventing the Estimate action from updating its status.
resolution: Set the Active flag to Y before clicking the Estimate button. No system change was required; the incident was rejected as expected business functionality.

investigation_summary: A validation mismatch occurred when clicking the Fullfill button because FDP used logic different from SC. The FDP validation was changed to match SC, tested successfully on UAT1 using Parts Internal Order# M001240322, and released to Prod on 15 Dec.

root_cause: FDP contained validation code/configuration that differed from SC for the Fullfill button quantity validation.

investigation_summary: UV Body Building Purchase Orders existed for the affected Additionaly body line items but were not mapped to the UV Sales order and therefore were not visible in the UI. When a user unmaps a PO through the UI, the PO parent sales order ID is set to null.

investigation_summary: Approval routing for Quote and Job Card was using the total of all Non-chargeable costs when a Free Cost line item was present, causing approval escalation up to HQ for JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71. The required logic was to evaluate only the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the applicable line item type: 42 (Free Cost) or 45 (Reworking). Separate total fields were created, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.
important_findings: For JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71, the presence of a Free Cost line item caused all Non-chargable values to be summed to 19190, exceeding the 10000 approval threshold.
The approval flow must use Non Chargeable Cost Total for Line Item Type 42 only when Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) exists.
The same line-item-specific calculation logic is required for Line Item Type 45 (Reworking).
The existing configuration behaved the same in UAT and required both Siebel configuration and approval flow changes.
New Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields were created for Line Item Type 42 and Line Item Type 45 and used for Quote and Job Card approver selection.
FDP UAT-1 confirmed that approvers were judged using only the Free Cost total before PROD deployment.
root_cause: The approval rule summed all Non-chargable costs whenever a Free Cost line item was present, rather than calculating and using the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the relevant line item type only.
resolution: Created separate Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields for Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) and Line Item Type 45 (Reworking), updated Quote and Job Card approver selection to use the applicable line-item-specific total, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.

investigation_summary: Employee records were being interfaced to KB despite the relevant data having been last updated in August. Investigation confirmed that records with the same employee code could include active and inactive entries, with HMCP004 identifying the active/inactive status in the outbound file. The interface logic was changed so records are sent to KB only when the employee master is updated, and duplicate employee-code records use the latest updated record. The fix was tested in UAT and released to Prod on December 15.
important_findings: The reported records were not duplicate records in the initial assessment: one employee record was inactive and another was active.
HMCP004 identifies whether an employee record is active or inactive and was sent in the file accordingly.
The incident required clarification of why data last updated in August was sent to the accounting magistrate on the prior day.
The interface to KB was changed to send affected records only when the employee master is updated.
For duplicate employee code records, the most recently updated record is interfaced to KB.
The fix was validated in UAT before release to Prod.
root_cause: The KB interface logic did not restrict outbound records to employee-master updates and did not select the latest updated record when employee codes were duplicated.
resolution: Updated the KB interface so it sends affected records only when the employee master is updated and selects the latest updated record for duplicate employee codes; tested in UAT and deployed to Prod on December 15.

The validation affected the function to relate an already Stocked Vehicle to Opportunity and was identified as not being a stated Opportunity BRD requirement.

resolution: Modified the logic so the Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag is set to 'N' when a vehicle is set to status 'Stocked-In' and sub-status 'Available'; the change passed UAT and was deployed to Prod.

investigation_summary: Recovery data for September and October required correction before release to Prod. Validation found that BZDO008 was generated using D/N price * Qty for price revision, while KB processes price revision and cycle count with the same logic. The UAT fix changed BZDO008 generation for both workflows and was validated before release to Prod.
important_findings: BZDO008 initially showed D/N price * Qty for price revision data.
KB processes cycle count and price revision using the same logic.
BZDO008 must contain D/N price only for both cycle count and price revision.
Records must not be created when D/N price is 0, because they cause an error on the KB side.
Price revision recovery data must use the same Posting date for all records; September 30 data must not include an October 1 Posting date.
The fix was completed and tested in UAT, approved, and released to Prod.
root_cause: BZDO008 generation for price revision used D/N price * Qty and allowed records with D/N price of 0, which was incompatible with the shared KB processing logic used for cycle count and price revision.
resolution: Updated the UAT and Prod program for both cycle count and price revision so BZDO008 is created with D/N price only, records with D/N price of 0 are not created, and recovery-data Posting dates are consistent across records. The change was tested in UAT and released to Prod.

investigation_summary: A mismatch was identified between Sales Price calculations displayed in Siebel UI and generated Bulk Invoice data. Siebel rounded the Sales Price before multiplying by quantity, while Bulk Invoice calculations used unrounded decimal values. The Bulk Invoice rounding logic was corrected, validated, and released to Production.
important_findings: Siebel rounded Sales Price before multiplying it by Qty.
Bulk Invoice calculated using Sales Price decimal digits without first rounding.
The differing calculation sequences caused a mismatch between Siebel UI and the Bulk file.
Rounding was fixed in Bulk Invoice.
The updated data was validated and the fix was deployed to Prod.
root_cause: Bulk Invoice did not round Sales Price before multiplying by Qty, unlike the calculation performed in Siebel.
resolution: Updated Bulk Invoice calculation logic to round Sales Price before quantity multiplication; the fix was validated and released to Production.

investigation_summary: The Credit Department Code mapping on JV for Parts Change Orders was reviewed and updated. The mapping was changed from the creating user’s 2 Digit Dealer Code to the parent order’s Inventory name. The change was implemented in UAT, validated by the requester, and released to Prod.
important_findings: The previous JV mapping used the 2 Digit Dealer Code of the user who created the Parts Change Order.
The required mapping source for Credit Department Code is the parent order's Inventory name on JV.
The mapping change was implemented on UAT and confirmed as working.
The validated change was released to Prod.
root_cause: Credit Department Code on JV was mapped to the creating user's 2 Digit Dealer Code instead of the parent order's Inventory name.
resolution: Updated the JV Credit Department Code mapping to use the parent order's Inventory name, tested it in UAT, and released it to Prod.

investigation_summary: The incident involved missing D21A file receipt for VIN# FK72FY-615070. Investigation identified that the relevant date is updated by reading TCB01 and linked the behavior to Defect MFTBCFFR-1619. important_findings: The D21A file had not been received for VIN# FK72FY-615070.
The date is updated by reading TCB01.
The issue was related to Defect MFTBCFFR-1619.

root_cause: The date update behavior when reading TCB01 was related to Defect MFTBCFFR-1619.
resolution: Fixed Defect MFTBCFFR-1619, deployed the fix to Prod, and scheduled the TCB01 file package on Prod.

investigation_summary: When a quote was revised with a planned delivery date earlier than the current date, trade-in consumption tax was set to null. The configuration was changed in UAT so the value is set to 0 instead of null, validated using Quote# 1-3Z5VZN rev.2, and released to PROD. Impacted records were extracted and recovered after the production release.
important_findings: The existing revised-quote functionality set trade-in consumption tax to null when the planned delivery date was less than today.
The UAT configuration was changed so trade-in consumption tax is set to 0 rather than null for planned delivery dates less than today.
The UAT change was validated with Quote# 1-3Z5VZN rev.2.
The change was released to PROD on 2023-11-06.
Affected production records were extracted and recovery was completed.
root_cause: Existing revised-quote configuration set trade-in consumption tax to null when the planned delivery date was less than today.
resolution: Changed the configuration to set trade-in consumption tax to 0 instead of null for revised quotes with planned delivery dates earlier than today, released the change to PROD, and recovered affected records.

investigation_summary: The "Ordered SO revised conditions" report initially returned Sales Orders based on the revised Quote last Approval Date, as defined in BRD of CR NV-08. A requirement clarification established that Sales Orders in "Pending" and "Pending Approval" status must not be returned by this filter. The required change was implemented and validated in UAT, then released to PROD.
important_findings: The existing functionality selected Sales Orders based on the revised Quote last Approval Date.
For the "Ordered SO revised conditions" report, Sales Orders with status "Pending" or "Pending Approval" must be excluded from the filter results.
The change was implemented in UAT and confirmed under reference A001235943.
The validated change was released to PROD.
root_cause: The report filter did not exclude Sales Orders in "Pending" and "Pending Approval" status.
resolution: Updated the "Ordered SO revised conditions" report filtering logic in UAT to exclude "Pending" and "Pending Approval" Sales Orders, validated the change, and released it to PROD.

investigation_summary: Service consumption-tax rounding in UAT-1 was not covered by the existing BRD rounding logic, which applied only to Parts and NV/UV. A temporary Siebel change was implemented to hard-code the calculated Round Type to round down. The change was validated in UAT1, approved, and released to PROD on 31 October.
important_findings: Existing rounding logic was configured for Parts and NV/UV, not for Service.
Service functionality did not reference the consumption tax master.
The Service change required directly modifying the hard-coded Round Type calculation in Siebel.
The requested rounding behavior was changed to round down.
UAT1 validation completed successfully and the change was approved for PROD deployment.
root_cause: Service was excluded from the existing consumption-tax rounding requirements and logic; its functionality did not reference the consumption tax master, while rounding was configured only for Parts and NV/UV.
resolution: Hard-coded the Siebel Round Type calculation for Service to round down, validated the change in UAT1, and deployed it to PROD in the 31 October release.

investigation_summary: APIs failed after the oneAPI KONG Gateway server experienced an unplanned reboot on 16-Oct-2023. The reboot caused Docker services/containers responsible for backend API connectivity to fail. Service was restored by starting all affected Docker containers, and preventive monitoring actions were initiated.
important_findings: The oneAPI KONG Gateway server rebooted unexpectedly on 16-Oct-2023.
The reboot caused Docker services/containers responsible for API connections to fail.
Failed Docker Gateway containers prevented backend API hits and caused user errors.
All affected Docker containers were started to restore API functionality.
Siebel raised the unplanned reboot concern with Azure support.
The KONG Gateway server is being added to FORCEMON monitoring for real-time server-health alerts.
root_cause: An unplanned reboot of the oneAPI KONG Gateway server caused the Docker services/containers responsible for API connectivity to fail.
resolution: Started all Docker containers/services connected to backend API hits, restoring API functionality.

resolution: Updated SMDO056 to map Approved person of customer Field instead of Quote Approver Field for BIP Monthly Invoice, tested the change in UAT, and released it to Production.

resolution: Removed the 5SCId filter from the Sales Order Change list applet, validated the change in UAT1/UAT, and implemented it in PROD.

investigation_summary: A posting-date mismatch occurred for Job Card I000011402 after the job card was re-edited without any amount changes and closed again on a later date. No new journal voucher was created during re-edit because the Job Card amount was unchanged, while the existing journal voucher retained the first closure date. Recovery was completed under SR MFTBCFFR-1887, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Re-editing the Job Card without changing its amount did not create a new journal voucher.
The journal voucher had been created when the Job Card was first closed, so its posting date remained the first completion date.
Closing the re-edited Job Card on a later date changed the Job Card settlement date.
The differing journal voucher posting date and Job Card settlement date caused the mismatch.
Re-edit functionality was disabled.
Recovery for Job Card I000011402 was completed in SR MFTBCFFR-1887.
root_cause: The Job Card was re-edited without an amount change and closed on a later date. Because no new journal voucher was created for an unchanged Job Card amount, the existing journal voucher retained the first completion date while the Job Card settlement date changed.
resolution: Recovery of Job Card I000011402 was completed in SR MFTBCFFR-1887.

investigation_summary: The D2S Invoice Mismatch process incorrectly set the match flag to N when comparing "Sales Order Item" with "D2S Sales Order Line#". The fields were configured as Text, preventing proper comparison. Their data types were changed to NUMBER, validated in UAT, and released to Prod.
important_findings: D2S Invoice Mismatch compares "Sales Order Item" with "D2S Sales Order Line#".
A mismatch between these fields sets the match flag to N.
The compared fields were configured with the Text data type, causing improper comparison.
Changing both fields to the NUMBER data type resolved the issue in UAT.
The change was approved and released to Prod.
root_cause: "Sales Order Item" and "D2S Sales Order Line#" were configured as Text, causing improper comparison in D2S Invoice Mismatch.
resolution: Changed the data type of "Sales Order Item" and "D2S Sales Order Line#" to NUMBER, validated the fix in UAT, and released it to Prod.

investigation_summary: The Activity for JC# I000008899 in Prod was created from a Service Effort Line Item of a UV Quote. The Service Quote remained In Progress because the user selected the Job Card from the Activity after creating it, rather than creating the Job Card from the Internal Work Request. The workflow was confirmed to operate correctly in UAT and Prod according to UV-16 CR, and the issue was rejected as user-miss operation.
important_findings: Activities created from UV Inventory support internal approval of SV-Quote through Process #2, implemented under FDP CR UV-15.
Activities created from UV Quote follow Process #1 from the start of FDP.
JC# I000008899 Activity in Prod was created from a Service Effort Line Item of a UV Quote.
The Service Quote stayed In Progress because the Job Card was selected from the Activity instead of being created from the Internal Work Request.
The UV-16 CR business process was verified as working correctly in both UAT and Prod environments.
root_cause: User-miss operation: the Job Card was created separately and then mapped to the Activity, instead of creating the Job Card from the Activity/Internal Work Request workflow.
resolution: No product change was required. The issue was rejected after confirming that the UV-16 CR workflow operates correctly in UAT and Prod; users must create the Job Card through the intended Internal Work Request/Activity process.

investigation_summary: Following the JCT Implementation, Trade In Consumption Tax logic was updated on the Quote header in NV and UV. Existing Quote records without a Trade In vehicle had null Trade In Consumption Tax values, causing dependent calculation fields to be null. A recovery updated null values to 0, after which users could output invoices from AKB with correct values.
important_findings: JCT Implementation updated Trade In Consumption Tax logic on the Quote header in NV and UV.
Quote records created after the JCT release were handled by the updated logic.
Existing Quote records with no Trade In vehicle had null Trade In Consumption Tax values.
Fields whose calculations depended on Trade In Consumption Tax were also null.
Recovery changed affected Trade In Consumption Tax values from null to 0.
Invoices could be output from AKB with correct values after the recovery.
root_cause: Quote records without a Trade In vehicle had null Trade In Consumption Tax values, which caused dependent calculation fields to become null.
resolution: Recovered all affected Quote records by changing Trade In Consumption Tax values from null to 0.

investigation_summary: Actual Labour Hour values in Power BI were initially discrepant because the column was aggregated differently from the SC (1-10 report). After removing the aggregation, a further issue was identified: cancelled work order labour hours were included in the 1-10A report. An ODI Package filter was implemented and validated in UAT and PROD to exclude cancelled work order status; historical JC values were provided in an Excel recovery file.
important_findings: Actual Labour Hour was incorrectly summarized in Power BI, while the corresponding SC (1-10 report) column was not summarized.
Removing the Power BI aggregation corrected the initial discrepancy and did not require data recovery because values were recalculated using the revised logic.
The 1-10A report and SC PBI included labour hours from cancelled work orders, including JC I000013477 and JC I022120457.
An ODI Package filter was added to exclude work orders with cancelled status.
The ODI filter affected JCs updated after implementation; earlier JCs required corresponding DB_LAST_UPD updates for recalculation.
UAT validation using JCs I001235533 and I001235538 confirmed that cancelled work order labour hours were excluded from PBI.
root_cause: The ODI Package did not filter out cancelled work order status, causing cancelled work order labour hours to be included in Actual Labour Hour calculations. The initial discrepancy was additionally caused by aggregation of the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI.
resolution: Removed aggregation from the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI and deployed an ODI Package filter in PROD on 13-OCT-2023 to exclude cancelled work orders. An Excel file was provided with updated and previous Actual Labor Hour values for earlier JCs.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned incorrect bottom-page total handling on the Non Genuine Instruction Slip and unintended total values on the Non Genuine Delivery Slip. The Non Genuine Instruction Slip bottom-page total was corrected, while the total tag was removed from the Non Genuine Delivery Slip because it was originally intended to be blank. The validated changes were released to the prod environment.
important_findings: The requested correction applied to the Non Genuine Instruction Slip, not the Non Genuine Delivery Slip.
The bottom-page total for the Non Genuine Instruction Slip was fixed.
The Non Genuine Delivery Slip should not display total values on pages below the slip.
The total tag was removed from the Non Genuine Delivery Slip.
Changes were validated, approved, and implemented in the prod environment.
root_cause: The total-value behavior was applied to the wrong slip: the Non Genuine Delivery Slip displayed totals despite being intended to remain blank, while the Non Genuine Instruction Slip required the bottom-page total correction.
resolution: Corrected the bottom-page total on the Non Genuine Instruction Slip and removed the total tag from the Non Genuine Delivery Slip; the approved changes were deployed to prod.

investigation_summary: In the affected service quote, External WO line item ML254826 was included in Service Quote Header Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax). Investigation determined that the user changed the outsourcing carry in Flag from 'N' to 'Y' after customer approval and created a PO without running the Update Quote Header Process. This was classified as a user operation issue rather than a system bug.
important_findings: The External WO line item ML254826 was calculated in Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) on the Service Quote Header.
The External WO was initially created with outsourcing carry in Flag value 'N'; a Parts Internal order would have been required to complete the WO after customer approval.
After the quote was customer approved, the user changed the Outsourcing flag to 'Y' and created the PO.
The Update Quote Header Process was not run after the flag change, leaving Total Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) unchanged.
Calculated fields caused Chargeable Cost on the quote line items to change to 0.
The scenario was replicated in UAT1 using Quote# 1-3Y0ZUP and JC# I001235319.
root_cause: The Outsourcing flag was changed from 'N' to 'Y' after customer approval and PO creation without running the Update Quote Header Process, leaving the Service Quote Header Total Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) unchanged.
resolution: No system fix was required; the issue was rejected as a user operation error. The Update Quote Header Process must be followed after changing the Outsourcing flag.

investigation_summary: A change was deployed to UAT1 and validated in UAT, where JV creation was confirmed to be correct for the provided test records. Recovery was completed using Reverse JV and New JV files, with unnecessary highlighted New JVs excluded. The change was subsequently released to Prod.

investigation_summary: PBI Report SV 1_01 and 1_10A showed inflated Sales Price for affected JCs because Warranty Claim data introduced multiple claim records per work order through a report join. Canceled historical claims and newly generated Submitted claims were both associated with the same JC. Okayama Fuso agreed to remove the FALCON column, and an AMS-CR would be submitted before closing the incident.
important_findings: A change associated with MFTBCFFR-1524 added Warranty Claim fields, including CLAIM_PAID_DATE, CLAIM_STATUS, ACCEPTED_TOTAL_AMOUNT, Claim Status, and Claim Number, to the FDP SV PBI report through a join.
For JC I000011334, multiple claims existed for a work order because initial claims were canceled and new claims were generated with Claim Status "Submitted."
The Warranty Claim-derived "FALCON Status" field produced multiple PBI records for a JC, resulting in multiple Sales Price values and inflated Sales Price.
The issue affected JCs beyond the initially reported cases, including I000018287.
Filtering Field Fix Status to exclude "Canceled" was considered, but could remove JCs such as I000018287 and was not confirmed as a suitable general solution.
Okayama Fuso agreed to remove the FALCON column rather than apply an alternative filtering solution.
root_cause: The join introduced for Warranty Claim/FALCON fields returned multiple claim records for the same work order and JC, including canceled and Submitted claims, causing duplicate PBI records and inflated Sales Price.
resolution: Remove the FALCON column via an AMS-CR.

investigation_summary: The incident required a change to the Posting Date logic for JV of TOB Invoice. The ticket was converted to an AMS-CR, and the agreed solution added a column to Invoice calendar containing the last date of the previous month. The change was developed and tested in UAT, validated by the requester, and implemented in the Prod environment.
important_findings: The agreed correction was to change Posting Date logic for JV of TOB Invoice.
A new Invoice calendar column was required to hold the last date of the previous month.
The new column value is mapped to Posting Date for JV of TOB Invoice.
The ticket type was changed to AMS-CR.
Development was completed and internally tested in UAT before requester validation.
After validation completed, the required changes were deployed to the Prod environment.
root_cause: The existing Posting Date logic for JV of TOB Invoice required a business-rule change to use the last date of the previous month from Invoice calendar.
resolution: Added a new Invoice calendar field containing the previous month's last date and changed the Posting Date mapping for JV of TOB Invoice to use this value; the change was tested in UAT and deployed to Prod.

investigation_summary: The issue was caused by user removal of the editable Branch field in the Parts Internal Order List Applet, which also removed the inventory code. The behavior was not reproduced in UAT1 and RT2. The Branch field was made read-only, and a view matrix change was raised under SR MFTBCFFR-1856 to address the problem.
important_findings: In the Parts Internal Order List Applet, the Branch field was editable.
Removing the Branch field removed the associated inventory code.
The issue was identified as user miss-operation rather than an environment-specific defect.
The behavior was reported as working correctly in UAT1 and RT2.
The Branch field was made read-only and a view matrix change was raised in SR MFTBCFFR-1856.
root_cause: The editable Branch field in the Parts Internal Order List Applet allowed users to remove the branch value, which removed the inventory code.
resolution: Made the Branch field read-only and raised SR MFTBCFFR-1856 to change the view matrix.

investigation_summary: The NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync excluded cases where a revised quote was created before Sales Posting, allowing quote changes to remain linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed. An AMS-CR was implemented for NV and UV to handle revised quotes created before Sales Posting, including cancellation, active/sub-quote reassignment, and validation for pending approvals. The change was validated on UAT1, including a corrected UV rejection-status case, and released to PROD on 5 December.
important_findings: The original sync logic ignored Sales Order sync when the 3rd revised quote was created before NV SO Sales Order.
Revised quotes created before Sales Posting could allow edits to Model Code, option, color, and tire while linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed.

For In Progress or Rejected quotes created before Sales Posting, Delivery Completion approval must cancel the quote and move the active flag and only sub quotes created in the previous revision to the Sales Posting-synced quote revision.

For Pending Approval quotes created before Sales Posting, approval generation or Delivery Completion Approval must show: "There is a correction request request for approval for this order, please check."
During UAT1 validation, UV Quote 1-431G92 rev.5 remained Rejected after Sales Posting; this was resolved and retested with SO E001239841 and Quote 1-43BOUX.
Impacted NV and UV data was extracted after the PROD release for recovery through SRs where applicable.
root_cause: NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync was conditioned on whether a revised quote was created before or after Sales Posting, causing sync processing to be skipped for revised quotes created before Sales Posting.
resolution: Released an AMS-CR for NV and UV that syncs all NV SO Sales Posting Completed cases regardless of revised-quote creation timing; it cancels applicable In Progress/Rejected quotes, updates active flags and prior-revision sub quotes, and blocks Pending Approval quotes with a validation error. The UV UAT1 status-handling defect was corrected before PROD release.

investigation_summary: An AMS-CR was implemented to prevent accounts/codes with Account Type "NULL" from being selectable in the JC/JCO Bill To and Ship To Account Code Pick Applet. The change was validated in UAT-1 and deployed to PROD. Post-release verification confirmed that accounts with Account Type "Null" were no longer displayed.
important_findings: The affected target was the JC/JCO View, specifically the Bill To and Ship To Account Code Pick Applet.
Before the change, codes/accounts with Account Type "NULL" could be selected or displayed.
The required changes were completed and validated in UAT-1.
The AMS-CR changes were deployed to the PROD environment.
PROD verification confirmed that accounts with Account Type "Null" were no longer displayed.
root_cause: The Bill To and Ship To Account Code Pick Applet allowed accounts/codes with Account Type "NULL" to be selected and displayed.
resolution: Implemented the AMS-CR change to exclude Account Type "NULL" accounts/codes from the Bill To and Ship To Account Code Pick Applet, validated it in UAT-1, and deployed it to PROD.
technical_entities: Bill To and Ship To Account Code Pick Applet

investigation_summary: An Order block was applied in D2S to customer codes SA720301, SA720302, SA720303, SA720304, and SA720305 as part of a request covering approximately 288 customer codes. The block was subsequently removed, allowing the customers to order parts normally. All affected orders were confirmed recovered and the incident was closed.
important_findings: D2S applied an Order block to SA720301, SA720302, SA720303, SA720304, and SA720305 at approximately 10:15 JST.
The five customer codes were included in a list provided for an Order block request involving approximately 288 customer codes.
D2S removed the Sales Block from the five customer codes.
All affected orders were confirmed recovered.
root_cause: An Order block/Sales Block was applied to the five customer codes in D2S based on the provided request list.
resolution: D2S removed the Sales Block from SA720301, SA720302, SA720303, SA720304, and SA720305; all orders were recovered.

Validation identified UV trade-in journal, tax, and account-assignment feedback, after which validation was completed and the changes were approved for Production. The changes were deployed to PROD and GI recovery was completed.
important_findings: UAT1 testing used NV order A001234183 and UV order E001234227.
NV GI validation covered Modification, Carry-in-Retrofit, Carry-in-Sbody, and Trailer & Forklift scenarios.
UV validation reported a missing trade-in loss(profit) journal.

investigation_summary: PO Allocation requests received while the material master and Siebel production version creation job was executing failed because the required product version was not yet available. The issue was related to MFTBCFFR-1690; after EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023 reduced job timing, the issue did not recur.
important_findings: PO Allocation requests conflicted with the Product creation job.
The allocation failed when it arrived while the material master and Siebel production version creation job was running.
The product version was unavailable at the time the PO Allocation request was processed.
EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023 reduced job timing and prevented recurrence.
root_cause: A timing conflict between PO Allocation processing and the material master and Siebel production version creation job caused allocation requests to be processed before the product version was available.
resolution: Performed EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023, reducing job timing; the issue did not occur again afterward.

investigation_summary: UAT failures identified issues with the print pop-up, FUSO Logo sizing, and a blank Branch Head name in the UV Quote BIP report. The printing pop-up and FUSO Logo were corrected in UAT1, after which UAT passed. The blank Branch Head was identified as a separate production configuration issue and was assigned to incident MFTBCFFR-1770.
important_findings: The print-out process displayed a Microsoft Word Message during UAT.
The printing pop-up was corrected in UAT1.
The FUSO Logo size was corrected in UAT1 to match NV Quote.
Branch Head was not being set during UV Quote creation, so it was blank in the UV Quote BIP report.
The Branch Head configuration issue exists in SC PROD and FDP PROD and was deferred to MFTBCFFR-1770.
UAT passed after the UAT1 corrections.
root_cause: Branch Head was not set during UV Quote creation due to configuration in SC PROD and FDP PROD, causing the Branch Head name to be blank in the UV Quote BIP report.
resolution: Corrected the printing pop-up and FUSO Logo in UAT1; UAT passed. The Branch Head configuration issue was assigned to PROD incident MFTBCFFR-1770.

investigation_summary: The reported behavior was verified to be the same as SC. The incident was determined not to require corrective action and was rejected.
important_findings: The behavior matched SC.
No product defect or configuration issue was identified.
The incident was rejected.
resolution: Incident rejected because the behavior was confirmed to be consistent with SC.

investigation_summary: For Model Code EB80G41S00M, MC 3, M Body G9H0, and Color Code SA, the relevant record was the first line of the processed file and was ignored during Color Master File Import. As a result, no value was available in Price Master for that combination. Price Master was corrected on PROD.
important_findings: The combination Model Code EB80G41S00M, MC 3, M Body G9H0, and Color Code SA was on the first line of the processed file.
The first-line record was ignored during Color Master File Import.
The ignored import record caused the corresponding value to be unavailable in Price Master.
Price Master was corrected in PROD.
root_cause: The first-line record in the processed file was ignored during Color Master File Import, leaving no Price Master value for Model Code EB80G41S00M, MC 3, M Body G9H0, and Color Code SA.
resolution: Corrected the missing Price Master entry on PROD for the affected combination.

investigation_summary: A Completion date field was added to address a data issue affecting cycle count data sent to KB. The change was validated before and after implementation in the Production Environment, and KB received the cycle count data correctly. The Production implementation was verified successfully.
important_findings: The Completion date field was added.
KB received cycle count data correctly after the change.
Required AMS CR changes were implemented in the Production Environment.
Production validation was completed successfully.
Recovery data for 1st Sep to 19th Sep and restart of the daily batch process were requested after Production release.
resolution: Implemented the required AMS CR changes, including the Completion date field, in the Production Environment and completed successful validation.

investigation_summary: Consumption Tax was missing on Purchase Contracts created through specific workflows. The initial fix covered creation from the UV Purchase Quote list applet, but UAT identified the remaining Assessment Request (Auction Purchase) scenario. The logic was corrected, deployed to Production Environment, and affected historical records were data-patched.
important_findings: The Purchase Contract creation case from the UV Purchase Quote list applet was initially not handled.
UAT confirmed Consumption Tax was displayed for Purchase Contracts created from the UV Purchase Quote list applet after the initial fix.
UAT then identified missing Consumption Tax for Purchase Contracts created from Assessment Request with Assessment Type "Auction purchase".
For Purchase Contracts created from Assessment Request (Auction Purchase), Consumption Tax was corrected to match UV Purchase Order Consumption tax.
Existing records created before the fix did not contain Consumption Tax and required data patching.
root_cause: Consumption Tax population logic did not handle Purchase Contract creation through the UV Purchase Quote list applet and the Assessment Request (Auction Purchase) workflow.
resolution: Implemented the required Production Environment changes to populate Consumption Tax for the affected Purchase Contract creation workflows and data-patched the identified recovery records.

investigation_summary: Dealer code was not sent because supplier code was not configured for the 11SC (Dummy Record) in UAT2 (RT2), while UAT1 worked correctly. After supplier code was set, dealer code was sent correctly; however, FDP PROD received garbage characters from TOB instead of the expected text format. A TOB correction was completed and validated through UAT1 transmission/reception testing, with DJ2L receipt confirmation successful.
important_findings: UAT1 processed the data correctly, while UAT2 (RT2) had no supplier code configured for 11SC (Dummy Record).
Setting the supplier code in RT2 enabled Dealer Code to be sent correctly.
FDP PROD received garbage characters from TOB when data containing Dealer Code was sent.
TOB was corrected and confirmed in the test environment.
UAT1 testing used D21A, D21N, and D21F chassis; D21F recycling status was set to “under construction”.
DJ2L receipt confirmation was successful after the TOB correction.
root_cause: Supplier code was not set for 11SC (Dummy Record) in UAT2 (RT2), preventing Dealer Code from being sent. A separate TOB issue caused FDP PROD to receive garbage characters; the specific technical cause was not documented.
resolution: Set the supplier code in RT2, correct TOB, and validate TOB transmission/reception in UAT1. DJ2L receipt was confirmed successfully.

investigation_summary: FALCON did not receive the Registration Date for NV Sales Order# A000002120 warranty registration due to a code issue in the interface data processing. Investigation found that the UAT-1 program had been changed after SIT because of another FALCON failure. The program was restored to the SIT-approved state, deployed to PROD, and FALCON confirmed correct receipt of the Registration Date.
important_findings: The issue was a code defect affecting interface data sent to FALCON.
The UAT-1 program was modified after UAT SIT in response to another FALCON failure.
The corrective release restored the program, including UAT-1, to the state approved in SIT.
Recovery was completed for NV Sales Order# A000002120 warranty registration.
After the PROD deployment, FALCON received the Registration Date correctly.
root_cause: The UAT-1 program was changed after SIT due to another FALCON failure, causing the interface not to send data to FALCON.
resolution: Restored the program to the SIT-approved state, deployed the changes to PROD, and verified that FALCON received the Registration Date correctly.

investigation_summary: The reported behavior was analyzed and confirmed to work the same way in SC. The incident was reclassified as an Additional CR, and changes were implemented to update the retrofit flag. The changes were validated in UAT and then deployed to the Prod Environment.
important_findings: The behavior was confirmed to be the same in SC.
The incident was changed to an Additional CR after man-day effort information was provided.
The implemented change updates the retrofit flag.
The change was implemented and confirmed in UAT for NV SO# A001234506.
The required AMS CR changes were deployed to the Prod Environment.
resolution: Implemented the required Additional CR/AMS CR changes to update the retrofit flag, validated them in UAT, and deployed them to the Prod Environment.

investigation_summary: UV Purchase Order cost posting had been stopped following a discussion on 1st Aug. Cost posting was re-enabled, validated successfully, and the change was deployed to PROD.
important_findings: UV Purchase Order cost posting was stopped after the 1st Aug discussion.
UV cost posting was enabled for validation.
Validation completed without issue.
The change was deployed to PROD.
resolution: Re-enabled UV cost posting and deployed the validated change to PROD.

investigation_summary: The NV Sales Posting journal was reviewed after Recycle posting had been removed per the business request on 14 June 2023. Other event journals were created successfully, and a change was made to add all option costs to chassis cost posting. Validation was completed and the change was deployed to PROD.
important_findings: Recycle posting in the NV Sales Posting journal was removed per the business request on 14 June 2023.
Recycle posting will not be created unless a code change is made to re-enable it.
Journals were created successfully for Sales Price, Sales Consumption Tax, Reg Expense Taxable, Reg Expense Taxable Tax, and Ref Expense Non Taxable.
The chassis cost posting was changed to include the total cost of all options.
The change was validated and deployed to PROD.
root_cause: Recycle posting was intentionally removed from the NV Sales Posting journal per the business request.
resolution: Updated chassis cost posting to add all option costs, completed validation, and deployed the change to PROD. Recycle posting remains disabled unless a future code change is requested.

investigation_summary: UAT initially failed multiple times for the updated BIP reports. The confirmed issue was an imbalance in Sales Order Sheet 2 compared with Sales Order Sheet 1. The feedback was implemented in the UAT environment, and UAT subsequently passed.
important_findings: UAT failed after initial BIP report updates.
Sales Order Sheet 2 was unbalanced and was required to match Sales Order Sheet 1.
The reported feedback was implemented in the UAT environment.
UAT passed after the implementation.
root_cause: Sales Order Sheet 2 contained an imbalance and did not match Sales Order Sheet 1.
resolution: Implemented the required feedback for the BIP reports in the UAT environment, including correcting the Sales Order Sheet 2 imbalance; UAT passed.

investigation_summary: PO creation succeeded in Siebel and Azure gateway logs showed a successful response from D2S CPI, but concurrent order requests caused an issue in D2S. D2S confirmed that its file based interface from CPI to D2S could not handle requests for different order numbers processed at the same time. D2S applied a solution on FDP PROD, and no further problems were reported before closure.
important_findings: PO Creation was successful on the Siebel side.
Azure gateway logs showed a successful response from D2S CPI.
Siebel can handle concurrent requests for different orders.
D2S could not handle concurrent requests for different order numbers because of the file based interface from CPI to D2S.
D2S confirmed that a solution was applied on FDP PROD.
root_cause: D2S could not handle concurrent requests for different order numbers through the file based interface from CPI to D2S.
resolution: D2S applied a solution on FDP PROD; no new problems were reported afterward.

investigation_summary: The Cycle count batch was updated to interface all records rather than only records with Status = Good. Posting date logic was changed to use the new "Completion Date" field because users can modify the End Date. The changes were deployed to the Production Environment and validation was completed.
important_findings: The Cycle count batch had a Status = Good / On Hand filter that excluded records requiring interface.
All Cycle Count records must be interfaced regardless of On Hand/Good status.
End Date must not be used for posting date because users can change it.
A new "Completion Date" field was added for posting date determination.
For multiple cycle counts for the same part#, multiple Before and After Revision entries are loaded.
The required changes were implemented in the Production Environment and validated.
root_cause: The Cycle count batch filtered records by Status = Good / On Hand and used an unsuitable date field for posting because End Date can be changed by users.
resolution: Removed the On Hand/Good filter, added and used "Completion Date" for the posting date, and deployed the changes to the Production Environment.

investigation_summary: In the Part Return Order PO to Supplier flow, shipments were created only when the order status was Pending Approval. Auto Approval bypassed Pending Approval and updated the status directly to Approved, preventing shipment creation. The logic was changed to create shipments when the status updates to Approved, validated in UAT1, and deployed to Production Environment.
important_findings: Shipment creation in the Part Return Order PO to Supplier case was originally triggered only at Pending Approval status.
Auto Approval updated the order status directly to Approved, bypassing the existing shipment-creation trigger.
The fix creates the shipment when the PO Return Order PO to Supplier status updates to Approved.
The change was validated in UAT1 before deployment to Production Environment.
root_cause: The shipment-creation logic depended on the Pending Approval status, which Auto Approval bypassed by directly setting the status to Approved.
resolution: Updated the Part Return Order PO to Supplier logic to create shipments when the status is updated to Approved; the change was validated in UAT1 and implemented in Production Environment.
technical_entities: Part Return Order PO to Supplier

investigation_summary: AMS CR 610007455 PT_Add PO Return Cancel required FDP behavior to prevent cancellation when a shipment is in Shipped status. The change was implemented and made available on UAT1 for validation, then approved for release. The required changes were subsequently implemented in the Prod Environment.
important_findings: For Stock Transfer or PO to MWH, cancellation must not be allowed when shipment status is Shipped.
For SC, the cancel button must be disabled when shipment status is Shipped.
The same Shipped-status cancellation restriction was required in the FDP version.
Changes were implemented on UAT1 and later released to the Prod Environment.
resolution: Implemented AMS CR 610007455 PT_Add PO Return Cancel changes in the Prod Environment after UAT1 validation and approval.
technical_entities: AMS CR 610007455 PT_Add PO Return Cancel

investigation_summary: A UV Sales Order could map a Purchase Order that was already associated with a Parts Sales Order when the same VIN was used. The mapping logic did not exclude Parts Sales Orders, causing Parts Sales Order M000006663 to be mapped with UV Sales Order E000007349 for VIN FG508BD-430572. The mapping condition was updated, recovery was completed, and the change passed UAT before deployment to Production Environment.
important_findings: Parts Staff processed Purchase Quote and Parts Sales Order M000006663 using VIN FG508BD-430572, which mapped the Purchase Order to that VIN.
Branch Sales created UV Sales Order E000007349 with the same VIN and used the map button to select the UV Purchase Order.
The existing mapping logic also mapped the Parts Sales Order associated with the Purchase Order to the UV Sales Order.
The scenario was not handled in the application and also existed in FDP UAT.
The fix was implemented in UAT, passed UAT, and was subsequently deployed to Production Environment.
Recovery of the affected data was completed.
root_cause: The UV Sales Order map-button logic did not exclude Parts Sales Orders already mapped to the selected Purchase Order, allowing a Parts Sales Order to be mapped to a UV Sales Order when both used the same VIN.
resolution: Updated the UV Sales Order mapping condition to omit Parts Sales Orders associated with the selected Purchase Order, completed data recovery, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it to Production Environment.

investigation_summary: The investigation confirmed that the amount sent from Siebel was correct because records with "Missing" status are not interfaced to KB. MDIS reported that Inventory ID 1-3URB0G was missing; it was not sent because its Counted date was 2023/09/11 07:45:22 PM and cycle count data is sent daily based on Counted date. A change request, MFTBCFFR-1743, was created to address the date-mapping issue.
important_findings: Only records with Availability and Status of On Hand/Good are interfaced to KB.
Records with "Missing" status are excluded from the Siebel-to-KB interface amount calculation.
Cycle count data is sent daily using the Counted date as the selection logic.
Inventory ID 1-3URB0G was not sent because its Counted date was 2023/09/11 07:45:22 PM.
Multiple cycle counts for the same Part# on the same day can create ambiguity for "Before Cycle Count" and "After Cycle Count" quantities.
root_cause: The daily cycle count interface selects records based on Counted date, causing Inventory ID 1-3URB0G to be excluded from the expected transmission/reporting period.

investigation_summary: Parts orders could be created when required Job Card customer-related fields were blank, allowing incomplete values to be copied to the parts order. The implemented Additional CR added validations before parts-order creation for both Customer Code and Bill To Basic Account Code. The changes were validated in UAT1 and deployed to the Production Environment.
important_findings: A parts order could be created when the JC Customer Code was blank.
The Bill To Basic Account Code is copied to the parts order and also must be populated in the JC.
Branch-CS-Staff had editable access in View Role Matric, allowing Customer Code values to be edited; changing this access to read-only was deferred to a separate SR.
Validation was added to the WO'sButton to prevent parts-order creation when Customer Code or Bill To Basic Account Code is blank.
The UAT1 implementation was validated and approved for PROD release before deployment.
root_cause: Missing validation on the WO'sButton allowed parts-order creation when the Job Card Customer Code and Bill To Basic Account Code were blank.
resolution: Implemented and deployed validations in UAT1 and the Production Environment requiring both Customer Code and Bill To Basic Account Code to be entered on the JC before creating a parts order.

investigation_summary: Sales orders A000001195 and A000003231 were investigated for absence from the NV 3-06 report. Both are Child Order Sales Order cases with Required Quantity greater than 1, and the current report configuration filters out sales orders with Required Quantity greater than 1. The behavior matches the SC configuration, so the issue was not a defect.
important_findings: Sales orders A000001195 and A000003231 have Required Quantity greater than 1.
The affected orders are Child Order Sales Order cases.
The NV 3-06 report configuration filters Sales Orders based on Required Quantity.
Sales Orders with Required Quantity greater than 1 do not appear in the NV 3-06 report.
The configuration behaves the same as SC.
root_cause: The NV 3-06 report's current Required Quantity filter excludes Child Order Sales Orders with Required Quantity greater than 1.
resolution: Confirmed expected behavior consistent with SC and rejected the bug.

investigation_summary: When License Plate Number Fee or Illuminated License Plate Fee was blank, the consumption tax value sent to KB was 0. The issue was reproduced in UAT1, fixed there, and validated by creating an invoice in the Shōzobugyo test environment where consumption tax displayed correctly. The required change was then deployed to Production.
important_findings: Blank License Plate Number Fee caused consumption tax to be sent as 0 to KB.
Blank Illuminated License Plate Fee caused consumption tax to be sent as 0 to KB.
The issue also existed in UAT1.
After the UAT1 fix, an invoice created in the Shōzobugyo test environment displayed consumption tax correctly.
The approved fix was implemented in the Production environment.
root_cause: When License Plate Number Fee or Illuminated License Plate Fee was blank, the system sent a consumption tax value of 0 to KB.
resolution: Fixed the handling of blank License Plate Number Fee and Illuminated License Plate Fee values in UAT1, validated the corrected consumption tax display, and deployed the required changes to Production.

investigation_summary: SV_Run Report settings differed from UAT-1. The BIP View Association (LOV) was updated according to the revised business-provided Excel list, validated in UAT-2, and deployed to Production.
important_findings: The reported discrepancy was that SV_Run Report settings were different from UAT-1.
BIP View Association (LOV) was updated based on the revised business-provided Excel list.
The changes were implemented in RT2 and verified in UAT-2 to match UAT-1.
The verified changes were deployed to Production.
root_cause: BIP View Association (LOV) configuration did not match the updated business-provided list and differed from UAT-1.
resolution: Updated the BIP View Association (LOV) according to the revised Excel list, validated the changes in UAT-2, and deployed them to Production.

investigation_summary: PNC Master was missing from the Biz approved Initial Set up master list, making it unavailable in RT and PROD. The master data was imported from SC to FDP, validated in RT2, and then uploaded to PROD. The PROD upload was confirmed with no issues and the incident was closed.
important_findings: PNC Master was not included in the Biz approved Initial Set up master list.
The missing master data was unavailable in both RT and PROD.
Import steps were initiated to upload PNC Master from SC to FDP.
The data upload was completed and validated in RT2 before PROD release.
PNC Master was uploaded to PROD and confirmed without issues.
root_cause: PNC Master was absent from the Biz approved Initial Set up master list.
resolution: Imported PNC Master from SC to FDP, uploaded and validated it in RT2, then released the data to PROD.
technical_entities: Biz approved Initial Set up master list

investigation_summary: Vehicle master records required the VIN# in the Vin Number, Serial Number, and Key fields. D21A, D21C, and D21E updated Vin Number and Serial Number but did not populate Key because of an existing configuration issue since the SC version. The configuration was corrected, validated in UAT1, and deployed to Production.
important_findings: The vehicle master contains Vin Number, Serial Number, and Key fields, each requiring the VIN# value.
D21A, D21C, and D21E processing populated Vin Number and Serial Number but omitted the Key value.
The missing Key population was caused by an existing system configuration issue from the SC version.
Impacted chassis order records were recovered by updating the Key column with the VIN Number, with no impact to the KB interface after recovery.
UAT1 verification confirmed no chassis orders created after September 8 had a blank Vehicle identification number before the Production release.
root_cause: System configuration for D21A, D21C, and D21E omitted mapping/population of the vehicle master Key field with the VIN# value.
resolution: Corrected the D21A, D21C, and D21E configuration so Vin Number, Serial Number, and Key are populated with VIN#, validated the change in UAT1, and implemented it in Production. Impacted records were recovered until the Production fix was applied.

investigation_summary: The Real Time Invoice API returned incorrect invoice delivery and registration dates because date mappings did not account for whether registration and delivery were completed or pending. The initial UAT logic was partially implemented and migrated to production. A fix was validated in UAT1 for NV and UV sample requests and then deployed to the production environment.
important_findings: During initial Real Time Invoice API development, Planned Delivery Date and Requested Registration Date were mapped to the Invoice.
The initial mapping failed for orders where Registration and Delivery were completed, for which Actual Delivery/Registration Date should have been displayed in the Invoice.
Mapping Actual Delivery/Registration Date unconditionally was also incorrect; the logic needed to distinguish completed versus pending registration and delivery.
The partially implemented UAT logic was migrated to production, causing the incident.
UAT1 validation for NV order A001233104 and UV order E001233107 returned "Invoice details returned successfully." with DeliveryDate and RegisteredDate values.
root_cause: Invoice date-mapping logic in the Real Time Invoice API was partially implemented and did not conditionally select Planned/Requested dates versus Actual Delivery/Registration dates based on registration and delivery completion status.
resolution: The fix was implemented in UAT1, validated by UAT testing, approved for release, and deployed to the production environment.

investigation_summary: A delay was reported for communication sent from the FDP Siebel System. The message was confirmed as sent at the same time from FDP Siebel System, and the issue was escalated to the D2S Team for investigation; no technical cause or corrective action was documented.
important_findings: Communication from the FDP Siebel System was reported as sent at the same time.
A delay was identified and raised with the D2S Team.
The incident was closed without documented investigation findings or remediation.

investigation_summary: The incident concerned Tax Confirmation during an Initial Registration Request. The implemented workflow change cancels the Initial Registration Request when the user selects "Change Request", creates a New Registration request with an editable Expense Item, and performs Tax Confirmation afterward. The change was validated in UAT and deployed to the Production environment.
important_findings: Selecting "Change Request" during Tax Confirmation cancels the Initial Registration Request.
A New Registration request is created with the Expense Item editable.
Tax Confirmation is performed after creation of the New Registration request.
The change was confirmed in UAT and then applied to the Production environment.
resolution: Implemented and deployed a workflow change that cancels the Initial Registration Request on "Change Request", creates an editable New Registration request, and performs Tax Confirmation afterward.

investigation_summary: BIP reports for Quote 34 omitted expected line items when cancelled items occupied the page-2 positions. The existing BIP template logic paginated 22 line items per page before excluding cancelled lines, resulting in an empty page. The filtering logic was moved from the BIP template to Siebel so that only non-cancelled line items are sent to BI Publisher. The change was tested in UAT1 and deployed to Prod after validation.
important_findings: Quote 34 had cancelled line items from line 15 through line 53.
The BIP Report logic printed 22 line items per page and ignored line items with Cancelled status.
All line items allocated to page 2 were cancelled, so no line items were printed on that page.
Filtering of cancelled line items was moved from the BIP template to Siebel.
Siebel now sends only non-cancelled line items to BI Publisher.
The change was tested in UAT1 and implemented in Prod Environment.
root_cause: The BIP template paginated line items before excluding Cancelled items; because all items assigned to page 2 were cancelled, the page printed no line items.
resolution: Moved cancelled-line filtering from the BIP template to Siebel, so Siebel sends only non-cancelled line items to BI Publisher; the change was tested in UAT1 and deployed to Prod Environment.

investigation_summary: PO return drill-down behavior differed from PO drill-down, opening a page below the details screen instead of above it. Drilling down from the PO return parent order number also displayed an error screen. The fixes were implemented and validated in UAT1, then released to Production.
important_findings: PO drill-down displayed a page above the details screen, while PO return drill-down displayed a page below the details screen.
Drilling down on the parent order number of a PO return displayed an error screen.
An initial UAT1 implementation did not resolve the parent order drill-down error and required further correction.
The corrected implementation was validated in UAT1 and approved for Production release.
Required changes were implemented in the Production environment and the incident was closed.
resolution: Updated PO return drill-down navigation to match PO behavior and fixed the error when drilling down on the PO return parent order number; changes were validated in UAT1 and released to Production.

investigation_summary: A production issue affecting a BIP report was resolved after clicking the template upload button again. The available comment indicates the template may not have been uploaded correctly initially.
important_findings: The issue occurred in production.
The affected component was a BIP report template.
Clicking the template upload button again restored correct operation.
The initial template upload may not have completed correctly.
root_cause: The template for the BIP report may not have been uploaded correctly initially.
resolution: Re-uploaded the template by clicking the template upload button again.

investigation_summary: PO to D2S stock orders created by the Replenishment job had a blank Department Code because they were created by the SADMIN batch user, which had no branch code assigned. A fix was implemented and validated in UAT1, then released to the Production Environment. The change also set Inventory Name as the Department Code for Parts Purchase Orders and used Received Date as Posting Date.
important_findings: Normal PO to D2S orders populate Department Code from the branch code of the Created By User.
Stock orders are created by the Replenishment job through the Batch Job user SADMIN, which has no assigned branch code.
The stock-order scenario was not tested during SIT/UAT.
The UAT1 fix was tested using PO N001233022 and approved for production release.
Production changes set Inventory Name in Department Code for Parts Purchase Orders and set Received Date as Posting Date.
root_cause: PO to D2S stock orders were created by the Replenishment Batch Job using SADMIN, and SADMIN had no branch code assigned; therefore Department Code was populated as blank.
resolution: Implemented and released changes to the Production Environment to populate Department Code from Inventory Name for Parts Purchase Orders and use Received Date as Posting Date.

investigation_summary: The issue was fixed and made available in UAT1 for verification. After confirmation that no problem remained, the changes were released and deployed to PROD.

The approved changes were deployed to PROD on 12 September 2023.

No corrective action was documented in the comments.
important_findings: The issue was reported as a High Price issue for JC I000002130 and Quote 1-9IZB5.
Multiple line items in the Service Quote were updated after the Approval Request was generated.
For JC I000002130, Parts Internal Order line-item cancellation occurred at 2023/09/04 05:15:07 PM, after Service Quote Generate approval was clicked at 2023/09/04 04:41:50 PM.
The same sequence was identified for JCs I000002130 and I000004708.
root_cause: Users cancelled parts from Parts Internal Order after clicking Service Quote Generate approval, causing Service Quote line-item updates and the High Price issue.

investigation_summary: PO cancellation processing failed because the MF_PO_CANCEL_REASON LOV value FJ was not present in FDP. FJ had been added in SC after the FDP cutoff date. Reject reason codes FJ, ZF, and FN were added to UAT1 and Production, and the affected Purchase Orders were recovered.
important_findings: MF_PO_CANCEL_REASON LOV value FJ was missing from FDP.
FJ was added in SC after the FDP cutoff date under SR: 540074495.
Reject reason codes FJ, ZF, and FN were added in the UAT1 environment and Production environment.
Purchase Orders receiving FJ reject reason had failed on the Siebel side.
Recovery was completed for the affected Purchase Orders.
root_cause: The MF_PO_CANCEL_REASON LOV value FJ was not present in FDP because it was added in SC after the FDP cutoff date.
resolution: Added reject reason codes FJ, ZF, and FN to UAT1 and Production, then completed recovery of the affected Purchase Orders.

investigation_summary: The issue occurred in the UAT1 and RT2 environments regarding availability of the Mapping Quote BIP report from the Job Card detail view. The investigation determined that mapping the report to the Job Card detail view was technically infeasible because the report is based on a service Quote while the view is based on a Job Card. The BIP report was removed from the Job Card detail view and remains available from the service quotation list and detail view.
important_findings: The issue was observed in UAT1 and RT2 environments.
The Mapping Quote BIP report is based on a service Quote.
The Job Card detail view is based on a Job Card.
Mapping the Mapping Quote BIP report to the Job Card detail view was determined to be technically infeasible.
The report can be generated from the service quotation list and detail view.
root_cause: The Mapping Quote BIP report is based on a service Quote, whereas the Job Card detail view is based on a Job Card, making the report mapping technically infeasible.
resolution: Removed the Mapping Quote BIP report from the Job Card detail view; the report remains available from the service quotation list and detail view.

investigation_summary: NV Quote allowed a Closing date value of 30 in the Approval Information tab, while NV Sales Order accepted only 10, 20, or EOM. Auto Order failed when creating an NV SO with the unsupported value. The logic was corrected in UAT, validated, and deployed to Production.
important_findings: The Finance Tab of NV Quote and NV Sales Order restricted Closing date values to 10, 20, and EOM.
The Approval Information tab of NV Quote allowed additional Closing date values, including 30.
Selecting 30 in Approval Information caused an error during Auto Order because 30 could not be entered in the NV SO Closing date field.
The initial UAT implementation failed because Baseline type behavior did not match SC incident#520320920 requirements.
The corrected logic makes Closing Date non-editable when Baseline type is "Closing" and clears Closing Date when Baseline type changes from "Closing" to "On Delivery".
root_cause: Inconsistent Closing date validation between the NV Quote Approval Information tab and NV Sales Order allowed an unsupported value (30) to be selected, causing Auto Order to fail during NV SO creation.
resolution: Updated the Closing date and Baseline type logic in UAT, validated the changes, and deployed the required changes to Production.

investigation_summary: Tax Finalization Journal entries for SV Expense Posting created journals with a blank credit-side Client code because the required Vendor Code was not available from the Service screen. Vendor Code is mapped from the tax redger master.
Tax Finalization Journal refers to Vendor Code for both NV/UV and SV cases.
Vendor Code was not available in the Service screen for SV Expense Posting; Expense Payee Code was considered as the applicable source.
Code changes for SV Expense Posting were validated in UAT2 by re-triggering the journal for JC:I000009394.
The required changes were deployed to the Production environment after UAT2 validation.
root_cause: The Tax Finalization Journal logic did not populate the credit-side Client code correctly for SV Expense Posting because Vendor Code was unavailable from the Service screen.
resolution: Updated the code to reflect the correct Client code for SV Expense Posting, re-triggered and validated the journal in UAT2 for JC:I000009394, then deployed the changes to Production.

investigation_summary: A cancelled Assessment record required recovery after the vehicle was restocked. The Assessment Request vehicle-value update depends on a change to the UV Inventory vehicle value. Because UV Inventory already contained the same value, 1,034,500, no inventory update occurred and the downstream Assessment Request update was not triggered. Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered, and the proposed recovery approach was to null the UV Inventory vehicle value before recovery.
important_findings: The issue could not be replicated in UAT1 or RT2, and other Assessment Requests worked correctly in PROD.
Vehicle H000000001 was restocked and cancelled through SR#MFTBCFFR-1637.
The workflow is: Assessment Request Stock in Verification Completed; UV Inventory vehicle value updated from UV Purchase Order; Assessment Request vehicle value updated from the UV Inventory update.
UV Inventory already held vehicle value 1,034,500 after Assessment #H000000001 completed a re-evaluation request with the same value.
Because the UV Inventory value did not change, the downstream Assessment Request update trigger did not execute.
Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered with Vehicle Value 1,034,500.
root_cause: UV Inventory already contained vehicle value 1,034,500, so the update from UV Purchase Order produced no value change and did not trigger the downstream Assessment Request vehicle-value update during recovery of a cancelled Assessment.
resolution: Recovered Assessment Number H000000037 with Vehicle Value 1,034,500. For cancelled-Assessment recovery cases, add a recovery step to set the UV Inventory vehicle value to null so the subsequent update triggers the Assessment Request update.
technical_entities: Assessment Request Stock in Verification Completed

investigation_summary: The issue involved the first record in BIP being the Header of the D21G file and was reproducible in the UAT1 environment. important_findings: The first record on BIP was identified as the Header of the D21G file.
The same issue occurred in the UAT1 environment.
The fix was implemented and verified in UAT1 before approval for PROD release.
Required changes were deployed to the Production environment.
Recovery was completed for D21G files output on 8/29/23, 8/30/23, 8/31/23, and 9/1/23 at 9:55 AM.
resolution: Implemented the required changes in Production and recovered the affected D21G output records.

investigation_summary: PO Creation outbound calls to D2S intermittently failed with an internal error and affected PO records were initially recovered by repushing. D2S identified DNS anycast route instability caused by flapping of the track associated with the IP route. D2S removed the track from the static route, after which the DNS anycast route stabilized; no further D2S failures were recorded during one-day monitoring.
important_findings: The DMS_PO_CREATION outbound call failed at DMS_PO_CREATIONPort with an internal error referencing MPL ID AGTuzXKF0wh4rvW5ufoSPGKUIqtU.
Repushing failed PO Creation requests processed successfully, and all records through 31 August were recovered.
D2S initially reported a timeout and increased the read timeout in CPI.
D2S later identified DNS anycast route flapping caused by flapping of the track associated with the IP route.
Removing the track from the static route stabilized the DNS anycast route; the reconfigured track remained under monitoring and was not yet reattached to the static route.
root_cause: Flapping of the track associated with the IP route caused DNS anycast route flapping on the D2S side, resulting in intermittent D2S PO Creation failures.
resolution: D2S removed the track from the static route, stabilizing the DNS anycast route. Failed requests were repushed and recovered, and the incident was closed after one day without further D2S failures.

investigation_summary: The issue occurs in an NV Quote when a Model Code with options is changed. Repricing does not update Total List Price and Actual Cost on the Quote Line Item. The behavior was confirmed to be the same as an existing SC issue; a logic refinement in FDP was proposed through an AMS-CR, and the incident was requested for rejection.
important_findings: Reproduction flow: create Opportunity and Quote, add Model Code, Option, Color, and Tire, change the Model Code, then open the Option Screen.
When a Model Code having options is changed in an NV Quote, repricing does not update Total List Price and Actual Cost in the Quote Line Item.
The issue existed in the SC version for Total List Price and was migrated from SC.
Manual recovery was proposed and a recovery Excel file was provided for confirmation.
The proposed permanent fix was to refine FDP logic to update Total List Price and Actual Cost after Model Code changes in an NV Quote via an AMS-CR.
root_cause: Repricing logic does not update Total List Price and Actual Cost in the Quote Line Item when a Model Code having options is changed in an NV Quote.

investigation_summary: For Retro Option quotes, the Cost value was incorrectly sourced from Operation Cost in Option Price Master instead of Operation Cost in Retro Option Master. The scenario was reproduced in UAT and fixed in UAT1 and UAT2. After UAT approval, the change was deployed to Okayama PROD.
important_findings: Retro Option Cost value was sourced from Operation Cost in Option Price Master.
The required source for Retro Option Cost value is Operation Cost in Retro Option Master.
The scenario was not previously covered and behaved the same in UAT.
The fix was validated in UAT1 and UAT2 before deployment to Okayama PROD.
root_cause: Retro Option logic fetched the Cost value from Operation Cost in Option Price Master rather than Operation Cost in Retro Option Master.
resolution: Corrected the Retro Option Cost-value sourcing logic, validated it in UAT1 and UAT2, and deployed the change to Okayama PROD.

investigation_summary: View navigation with data load was not handled correctly across position types, reproducing on UAT1 with Branch-Sales-Staff. The "Me" filter did not display list results for both ordered chassis status and stock cars. The filters were changed to remove "Me" and retain only "All", validated in UAT, and deployed to Production.

View navigation with data load was not handled correctly for position types.
The "Me" filter did not display records in the list.
Filters were corrected for both ordered chassis status and stock cars by removing "Me" and retaining only "All".
The change was confirmed in UAT before deployment to Production.
